in writing, i am pleased that today we are discussing with the commission and the council concrete measures, especially financial, to implement the youth guarantee at member state level. the current youth employment situation is tragic in most member states of the european union, including lithuania, and is only getting worse. young people do not need pretty words and promises, but effective and targeted guarantees. the commission's initiative to give our young people the opportunity to start work, study or do an internship no later than four months after they have completed their studies or become unemployed is welcome, but i would like to ask the commission how and when the member states intend to implement these objectives. particular attention should be paid to helping those member states which have already 'buckled down' or are still cutting their budgets to implement this programme. in addition, in addition to highlighting the record-breaking youth unemployment, concrete actions should be taken to help business companies and enterprises to create as many new jobs as possible for young people, and to ensure closer coordination and cooperation between educational institutions, governments and employers. moreover, the creation of programmes and initiatives alone will not solve the current problems of youth employment. the commission should provide specific financial support for this programme in the member states, otherwise the youth guarantee will remain a model of good intentions and expectations.
in writing. the youth guarantee initiative discussed by the european parliament today is a major incentive for the eu member states' ministers for social affairs and employment to focus on targeted actions to reduce youth unemployment and social exclusion. the youth guarantee scheme provides very specific and clear targets for young people under 25 and under 30 with a tertiary education to be able to enter employment, further education or training within four months of leaving school or losing their job. that is a commendable example. because when the criteria for achieving the goals are clearly stated, the effort is likely to be more effective. experience has shown that abstract language and the declaration of the need to tackle the problem of youth unemployment, which is approaching the critical threshold, without clear criteria for monitoring the situation and justifying the results, have been simply ineffective. it remains to be seen whether the member states' ministers will accept the proposed action plan and take the initiative in their own countries to focus the efforts of business and public authorities to tackle the problem.
mr president, 13 january is an outstanding day for the freedom of europe. today we mark the 30th anniversary of the acknowledgment of the truth by the european parliament. on 13 january 1983, a resolution was adopted which recognised the fact of occupation and annexation of lithuania, latvia and estonia by the soviet union and called for action by the international community. eight years later on the same date, on 13 january 1991, it took the ultimate sacrifice to defend my country’s freedom, when the soviet military attacked singing masses in vilnius with tanks and bullets. this desperate act by the kremlin left 14 defenceless people dead, many hundreds injured, and the world shocked. today europe is free and reunited, and i want to thank this house and each and every one who dared to speak out at that time for truth and freedom. however, when it comes to cooperation among the eu countries in bringing to justice those who committed crimes against humanity, there is still a lack of understanding. i call for deeper knowledge of the most recent history of europe. truth and remembrance solidifies our union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on sustainable urban development, which aims to promote the competitiveness of the eu as a whole by exploiting the potential of the eu's regions and urban areas. it is proposed that medium- and long-term action plans for urban areas be developed to complete and restore parts of cities, restructure abandoned areas, support artistic and cultural heritage and optimise the use of cohesion policy funds to achieve these objectives. as the most vulnerable groups of the population (who are often excluded) are threatened by urban regeneration processes, i agree that priority should be given to ensuring the social sustainability of urban regeneration by providing for appropriate housing policies and services, and the integration of vulnerable and excluded groups in urban areas. it is important to give citizens access to public spaces, parks and places for leisure, culture and sport. i also support calls for incentives to combat energy inefficiency, reduce urban pollution and noise, and ensure sustainable mobility, quality water supply and waste management services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because european cities are one of the main centres of scientific and innovation, cultural and technological flourishing, home to more than two thirds of the european population. on the other hand, cities also suffer from the main problems of unemployment, poverty and discrimination. it could be argued that the further our cities develop, the more economic, social and territorial development will take place in the future. urban development and regeneration is one of the key indicators for the creation of a european model of sustainable urban development. the contribution of programmes such as urban was crucial, as they also implemented measures for social inclusion, such as a new approach to urban regeneration, a common vision to go beyond all social, economic, environmental and infrastructure measures. it is also important to emphasise the need to pay greater attention to the suburbs and their inhabitants. if we can move the city even further into the suburbs, the suburbs could become the basis for a new model of social and economic development. in order to maximise the achievement of the objectives and results set out in the europe 2020 strategy, all sectors, levels of government and territories should be involved and encouraged to cooperate in order to overcome the eroding trends that have emerged during the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - i voted for this document. more than two thirds of europe's population now live in cities. cities are the flourishing spaces of science and technology, culture and innovation. on the other hand, cities also have the most problems, such as unemployment, discrimination and poverty. as cities address the challenges of climate change mitigation, job creation, well-being and quality of life, we need to focus on sustainable urban development. the way our cities develop is the way our economic, social and territorial development will develop in the future. urban renewal and regeneration, seen as sources of wealth and opportunity, is one of the key challenges facing the eu in strengthening the links between urban and development and between the city centre and the suburban areas.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because urban development and renewal are an integral part of the recovery and growth of the eu economy as a whole, and at the same time of the eu's global competitiveness. in the implementation of cohesion policy, particular attention must be paid to the development of regional and urban areas, to the question of the social sustainability of urban regeneration. improving the living environment and quality of life will help attract a highly skilled workforce and thus contribute to attractive job creation, economic growth in the country's smaller cities and business competitiveness. to ensure a better quality of the environment, it is necessary to combat inefficiently the use of energy and local potential. it should be noted that the preservation of the natural, cultural and historical heritage is an integral element of the quality of life and that an integrated approach is therefore required to achieve this objective in this field.
in writing. − the report tackles the issue of sustainable urban development which represents the engine of the economy, manufacturing and employment. cohesion policy should focus on sustainable urban development which plays a key role in achieving the objectives of europe 2020 and which is a source of economic growth. economic growth can only be sustainable if it is led by measures designed to reduce poverty, social exclusion and environmental hazards. however, nowadays urban areas face many challenges which at this time of economic crisis are difficult to deal with. that is why the set of actions mentioned in the report could serve as a guideline in order to achieve sustainable urban development. such actions include urban and social regeneration, energy efficiency and the fight against poverty. lithuania, as a country where the majority of the population lives in urban areas, has to take actions in order to prevent urban decline, promote urban regeneration and support actions to reinforce social cohesion. i welcome the importance of this report for future cohesion policy and believe that urban development is vital for sustainable growth in lithuania. the eu can only be competitive if cohesion policy fully uses the potential of its urban areas.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for more efficient and effective eu funding programmes to develop eu territorial cohesion policy, interaction and coordination. in the context of the economic crisis, cohesion policy funding has become increasingly important for the eu's regions, alongside the need to ensure that the funds are spent properly. the proposal also provides for the involvement of local and regional authorities in all stages of the development and implementation of eu funding programmes, so that economic and social needs are addressed at the level closest to the citizens. i support the proposals made to clarify the rules, checks and eligibility criteria for funding. the application of the proposed measures must be kept as simple as possible in order to avoid an additional administrative burden for local authorities. i also support the possibility for these institutions to use more than one eu funding programme to support projects, thus improving the efficiency of funding. the funds must be allocated in a way that addresses the eu's long-term social and economic challenges.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the aim of the common provisions regulation, or cohesion policy, is to reduce disparities between the regions of the european union by strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion. it is important to note that the joint strategic programme includes mechanisms to improve coordination between the funds (erdf, esf, cohesion fund, eafrd, emff) and other eu policies. in this context, it can be argued that territorial cohesion, covering the various cohesion policy areas, is already recognised as a key eu objective in the lisbon treaty. it is important to note that territorial cohesion objectives are inextricably linked to economic and social challenges. however, it is important to ensure a proper balance between the development and implementation of cohesion policy and the necessary checks on the use of funds and their effectiveness. it is therefore important to develop simpler and clearer rules for the use of financial instruments, ensuring greater efficiency for all five funds.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because cohesion policy aims to reduce disparities between the eu regions. this is attempted by strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion. in the current economic environment, it is clear that cohesion policy funding is becoming increasingly important for europe's regions and that there is a growing need to ensure that money is spent more effectively so that citizens can benefit from eu funding. i supported the proposals in the general provisions regulation as they call for better coordination and integration of funding programmes to ensure a greater impact of funding.
in writing. − i agree with the provisions in the document adopted today that greater integration of the funds must be provided for and that more effective mechanisms for integrating the funds must be established. often the same project could be implemented more efficiently by funding it from another fund, but the mechanisms are too complex and inflexible to allow this (in lithuania, unfortunately, this was one of the obstacles that led to the slow renovation of buildings). this results in a double loss: lost funds and failed projects. i therefore welcome parliament's position in calling for simpler and more flexible mechanisms for the integration of the funds.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the eu as a whole will prosper only if the development of all its territories is balanced. it should be noted that territorial cohesion is horizontal, covering a wide range of sectors. the funding of eu cohesion policy must therefore remain stable in order to achieve convergence. a stronger and more integrated territorial approach is needed to promote greater integration and cooperation between european funds. i believe that we need to create simpler and clearer common rules to ensure the effectiveness of the funds and to facilitate the wider use of financial instruments and the reduction of administrative burdens. local communities must be involved in the development and adoption of decisions relating to specific regions and areas, and partnerships and networks must be encouraged. only by working together will these measures reduce the territorial gap between eu regions, prevent territorial isolation and ensure equal prosperity for eu regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the harmonisation of the solidarity fund regulation, simplifying the funding procedures and providing clearer, more precise and more transparent definitions. the solidarity fund, one of the most effective and well-reviewed eu instruments, supports emergency rescue operations for people affected by disasters and eases the burden on member states in the event of a disaster. the current long duration of mobilisation of the fund, the excessive length of administrative procedures, and the delay in providing assistance to affected member states often result in the failure to achieve the expected results. the solidarity fund needs to be more flexible, more effective and more visible, and i therefore support the proposals set out here to clarify the scope and scope of the fund, to remove any possible legal uncertainty. most of the administrative problems relate to applications for the exceptional category of regional disasters, so it is essential to clarify the criteria for receiving support from the fund in the event of a so-called minor disaster. disaster prevention is the simplest and cheapest way to reduce vulnerability in the event of a disaster, and i therefore support the call for eu regions to make more use of the various disaster prevention funding opportunities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union has already set up an eu solidarity fund in 2002 to respond adequately to the consequences of natural disasters. it is worth noting that since its creation until september 2012, the fund has provided financial assistance to compensate for the damage caused by 49 disasters (mainly fires and floods). it is clear that this solidarity fund is an important tool for rescuing many countries and their people in the event of a major disaster. however, the fund's activities have recently received increasing attention and criticism from many member states. this may be due to the fact that the number of applicants to the european commission has increased in recent years, partly because of the increase in accidents and partly because the current rules are not sufficiently clear, i.e. the wording of the regulation on accidents of this type is ambiguous. for example, it is not clearly defined which disaster qualifies for aid when applications are submitted under the exceptional rules applicable to exceptional regional disasters. in order to avoid further discontent between the parties, it is necessary to define clearly and precisely the concept of disaster, by establishing common criteria for assessing the extent of the damage caused and by setting limits which are adapted to take account of the territorial level concerned.
in writing. - i agreed to this. the solidarity fund is important as a key instrument through which the eu can respond to major disasters occurring on the territory of the union or in countries negotiating accession to the eu. despite the positive perception of the fund by the majority of eu citizens, it is necessary to improve its operation to make it more flexible and visible. this would also increase the confidence of eu citizens in the eu. the current duration of the mobilisation of the fund is excessive and needs to be shortened. it is also necessary to improve the efficiency and speed of the administrative procedures necessary to mobilise the fund, which involve the intervention of three eu institutions before approval, thus making the procedures too long and prolonging the time until assistance is provided to the affected member states, and thus not achieving the expected results.
in writing. - i agree with this report. the solidarity fund is one of the best instruments available to the european union. in the light of new needs, the fund should become more flexible and efficient, with a permanent capacity to respond effectively to new challenges. in particular, the funds of the solidarity fund following a natural disaster should be mobilised as quickly as possible and efficiently, and applications for financial assistance should be processed swiftly. the time taken to provide assistance to the population of regions affected by natural disasters should therefore be reduced and bureaucratic procedures simplified. however, it is essential to ensure that new amendments to the regulation do not create additional burdens for the budgets of the union or the member states.
in writing. − the european solidarity fund, established in 2002, is a relief instrument for eu member states or candidate countries affected by natural disasters. over the past decade, certain weaknesses in the fund's operations have become apparent. natural disasters often cause more damage than the solidarity fund can cover, and the process of disbursing aid is complex and time-consuming. this makes the recovery process in the member state more difficult, as funds reach the regions too late. i voted in favour of this report because the proposals contained in it will give the solidarity fund flexibility and allow it to respond more quickly to disasters. the proposed amendments will facilitate the disbursement of aid to the affected countries. only in this way will the solidarity fund be able to remain one of the most important, effective and appreciated union instruments for showing solidarity with its citizens.
in writing. − the report speaks of the changes to the regulation governing the solidarity fund (eusf) that are essential for the operability of the fund. the importance of the eusf is well-known. ever since the creation of the solidarity fund and up until now, eusf has proven to be one of the most successful union instruments and a useful tool to intervene in the event of a disaster. many expectations were placed on that fund but changes in the economic situation of the eu have led to the need to introduce modifications. the regulation governing the eusf has to be adapted to new needs and readjusted to current circumstances in the eu. such changes as mentioned in the report can be very efficient as they will improve the functioning of the fund by simplifying the eusf’s procedures and by increasing the transparency of the criteria used for mobilising the eusf. that is why, after taking into consideration all the aforementioned points, i welcome these changes which will increase the efficiency, transparency and flexibility of the eusf. and i consider them to be important, as they will improve coherence in the eusf’s functioning in order to respond properly in the event of a disaster.
in writing. − i support the proposal to draw up a legislative initiative on a single administrative law, binding on the institutions, bodies, agencies and offices of the european union, with a focus on the administrative procedure and with certain guarantees for businesses and citizens interacting with the eu administration. while most eu institutions and bodies currently use different codes of conduct, a common administrative procedural law will provide an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the eu and protect citizens' rights. the eu institutions must ensure that the matter is dealt with swiftly, transparently and effectively, and i therefore support the proposals made to codify the basic principles of good administration in the new regulation and to establish a procedure to be followed by the eu administration in its dealings with eu citizens and businesses. greater guarantees will increase citizens' confidence in the eu administration and, in the process, in the european union as a whole.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to promote transparency and accountability and to increase citizens' confidence in the administration of the european union. as early as 23 march 2010, the legal affairs committee set up an eu administrative law working party, thus aiming to assess the eu's administrative law. the aim of the evaluation is to give greater attention to the administrative procedure and to provide the necessary safeguards for businesses and citizens dealing directly with the union administration. it is worth noting that this eu right of administrative procedure would provide citizens and legal persons with more legal certainty, in other words clearer rules, when dealing with the union administration. this could be achieved by clearly defining, by codifying general principles of administration, the basic rules which should underpin the union's administrative activities. it should be noted that these rules should, in particular, promote transparency and accountability and increase citizens' confidence in the eu administration.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. as the eu's remit expands, citizens increasingly come into direct contact with the eu administration and are not always guaranteed the relevant procedural rights they could exercise against the administration if they were to need to. administrative procedural law offers the possibility of strengthening the legitimacy of the union and of conferring on citizens and legal persons clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their dealings with the union administration. the proposed code would therefore help to remove the ambiguities created by the fact that most union institutions and bodies currently have their own different codes at the same time. it would ensure that the institutions and bodies apply the same basic principles in their dealings with citizens and that they emphasise the importance of these principles to both citizens and officials.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in particular, coherent and comprehensive sets of codified administrative law rules must be developed at eu level. this will provide an effective 'safety net' for all eu businesses and citizens. the new regulation should give special importance to the principles of good and sound administration and should set clear minimum quality standards and procedural guarantees. i believe that the new code will ensure a high level of transparency, efficiency, speed of handling and enhance citizens' trust in the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a law on informing and consulting employees in the context of company restructuring. due to the global economic crisis of 2008, restructuring is becoming an increasingly common practice among companies. at present, national legislation governing the liability of employers towards their employees in the context of restructuring is very different, and i therefore agree that it is necessary to introduce legislation at european level. the restructuring of enterprises must avoid mass redundancies and the decline of entire regions or industries. during the restructuring process, all stakeholders should be informed, including the explanation of the restructuring and the circumstances underlying it, and the employees' representatives should be involved in the process. i agree that appropriate information measures should be taken before the planned restructuring and that vocational retraining courses should be organised as a matter of urgency. i also support that firms should plan for redundancies as a last resort.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because restructuring would ease the changes experienced by workers and businesses as a result of overcapacity, modernisation and structural adjustment. as the annual growth survey shows, "only by offering lower prices than competitors, and without providing good products, methods and services, it can be difficult to succeed in global markets". it is therefore necessary to re-launch the dialogue with the social partners, as this can redistribute resources to new sectors and open up new opportunities for workers (when their jobs are at risk). the european restructuring framework could thus help to create a comprehensive environment of mutual trust. it is important to note that the commission sought specific advice on how to further develop policy in this area. on 17 january 2012, it published a green paper on restructuring and anticipation of change. what can we learn from recent experience? recognising that technological change and innovation can force companies and workers to develop adaptation strategies. however, it is also believed that innovation, combined with research and education, can be an effective way for europe to emerge from the crisis. only a strong social dialogue based on mutual trust and shared responsibility would ensure that the interests of enterprises in terms of competitiveness and sustainability and the interests of their employees in terms of social and employment conditions, health and working conditions are properly protected.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal as it is widely recognised that any restructuring process, especially one of wider scope and significant impact, should inform stakeholders, giving an explanation of the restructuring and the circumstances underlying it. the measures to be taken to achieve the objectives, the justification for the choice and other options must also be provided, subject to full and comprehensive involvement of the employees' representatives at all levels of the procedure, which requires preparation to take place in advance, giving the stakeholders the opportunity to prepare for consultation before the company's decision is taken. this proposal aims to promote and facilitate information and consultation in the context of economic change and to improve the way in which undertakings, workers' representatives, public authorities and other stakeholders, taking into account the different responsibilities of each of them at different stages of restructuring, plan, prepare and manage restructuring of undertakings in a socially and environmentally responsible manner throughout the union.
in writing. − in particular, a mechanism must be established to prevent any kind of abuse and to reduce the negative impact of the restructuring process. it should be noted that this process has a particularly negative impact not only on the dismissed but also on the existing employees, which requires not only social but also psychological support. it should be noted that any restructuring process must be preceded by an appropriate preparatory process. it is essential that all relevant stakeholders are properly informed and actively involved in this process. it is also necessary to implement measures to avoid mass redundancies and the decline of entire regions.
in writing. − the communication on restructuring and the return to human capital is very timely in the face of the economic crisis. and while restructuring is a normal part of business development, it also has its painful side. for example, last year 274 businesses were restructured in the eu and 74 000 people lost their jobs. it is therefore essential that employees are informed in good time of the forthcoming restructuring of the company and that the public authorities assess in advance the impact of the restructuring on the region as a whole. such social dialogue between the public authorities, the management of the company and the trade unions of the employees would have facilitated the consequences of the restructuring. sometimes all the employees of a family work in the same company undergoing restructuring and all of them may lose their jobs at the same time. when unemployed in their home country, they often move to the uk, sweden or germany, the netherlands, france, etc. for any job. the loss of skilled workers and the countries that are experiencing the most painful economic crisis may face another skilled human resource crisis in the future. it is therefore essential to ensure in a timely manner that human capital is not demotivized after corporate restructuring and that people remain to live and work in their own country. in the future, therefore, i believe that at least minimum standards of protection for workers should be established at eu level in order to ensure that workers have basic social protection, as this is now a matter for the member states alone.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the eu strategy for the horn of africa. the security situation on the somali peninsula is an important issue at both international and european level. the movement of persons of somali origin into the eu and the existence of terrorist organisations, often financed by piracy and kidnapping, pose a threat of international terrorism. i welcome the eu strategy on the somali peninsula, which aims to better coordinate eu external action in this strategic region, to ensure security, to consolidate the rule of law. the aim is to build democratic institutions, promote economic growth and reduce poverty, and support regional political and economic cooperation. i support the proposals to invest more resources in igad (the instrument for enhancing cooperation, integration and security at regional level) to support effective political dialogue in all states participating in the instrument. it is necessary to promote the response capacity of the african union institutions in the field of crisis management. i support the proposal to extend the mandate of operation atlanta (to combat piracy and enhance maritime security off the coast of somalia) by providing for appropriate funding and patrol vessels. it is also important to support agriculture, animal husbandry and programmes that provide access to water.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the somali peninsula is one of the poorest regions in the world, with millions of people at risk of famine. it is important to note that the region has been the scene of several rebellions, of constant piracy along the coasts, and of many other conflicts. it is clear that sustainable development cannot be achieved in an environment of unstable governance, and poverty and underdevelopment are conflict-driven factors that affect the security of neighbouring countries and the continent as a whole. the european union is therefore working with the african union intergovernmental development authority and other national efforts to effectively break the cycle of insecurity, instability, poverty and mismanagement. it could be argued that there is no quick solution to the instability in the country, and that a lasting and promising peace could be achieved on the basis of responsible and strong democratic institutions, the rule of law and respect for human rights. extremism and insurgency are known to be a consequence of poverty and hunger, and it is therefore essential that the eu and other organisations continue to provide independent and impartial humanitarian assistance and pursue further actions in the peace and resilience initiative.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. it is noted that the political instability and ongoing conflicts in the region have destroyed almost all prospects for sustainable economic development in the region. the instability in the region poses a growing threat not only to the security of its peoples but also to the rest of the world. it is worth noting that in implementing measures to strengthen security in the region and to combat terrorism and piracy, we must first of all aim at eradicating poverty in the region. the eu should play an active role in supporting the well-being of the people of the somali peninsula and in helping them to move out of poverty and towards self-sustaining economic growth. i believe that it is necessary to promote respect for constitutional norms and to make greater efforts in the areas of institution building, democratic consolidation and democratisation.
in writing. − the horn of africa is one of the poorest regions in the world. the strategic framework for the horn of africa is a chance for the region to achieve peace, stability and prosperity. its goal is to build strong political structures and contribute to conflict resolution. in addition, the horn of africa is of high geostrategic importance for the eu. political stability in this region has greater impact on europe. i voted in favour of this report, because the strategy on the horn of africa reinforces the eu’s response to the lack of stable political, democratic, social and economic conditions for the people in the region (especially for the young), tackles security concerns, and consolidates peace, the rule of law and respect for human rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because genetic resources are one of the most important factors for the survival of species (and the recovery of ecosystems). the loss of genetic diversity, which is accompanied by the loss of biodiversity, is a major challenge for humanity. in this regard, bio-piracy has become a major problem for developing countries. it is important to note that although there is no common definition of bio-piracy, the term is generally used to describe situations where biological resources are taken from local communities or indigenous peoples and patented, and the profits derived from them do not benefit the communities in which those resources originated, which discovered their special properties and exploited them. in this context, it is important to ratify the nagoya protocol as an important instrument in the fight against biological piracy, to restore fairness through the exchange of genetic resources. only in this way will a clear and coherent system of property rights be established.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the protection and conservation of genetic diversity is an important issue in the pursuit of the millennium development goals. genetic resources are of particular importance for sustainable agriculture and food security. genetic diversity is also one of the most important factors for species survival and ecosystem recovery. the loss of genetic diversity, which is therefore accompanied by the loss of biodiversity, is a major challenge for humanity. although genetic diversity is vital for human survival, it is being lost at an alarming rate. such loss of diversity raises new problems for owners and users of genetic resources. the holders are usually the most biodiverse developing countries, while the users are usually developed countries. in this regard, bio-piracy has become a major problem for developing countries. although there is no common definition of bio-piracy, the term is generally used to describe situations where biological resources are taken from local communities or indigenous peoples and patented, and the profits derived from them do not benefit the communities in which those resources originated, which discovered their special properties and exploited them. it therefore calls for the urgent ratification of the nagoya protocol as an important instrument to combat bio-piracy and to restore fairness and justice in the exchange of genetic resources.
in writing. − while sustainable development and aid to third countries are important objectives and principles of the eu's functioning, i would like to stress that the principle of environmental integration must not be forgotten in their implementation. one of the elements of this principle is food safety and the proper traceability of products, which unfortunately is not possible without ensuring adequate protection of plant origin.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the ever-increasing illegal exploitation of genetic resources and bio-piracy require more effective mechanisms to combat them at eu level. in particular, i support the proposal to introduce mandatory requirements for the disclosure of the origin of genetic resources in patent procedures. this will create an effective control mechanism and the possibility to verify that genetic resources have been legally acquired. transparency and legal clarity will also be ensured for resource providers, inventors and investors. it is also essential to ensure access to genetic resources and to restore their fair and equitable exchange. i think that more attention should be paid to the dominance of industrial seeds on the market, which is having a negative impact on the seeds of traditional varieties.
in writing. − the protection of genetic diversity, the preservation of genetic diversity are key words in the achievement of the millennium development goals. genetic diversity is one of the most important drivers of the regeneration of species and ecosystems as a whole, and the irreversible loss of genetic diversity associated with biodiversity loss is therefore a major challenge for humanity. although genetic diversity is vital for human survival, it is being lost at an alarming rate. such loss of diversity raises new problems for owners and users of genetic resources. today, the largest share of genetic resources is held by developing countries with high biodiversity. biopiracy has become a major problem in developing countries. although there is no common definition of bio-piracy, the term is generally used to describe situations where biological resources or folk medicine recipes are taken from local communities and patented, and then used for profit by pharmacists or the cosmetics industry, with the resulting profits not benefiting the communities in which the resources were discovered. the rapid ratification of the nagoya protocol in the eu member states and beyond is therefore essential. we need a credible countermeasure to bio-piracy, to restore the proper exchange of genetic resources. i am pleased that lithuania is one of the first eu countries to have ratified the nagoya protocol.
the idea of a single europe, united in a community of equal states, is more relevant today than ever. we can't pretend not to see this. otherwise, we may face a time when our common ambition to be a strong, independent and distinctive community will be divided by individual aspirations to be stronger than others. we cannot create a community of equal and more equal states. it's a short enough walk. in the face of economic and political turmoil, accompanied by the constant unemployment that accompanies it, we are unable to agree on important issues such as how and which way europe should go. only free, equal, strong and independent national states are the foundation of a strong european union. and you can be sure that the more talk there is about federalism and more centralization, the more negative public sentiment there will be.
i would also like to congratulate the rapporteur on this very important report. since the beginning of the crisis, there has been talk of the largely uncontrolled activities of credit rating agencies and their enormous and often, as we have seen, destructive influence not only on the borrowing prospects of member states but also on their long-term economic growth and the future development of individual countries. it is good to see that the conclusion is being reached that it is necessary to have a rating agency of its own and to improve it. today, i think there is a significant step forward in terms of greater scrutiny of credit rating agencies, transparency of their operations, and the definition of principles and standards. i hope that in the future this will also lead to the creation of a european union-wide credit rating agency, which would bring some benefits not only to the financial system of the european union but also to the rated member states, and on the basis of the data collected, some future forecasts could be made.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations. i think it is important to recast the directive on the approximation of the already existing legislative and administrative provisions on the classification, packaging and labelling for such preparations. it would ensure legal continuity within the sectoral framework and would also close gaps that might exist regarding confidentiality and intellectual property rights protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a recast of the dangerous products directive (dpd) (1999/45/ec). the directive on the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations is proposed to be codified without changing its substance in order to bring its provisions into line with the newly-entering lisbon treaty. the directive sets out the criteria for determining whether a substance is classified appropriately. the classification reflects the type and severity of the hazard posed by the substance, i.e. the potential harm to humans and the environment. as all the amendments to the new gpa are based on the need to replace old provisions that are no longer necessary with new ones in order to ensure their clarity and precision, i support this proposal.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the dangerous products directive regulates the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous products, i.e. mixtures or solutions of two or more substances. a recast of this directive on dangerous preparations has been proposed in order to codify the corrective acts and to align the provisions relating to the commission's power to adopt delegated and implementing acts with the treaty of lisbon. all the amendments made to the new version of the directive are based on the need to update the proposal in line with the treaty of lisbon and to replace old provisions which are no longer necessary with new ones, while ensuring clarity and precision of the applicable provisions.
in writing. − voting in favour of this report is predominantly due to the offers of regulations concerning the three main elements involved with preparations: classification, packaging and labelling. it is important to ensure the safety of both our health and our environment, and correctly classifying and labelling solutions would further ensure safety in these fields, as would packaging these solutions with extreme care under the guidelines set forth in the legislation, so that during transport all necessary precautions are met without any consequences.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 on the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean sea, in order to bring its provisions into line with the newly-entering treaty of lisbon. in view of the deteriorating state of some fish stocks in the mediterranean, the regulation aims to ensure the conservation and sustainable exploitation of the stocks. as the protection of fish stocks is the main objective of the regulation, i support the proposal to include the word 'protection' in the title of the regulation.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i believe that these amendments, which lay down procedural provisions for the exercise of the commission's powers, will strengthen sustainable fishing in the region. the delegated and implementing measures provided to the commission will help to establish more effective mechanisms for the management of sustainable use of resources and thus contribute to improving the use of living water resources and the protection of vulnerable habitats.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the conclusion of the nagoya-kuala lumpur supplementary protocol, which specifies measures which need to be taken in the event of damage by living modified organisms that adversely affect the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, taking also into account risks to human health. living modified organisms (lmos) resulting from modern biotechnology might move from one country to another. therefore, the cartagena protocol establishes an advance informed agreement (aia) procedure for ensuring that countries are provided with the information necessary to make informed decisions before agreeing to the import of such organisms into their territory. i agree with the rapporteur that the nagoya-kuala lumpur supplementary protocol will greatly contribute to achieving the objectives of the convention on biological biodiversity and of the cartagena protocol on biosafety. moreover, this supplementary protocol will specifically address liability and compensation for damage to biodiversity resulting from lmos. now it is important that all eu member states sign and swiftly ratify this supplementary protocol.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation because the nagoya and kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and compensation will help to achieve the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biosafety. the cartagena protocol on biosafety of the convention on biological diversity is an international treaty that regulates the movement of living modified organisms produced by modern technology from one country to another. the protocol establishes a prior informed consent procedure to ensure that parties are provided with the information necessary to make an informed decision before agreeing to allow the introduction of those organisms into their territory. the biosafety clearing-house is established under this protocol to facilitate the exchange of information on living modified organisms and to assist the parties in the implementation of the protocol. the rapporteur of the european parliament supports the council decision approving, on behalf of the european union, the nagoya and kuala lumpur additional protocol on liability and compensation in matters falling within the union's competence. it is also welcome that the additional protocol has been signed by a majority of member states. the european parliament therefore calls on them to ratify it swiftly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal as the cartagena biosafety protocol to the convention on biological diversity is an international treaty regulating the movement of living modified organisms produced by modern technology from one country to another. the protocol establishes a prior informed consent procedure to ensure that parties are provided with the information necessary to make an informed decision before agreeing to allow the introduction of those organisms into their territory. the protocol refers to the precautionary principle and reaffirms the precautionary provisions contained in the rio declaration on environment and development. the biosafety clearing-house is established under this protocol to facilitate the exchange of information on living modified organisms and to assist the parties in the implementation of the protocol. the provisions of the eu cartagena protocol on biosafety are incorporated into eu biosafety legislation. they enshrine the precautionary principle as a fundamental principle. the provisions on liability of the nagoya and kuala lumpur additional protocol are incorporated into directive 2004/35/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 21 april 2004 on environmental liability for the prevention and remedying of environmental damage, which establishes a 'polluter pays' system for environmental damage.
in writing. − today, when the european union and the member states have not yet fully decided on the regulation of the introduction and use of living modified organisms and related products, it is important to ensure that a mechanism is in place for the identification and compensation of damage caused by the movement of such organisms. i therefore support the eu's accession to the international agreements necessary to establish such mechanisms.
in writing. − we must do everything we can to contribute to the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity. to this end, each member state should ratify the additional protocol on liability and reparation in matters falling within the union's competence as a matter of urgency. the eu must set high standards of environmental protection. it is essential to establish an effective compensation mechanism by regulating in detail not only environmental restoration but also preventive and compensatory measures.
in writing. − when considering living modified organisms (lmos) and biotechnology, it is of utmost importance to maintain strict guidelines for the importation and exportation of such. a clear structure of trade formality is necessary as well as the assurance that all precautions have been taken before agreeing to the importation of lmos and biotechnology. another important aspect of the precautions outlined in this report is the ability to channel liability if damage is caused during the transaction. this is exhibited in the liability and redress aspect of this legislation. while the protocol mainly directs attention to administration procedures and requirements, it also concerns human health and biodiversity. to have both of these elements outlined in the guidelines for the legislation is extremely important during the implementation of the protocol. therefore this legislation covers the most essential elements concerning biosafety. i voted in favour of this report, because it helps further ensure biosafety among the eu’s countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because comprehensive measures are needed to continue to address the problems facing many eu member states, which are having a negative impact on social and economic development and political stability. it is worth noting that the effects of the economic and banking crisis have not reduced the euro area's public debt to gdp ratio over the recent period, from 86,2% in the first quarter of 2011 to 88,2% in the first quarter of 2012. also, current problems such as high youth unemployment can have serious implications for future economic growth and it is therefore necessary to take concrete measures to address the problems now. in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, member states need to implement innovation policies, provide more flexibility and security in the labour market (flexicurity), improve training programmes, reduce youth unemployment (by better matching youth qualifications with labour demand), create a more favourable environment for new business creation and take other similar measures to ensure further economic development and political stability. while these proposals cannot overcome the effects of the crisis all at once, they should aim to increase the credibility of fiscal adjustment and to reduce its short-term impact on growth, which in the longer term would also help to develop better policy frameworks.
in writing. − the economic, financial and banking crisis has not abated and has shown that public finance problems are having a negative impact on socioeconomic development and political stability. the crisis cannot be overcome by recent reforms of the eu's economic and budgetary management system alone. i voted in favour, as comprehensive measures are needed to address the problem of excessive macroeconomic imbalances in a symmetrical way and to improve the overall level of social and economic convergence and solidarity in the economic and monetary union. a credible commitment to growth-friendly consolidation measures is a prerequisite for a sustainable solution to the excessive debt and deficit problems of many euro area member states.
in writing. − i support this resolution because the long-term sustainability of public and private finances is a prerequisite for stability and growth. most member states face significant difficulties in restoring the sustainability of public finances. particular attention shall be paid to long-term fiscal consolidation strategies. it is also essential to ensure that consolidation of public finances is not carried out at the expense of social security and public service systems.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution because the eu's regulation, supervision and supervision of financial markets is far from perfect. credit rating agencies are now supervised in the european union by a new european securities and markets authority (esma) which can punish them for breaching the rules. i would recall that the european parliament already called for a stronger regulatory framework in its resolution of june 2011 and stressed the need to reduce the burden placed on credit rating agencies. this european parliament resolution is an attempt to strengthen the regulation and supervision of eu financial markets by proposing amendments and additions to the rules on the operation and supervision of credit rating agencies. i think that both the eu and lithuania need this, because the consequences of the published ratings have been and can be very painful, with losses in the millions of euros. in the past, the publication of credit ratings has sometimes, without any serious basis or in the interests of anyone, damaged the credibility not only of individual investors but also of states. in this resolution, the european parliament seeks to avoid as much as possible conflicts of interest in credit rating agencies and the ratings they publish, so that national credit ratings are published more frequently than they are now, at least twice a year. in addition, credit agencies are required to be more transparent in their activities. never again should the timing and manner of disclosure be subject to the unilateral decisions of credit rating agencies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to tighten the regulation of credit rating agencies, whose decisions determine the economic and political prospects of countries and the cost of borrowing on the international credit market. the main objective of the proposal is to reduce excessive interference by market participants in the field of credit ratings, to address conflicts of interest and to increase the transparency and competitiveness of the work of credit rating agencies. i support the proposals set out for investors to use eu internal ratings, with less reliance on external credit rating agencies, and for issuers of structured finance instruments to obtain credit ratings from two different agencies. i also agree that persons holding more than 10% of the capital of an agency should not hold 10% or more of the capital of a rated entity and that no member or shareholder of a rating agency should hold more than 5% of the shares of another agency. it is also necessary to set stricter requirements on the timing of the publication of national ratings, to improve the reasoning behind the publication of ratings by agencies and to avoid the publication of direct policy recommendations to member states. it is important that investors have the possibility to hold a credit rating agency liable for any damage suffered as a result of a breach of rules that has affected the rating outcome.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the activities of credit rating agencies have a significant impact on the behaviour of economic and financial actors and on the functioning of public institutions. for its part, the european parliament adopted a legislative resolution in june 2011 (based on the commission communication of june 2010) calling for a strengthened regulatory framework and highlighting the need to reduce over-reliance on credit rating agencies. the proposal for a regulation (com ((2011) 0747)) amending regulation (ec) no 1060/2009 states that the rules governing sovereign credit ratings in any form should be strengthened in order to improve the quality of such ratings. i think that most of the things proposed are very important and most of them can be accepted in principle, but some provisions still need to be clarified and strengthened to avoid undesirable consequences in the implementation of these measures.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the activities of credit rating agencies have a significant impact on the behaviour of economic and financial actors and on the functioning of public institutions. i voted in favour of this proposal because it should help to put credit rating agencies back in their rightful place. this means that their ratings should be treated as information to be taken into account, but not that the agencies themselves should have a special status or automatically exert a procyclical influence detrimental to the activities of economic and financial actors and public institutions. never again should the timing and manner of disclosure be subject to the decisions of unilateral credit rating agencies, even when the information provided is not substantially new or original, in particular as regards the state and prospects of the public sector.
in writing. − these amendments to the regulation will help to limit the influence of credit rating agencies on the behaviour of economic and financial actors and will introduce new transparency requirements. i believe that it is appropriate to extend the scope of the rating rules in order to increase the scrutiny of their operation. in particular, very strict restrictions on the establishment and publication of sovereign credit ratings should be imposed. this will create favourable conditions for improving the quality of sovereign credit ratings. in addition, the commission should adopt as soon as possible a decision on the establishment of an independent european credit rating agency to carry out credit assessments of sovereign debt.
in writing. − governments are increasingly dependent on the credit rating of sovereign debt issued by rating agencies. however, the liability of these institutions has not been properly controlled to date. the legislative gaps have had a negative impact on national economies. i therefore agree with the view that there is a need for better regulation and supervision of the financial services market. i voted in favour of this report because the european commission and the rapporteur of the european parliament have put forward innovative proposals on the civil liability of credit rating agencies and the mandatory rotation requirement. the envisaged measures will ensure greater transparency of rating methodologies and increase competitiveness in the market for credit rating agencies, which is currently dominated by a small number of large agencies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to amend directive 2009/65/ec on the laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and directive 2011/61/eu on alternative investment fund managers (aifs). the regulation on credit rating agencies (cras) requires these agencies to adhere to strict conduct of business rules in order to mitigate potential conflicts of interest and to ensure a high level of quality and transparency in ratings. however, the risk that financial market participants, including ucits and aifs, may rely too heavily on credit ratings has not been sufficiently addressed in the cra regulation. i therefore support the proposals put forward to address this issue by improving the regulatory framework for agencies.
in writing. - i voted for this document. due to the impact of the financial crisis, investors, including ucits and aifs, rely too heavily on credit ratings when investing in debt instruments and do not necessarily assess the creditworthiness of the issuers of such debt instruments themselves. therefore, in order to improve the quality of the investments of ucits and aifs and thus to protect the investors of those funds, it is appropriate to require ucits and aif managers to avoid automatically relying solely on external credit ratings when assessing the risk associated with the investments of ucits and aifs they manage. it is therefore proposed to improve the internal risk management processes and systems of ucits and aifms and to follow a general principle to avoid over-reliance on external credit ratings.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is necessary to establish strict regulatory rules to protect investors and markets from potential shortcomings. i believe that these amendments will help to ensure that external credit ratings are not used as the main criteria for assessing the assets of csds. in particular, a strict regulatory mechanism should be established to ensure that those entities do not rely unconditionally on credit ratings. they should themselves assess the opinions of credit rating agencies and take their own decisions, as a credit rating is only an opinion on relative credit risk.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to amend council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 of 18 september 2007 establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks and the fishing opportunities available in the baltic sea. the main objective of this plan is to ensure the sustainable exploitation of the cod stock in the baltic sea by setting tacs. it is important to ensure that the plan is kept up to date with the latest scientific advice as science progresses. the proposed amendments are designed to ease the restrictions on cod fishing in the baltic sea, as the baltic sea stocks are slowly recovering, according to statistics. i support the proposals that are being put forward to allow small-scale fisheries to catch cod in the baltic sea in the summer, i.e. during the prohibition season. the coastal cod fishery in summer will not have a negative impact on these fish, which do not spawn far from the coast.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it updates the rules that fishermen must follow to conserve fish stocks and ecosystems. technical measures shall lay down rules on fishing zones and gear used in contravention of the requirements on the allowable amounts and on the catch. these measures provide for minimum landings, minimum mesh sizes, zones and prohibition periods, catch limits, fishing gear to ensure a higher selectivity and measures designed to protect the marine environment. the current commission proposal aims to extend the rules on technical measures for a further transitional period until the adoption of a regional framework for technical measures under the cfp. the current proposal for technical measures should not preclude decisions on landing obligations to be undertaken under the cfp basic regulation, and the temporary nature of the legislation should be clearly linked to the envisaged regional scheme of technical conservation measures after the adoption of the new cfp. the technical measures for specific cases and zones need to be carefully developed and cannot be seen as general rules that could be applied in the same way to all member states.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as the extension of the technical rules during the transitional period is necessary to ensure sustainable fishing, the best management of the resources and to prevent an increase in the amount of fish being released into the sea. this will facilitate the development of a new system of technical measures. it should be noted that the consequences of overfishing can be very serious for the safety and lives of fishermen. in this context, the new system should be developed taking into account the variability of fisheries management and scientific advice. only by implementing these measures will sustainable fishing and the appropriate protection of ecosystems be ensured.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the youth guarantee. i am pleased that the european parliament has endorsed this proposal from the council and the commission, as it will be a measure to ensure that all young eu citizens and legal residents under the age of 25 and under the age of 30 who have recently completed higher education receive a quality job, continuing education or traineeship offer within four months of becoming unemployed or leaving formal education. i agree with the rapporteur that the effective implementation of the 'youth guarantee' initiatives requires close cooperation between the commission and the member states, as well as cooperation at national level between the social partners, local and regional authorities, public and private employment services, and local and regional education and vocational training institutions. this will be one of the means of combating the consequences of the economic crisis and of overcoming the high unemployment rate, which is unprecedented in the eu.
in writing. - i voted for the youth guarantee. today, youth unemployment in the european union stands at 23.7% (5.68 million young people), while in lithuania, about 24.2% of young people are unemployed. the main objective of the youth guarantee is to ensure that no young eu citizen is left without a job, education or traineeship. the aim is to ensure that persons under 25 and those under 30 with a higher education qualification receive a quality job, training or traineeship offer no later than four months after the date of their graduation or unemployment. i support the proposal to introduce this scheme in all eu member states with the support of the european social fund and other eu funds. i agree that this initiative should be complemented by a quality assurance system to ensure that education and workplaces provide adequate remuneration, good working conditions and health and safety standards. as the level of preparedness of the countries to adopt the 'youth guarantee' initiative varies, the commission should support those member states that are experiencing financial difficulties. i support calls on the commission to monitor closely the implementation of the youth guarantee and, where appropriate, to identify countries that do not comply.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and welcome the european commission's 'youth guarantee' initiative, which will ensure that young people are given the opportunity to start work, study or do an internship no later than four months after their graduation or unemployment. however, i would urge the commission to provide the member states with financial support as soon as possible to implement this programme in the member states. the effectiveness of the 'youth guarantee' programmes requires close cooperation between the commission and the member states, the national (sectoral) social partners, local and regional authorities, employment services, local and regional education and training institutions and other relevant actors. moreover, if member states were to succeed in restructuring the standards of education and vocational training for young people, this would also significantly increase the opportunities for young people to enter employment and to choose careers. the current youth employment situation is tragic in most member states of the european union, but not all countries are equally prepared to adopt the 'youth guarantee' programme. particular support should be given to those member states which are experiencing financial difficulties or/and are undergoing austerity measures in their countries.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. the economic crisis that has hit has led to a significant increase in unemployment, especially among young people, to unprecedented levels. the crisis has led to the employment of young people in precarious employment conditions - short-term contracts, part-time contracts, etc. the commission therefore wanted a 'youth guarantee' initiative in its youth employment package. in such a case, young people should first be given a personalised assessment of their needs and then be provided with tailor-made and appropriate services. research shows that youth unemployment often leaves long-term scars such as an increased risk of future unemployment and persistent social exclusion. member states should therefore make greater efforts to increase youth employment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the duty and responsibility of every state to help young people to become established in life, because the well-being of a country depends on how young people feel and settle in their homeland. attention should be paid to the fact that young people are one of the most vulnerable groups in society, facing a very complex and different social environment. youth unemployment is a major european problem, driving emigration and other negative consequences. most member states keep count of the number of young people who go abroad each year to look for work as a source of livelihood, without any hope of finding it in their parents' land. in view of the high level of youth unemployment and social exclusion, close cooperation between the commission and the member states is necessary. any measure and initiative envisaged should be tailored to the needs of young people. first, more opportunities for job offers or further training should be provided. it is essential to ensure that young people who have completed higher education receive a quality job, continuing education or traineeship offer within four months of becoming unemployed or leaving formal education, as young people have been hit hardest by the economic crisis.
in writing. − youth unemployment is currently very high in the european union, with one in two young people in some countries not in employment or training. the economic crisis has made things even more difficult. the current employment problem is not limited to young people without a higher education, but also includes young people with a bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree. statistics show that one in five of the unemployed has never had a job, and three quarters are under the age of 25. failure to help young people find work is a huge potential loss for eu countries. i voted in favour of this resolution because it clearly emphasises the need to enable young people who have completed their education to find employment, to undertake an apprenticeship or to improve their qualifications in other ways. the resolution proposes that all eu countries adopt the 'youth guarantee' programme proposed by the social democrats, under which states would commit to giving every young person the opportunity to develop and work. we must ensure that the current generation of young people does not become a lost generation.
in writing. − the consequences of the financial and economic crisis and the recession have led to a dramatic impact on the situation of young people seeking for a job. unemployment amongst young people is hitting peaks not seen for almost 20 years and the risk of poverty and social exclusion amongst this population group is constantly growing. the situation is worrying in lithuania. lithuania is largely hit by the economic crisis; youth unemployment in lithuania has risen from 13% to 27.5% – that is more than double the country’s unemployment rate for its total workforce. a youth guarantee can provide lithuania with the tools to overcome this trend and reform education and training standards for young people. introducing a youth guarantee can help to redress the situation of youth unemployment and can become a strong instrument for a change in tackling it. i welcome this initiative and i am convinced that promoting exchanges of good practices among member states and following these practices can unite member states in their efforts to increase youth employment. i believe that lithuania will take a proactive approach in this regard and will make employment of young people a top priority in its policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on strengthening the role of eu cohesion policy in the implementation of the new european energy policy. the objective of european energy policy is to ensure security of energy supply, sustainability, competitiveness, diversification of energy sources and affordability for consumers. energy investment in the eu is part of the cohesion policy, which aims at smart and sustainable growth and the transition to a low-carbon economy. i support the calls for an eu-wide incentive scheme for renewable energy sources and for administrative capacity building at member state, regional and local levels for the institutions that use eu funding. as the cohesion fund is becoming increasingly difficult to use due to bureaucratic obstacles and lack of clarity, i support the proposal to simplify the rules and procedures for submitting applications and to increase the flexibility of the fund. it is also important to regularly check how cohesion funding is allocated to energy projects and whether projects are effective. i believe that the commission should develop an eu-wide cooperation programme to help improve cooperation between regions that use a lot of eu funds to implement an energy project and those that use little eu funds and to facilitate the sharing of best practices.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the transition to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth requires support for the transition to low-carbon and energy-efficient technologies in all sectors of the economy. european energy projects could contribute to regional development and enhanced cross-border cooperation, thus helping regions to improve their capacity to manage energy resources. in addition, investments in low-carbon and renewable energy sources, energy efficiency and other measures can boost regional economic growth and job creation.
