in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because as energy prices rise, so do local and regional disparities. in this context, it is essential to maintain the eu's cohesion in the implementation of the new energy policy. i believe that the energy projects under way are an integral part of regional development and closer crossborder cooperation, which stimulate regional economic growth. it is essential to ensure that an effectively functioning incentive system for the use of renewable energy sources is widely applied in the eu. support should be given to cities and regions for the implementation of investment projects, with particular attention and financial support for energy efficiency projects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the possibility of issuing stability bonds. the resolution calls on the european commission and the eu member states to explore ways of consolidating national debts and to present a possible plan for their implementation. the proposal aims to prevent abusive debt consolidation and to strengthen the euro area. today, the euro area has a single currency, but it does not have a common bond market or a common budgetary policy. i support the proposal to set up a european debt repayment fund without waiting, and to consider the possibility of amending the eu treaty to legalise the joint issuance of national and, later, european debt securities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a contribution by the european parliament to the eu's general debate on the creation of stability bonds. this measure, which could correct erratic fiscal trends, macroeconomic imbalances, debt levels and ceilings on member states' budgets, would be completely new, as no country in the world has tried to put such a measure into practice. the euro area is in a unique position in this respect, as its member states share a common currency but do not have a common budgetary policy or a common bond market. the prospect of common bonds would be an important signal to financial markets to preserve the integrity of the european monetary union, to help return the economy to stability and to reduce uncertainty, especially if we make progress on eu financial and budgetary integration and surveillance. however, it should be noted that even under the system of issuing general bonds, each member state would have to repay its entire debt and the issue of general bonds would not guarantee the fulfilment of the debt obligations of the member state. in its report, parliament therefore stressed the importance of establishing a proper sequence of actions for the creation of this instrument, as well as the need to draw up a binding action plan similar to the maastricht criteria for the introduction of the single currency. parliament also recommended that the commission emphasise the criteria for withdrawal and accession to the instrument, based on strict fiscal consolidation and budgetary discipline, taking into account the current crisis and the fiscal adjustment applied in some euro area countries.
in writing. - i support this resolution. stability bonds will help to alleviate the sovereign debt crisis, strengthen the euro area financial system and increase financial stability. in addition, member states will be given greater access to sources of refinancing. the temporary european debt relief fund will help to reduce debt to sustainable levels and ensure affordable interest rates. i also support the proposal to introduce euro banknotes in order to protect the member states adequately against illiquidity. in addition, the issuance of a common european debt securities will give member states greater scope for structural reforms. however, in all cases, the implementation of this initiative and the enhancement of financial stability and the effectiveness of monetary policy require the maintenance of the existing market discipline and the high credit quality of the stability bonds.
in writing. mr president the economic partnership agreement between the eastern and southern african states and the european community and its member states is the culmination of many years of negotiations which have not yet been fully concluded. the acp states and the european union have decided to sign new trade agreements in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) to replace the unilateral system of trade preferences favourable to the acp countries. the union's objective in creating the agreement was clear: to integrate the acp countries into the world economy, to create more efficient regional markets operating on a predictable and stable basis and to increase trade, especially with the countries of eastern and southern africa. it is estimated that imports from this part of africa to the eu amount to only around 0,2% of all eu imports. exports, on the other hand, are in the region of eur 4 billion, indicating limited trade opportunities. the conclusion of the agreement does not appear to improve this situation in line with the union's expectations. this is evidenced by the large number of african countries that have withdrawn from the negotiations, as they felt that the agreement would put them in a less advantageous position than they are now. some provisions of the agreement should therefore be reconsidered so that the benefits of trade are long-term for all contracting parties. the agreement should also not limit the country's responsibility for its own development but promote it on the basis of regional integration in africa.

in writing. - i voted for this motion. the spread and relative position of the aegean islands impedes the supply of goods and trade, which leads to a significant increase in transport costs. the existing transport networks are not sufficient, and the old fleet does not improve the situation. the limited size, lack of access both to and from the islands, the declining and ageing population, the lack of basic goods and public services such as water, electricity, heating and other complex conditions are factors that set the aegean islands apart. this creates a double isolation, with the smaller islands being supplied from the central islands. the new proposal, which provides for specific agricultural measures for the smaller aegean islands to improve the supply and trade situation, is therefore intended to improve rather than to amend the existing regulation.

in writing. - i agreed to this. the programme for the outermost regions and islands (posei) was launched in 1991 to help the french overseas departments and later extended to the outermost regions of other eu countries. the profitability of the agricultural products and industries of these outermost regions depends on this programme. the posei programme comprises two separate schemes. in particular, in these regions, the specific supply arrangements apply to products intended for direct consumption, to products intended for the processing or packaging industry or to products intended for feed or agricultural use. the financing under the special supply arrangements is capped in each country to avoid unfair competition with island products. on the other hand, the other part of the posei programme, which provides for about 80% of the aid and is very consistent, includes specific measures to support local production of agricultural products, which play a crucial role in ensuring the viability of this activity. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal, because in these times of crisis, when unemployment in these regions is often higher than the national average, it is not only necessary to maintain this programme, but also to strengthen it as much as possible.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on improving access to finance for smes. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are of great importance to the european union. they are the backbone of the european economy and an important driver of economic growth in the european union. smes are a major contributor to job creation in the 27 member states of the european union. however, the economic crisis has made smes particularly vulnerable, making it increasingly difficult for them to obtain credit for business development as creditors have become more cautious. due to the stricter capital requirements, creditors often ask for additional personal guarantees in addition to the usual bank guarantees. this may constitute an additional obstacle for entrepreneurs to set up or invest in their smes. i support the proposed possible solutions to improve access to finance for smes: 1) to increase the professionalism of the sector; 2) to establish better cooperation and exchange of information between smes and creditors; 3) to monitor the financial situation of smes on a more regular basis; (4) to lay down clear rules for the application of (personal) guarantees; (5) to establish clear rules on early repayment of credit, the imposition of possible fines and the calculation of lost profits for creditors. however, it is also important that the commission is flexible in its approach to financing the growth of smes and supports alternative financing instruments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on improving access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the financial crisis in the eu has led some creditors to become more cautious in lending to smes. in addition, the introduction of new and stricter rules (e.g. financial institutions and capital requirements rules) made it even more difficult for these companies to obtain financing. the proposal aims to create more favourable bank loans for smes, alternative forms of risk capital, clearer and more effective rules for cooperation with creditors and faster settlements with them. i support the suggestions that eu and national authorities should exercise caution when drawing up new rules on capital requirements, that a clear rule on the repayment of credit, the imposition of possible penalties and the calculation of lost profits for creditors should be developed, and that alternative financing instruments should also be supported. as households in some countries have large amounts of savings in bank accounts, i support the call on the commission to explore how to enable these savings to be actively used, for example by providing tax incentives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are of vital importance to european economic development, as they contribute to job creation in all eu member states. it is no wonder that the crisis has led to a downturn in the activity of smes. one reason is that creditors have become more cautious. in other words, new, stricter rules on capital requirements for both eu and national authorities have been introduced, making it more difficult for smes to access finance. while preventive measures are justified in times of crisis, eu and national authorities should exercise caution when developing new capital requirements rules. in the absence of a single impact assessment covering all the different rules implemented, the implications for the financial sector and for access to finance for smes are highly uncertain. another problem faced by smes is the lack of transparency, for example in early repayment of loans. the funding loss and the additional penalty are not always properly indicated in advance. sometimes the total cost of repaying a pre-financing loan is so high that smes cannot afford it and therefore cannot reconsider their investment and decision to take out a loan. it is important to note that while there is no one-size-fits-all solution for the different types of sme activity, the combined efforts of the eu member states could increase the professionalism of the sector by establishing clear rules for the application of guarantees, by establishing better cooperation between smes and creditors (exchange of information) and by monitoring the financial situation of smes on a more regular basis.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are of great importance to the european union (eu). smes create around 90 million jobs in the eu, 30% of which are in micro-enterprises, and 85% of all new jobs between 2002 and 2012 were created by smes, and in particular in start-ups. smes are the backbone of the european economy and an important driver of growth in the eu economy. smes are a major contributor to job creation in the eu-27. however, smes are vulnerable. and that became clear when the crisis started. the crisis has led some creditors to become more cautious in lending to smes. in addition, the introduction of new stringent rules, such as those on financial institutions and capital requirements, which are enforced by both eu and national authorities, has made it more difficult for smes to access funding. the proposal therefore aims to simplify the regulatory and administrative environment for smes. this would further promote the simplification of administrative procedures at european, national, regional, local and cross-border levels, in order to create a clear and transparent legal framework that seeks to limit the complexity of regulation that often constitutes a barrier for smes to apply for eu funding.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the accession of bulgaria and romania to the european union has led to the enlargement of its customs union. the european union was therefore obliged under the rules of the world trade organisation (wto) to enter into negotiations with wto members with a negotiating power over any acceding country's list of commitments in order to agree on a mutually acceptable countervailing arrangement in order to avoid an increase in the mandatory duties and the associated significant losses. such adjustment is necessary if the adoption of the external tariff regime of the eu results in an increase in the customs duties in relation to the duties for which the acceding country has committed itself to the wto, taking account of the reductions in customs duties for the same group of goods made by the other countries of that union on the establishment of the customs union. these agreements address two issues in order to implement wto requirements. first, the compensation of higher customs duties, which is usually carried out by setting a country tariff quota or increasing the existing quota (s). secondly, the pre-accession erga omnes tariff quota for bulgaria and romania (not country specific but worldwide) should also be added to the existing eu erga omnes tariff quotas.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on transparency of medicines prices. the european parliament supported the commission's proposal to update the existing legislative framework in order to clarify the procedural obligations of the member states and to ensure the effectiveness of internal market legislation, both in order to avoid delays in decisions on pricing and compensation and to remove barriers to trade in pharmaceutical products. while the exclusive competence of the member states to decide on the prices and reimbursement of medicinal products must be respected, minimum procedural requirements should also ensure legal certainty and transparency for the national competent authorities, promote the production of medicinal products and the placing on the market of generic medicinal products, and encourage research and development of new medicinal products. this would allow all european patients to have access to affordable treatment and better and cheaper medicines.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the transparency of measures regulating the prices of medicinal products for human use. the aim of this proposal is to speed up the marketing of generic medicines by simplifying the procedure for national decisions on the price of medicines and reducing the time taken to reach these decisions. generic medicines are cheaper analogues of existing medicines that are sold after the expiry of a patent. according to the commission, such medicines are up to 40% cheaper than originals, and therefore the companies holding the patent seek to prolong their exclusive right to sell originals by not placing their analogues on the market for as long as possible. it is essential to change this and to enable eu citizens to buy cheaper medicines. it is intended to set a 60-day deadline for the adoption of a decision on the pricing and reimbursement of generic medicines (today this can take up to 700 days). i support this proposal and the proposal to require the pharmaceutical control authorities to disclose the names and declarations of interests of their experts who take decisions on the prices and reimbursement of medicinal products, and the proposal to publish once a year the lists of reimbursed medicinal products and their prices.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to ensure the production of medicines and the access to the market for generic medicines. research and development of new medicines should also be encouraged in order to improve access to affordable treatment for all european patients. it is important to note that, although member states are responsible for their health systems, health services and the organisation of healthcare, each member state may take measures to control the consumption of medicines, regulate prices or set conditions for public funding. the commission's proposal therefore aims to systematize the minimum requirements in order to ensure that national measures, in particular those governing the pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products for human use, do not conflict with the principle of free movement of goods. to that end, the directive lays down a number of procedural requirements designed to ensure the transparency of the pricing and compensation measures adopted by the member states, including the time limits or obligation to take the relevant decisions. in short, to ensure that the competent national authorities state the reasons for each of their decisions and provide the applicant companies with appropriate remedies. these proposals should contribute to an effective and safe health policy that is patient-oriented and aims to ensure the best value for money.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. the overall objective of this proposal should be to update the existing legislative framework in order to clarify the procedural obligations of the member states and to ensure the proper functioning of the common market and the effectiveness of internal market legislation, both in order to avoid delays in decisions on pricing and compensation and in order to remove obstacles to trade in pharmaceutical products. these new rules should speed up the introduction of generic medicines on the market. these are cheaper analogues of existing medicines that can be sold under their own brand after the patent has expired. that's why some medications should be avoided.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i believe that decisions on the pricing and reimbursement of medicines must be taken in a timely and transparent manner, carefully balancing the obligation to preserve the competence of the member states in the field of public health with the need to ensure the effectiveness of the directive in achieving the internal market objectives. i agree with the rapporteur's suggestions that provisions relating to the transparency of the decision-making process and the decisions taken should be strengthened, as this is a growing need in society, particularly in the case of pharmaceutical prices and reimbursement. i therefore consider that the proposal to require the competent authorities to disclose the names and declarations of interests of experts who are members of their decision-making bodies is particularly appropriate. i believe that such provisions and increased disclosure of documents and information will improve the transparency, integrity and independence of the decisions taken.

in writing. − eu legislation on medicines prices is 25 years old. at present, the financial sustainability of the healthcare systems of the member states is not able to bear the burden of the economic crisis and of budgetary austerity policies. the pharmaceutical market and patient needs have changed considerably over this period, which requires updated, more advanced regulatory frameworks and greater transparency. i voted in favour of this report because it is useful not only for the member states but also for patients and the pharmaceutical industry, which creates many jobs. patients want a more transparent pricing system for medicines, which will make it cheaper and faster for them to get the medicines they need. it is important for countries to save more budgetary resources, which will guarantee the development of generic medicines in the market.
in writing. − while the exclusive competence of the member states to decide on the prices and reimbursement of medicines should be respected, we know that the prices of the same medicines vary considerably between member states. pharmacists usually argue that the price of drugs depends on the size of the country, and therefore the size of the market, and that the larger the country, the cheaper the drugs. the price also varies because some medicines are reimbursed for the same medicines and others are not. the lack of transparency in the pricing of medicinal products in the member states leaves a wide margin for non-transparent pricing and unjustified profit-raising by pharmaceutical companies. i am in favour of a transparent system for the pricing of medicines. i am in favour of a 90-day period for setting the price of the medicine and the compensation mechanism. i think in the long run, we'll be well prepared for the introduction of a new drug. i also believe that we need to reduce barriers to entry and give patients access to newly developed medicines. it is necessary to ensure that the eu medicines agency is able to fulfil its supervisory role effectively. i am calling for more transparency in drug prices, and for drug price regulators to be able to give us access to affordable medicines. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr parvanov, on his excellent work. public health is a great asset, not a burden. the eu must promote research and the development of new medicines with the ultimate aim of improving access to affordable treatment for all european patients.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution, which has a major impact on fishermen in the baltic sea region. the baltic sea is rapidly depleting its fish stocks as a result of intensive fishing. if we do not draw conclusions now and take measures to ensure that fish stocks are used sparingly, and if we do not implement strategies for the recovery of fish stocks, we will be in a sorry position in a few years' time: we will have fishermen but no fish, and fishermen will have nothing to fish. i voted in favour of this resolution in order to support the position of lithuanian naturalists, i.e. the principle of maximum sustainable yield, the definition of fishing capacity, the prohibition of discarding non-targeted catches, etc. it is expected that only as many of a given species as can be replaced in a year will be allowed to be caught each year. this would help to restore the depleted stocks by 2020. this would result in an additional 15 million tonnes of fish and create 37 000 new jobs. the eu plans to develop more accurate multiannual fisheries management plans based on scientific data provided by the member states. i am pleased that in voting on the european parliament's recommendations to the council of the eu on the eu's common fisheries policy framework regulation, we, the meps from the countries surrounding the baltic sea, have come together as much as possible, even across party lines. it turns out that the interests and positions of the people living around the baltic sea and the mediterranean sea on fish and fisheries policy differ considerably, and in some cases even radically.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). the reform aims to tackle overfishing, the depletion of fish stocks and unemployment in the eu's coastal regions. despite the lack of scientific data, the commission estimates that around 75% of eu fish stocks are over-exploited and that the eu loses around €1.8 billion a year as a result of poor fisheries. the proposal aims to establish sustainable fishing quotas, to prohibit fishermen from discarding unwanted fish, and to establish, from 2015, the principle of maximum sustainable yield, whereby the annual catch is to be sufficient to restore the stock. the objective is to restore depleted stocks by 2020. i agree that one of the problems that needs to be addressed is the lack of scientific data and the disregard for scientific advice. i agree with the above and with the proposals to provide for additional research programmes, to ensure that all fish caught are landed, to direct financial support towards selective fishing.
in writing. - i agreed to this. the european union's common fisheries policy (cfp) is essential to ensure the environmental, economic and social sustainability of fisheries management. the objectives of the common fisheries policy have not yet been achieved. the current cap has been a fundamental failure. it has become clear that it is not possible to solve longstanding problems such as overfishing, overcapacity, the poor economic situation of many fisheries enterprises and the social problems caused by the decline of fisheries in many coastal regions. the reform of the cfp is necessary to avoid the continuing depletion of large fish stocks, fleet overcapacity, low profitability and economic resilience of many fleets. over the past few decades, european waters have suffered a sharp decline in fish stocks and some species are at risk of disappearing completely. one in four fish caught is thrown back into the sea dead. this is a total waste of resources, as more than 60% of the fish consumed in europe is currently imported. the fisheries sector is almost unprofitable and in many cases only survives thanks to subsidies. the high financial burden encourages short-term planning and unwise and inappropriate activities that cause serious damage to the marine environment. the need for urgent reform of the cap is therefore more evident than ever.
in writing. − today we have confirmed our position on a very important issue, which will determine the future of the eu's common fisheries. while the document contains many important provisions aimed at preserving fish stocks for future generations, i would like to highlight one such measure. scientifically based management of fish stocks and quota management will ensure that stocks are not only not depleted, but also recover. this measure is particularly relevant for a sea such as the baltic sea, where fish stocks have recently been declining significantly due to very intensive fishing. i believe that these methods will help future generations to conserve fish stocks in other seas.
in writing. - i support this resolution. in order to ensure the sustainable use of marine resources, the principle of maximum sustainable yield needs to be applied more effectively. i think that the council should take into account the regions whose local community depends on fishing and related activities when setting the quotas each year. it is essential to ensure that marine biological resources are protected from the negative effects of fishing. i therefore support the application of certain special conservation measures, granting exclusive or preferential access to certain parts of the fleet and authorising the use of certain fishing gears only. access to fisheries resources shall be based on transparent and objective environmental and social criteria. more attention should be paid to research and innovation in order to develop better, innovative fishing and slaughter methods. states must be provided with sufficient funding for fisheries, scientific data collection and research and innovation programmes.
in writing. − overfishing has created a large issue in the socio-economical aspect of the european union and has adversely affected multiple areas. the environment is becoming less sustainable due to the decrease in fish. many small and large fisheries are becoming less and less profitable and are in turn creating more unemployment. these two elements create a large economy. the amount of fish caught has dropped from 8.1 million tonnes in 1995 to 4.9 million tonnes in 2010. the eu, while not the largest, still has 68 % of overfished stocks. the majority of this lies in the northeast atlantic because that is the location with the most volumes in kilotonnes of live weight. denmark, spain, the uk and france are the countries that catch the most fish. i voted for this report, because it will address these issues: the obligation to land all catches and the discard ban will help increase sustainability of fish. therefore, with these amendments we will see the greatest improvements within the fishing industry in the european union as long as they are adopted in a harmonious manner.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on vehicle noise levels, which aims to reduce the impact of noise from cars on public health and the environment. about half of the eu's urban population is exposed to noise levels above 55 decibels caused by car traffic. the proposal provides for a gradual reduction in vehicle noise levels: after six years from the entry into force of this document, the noise level of new passenger cars will not exceed 68 decibels (currently 74 decibels are allowed), and after eight years this limit will be set for all new vehicles. i support the proposal to introduce a labelling system to inform consumers about the noise emissions of new cars and thus encourage the purchase of low-noise vehicles. i also support the proposal to set minimum noise requirements for electric cars which are quiet and pose a threat to pedestrians.
in writing. - i voted for this document. its main objective is to protect public health and the environment through measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. motor vehicles are one of the main sources of noise pollution. exposure to constantly high levels of noise is thought to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances and tinnitus. a new method of measuring the sound level of motor vehicles and new noise limits for different categories of light, medium and heavy-duty vehicles should be established. this would undoubtedly be an important step forward in reducing the impact of noise emitted by motor vehicles on public health and the environment.
in writing. - i support this resolution. to reduce environmental noise and ensure safety on the roads and at work, it is necessary to establish strict methods, new limit values that apply uniformly throughout the eu. in order to protect the internal market for motor vehicles with regard to their sound emission level and to promote low-noise vehicles, manufacturers and distributors should be obliged to indicate the noise level of a vehicle. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to take a decision on the application of the directive in the light of the findings of the court of justice. electric and hybrid cars are too quiet for the acoustic blind to recognize them. they can't see or hear them coming. this puts their own health and the lives of others at risk. in view of this, i support the proposal to equip silent cars with audible warning systems that clearly indicate the vehicle's state. this is one of the most effective ways to protect the blind.

in writing. - i voted for this document. it is important for all member states that the commitments they have made in relation to migration are not undermined by the economic difficulties experienced by some member states. an increase in the co-financing rate from the external borders fund for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability would allow them to avoid or reduce such difficulties. this would therefore benefit europe as a whole, as the failure of one member state to manage migration flows effectively affects not only the country concerned but also many other member states.
in writing. - i voted yes. the 2007 decision on the external borders fund is modified to take account of the need to make the fund available to eu countries struggling with the consequences of the economic and financial crisis, with their national resources increasingly limited. this is necessary to ensure the eu's common objective of developing a comprehensive eu migration policy that contributes to the eu's competitiveness, social cohesion and the creation of a common eu asylum system. therefore, the union co-financing share will be temporarily increased and the national co-financing share will be reduced for countries experiencing severe financial stability difficulties. the effective protection of the eu's external borders is one of the priorities of lithuania's forthcoming presidency of the council of the eu.
in writing. − i support the proposal to increase the co-financing rate for countries in particular financial difficulty and at the same time to reduce the national co-financing rate. budgetary constraints in some member states prevent the effective implementation of programmes and the continuity of projects. moreover, states alone are unable to address the important challenges of migration, asylum and external borders. they need eu financial support. in particular, it is necessary to facilitate the receipt of eu funds for the management of migration, asylum and external borders. secondly, the availability of funds to member states should be improved in order to enable them to implement their annual programmes under the funds.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the extension of the technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine animals. the aim of this proposal is to ensure the protection of eu fisheries resources. according to the commission, about 75% of the european union's fish stocks are overfished and the union loses around eur 1.8 billion a year as a result of inadequate fishing. technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources are the rules that eu fishermen must follow when fishing in order to ensure that the fisheries are sustainable. these measures play a key role in the decision-making process on the size of the potential allowable catch. they lay down rules on fishing zones, prohibited gear periods, etc. i agree with the suggestions that these measures cannot be seen as general rules applying in the same way to all member states. it is necessary to develop technical means for specific cases and zones. one of the problems to be addressed is the failure to take account of scientific advice, and i therefore support the call to take account of the variability of fisheries management and scientific advice in the formulation and development of these measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to lay down specific rules on fishing zones and gears in order to conserve fish stocks and protect their ecosystem. it is necessary to develop conservation conditions for fish stocks taking into account the variability of fisheries management and scientific advice. it is important to note that the council regulation on fisheries was drafted with a view to subsequently amending it to establish a permanent framework of technical measures in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, but no political agreement was reached. european fishermen need legal clarity, and the word 'provisional' does not offer any guarantees in this area. poor preparation or the setting of inadequate technical means may lead to the development of improper fishing practices and, in certain cases, to the risk to the lives and safety of fishermen, which would be completely unacceptable. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the conditions for the participation of the candidates in the tendering procedure.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. i agree that measures are needed to ensure that fish stocks are fished sustainably and that the ecosystems in which fish live are preserved. in addition, these measures need to be formulated and developed taking into account the variability of fisheries management and scientific advice.
in writing. − i support the amendments to this regulation which provide for the extension of the rules on technical measures for a further transitional period. this will ensure legal certainty and the protection of marine resources. it should be noted that ensuring the proper protection of fish stocks is essential to ensure sustainable fishing. technical conservation measures for fisheries resources will help to prevent depletion of resources and maintain the good environmental status of marine ecosystems. particular attention should be paid to the reduction of discards and measures should be introduced to combat environmentally harmful fisheries effectively. in order to continue to ensure the proper conservation and management of marine resources, i believe that the commission should be empowered to take immediate action if necessary to protect marine resources.
in writing. − the main issues at hand for the conservation of fishery resources are the multi-annual plan of the salmon sector in the baltic, shark fining in southern europe and small-scale fisheries. all of these issues at hand require a precise amount of regulation to ensure the success of each of these programmes under the amendments to the conservation of fishery resources. while this will be difficult to carry out, if we collectively join forces in a manner that is unified this can result in great achievements across many sectors of our union. i voted in favour of this report, because the multi-annual plan for the baltic salmon stock will manage to increase stock to ensure maximum sustainability, as well as yield. the eradication of shark fining will both improve the ecosystems for sharks and help small-scale fisheries. because of this, the economy will also be improved because three out of every four small-scale vessels are generating jobs and increasing incomes, boosting the economy within their local communities, as well as nationally. all in all sustainability will be the principal outcome from this proposal. the socio-economic sector as well as the environmental sector will all profit generously from these amendments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the elimination and prevention of all forms of violence against women and girls. violence against women remains a global epidemic. one in three women has been beaten, raped, sold or otherwise abused at some point in her life. violence affects women and girls worldwide, irrespective of factors such as age or economic status, and it also harms families and communities, imposes significant economic and social costs, and limits and hinders economic growth and development. unfortunately, violence against women is also a problem in the european union. the eu must do more to eliminate violence against women and gender-based violence within its own territory in order to lead the world in the defence of human rights. i therefore support the call in the resolution for the eu and the member states to devote more resources to ending violence against women and girls, including resources at local, national, european and global levels, and to support those organisations and individuals working to end violence against women and gender-based violence, in particular non-governmental organisations working in this field.

mr president, we have a request to have a split vote on paragraph 62. i would like to propose an oral amendment to that paragraph in two parts. the first part would be to add the words ‘be communicated to the european parliament’, and the second part to add the words ‘where possible’. paragraph 62, if amended, would therefore read as follows: ‘expects the development of eu human rights country strategies to be duly coordinated with eu action in the un forums; reiterates its recommendation that eu country strategies on human rights be communicated to the european parliament and be made public where possible in order to give visibility to the eu’s commitment to human rights in third countries and for those struggling for human rights to find support in these documents’. a split vote is not necessary if the text is adopted with that wording.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which supports the commission's proposal for a european innovation partnership, which promotes a new approach to ageing as an opportunity for the future, rather than a burden on society. the european union is currently undergoing demographic change. the eu population is ageing rapidly: the number of people aged 65 and over will almost double from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million in 2060. we need to encourage the eu, the member states, regions, cities and municipalities to adapt to the needs and (remaining) capacities of their ageing populations. the conditions for the active and healthy maturation and ageing of these people must also be ensured. when looking at ageing from a life-long perspective, it is clear that many life circumstances, conditions and events can influence the ageing process and its quality. furthermore, when thinking about the environment in a broad sense (including ecological factors, social and demographic and socio-economic indicators), it becomes clear that the human environment is one of the main determinants of people's ability to enjoy an active and healthy life well into old age, as well as to live independently for as long as possible. i therefore agree with the rapporteurs that the european commission must pay particular attention to the multifaceted relationship between the ageing population and its environment in order to ensure the long-term success of the european innovation partnership on ageing and health.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union is undergoing rapid demographic change, one of which is the ageing of the population. the number of people aged 65 and over is set to almost double from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million in 2060. in addition, the proportion of the population aged over 60 years was 20% in 2010 and is expected to rise to at least 35% by 2050. there are many factors that influence this demographic process. research has shown that there is a relationship between place and person, in other words, the conditions that characterize a place (environment) influence human maturation and aging. the importance of location in the relationship between man and the environment is often an important factor, as the environmental impact of the micro- and macro-levels must be taken into account. thus, in order to take account of the impact of micro and macro-levels, it is important to assess not only the built environment, access to (meat) transport and access to appropriate care and treatment services, but also the employment opportunities, the problem of health inequalities and the possibilities for social activism and management. environmental aspects (e.g. noise pollution, indoor and outdoor air quality) should also be considered. this is certainly not a quick and easy task, but it is a major step towards the eu 2020 strategy's goal of increasing healthy human life expectancy by two years by the end of the decade.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. it is a proposal for a european innovation partnership that promotes a new approach to ageing as an opportunity for the future, rather than a burden on society. it is considered that this approach should also include a clear and unambiguous strategy to promote social objectives without any stigmatisation or discrimination and to formally recognise the role of older people and the importance of their experience and contribution to society and the economy. adequate basic conditions for people to work longer and be productive need to be created, both by increasing labour market flexibility by ensuring lifetime working time and part-time work, and by providing suitable forms of employment contracts and flexible retirement regulation for older people, such as partial retirement or supplementary retirement schemes, ensuring that adequate social protection is always provided. it is emphasised that ageing must be seen as an opportunity rather than a burden and that the value of older people, their experience and their continuing contribution to society must be recognised and promoted. the commission's clear intention to promote the vitality and dignity of older people in europe through innovations relevant to them, to strengthen the culture of active ageing in a europe that is good for all generations and to shape this process together with recognised partners from the research community and civil society is therefore welcomed.

in writing. − statistics show that the current european union society is ageing. in 2010, people aged over 55 already accounted for 30% of all eu citizens. this is projected to reach 37% by 2030. the promotion of healthy and active lifestyles must become one of the eu's top priorities. we should not look for short-term economic solutions or save at the expense of the older generation, especially in the face of the current financial crisis. the number of elderly people in poverty is increasing, and this has a direct impact on their health. we cannot reduce funding for programmes in this area. this will not only permanently reduce the already poor quality of life of the elderly, but also increase the costs of care and treatment for the elderly in the long term. i voted in favour of this report because it contains provisions which will help to create a better, happier and healthier quality of life for older people. we must improve the conditions of the elderly, give them more opportunities to move. we must continue to promote the importance of older people's empowerment and solidarity between generations that the eu highlighted in 2012.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the aim of the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is to ensure that international trade in wild fauna and flora does not threaten the survival of species in the wild. the main causes of biodiversity loss today are wildlife exploitation, illegal trade in fauna and flora, habitat destruction, climate change and human depletion of natural resources. the commission should therefore ensure continuity of funding in its development assistance to achieve the objectives of cites, namely to continue the monitoring illegal elephant hunting (mike) programme, to ensure the protection of recorded marine species, to end the unsustainable and unethical trophy hunting that has led to a significant decline in the african lion population, and more. in addition, the commission and the member states of the european union should explore the possibility of providing long-term financial support to cites through the european development fund.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. cites is the most comprehensive global agreement in force for the conservation of wild fauna and flora, aimed at preventing the over-exploitation of wild fauna and flora in international trade. cites aims to ensure that international trade in wild fauna and flora does not threaten the survival of species in the wild. the eu and the member states are therefore encouraged to use the precautionary principle as a guiding principle in all decisions on working papers and proposals for cites annexes, taking into account in particular the 'user pays' principle, the concept of the ecosystem and traditional conservation principles. it also calls for a united position and for the speed and efficiency of internal decision-making procedures to be improved in order to swiftly agree on an internal eu position on cites cop 16 and to fully leverage the strength of all 27 eu parties to the convention to ensure that decisions at the 16th meeting of the parties to the convention are taken in accordance with the precautionary principle. the eu is called upon to take a leading role in protecting endangered species, to actively participate in the cites negotiations and to promote the closure of the convention's loopholes that are aggravating the situation. it is also desirable that the eu and the member states establish stronger links and alliances with third countries before and during the conference. it is desirable that the cites parties consider additional opportunities to enhance cooperation, coordination and interaction between the parties to the convention on biological diversity at all relevant levels.
in writing. − the eu's participation in the 16th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is another opportunity for the european union to show how the provisions of the eu treaties that state that the eu and its member states should have a united position in international organisations or at meetings of the parties to international conventions work. with up to 200 species disappearing every day worldwide, according to un data, it is important to ensure effective protection of endangered species. the continued failure of elephant conservation is of particular concern. the production of ivory as a nonessential commodity, when much cheaper alternatives exist, is an unjustified luxury. speaking with one voice is therefore the only way to achieve and ensure a unified eu position.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important that a member state faced with large-scale vat fraud has a rapid reaction mechanism that would improve its ability to effectively combat complex fraud schemes. it is worth noting that eu and national budgets suffer several billion euro losses each year as a result of vat fraud. for example, between june 2008 and december 2009, an estimated eur 5 billion was lost to value added tax fraud in the area of greenhouse gas emission allowances. the strategy currently used to combat vat fraud is slow and complex and does not allow the member state concerned to take the necessary action to put an end to the fraud. the rapid response mechanism would grant member states a derogation within one month. it is also envisaged that the derogation will be valid for up to one year. this would allow the member state concerned to start combating fraud almost immediately, pending the adoption of long-term measures. however, before any anti-fraud measures are implemented, the proposed measures must be properly investigated. this proposal would indeed enable member states to respond more quickly and effectively to vat fraud.
in writing. − billions of euros are lost every year to eu countries' budgets as a result of illegal vat fraud. vat fraud causes enormous damage to property, distorts competition and disrupts the functioning of the single market. we must therefore work together to find a cure for vat fraud. i believe that the vat rapid response mechanism is one of the most effective ways of preventing tax fraud. this allows states to respond flexibly to fraud and to combat complex fraud schemes more effectively. in particular, the states will be able to take certain emergency measures as a matter of urgency by applying the reverse charge mechanism. moreover, the speedier procedures and shorter deadlines will ensure a more effective fight.
in writing. − dear colleagues, in times of budgetary constraints and fiscal austerity, appropriate measures against vat fraud are really necessary. measures such as the quick reaction mechanism (qrm), as listed in this proposal, will enable member states to respond efficiently to vat fraud. the ‘reverse charge mechanism’ as well as other anti-fraud measures established under the qrm will improve the chances of ms to effectively tackle fraud schemes such as carrousel fraud and to reduce the possibility of irreparable and considerable financial losses for national and eu budgets. furthermore, the qrm will enable the member states to proceed faster, allowing them to counteract fraud immediately. i welcome this proposal and agree with all measures aimed at fighting tax fraud in the eu and safeguard public revenue. i consider that all member states, including lithuania, have to increase their efforts in fighting tax fraud and evasion which are harmful for a legitimate business climate. and i also think that the eu needs more structural changes to the vat systems in order to make the single market’s functioning more transparent, efficient and coherent. the enhanced fight against fraud now is a key element in maintaining the economic stability across its member states and the eu in general.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the regulation of energy infrastructure projects, which aims to accelerate the completion of the internal energy market and achieve the eu's energy policy objectives. the proposal aims to modernise and extend europe's energy infrastructure, to connect cross-border networks and to strengthen market integration and competitiveness and the integration of energy from renewable sources. this regulation lays down the infrastructure priorities and the procedures and criteria for projects of common interest, giving the competent authority in each member state the responsibility to coordinate the permitting process for projects, setting standards of transparency and the maximum duration of the permitting process. i support the proposals put forward to give the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer) a greater role in ensuring the development of crossborder networks, the coordination of investments and consumer protection. i agree that it is necessary to establish a more efficient procedure for granting project authorisations and a single window principle that national authorities will have to respect when granting project authorisations. it is important that european coordinators are given specific powers to oversee projects experiencing implementation difficulties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the acceleration of the renewal of existing energy infrastructure and the development of new energy infrastructure is crucial to achieving the union's energy and climate policy objectives. for the union as well as for lithuania, the deployment of integrated networks and smart grids is of paramount importance in ensuring a competitive and well-functioning integrated market, in order to optimise the use of energy infrastructure, to increase energy efficiency and to integrate diverse renewable energy sources, and to promote growth, employment and sustainable development. the proposal defines nine priority geographical corridors and three thematic priority areas, sets out the rules for the classification of projects as projects of common interest (pis) and provides for one authority in each member state (one-stop-shop) to monitor and speed up the pip authorisation processes. the measures provided for in this regulation are intended to continue and complement the union's energy policy, namely to complete the internal energy market, to ensure security of supply, in particular in the gas and oil sectors, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 20%, to increase the share of energy from renewable sources in final energy use to 20% and to increase energy efficiency by 20% by 2020. this will enable the union to adapt its infrastructure to further reduce carbon emissions in its energy system by 2050 and to prepare for the interconnection of regions with high renewable energy production capacity and electricity storage potential.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it established that the european commission, as the institution responsible for responding to complaints from eu citizens and helping to identify instances of maladministration by eu institutions, had infringed the ec treaty by failing to take action to ensure that austria's infringement was properly investigated. in 1999, the expansion of vienna airport was started and several construction projects were started. the commission has decided that an environmental impact assessment, as provided for in directive 85/337/eec, should be carried out. since the development permit had been granted and the project was due to be completed shortly, the objective of the directive could not be achieved and the commission therefore agreed not to continue the infringement procedure on condition that austria carried out an ex post environmental impact assessment which would be as close as possible to an ex ante environmental impact assessment. the complainants criticised the commission's actions and lodged a complaint with the european ombudsman. this communication constitutes a re-recommendation by the ombudsman to the commission.
in writing. - i voted for this report. as an institution, the ombudsman examines complaints from eu citizens and identifies instances of maladministration by eu institutions. in this case, the commission did not act on the infringement committed by austria. the commission concluded that an environmental impact assessment as provided for in directive 85/337/eec (the environmental impact assessment directive) should have been carried out. the commission also considered that the fact that the development permit had been granted and the project was almost completed and was due to be completed shortly prevented the objective of the eia directive from being achieved. in consultation with the austrian authorities, the commission agreed not to extend the infringement procedure on condition that austria carries out an ex post environmental impact assessment which is as close as possible to an ex ante environmental impact assessment and which allows a full assessment of the environmental impact of the projects. the complainants criticised the commission's handling of the case and lodged a complaint with the european ombudsman. this report constitutes a re-recommendation by the ombudsman to the commission.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a european union-wide set of rules for accounting for greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions from land use and forestry (lulucf). the eu's greenhouse gas emissions are largely generated by energy production facilities, but a large proportion of emissions are stored in trees, soil, biomass and wood. the aim of this proposal is to integrate the lulucf sector into the eu's efforts to reduce ghg emissions, thus contributing to climate change mitigation, biodiversity conservation and sustainable resource use. i agree with the proposals here to align the accounting rules with the commitments and rules of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol. it is important that accounting methodologies comply with recognised principles of transparency, comparability, completeness and accuracy. it is also necessary to examine the actions to be taken by member states to reduce ghg emissions in the lulucf sector, and the commission should provide guidance and technical assistance to that end.
