in writing. - i voted for this document. it aims in particular to establish a legal framework of sound, harmonised, comprehensive and specific accounting rules for the land use, land-use change and forestry (lulucf) sector. i supported this proposal because it is ambitious and is based, among other things, on the need to establish a more robust accounting system to incorporate the recommendations of international agreements into eu law.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i believe that the agriculture and forestry sectors should be included in the eu's climate change commitments. those activities would contribute to limiting emissions of ghg and increasing removals from the atmosphere and enhancing the impact of changes in land use on the overall objective. in order to enhance climate change mitigation efforts and their visibility in agriculture, forestry and related sectors, a harmonised legal framework should be established to provide clear and robust rules for this sector. it should be noted that such regulation should not create an additional administrative burden.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the establishment of european union-wide rules for accounting for greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions from land use and forestry (lulucf). the main sources of ghg emissions are energy-producing facilities, but a large proportion of emissions are stored in trees, soil, biomass and wood. the aim of this proposal is to integrate the lulucf sector into the eu's efforts to reduce ghg emissions, thus contributing to climate change mitigation, biodiversity conservation and sustainable resource use. i support the proposals set out here to align the accounting rules with the commitments and rules of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol. it is important that accounting methodologies comply with recognised principles of transparency, comparability, completeness and accuracy. it is also necessary to examine the actions to be taken by member states to reduce ghg emissions in the lulucf sector, and the commission should provide guidance and technical assistance to that end.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to simplify and strengthen the eu's greenhouse gas monitoring and reporting rules and to enhance the eu's credibility in relation to developing countries by providing transparent and detailed information on the types and amounts of aid provided. the proposed wording aims, inter alia, to help member states implement the climate and energy package, to improve the timeliness, transparency and comparability of data provided, to ensure compliance by the union and its member states with international monitoring and reporting obligations, including reporting on support to developing countries, to facilitate the development of new union climate change measures. the proposed mechanism will help ensure the harmonisation of the different objectives of the climate and energy package, and it also extends the scope of reporting and monitoring provisions to include the percentage of energy from renewable sources and the total final energy consumption.
in writing. - i agreed to this. timely, reliable and accurate greenhouse gas emissions data are crucial to knowing whether the eu and its member states are doing well enough to meet targets and develop proactive new policies to tackle climate change. the proposal therefore aims to simplify and strengthen the rules for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions in the eu.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as the mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and other climate change-related information should function effectively at eu level. accurate and comprehensive monitoring, emission reporting and other climate change data are key elements for the effective implementation of international commitments. in order to ensure reliable and objective information, transparent, accurate and consistent reporting should be provided. however, in all cases, the principle of proportionality must be strictly respected in the data collection process. the commission should prepare reports based on the reduction of carbon dioxide. it should be empowered to request the necessary information from the member states and to verify its accuracy, timeliness and consistency.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the creation of a european platform for the electronic settlement of disputes between buyers and sellers (esc). the proposal aims to establish rules that will enable buyers and consumers of services to benefit from a low-cost and fast out-of-court dispute settlement system in the european union. the alternative dispute resolution option already exists in some member states, but consumers are not very aware of it, with only 5% of consumers unhappy with their purchases having used it in 2010. the proposal aims to oblige eu countries to ensure this across all sectors and regions. to this end, a website (ges) will be created in all eu languages to allow electronic complaints about goods or services purchased online to be made throughout the eu. the website will also provide a selection of dispute resolution procedures. i agree with the suggestions made that the decision period should not exceed 90 days from the receipt of the complaint and that consumers should be able to access ges free of charge or for a symbolic fee. i believe that this system would make a major contribution to the promotion of e-commerce in the european union and would save millions of euros.
in writing. − for both consumers and businesses, e-commerce has many benefits ranging from lower prices and greater consumer supply to job creation. many consumers, especially younger ones, would find it difficult to imagine the absence of e-commerce services today. this shows the success and growth potential of this market. e-commerce is also growing and improving every day. in the last few years alone, remarkable progress has been made and, it must be acknowledged, such positive developments have been driven by measures taken to increase consumer confidence in the market for e-commerce and online services. electronic dispute resolution for consumer disputes is another step towards increasing trust in e-commerce. i believe that the creation of an electronic platform where all consumers can resolve disputes out of court and submit complaints online in all the official languages of the european union, when the recipient and the provider of the service are located in different eu member states, will make a significant contribution to the creation of a truly unified e-commerce area.
in writing. - i agreed to this. the legislation provides for the creation of a website, overseen by the european commission, where electronic complaints about goods or services purchased online can be made in all eu languages. the standard complaint form will be available to be filled in and the most appropriate dispute resolution scheme will be chosen. each stage of the dispute settlement will be visible online and the transfer of information will be protected by eu data protection rules. consumers and traders, especially small ones, feel insecure about online trading because they do not know where to turn when problems arise. this new regulation should therefore give them the confidence to buy and sell across the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on electronic dispute resolution for consumers, which aims to create an electronic dispute resolution platform. this document is closely linked to the directive on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes, which we have recently discussed. it is welcome that the notice specifies the specific time limits within which the dispute should be resolved, the legally binding or non-binding nature of the outcome of the procedure, etc. ensuring adequate consumer protection must be a constant pursuit. this not only encourages consumers to defend their rights, but also encourages both producers and service providers to avoid abuse and to provide quality goods and services to the market.
in writing. - i agree with the position that has been put forward. an effective functioning of the electronic consumer redress mechanism will ensure a well-functioning system of consumer protection at eu and national level. in particular, all obstacles to the settlement of disputes relating to the cross-border sale of goods by electronic means must be removed and the provision of services by electronic means must be ensured. these measures must be directed at the protection of the rights and claims of the individual already infringed. the electronic consumer dispute resolution mechanism shall be easily accessible and free of charge. the rules should be sufficiently flexible. i believe that the proper functioning of the procedures will not only benefit consumers, but will also stimulate the development of online commerce, create new opportunities for businesses and help the economy to grow.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the establishment of rules which will allow eu customers and consumers of services to settle disputes arising from the sale of goods or the provision of services by simple and inexpensive out-of-court means. consumers and sellers will be able to settle disputes over substandard goods with the help of neutral arbitrators (e.g. mediators, ombudsmen, complaints boards). the alternative dispute resolution option already exists in some member states, but consumers are not very aware of it, with only 5% of consumers unhappy with their purchases having used it in 2010. the proposal aims to oblige eu countries to ensure this across all sectors and regions. the commission will also develop an e-resolution platform (erp) to enable electronic complaints about goods or services purchased online to be lodged across the eu in all eu languages. the website will also provide a selection of dispute resolution procedures. i agree with the suggestions made that the decision period should not exceed 90 days from the receipt of the complaint and that consumers should be able to access ges free of charge or for a symbolic fee. i believe that this system would make a major contribution to the promotion of e-commerce in the european union and would save millions of euros.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a contribution by parliament to the adoption of the directive on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes. the lack of simple, inexpensive and appropriate means of dispute resolution is currently one of the obstacles facing many citizens in the european union. the losses to consumers from these problems amount to 0.4% of total eu gdp, but only 5% of consumers used adr in 2010. the eu treaty enshrines a high level of consumer protection as part of the free movement of goods and services. consumers will only shop in other member states if they know that there are problems with the goods or services they have purchased, and they will be able to defend their rights. entrepreneurs, especially smes, are also reluctant to carry out commercial activities in other member states, as they are reluctant to deal with the legal systems of other countries. the purpose of this directive is to address the problems of significant and persistent barriers to consumers and traders accessing the services of a well-functioning adr entity.
in writing. - i voted for this document. some eu countries already have alternative dispute resolution schemes, but consumers lack knowledge about them. the new directive obliges eu countries to provide this possibility in all sectors of trade and services. it will allow you to complain about goods or services purchased in a shop or online, no matter where in the eu you are. the disputes shall be settled within 90 days. the ep negotiators have ensured that the scheme is available free of charge or for a nominal fee. this directive is beneficial for both buyers and sellers. a low-cost and fast dispute resolution system is expected to save consumers millions of euros in the eu each year. it should also promote electronic trade between eu countries, which is essential for the growth of the european internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on alternative dispute resolution for consumers. we have emphasised the importance of consumer protection here in the european parliament on many occasions. the changes proposed by this communication will make it possible to resolve disputes concerning the sale of goods or the provision of services in the european union more quickly and easily. long redress procedures often discourage consumers from defending their infringed rights. as e-commerce expands, it is necessary to look for ways to simplify consumer protection. if we want to build a well-functioning eu legal system and ensure adequate consumer protection, we must work towards making dispute settlement simpler and more user-friendly. at the same time, it is necessary to ensure that information on such dispute resolution methods is available to the consumer.
in writing. − i believe that this directive, by providing for alternative dispute resolution to litigation, will ensure a high level of consumer protection and contribute to the effective functioning of the internal market. however, this regulation must be consistent and simplified. uniform dispute resolution practices must be developed throughout the eu and the principles of efficiency, transparency and fairness properly implemented. first, consumer and business confidence in the system must be increased. consumers must be given the opportunity to defend their rights properly by lawful means acceptable to them. this will help them save money and ensure equal rights to compensation.
in writing. − consumer protection in the eu still has gaps, which are particularly evident when dealing with e-commerce cases. many of them either did not resolve their disputes completely or went through a rather lengthy legal process. the electronic dispute resolution platform is a welcome tool that will provide consumers and businesses with a one-stop-shop solution for resolving disputes outside the court system, based on the alternative dispute resolution (adr) platform. this will enable consumers and sellers to settle disputes over defective goods with the help of neutral arbitrators. they shall propose a solution within 90 days or assist the parties to the dispute in reaching a mutual agreement. general principles to be followed by all gas entities, including appropriate competence, impartiality, transparency, efficiency and integrity, and the enforcement of these principles to be monitored by national authorities. currently, out-of-court dispute resolution is only available in some business sectors or only in certain areas in the eu, and in 2010 only 5% of consumers who were dissatisfied with their purchases made use of this option. the gas format will be particularly important in member states where a large number of pending cases are concentrated and therefore citizens are not guaranteed their right to a hearing within a reasonable time. i agree with the report, which is a very welcome and necessary initiative to protect consumer rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to develop sustainable cooperation with the overseas countries and territories (octs) in the indian ocean, the caribbean, the atlantic ocean and the pacific ocean. these countries are directly confronted with new challenges (such as the globalisation of trade, new environmental challenges, risks associated with climate change) that europe must also help address. the octs' natural assets and the opportunities for activity in them can make these countries and territories a key component of the european union's strategies and an innovative element in international negotiations. the current octs-european union association decision (oda) of 2001 establishes the legal framework for promoting octs' economic relations with the eu and octs' social and economic development. this decision shall expire on 31 december 2013. it is intended to renew and strengthen regional cooperation and support the octs as the eu's neighbours in the advanced countries and territories in the regions where they are located, and to promote the participation of the octs and their neighbours in the various fora.
in writing. - i support this resolution. although these countries are outside the eu customs territory and the single market, their citizens have eu citizenship, which requires effective and consistent cooperation. i believe that priority should be given to cooperation in areas of mutual interest in order to ensure sustainable economic and social development. this new agreement should provide a basis for increasing their competitiveness, meeting their needs, taking into account their specificities and differences. it should be noted that austerity policies have had a particularly strong impact on employment. this has had a negative impact on octs' cooperation with the eu in the implementation of public investment programmes. in this context, there is a need to strengthen regional cooperation and support octs and to promote their participation in eu communication programmes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive laying down general public health requirements relating to radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption. the aim is to incorporate the requirements and methods for monitoring these substances (radon, tritium, etc.) in order to maintain the uniformity, coherence and completeness of radiation safety legislation. i agree with the suggestions made here that, in order to ensure effective and consistent protection of public health in europe, it is necessary to incorporate in the directive the differences identified by the international commission on radiological safety between natural and human sources of radioactivity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the provision of safe drinking water to european citizens is one of the most important concerns of policies relating to human health and the environment. the quality of drinking water is currently regulated by council directive 98/83/ec (qd), including the regulation of pollutants such as toxic chemicals and radionuclides. however, the requirements for the monitoring of the tertiary and general indicative dose have not yet been implemented, despite the fact that member states had to comply with the drinking water directive by 2003. the commission's proposal aims to include the relevant requirements not in the csfs but in specific legislation based on the euratom treaty. it is important to establish requirements that ensure uniformity, coherence and completeness of radiation protection legislation in the determination of the parametric values, frequencies and methods for radioactive substances, i.e. radon, tritium and other radioactive substances.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. it aims to incorporate requirements for the monitoring of radioactive substances into specific legislation adopted under the euratom treaty in order to maintain the uniformity, coherence and comprehensiveness of radiation safety legislation at community level. it is a specific measure for monitoring the level of radioactivity in water intended for human consumption, with the aim of achieving a public health objective.
in writing. − in a european union with a high level of environmental protection, the quality of natural elements, especially those used by humans, must also be ensured. this is not the first time that the european commission has tried to justify lower environmental standards with the euratom treaty. i am convinced that the determination of water contamination by radioactive substances should not differentiate between different sources of contamination. i therefore support the resolution and the proposals contained therein to change the legal framework to ensure better quality of drinking water.
in writing. − i agree with the proposals presented, as there is a need to set clear and strict requirements for radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption. water is essential to man. human-induced radioactivity is a difficult problem to solve. radioactive substances are usually introduced into water by improper handling of radioactive waste. in view of this, the polluter pays principle and the pollutant brake conditions must be strictly applied in the case of man-made pollution. the damage that occurs must be covered by the perpetrator, not by the water user or the public. in order to maintain a high level of consumer protection, the quality requirements for mineral water should be as stringent as those for tap water.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the adoption of two pieces of legislation, the so-called 'two-pack' legislation, which would give the european commission greater powers to control the national budgets of the euro area countries. the aim of the proposal is to ensure financial stability and economic growth in the euro area by providing for measures to prevent excessive government debt. to this end, euro area countries will be obliged to submit annually to the commission their draft national budgets for the following year for evaluation. the commission will have the right to ask the member states to amend them if necessary. the surveillance of countries in economic recession will also be strengthened. i support the proposals set out to ensure that countries do not reduce their national budgets at the expense of investment in education, health and economic growth. it is also necessary to strengthen transparency and democratic accountability, and i therefore support increased oversight of the commission, the european central bank and the international monetary fund in countries experiencing economic difficulties following economic reforms. i am in favour of setting up a group of experts to assess the pros and cons of the debt relief fund and the euro notes. i agree that the commission should propose the relevant draft legislation as early as 2014 on the basis of its conclusions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the context of the ongoing financial and sovereign debt crisis, the proposal to strengthen economic and budgetary surveillance in member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to financial stability in the euro area is of great relevance. excessive government debt can have serious consequences for all member states of the european union and therefore a member state whose currency is the euro should be subject to stricter supervision if it is experiencing or is at risk of experiencing serious financial difficulties. this would ensure a rapid return to normalcy and protect other euro area member states from possible adverse side effects. in order to respond quickly, the decision-making procedures are to be adjusted. it is also proposed to create a legal protection system for member states at risk of default or default in the near future. in such a case, the commission could, after consulting the council, decide to apply this legal protection regime to the member state, inter alia by suspending the contractual provisions on final set-off or credit events.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the economic and budgetary surveillance procedures developed by the european union and the euro area member states in response to the economic and financial crisis that began in 2008 need to be broadly adopted in the light of the social and economic problems that this crisis has created. the deteriorating global financial situation has led to a sharp slowdown in growth in the union and serious financial difficulties for the member states. coordination of economic and social policies between member states can help to address these problems. the proposal therefore aims to apply stricter supervision to a member state whose currency is the euro if it is experiencing or is at risk of experiencing serious financial difficulties. this should ensure a rapid return to normal and protect other euro area member states from possible adverse spill-over effects.
in writing. − it should be noted that the financial crisis has clearly revealed the interrelationship between sovereign debt, financial stability and bank solvency. the coordination of economic and social policies must be in line with the democratic principles of the eu. in order to restore a sound and sustainable economic and fiscal situation in countries experiencing severe financial difficulties in a timely and operational manner, the provisions on enhanced economic and budgetary surveillance and enhanced economic policy coordination should be applied with the utmost care, after analysing all potential threats and carrying out a comprehensive assessment for each country. the application of surveillance measures must take account of more than the budgetary situation of the member states and the investment forecasts. it is essential that the commission acts expeditiously and that the alert mechanism is put in place in a timely manner to prevent adverse consequences. in addition, countries experiencing particularly severe financial stability difficulties should also take certain measures. in particular, they should identify measures to address the causes of the difficulties and develop macroeconomic adjustment programmes.

in writing. − i voted for this report because budgetary surveillance should always be one of the eu's main objectives in terms of promoting a high level of employment and ensuring adequate social protection. it is important to strengthen budgetary discipline across the eu by setting additional requirements for the monitoring of national budgetary policies, a common budgetary timetable and closer monitoring of budgetary decisions by member states subject to the excessive deficit procedure. the regulation on the effective enforcement of budgetary surveillance in the euro area provides for additional enforcement measures, namely financial penalties for member states. it is also important that eu budgetary policy is fully aligned with the new strategy for jobs and growth europe 2020, which aims to help the eu overcome the crisis and steer the eu economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, ensuring high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion.
in writing. - i abstained on this document. however, i do agree that there should be additional union instruments to coordinate and monitor the budgetary and economic policies of the member states. however, due care should be exercised at all stages and no material relating to the issuance plans of member states' debt securities, the extension of the maturity of outstanding debts or other significant transactions should be made public and should be used for internal coordination purposes only.
in writing. − to improve the performance of budgetary and economic policies, it is necessary to ensure that the budgetary procedures of the member states are compatible with the economic policy coordination framework. the tightening of budgetary and economic policies and the introduction of additional monitoring requirements require a thorough analysis, with particular attention to promoting employment and ensuring adequate social protection. i think it is appropriate to establish a common budgetary timetable. the procedures for monitoring and evaluating draft budgetary plans in the member states shall be in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. in addition, national budgets must be compatible with the economic guidelines.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the creation of a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the proposal aims to establish a legal framework under which the status of 'european venture capital fund' and the 'venture capital passport' can be granted to different types of investment funds. it sets out the criteria that the fund must meet in order to do so, the requirements that the managers of the venture capital fund must meet and the investment limits that are imposed on the use of the fund's assets. i support the proposals that the european venture capital fund should be obliged to invest 70% of the capital provided by its sponsors in smes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because venture capital funds stimulate economic growth, help create jobs and attract capital, encourage the creation and development of innovative companies, increase their investment in research and technological development and promote entrepreneurship, innovation and competitiveness, in the light of the objectives of the eu's europe 2020 strategy and the long-term challenges facing the member states as set out in the european strategy and policy analysis framework report 'world trends 2030'. in the absence of a common framework, there is a risk that member states may take different measures at national level, which would have a direct negative impact on and create obstacles to the smooth functioning of the internal market, as venture capital funds wishing to operate across the union would be subject to different rules in different member states. in this context, it is necessary to establish a common framework of rules on the use of the designation 'european venture capital fund', in particular on the composition of the portfolio of funds operating under that designation, their eligible investment vehicles, the investment instruments they may use and the categories of eligible investors who are entitled to invest in such funds under uniform rules throughout the union.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. as venture capital provides financing for companies that are typically very small, in the early stages of their formation as legal entities and with significant growth and expansion potential. in addition, the venture capital funds provide these companies with valuable experience and knowledge, business contacts, and advice on brand value and strategy. by providing finance and advice to those undertakings, venture capital funds promote economic growth, help create jobs and attract capital, encourage the formation and development of companies, increase their investment in research and technological development and promote entrepreneurship, innovation and competitiveness in the union.
in writing. − i support this resolution because venture capital funds are a source of economic growth. the elimination of distortions of competition is necessary to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market. a reliable and stable environment for investors must be created. in addition, smes have been strengthened in their growth and innovation. specific safeguards should be established and an efficient european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises should be established.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the creation of a sector focused on investing in legal persons engaged in non-profit-making activities aimed at achieving various objectives of a social nature. the proposal aims to establish a legal framework under which the various types of investment funds can be granted the status of 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and the corresponding passports. it sets out the criteria that the fund must meet in order to do so, the requirements that the managers of the venture capital fund must meet and the limits on investments that are made using the fund's assets. all new european social enterprise funds should clearly publish information on the types of targeted social enterprises, their selection methods and the ways in which the fund supports social enterprises. the rules applicable to social investment funds still vary from one member state to another and are often complex. i agree that the new proposal should simplify them.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report in the light of the fact that the crisis has led to a deterioration in the current situation in the area of gender equality, an increase in the risk of gender-based violence and poverty among older women, and a deterioration in the health of mothers and children. women are currently suffering the effects of measures taken by governments to reduce the general government deficit. women in the public sector are the most affected by budget cuts. in some member states, the number of employees in the civil service has been reduced by 25%. the various cuts in social benefits and the budget allocated to social infrastructure, education, childcare, healthcare and care of dependent persons have led to a shift of work in this area to the home, and in particular to women who have to leave paid work or reduce their working hours to perform work that the state no longer performs or can no longer afford. it is therefore necessary to consider the possibility of further adapting the structural funds to current conditions in order to provide additional support to the areas of women's employment likely to be affected by the crisis and to support in addressing childcare, training and employment opportunities. the commission's proposals on gender balance in management are also a step in the right direction. in addition, budget cuts should not be a reason to reconsider funding for associations and programmes to combat violence.

in writing. − the savings measures taken by member states during the crisis have had the greatest impact on the service and public sectors, which have traditionally been dominated by women. one third of women work part-time, accepting work on business licenses, working for minimum wage to earn some income to support their family, and later this choice of women is reflected in the size of their pension. another problem is that women are paid 16 to 17% less than men for the same work. after a baby is born, a woman's income typically drops by 12 percent. moreover, women often choose to take on less responsible responsibilities so that they can care for their family while working. i agree with commissioner reding that we must take measures today to ensure that childbearing and raising children and caring for the family do not lead to women's poverty in the future, because the family puts women at risk of their social security and pension throughout their working lives. today, as many as 60% of women in the eu have a higher education and 60% of women are in the labour market. we invest a lot in girls' education, but we also need to invest in their participation in the labour market. we need to promote female entrepreneurship. i support this report and congratulate the rapporteur on her excellent report. the crisis has highlighted the factors behind the decline in the position of women. equality is not just a word in the law, gender equality must become a reality.
in writing. - i agreed to this. throughout their lives, women and men are influenced by gender stereotypes in their thinking, from expectations about how boys and girls should behave in primary and secondary school to specific expectations later in life about career choices and their representation in the labour market. the negative gender stereotypes that underpin societal beliefs and attitudes and their prevalence have a negative impact on women and consequently limit their opportunities and choices in the social, economic and political spheres. i therefore support the successful use of the european social fund (esf) for long-term strategies to enable women to learn more about the labour market sectors where they are under-represented due to gender stereotypes and thus to make them more attractive. strategies should include affirmative action, lifelong learning and encouraging active girls to choose studies in areas that are not traditionally considered female-centred, such as information technology or mechanics, and should support work-life balance measures for men and women.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because, when the next parliamentary term begins in 2014, the european parliament (ep) will have to be composed of 751 members (750 members plus the president). following the entry into force of the treaty of accession of croatia, croatia will be allocated 12 seats in the parliament, bringing the total number of seats temporarily to 766. in order to bring the number of seats in line with the treaty provisions (751), the total number of seats will therefore have to be reduced by 15 seats. 3 of the 15 places will be compulsorily withdrawn from the german quota, which will be reduced from 99 to 96 places - the limit set by the treaty. the remaining 12 places will have to be reduced by one or more places (total of 12) by reducing the quota of the 24 member states (including croatia) which exceed the minimum of 6 places laid down in the treaty (currently malta, luxembourg, cyprus and estonia each have 6 places). the decision establishing the composition of the new parliament may also require more detailed arrangements for the redistribution of seats in order to take account of any changes in the population of the member states and/or to improve the interpretation and implementation of the principle of proportionality by decreasing the number of seats laid down in the treaty.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a reform of the common agricultural policy, which aims to ensure a stable supply of high-quality food to consumers in the european union and adequate protection of the environment. one of the most important reform priorities for lithuania is the fairer distribution of eu direct payments. as early as 2007-2013, some lithuanian farmers were forced to abandon agricultural activities due to the incorrect agricultural policy. this is also affecting the country's rapidly growing emigration flows. it is necessary to start the standardisation of benefits as early as 2014 and to ensure that no member state receives benefits below 75% of the eu average in 2019. as regards other aspects of the reform, i support the proposals made for direct payments to active farmers only, not to landowners, for a ceiling of 300 000 direct payments and for new compulsory environmental measures for which each eu country should allocate 30% of direct payments. i agree that these measures should be flexible, i.e. dependent on the size of the farm and the environmental protection measures already taken by the farmer. i also believe that risk management measures should be financed from the rural development programme budget rather than from the direct payments budget. it is important to allow farmers' organisations to negotiate ppas on behalf of their members, as this would allow them to strengthen their bargaining power.
in writing. − i voted for direct payments to agriculture and i am pleased that the amendment on direct payments to farmers in the baltic states, put to the vote in plenary by the representatives of the baltic states - lithuania, latvia and estonia - with the other members of the european parliament, was adopted. it is a major achievement that the majority of meps supported this amendment and that the situation of baltic farmers, including lithuania, will improve as regards direct payments. at present, the gap in direct payments to farmers in the baltic states is still large compared to other eu member states. our farmers compete with farmers in other eu countries on the same production, labour and agricultural raw materials markets, but the direct payments received by baltic farmers are well below the eu average, with little difference in production costs. under this adopted proposal, direct payments to farmers in the baltic states will start to increase and approach the eu average in a shorter period than was proposed in the original report of the european parliament's committee on agriculture. thus, if our farmers are given a level playing field and fair support, the agricultural sector in the baltic states would become viable and could participate and compete on equal terms in the common agricultural market.
in writing. − i abstained because i am not satisfied with the proposal presented, and because i want to draw attention to the large differences in direct payments to farmers in the baltic states compared to other eu member states. if the baltic farmers were to be given a level playing field, and this should be ensured by fair and equitable support, the agricultural sector in the baltic countries would become viable. i believe that by the end of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, direct support should be distributed fairly across the union in order to achieve full harmonisation of direct support to farmers' incomes in all member states.

in writing. − the importance of the eu’s energy policy lies in growth and economic competitiveness, creating jobs in the eu. i voted in favour of this report as the energy roadmap 2050 shows that each member state has to focus on such critical areas as emissions reduction, energy independence and energy security, renewable energy, energy efficiency, investments in advanced technologies, etc. furthermore, the current market environment is highly unpredictable, thus new strategies and innovative instruments should be promoted to encourage investment in infrastructure, enabling a quick adjustment to the rapidly changing environment. it is very important to adopt the strategy of regional energy specialisation, allowing regions to develop those energy sources which provide the most efficient means, but at the same time there is a need to pursue closer integration with neighbouring countries and regions, and to strengthen cooperation with partners.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for an energy action plan to 2050. the proposal aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80% by 2050, by reducing the use of the most polluting fuels, such as coal and oil, while improving the eu's competitiveness and security of supply. the objective of the plan is increased energy efficiency and a higher share of renewable energy sources. i agree with the suggestions that the reduction of energy consumption in buildings should be considered a key aspect of the eu's long-term energy policy. it is necessary to adopt ambitious strategies for the renovation of buildings and to explore scenarios for 'energy-intensive use of renewable resources'. i agree that it is important to exploit low greenhouse gas electricity generation (including renewables, carbon capture and storage and nuclear) in the future energy mix. it is also important to establish robust systems for investing in renewable energy sources, to ensure that agreements are not concluded in contravention of internal energy market legislation and to enable the commission to analyse agreements in order to verify their compatibility with that legislation.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because it is the european parliament's way of putting forward its proposals in the debate on the eu's energy action plan to 2050. as member states have an interest in reducing dependence on energy imports at volatile prices and in diversifying energy supplies, the main energy policy objective in the field of energy security is to reduce uncertainties that lead to interstate tensions and market failures that prevent suppliers and consumers from taking advantage of trade. energy security in the eu is based on the fundamental pillar of own energy resources and access to them. in this respect, it would therefore be most prudent for states to develop energy technologies in which they have the skills and experience to guarantee a stable and continuous energy supply, while respecting environmental and climate protection standards. for member states, in pursuit of energy security and energy independence, the focus should be on an energy interdependence model, with the rapid completion of the eu internal energy market and the infrastructure for a north-south and east-west smart grid covering all electricity grids. it is necessary to achieve a fully integrated european energy market by 2014, to fully implement internal energy market legislation in all member states and to ensure that no member state or region remains isolated from the european gas and electricity networks after 2015.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the eu's energy policy must be aligned not only with climate change and environmental protection but also with other priority areas of union policy, including security, foreign and neighbourhood affairs, trade and development policy, and the defence of human rights and democratic principles. the implementation of the eu's energy policy should aim at greater independence, including through energy efficiency, the promotion of renewable energy sources and the shift towards low-emission sources, thereby enhancing the union's competitiveness.
in writing. − energy policy has only been a matter of eu competence for a few years. nevertheless, it is important to define long-term and clear guidelines for the implementation of this policy and concrete action plans already today. i would like to highlight two priority areas of action which are also discussed in this document. on the one hand, the successful functioning of the eu energy market requires that the european union is no longer an energy island, that the rules of competition in the single energy supply market are enforced and that the development of new energy sources (e.g. shale gas) is guaranteed. on the other hand, energy is closely linked to environmental policy. efficient use of energy resources and energy saving are an essential element of eu energy policy to achieve both energy independence, cost reduction and environmental policy objectives. i therefore believe that energy policy action in these two areas should be a priority in both the short and long term.
in writing. − energy policy must be conducted on the basis of the principles of sustainable development, ensuring equal, universal and competitive access to energy resources. closer integration with neighbouring countries is necessary to achieve full independence from fossil fuels. the eu's priority projects must be clearly formulated, with the principle of the possibility of concentrating large-scale private investment. more attention should be paid to the achievement of the targets for energy efficiency, renewable energy and greenhouse gas emissions. it should be noted that the impact of its implementation on individual countries is not addressed in this plan. in addition, a strategy for closer cooperation between states and the creation of a european energy community should be developed to achieve the objectives set out in this plan. states must develop technologies that guarantee a stable and continuous supply of energy. i believe that by 2050, by using up all the low-carbon electricity generation, we should have a nearly zero-carbon electricity sector and low electricity prices. in this context, nuclear energy has a special role to play in reducing system costs and electricity prices.
in writing. − today energy policy is facing many challenges and needs to be adapted to a changing reality. the energy roadmap 2050 goes beyond the goals established in the energy 2020 communication and provides priorities for long-term energy orientations. targets set in this roadmap suggest a greater scope of governance than the eu actually possesses now, and establish the commitment to move to a low-carbon economy in 2050 and to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from 80 % to 95 % by 2050. the roadmap also proposes measures to increase energy efficiency and places a strong emphasis on renewable sources of energy. i welcome this report and consider that a coordinated energy policy and political commitment are needed in order to reconcile the application of the climate objectives with the necessity for energy security in the eu. this report takes into account the changes that the energy market is undergoing now and focuses on the future of an energy market by asking the question concerning renewable energy and shale gas. this question is particularly relevant for lithuania as the position of different stakeholders on shale gas and renewable energy is not homogenous and can be determined only in the future.
in writing. − there is a need to re-evaluate the safety of existing reactors in europe and to protect them against accidents which have been assessed as highly improbable. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on risk and safety assessments (‘stress tests’) of nuclear power plants in the european union and related activities because of the usefulness of this procedure and its character as an unprecedented exercise at world level. at the same time, i hope that the results of the stress tests will contribute to enhancing a nuclear safety culture in europe, thus setting a leading example internationally (especially after the fukushima accident). the results of this quite detailed analysis of the preparedness and safety of nuclear power plants against natural disasters or other external events in the eu and, to some extent, also in some neighbouring countries allows an ambitious and stable regulatory framework to be created for the safe continuation of nuclear activity in europe. i firmly believe that the results of the stress tests are very important for the safety of citizens worldwide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the risk and safety assessment of nuclear power plants in the european union (testing under harsh conditions). the proposal aims to encourage member states to implement without delay the nuclear safety recommendations issued following the eu inspections of the resilience of nuclear power plants to natural disasters. following the fukushima accident in 2011, this inspection was carried out at all 145 nuclear reactors. it assessed the safety of nuclear power plants in the event of extreme natural events, such as earthquakes and floods. almost all eu nuclear power plants are identified as in need of upgrades, at a cost of €25 billion. i agree with the calls for member states to make all necessary improvements without delay, but i do not think that the current principle that nuclear safety should be the sole responsibility of the member state where the nuclear power plant is located or is being closed is correct. in the event of a disaster, the consequences would extend beyond the member state, and the states themselves do not have sufficient experience and resources to manage these processes. i would therefore urge the commission to review the principles of nuclear safety and liability and to establish a mechanism for supervision and liability at eu level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because, in the light of the experience gained following the accident at the fukushima daiichi nuclear power plant in japan, the safety of nuclear power plants is becoming a matter of particular concern in the european union and worldwide. in the european union, 47 nuclear power plants with 111 reactors are home to more than 100 000 people within a 30 km radius. on the basis of the results of the stress tests, the national regulatory authorities concluded that there were no technical reasons for the closure of any nuclear power plant in the eu. however, stress testing has shown that almost all nuclear power plants have to implement certain safety improvements specific to each of them. the aim should be to publish guidelines for the assessment of natural hazards and limit cases by the western european association of nuclear regulators, to emphasise the importance of periodic safety checks, to implement recognised measures to increase insulation and to minimise the number of accidents caused by natural hazards and their potential consequences. to achieve this, it is necessary to implement the identified and necessary safety enhancement measures without delay, while stressing that measures relating to nuclear safety and security should not be affected by the collective savings measures adopted by member states in times of economic difficulty.
in writing. - i agreed to this. the results of the european union's nuclear power plants stress testing should contribute to the development of a nuclear safety culture in europe, so that it can serve as an example at international level. it is recognised that following the stress test, countries have started to implement or plan measures that will improve the safety of their power plants, in particular in the light of the experience gained after the fukushima events. the fact that the european nuclear safety regulators group and the commission have agreed on an action plan to implement the recommendations and that all actions to raise the nuclear safety thresholds following stress testing will be taken jointly at european level is also welcomed. on the basis of the peer review, the commission identified measures to be considered at eu level, thus encouraging all actors involved to take appropriate and immediate follow-up action, taking into account all the conclusions and recommendations made, including the best practices identified.
in writing. − i voted in favour of a resolution which contains many important comments and suggestions on eu leadership in shaping the highest international standards of nuclear safety and ensuring safety in eu member states. the european parliament's position that nuclear energy remains an important source of energy for reducing co2 emissions obliges the eu to pay particular attention to nuclear safety. i believe that stress testing should also include terrorist incidents and plane crashes. it is also necessary to ensure that this testing is carried out by third countries, including russia and belarus, which are building nuclear power plants close to the eu border. the astaravo nuclear power plant in belarus is located just 30 miles [50 km] from one of the eu capitals. an accident in the baltic sea in the kaliningrad area would immediately affect at least two eu member states. the current situation, with no consultation of affected parties, is very worrying. the reluctance of these countries to cooperate and share information with affected eu countries is already felt during the pre-construction phase, and the likelihood of coordinated cross-border cooperation in the event of a disaster seems particularly low. i think the eu should make its expectations clear to the third parties involved.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i believe that the highest and strictest principles of nuclear safety regulation must be applied not only in the eu but also globally to nuclear power plants, whether they are in operation or closed or closed. particular attention should be paid to those countries that have not applied transparent nuclear safety testing under stressed conditions, despite the fact that their power plants are located at the borders of eu member states. i think that prevention measures outside the facility are a very important issue. in view of this, the scope of stress testing should be extended to include off-site assessment of emergency preparedness. on the other hand, we must understand that testing the risks and safety of nuclear power plants under stress conditions cannot replace the comprehensive safety inspection of nuclear power plants.

in writing. − the endocrine is one of the most important systems in the body. the endocrine system regulates much of what happens in the body, including reproduction, metabolism, growth, salt and water balance and cardiac function. taking into account the fact that during the past 20 years, hormone-related disorders and illnesses like cancer, obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular diseases have increased and that endocrine disrupters are classified as risk factors for health, i voted in favour of this report because the protection of human health is an important eu policy. moreover, it is very important to make clear what is regarded as a substance with endocrine-disrupting properties, and criteria determining what constitutes an endocrine disrupter must be scientifically based. it is important to provide support for up-to-date research. i truly believe that protection of human health must be effective – to restrict the use of endocrine disruptors in products, such as cosmetics, toys, furniture, building products, food, etc. the fact that we do not know everything cannot be used as a pretext for inactivity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the protection of public health against hormones (ham). such substances are found in cosmetics, furniture, electronics, construction and textiles, and food. their effects are harmful to human reproduction, metabolism and the heart. the aim of the proposal is to clarify and reduce the available scientific knowledge on the human exposure to these substances. i support the proposals to restrict the use of these substances in products for specific target groups: children, young people, pregnant women. it is important to apply stricter safety requirements for the installation of pre-schools and schools and to reduce the number of permits for endocrine disrupting substances. it is necessary to include ham in the list of substances of very high concern in the reach regulation and to establish the testing requirements under existing eu legislation to determine ham.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because over the last 20 years there has been an increase in the incidence of disorders and diseases of the human endocrine system, including premature puberty, an increase in the incidence of deformed genitalia, an increase in the incidence of certain cancers and metabolic diseases. a growing body of research shows that endocrine disrupting chemicals and their combinations have an impact on both chronic diseases, including hormone-related cancers, obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and reproductive problems. proposals for definitions and testing of endocrine disrupting chemicals, as well as information requirements for chemicals placed on the market, and for eu legislation clarifying what is considered to be endocrine disrupting chemicals, need to be submitted as soon as possible. on the basis of the available scientific data, there is no sufficient basis for establishing no-effect limit values, therefore endocrine disruptors should be considered as non-limit values and any exposure to such substances could be hazardous. the eu should give priority to funding research into the health effects of endocrine disruptors and to support long-term studies, allowing for evidence-based evaluation of the long-term and multi-generational effects of endocrine disruptors.
in writing. - i voted for this document. in our daily lives, we are constantly exposed to endocrine-disrupting substances. they are found in food packaging, skin care products, cosmetics, building materials, electronics, furniture and floor coverings. many of the plastic products we find in our homes and workplaces contain one or more chemicals that are suspected of having endocrine disrupting effects. substances with endocrine disrupting properties are numerous and widespread, which means that individual consumers cannot protect themselves against them. appropriate measures should therefore be taken to reduce the exposure of humans to endocrine disrupting substances, together with increased efforts in studies to refine the available scientific knowledge on the effects of endocrine disrupting substances.
in writing. - i support this resolution. given that it is not possible for individual consumers to protect themselves against these substances, it is necessary to lay down more stringent safety requirements. the use of endocrine disrupting substances in products intended for specific target groups should be restricted at eu level. it is very important that endocrine disrupting substances are classified as substances without limit values, as they can severely impair the human immune system. in addition, specific measures relating to specific scientific criteria for the identification of endocrine disrupting properties shall be developed.
in writing. − over the past twenty years the rate of hormone-related disorders and illnesses has constantly risen. the increase in such disorders is explained by external factors such as lifestyle, and economic factors, nutrition, pathogens, drugs and other social causes such as stress. there is another factor which has been proven by a wide range of studies that can contribute to hormone-related disorders: exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals. the impact of chemical exposure is not immediately visible but can lead to an increased risk of hormonal disturbances, reduced fertility and reproductive abnormalities and can be particularly dangerous for pregnant women, children and young people. this parliament report calls for a reduction in exposure to these chemicals and provides an input for assessing relevant eu legislation, putting emphasis on the precautionary principle in the ongoing review of the eu’s strategy on endocrine disruptors. i welcome this report and consider that further appropriate measures need to be taken in order to identify endocrine disruptors, harmonise new testing methods and establish criteria for regulation. only concrete legislative measures can lead to the protection of citizens from substances with endocrine-disrupting properties and in turn could help to decrease hormone-related disorders linked to them.
in writing. − the european union is at a turning point in employment policy. trends reveal that there is a decline in the working-age population in europe and a clear human resources crisis. in the next 10 years, the number of people of working-age is expected to decline by 14 million. qualified immigration can make a key contribution to resolving this dual dilemma. i fully support this report because diverse, open and tolerant societies are more likely to attract skilled workers who possess the human and creative capital required for knowledge economies. employment is the key to successful integration. moreover, integration is a continuous two-way process requiring the involvement of both parties: non-eu nationals and the host society. therefore, it is necessary to combat discrimination against third-country nationals and eu citizens coming from other eu member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the integration of migrants and its impact on the eu labour market. despite an unemployment rate of around 10% (23.8 million people) in the eu, there is already a shortage of skilled labour. it is necessary to implement a high-quality integration policy for migrants in the eu, to provide equal access to the eu labour market for migrants and to provide for the rapid and inexpensive recognition of diplomas and qualifications. i support the proposals for the creation of a working group on interdisciplinary integration to address labour migration and labour market integration, with the participation of the directorates-general responsible for these areas and the european external action service. it is also necessary to establish a common eu coordination framework to help identify labour market needs and thus better manage labour migration. it is important to establish departure preparation offices in the countries of origin and host countries and to strengthen cooperation with third countries in the field of recurrent migration.
in writing. - i abstained in the vote on this proposal. integration is a continuous two-way process that requires the participation of non-eu nationals and the host society. while there are already many examples of good practice in the integration of migrants, asylum seekers and beneficiaries of international protection across the eu, mostly demonstrated by local authorities, there are still many problems to be solved and many questions to be answered.
in writing. - i voted no. the unemployment rate in the european union is around 10%, i.e. 23.8 million people, eu citizens, are currently out of work. unemployment rates, especially among young people, are particularly high in countries experiencing economic difficulties. this poses not only difficulties for economic growth but also social challenges. i therefore believe that the priority should not be so much to attract immigrants from third countries as to make every effort to reduce unemployment and to employ as many eu citizens as possible. we already know that in a few years, there will be a shortage of a certain type of specialist. the training of a skilled workforce that meets labour market needs could be achieved primarily by promoting close cooperation between business and training institutions.
in writing. − it is worth noting that the rapidly rising unemployment rate has already pushed many europeans to the brink of poverty. strict austerity policies prevent most countries from providing adequate basic health care and social security services to their citizens. the question therefore arises as to how they will provide such guarantees to third-country nationals. i believe that the problem of the demographic deficit in the union should be tackled, in particular, by strengthening the european social and financial environment. given the enormous unemployment in europe, it is unclear how and by what means immigrants could be integrated into the labour market. the focus should now be on rebuilding the eu's devastated labour market. only when the situation has stabilised can the integration of migrants be successful.
in writing. − today the european union is facing several challenges: demographic change, decline of the working-age population and a shortage of skilled workers. qualified migration can make a key contribution to facing these challenges successfully and can have a positive impact on the socio-economic development of the european union. in order to be successful, an integrated and differentiated approach to immigration is needed which aims to provide measures for the full integration of migrants in the receiving countries of the eu. this report provides a set of recommendations for the successful integration of migrants and calls for all possible steps to be taken to create a uniform, transparent system at eu level, including eu approaches to social security coordination for third-country nationals. i welcome this comprehensive report and consider that obstacles resulting from the institutional framework of receiving countries need to be removed. migrants represent a vulnerable high-risk group that faces discrimination and exclusion and is often affected by skills mismatch, low-wage jobs and unemployment. a well-managed and coherent migration policy can ensure migrants’ rights, protect them from discrimination and use their employment potential in order to ensure their full contribution to the economic development of the eu.
in writing. − i fully support this report because it is necessary to develop, implement and support a model for asbestos screening and registration to avoid asbestos-related diseases and other damage. this could be implemented by tightening the screening and registration of asbestos procedures and stepping up official inspections to ensure the effective and unhindered implementation of eu asbestos legislation, ensuring that civil engineers, architects and employees of registered asbestos removal companies are qualified and trained. moreover, the removal of asbestos-containing materials from buildings, especially in less economically developed member states and rural areas, places a financial burden on building owners, and this should therefore continue to receive active support at national and eu level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the possibilities of eliminating the health risks associated with asbestos. the world health organisation estimates that between 20 000 and 30 000 cases of substance-related diseases are reported annually in the eu alone, and that more than 300 000 deaths are expected in the eu by 2030. i support calls for the eu to develop and implement a model for asbestos control and registration. it is necessary to require owners of public and commercial buildings to check for the presence of asbestos-containing materials in their buildings, to draw up plans for the management of the risks posed by these materials and to ensure that this information is made available to staff. models for monitoring asbestos in the air and drinking water at workplaces, in residential areas and in landfills are also needed. it is important to establish the necessary requirements for the mandatory qualifications required to work with this substance, to develop action plans for its disposal and management and to include a harmonised strategy on asbestos in the future eu health and safety strategy 2014-2020. it is also important to oblige insurance institutions to adopt a common approach to the recognition of asbestos-related occupational diseases.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, according to the world health organisation (who), between 20 000 and 30 000 cases of asbestos-related diseases are reported annually in the eu alone and it is estimated that more than 300 000 people will die of mesothelioma in the eu by 2030. all types of asbestos are dangerous and their harmful effects are documented and regulated. asbestos causes diseases such as lung cancer and pleural mesothelioma, which develop when asbestos fibers are exposed to water or inhaled. the effects are recognised as hazardous to human health and may take several decades, sometimes more than 40 years, to become apparent. despite the ban on asbestos, it is still present in many ships, trains, bunkers, tunnels, galleries, public and private water supply systems and particularly in buildings, including many public and private buildings. furthermore, the current market surveillance measures are not able to ensure that asbestos is not imported into the european union market. the future european union strategy on health and safety for 2014-2020 should include a coherent strategy on asbestos and provide for effective measures to improve the collection and dissemination of technical, scientific and economic information and to help shape and implement national policies aimed at ensuring the safety and health of workers.
in writing. - i voted for this document. all types of asbestos are dangerous and their harmful effects are documented and regulated. the most harmful effects of inhaled asbestos fibres on health occur even decades after inhalation. it therefore calls for the development of eu models for the monitoring of asbestos in existing private and public buildings, including residential and non-residential buildings, land, infrastructure, logistics and pipelines. member states should establish public asbestos registers providing relevant information on the risks posed by asbestos to workers and employers planning renovation works, and complementing existing health and safety measures required under eu law.
in writing. - i support this resolution. asbestos is dangerous to humans and no safe level of asbestos has yet been established. the danger of asbestos to humans will only disappear when asbestos-containing substances are removed and replaced by harmless alternatives. i believe that asbestos removal programmes and prevention measures should be implemented at eu level. in particular, the mandatory checks for asbestos should apply. in addition, national long-term building renovation strategies should be aligned with asbestos removal strategies. more attention should be paid to initiatives aiming at replacing asbestos with solar panels.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because credit unions are voluntary groups of natural or legal persons whose purpose is to meet the needs of their members. they shall operate on the principles of voluntary and open membership and solidarity of members and shall be governed in accordance with democratic principles, thereby contributing to responsible and sustainable governance. in this context, it is necessary to coordinate strategies and measures to ensure a level playing field for credit unions, including a european statute giving them equal opportunities to organise and operate at european level and appropriate legal instruments to facilitate their cross-border and international activities. the statute should set out precise and clear conditions for the creation of a genuine and effective new category of european credit insurance companies and it is therefore essential to take into account the previous model of european body statutes, which, by giving member states a great deal of flexibility and without ensuring added value, failed to create the conditions for the successful use of this european instrument.
