in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a grant from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the egf shall support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in the world trade system. italy is to receive eur 3 689 474 to support the 1257 workers made redundant by itr service providers. there is a trend today for it service providers to move to third countries. financial assistance will be provided to finance a tailor-made package of services, including labour market integration measures, vocational training, technical courses for technicians, special courses for managers and engineers. it is also essential to adapt the training offered to the needs of the workforce and the business environment in the region.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because 1 257 workers were made redundant by the italian company agile s.r.l., which operates in the information and communication technologies (ict) sector. the economic and financial crisis had a more negative impact on the it sector than expected and the tightening of credit conditions had caused the company to face even greater difficulties, which led to its failure to find a suitable solution and to its bankruptcy in 2010. italy submitted an application to mobilise the egf, in respect of redundancies in the enterprise 'agile s.r.l.', on 30 december 2011 and supplemented it by additional information up to 2 october 2012. this application complies with the requirements for determining the amount of financial support as laid down in article 10 of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006. the commission therefore proposed to mobilise an amount of eur 3 689 474.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the link between the redundancies and the global financial and economic crisis is undeniable. the financial and economic crisis and its impact on the sector could not be foreseen. the impact of redundancies is particularly significant and requires an operational intervention mechanism. given the financial difficulties experienced by this italian company in the ict sector, it should be granted effective and operational support. this support will help redundant workers to reintegrate into the labour market. it will also be a show of solidarity with the people who have lost their jobs. the support provided will contribute to the promotion of long-term active labour market policies and contribute to the prevention of unemployment and early intervention in the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a grant from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the purpose of the egf is to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in the world trade system. the commission has decided to grant eur 3 941 999 to austria to support 320 workers made redundant by firms in the tobacco sector. financial assistance will be provided to finance a tailor-made package of services, including labour market integration measures, i.e. general education and vocational training for unskilled workers, vocational training for skilled workers, technical courses for technicians, special courses for managers and engineers. it is also essential to adapt the training offered to the needs of the workforce and the business environment in the region.
in writing. − i gave my consent to the proposal as austria had submitted an application egf/2011/010 at/austria tabak for financial support from the egf, following the redundancies of 320 workers in austria tabak gmbh and 14 suppliers and downstream companies in austria (of which 270 workers were foreseen for support under egf co-financed measures). redundancies due to the closure of the last production site of austria tabak in the hainburg brück leita area, following a decision by the company's owner japan tobacco international, resulting in a total of 320 redundancies. the commission therefore proposed to mobilise an amount of eur 3 941 999.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund should be mobilised to provide financial support to an austrian cigarette factory. it is worth noting that the egf plays a very important role in the reintegration of workers made redundant into the labour market. the support provided will help to avoid long-term unemployment in difficult labour market conditions and to successfully reintegrate people into the labour market. attention should be drawn to the need to establish a strict control mechanism to ensure that support is granted only to individual employees and not used for restructuring of firms or sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for an economic partnership agreement between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. the purpose of the proposal is to remove the country which has withdrawn from the list of regions or countries which have withdrawn from the negotiations. i agreed to the deal.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because a number of states had completed negotiations on agreements and could therefore be included in annex i to council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 of 20 december 2007 applying the arrangements for trade in products originating in certain states which are part of the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states provided for in agreements establishing or to be establishing economic partnership agreements. others have not taken the necessary steps to ratify their respective agreements. in accordance with article 2 (3) of regulation (ec) no 1528/2007, and in particular point (b) thereof, annex i to that regulation should therefore be amended by deleting those countries from that annex. in order to ensure that those countries can be readmitted as a matter of urgency to annex i to regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 after they have taken the necessary measures to ratify their respective agreements and before they enter into force, the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union should be delegated to the commission in respect of readmitting countries which have been deleted from annex i to regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 in accordance with this regulation. it is of particular importance that the commission carry out appropriate consultations during its preparatory work, including at expert level. in carrying out the preparatory work for and drafting delegated acts, the commission should ensure a simultaneous, timely and appropriate transmission of relevant documents to the european parliament and to the council.
in writing. - i agree with the position. the eu-acp economic partnership agreements are highly development-friendly. in particular, they help to remove existing barriers to trade and undoubtedly increase cooperation in all areas related to trade and development. in view of this, i consider it appropriate to empower the commission to adopt delegated acts in order to ensure that countries are removed from the list of countries and regions that have terminated negotiations in an expeditious manner. furthermore, the implementation of this mandate by the commission will allow for the re-inclusion of partners in annex i to that regulation as a matter of urgency. however, in order to improve economic and trade cooperation between the acp and the eu, it is essential that the commission, in carrying out the tasks assigned to it, not only reports to parliament on a more regular basis but also regularly consults at expert level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the eu emissions trading system is the most important tool for reducing industrial pollution in the eu in a cost-effective and efficient way. despite the fact that emissions have decreased since the introduction of the eu emissions trading system, there are currently significant inconsistencies in the system. the current economic crisis, combined with the large volume of external carbon credits linked to the clean development mechanism and the many regulatory provisions related to the transition to the third trading period (2013-2020), has resulted in a clear surplus of allowances. by the end of 2011, there was a surplus of 955 million allowances and this is expected to increase. as the surplus of allowances far exceeds demand, the price of carbon dioxide has fallen from eur 30 per tonne to eur 7 per tonne. this decline in the price of carbon is in contrast to the significant increase in sustainable scientific and technological innovation and is therefore a disincentive to invest in low-carbon technology and a growing risk of the european union becoming dependent on carbon-intensive infrastructure. the guidelines on certain state aid measures should therefore take account of these circumstances and criteria. in addition, the list of carbon leakage sectors should be revised to include energy-efficient sectors with relatively low carbon emissions.
in writing. - parliament has unfortunately demonstrated today that it is more influenced by the interests of the various interest groups than by the public interest. it has long been clear that the eu's emissions trading scheme cannot function as a stand-alone economic instrument operating in a free market. yes, the commission's proposal was not perfect and we need to start a wider debate on a fundamental reform of the atl system as soon as possible. the commission proposal, together with the parliament's proposals, would have created a kind of safe space for these discussions. unfortunately, without it, we are left with a largely ineffective eu climate change policy.
in writing. − in order to ensure the proper functioning of the market, the regulation adopted must be justified by an impact assessment which also improves the functioning of the market and ensures fair competition. the measures envisaged should be applied only in exceptional cases, in strict compliance with the rules laid down and without creating an additional burden for undertakings. in exceptional circumstances, the commission could change the auction schedule during the trading period. it is noted that the excess allowances not only reduce the price of carbon dioxide but also the investment in low-carbon technologies. i believe that a short-term structural measure should be applied to correct the market imbalance in the eu ets. timelines for the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances are an effective measure that does not adversely affect the stability of the trading system and does not distort markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the greenhouse gas emission allowance system. given that greenhouse gas emissions from aviation have increased by around 100% since 1990 and continue to increase, this issue needs to be addressed. the aviation greenhouse gas emissions trading system is too moderate, requiring other industries to reduce emissions by 21%, while aviation is only required to reduce emissions by 5%. however, we, the members of the european parliament, support the agreement reached with the council on the temporary (up to one year) exemption from the emissions allowance system for international flights to and from eu airports. intercontinental flights to and from the european union, involving airlines from both eu and non-eu countries, will be exempted from the emissions allowance system for one year. the objective of this agreement is a global agreement on emission reductions. i agree with the rapporteur that this decision can be seen not as a measure aimed at the application of european environmental standards at global level but as a measure aimed at identifying the most appropriate approaches to a common problem.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on a greenhouse gas emission allowance system. the proposal aims to temporarily exempt international flights from the emissions trading scheme, allowing the international civil aviation organisation (icao) to conclude negotiations on international co2 regulation. i support the proposals made to seek to agree in international negotiations market-based measures to ensure that the aviation sector is subject to the same pressure to reduce pollution as other sectors. since 1990, aviation greenhouse gas emissions have increased by about 100 per cent. it should be made clear that, in the absence of a satisfactory agreement, all international flights will be covered by the eu ets. it is also important to carry out a thorough analysis of the effects on competition between european and third-country airlines.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document. the aviation sector is distinguished by its international character and a global approach to tackling the rapidly increasing pollution from international aviation would be the most appropriate, as it is the most effective way to reduce aviation emissions. under the united nations framework convention on climate change, all countries are required to develop and implement national and, where appropriate, regional programmes that include measures to mitigate the effects of climate change. the union is committed to reducing its co2 emissions, including those from the aviation sector. while a one-year exemption for flights from or outside the eea is not a perfect solution, it does provide a better prospect of reaching a satisfactory international agreement this year than the possibility of continuing to apply existing legislation. i therefore believe that it is essential to accept this proposal and to remove the legal uncertainty surrounding the airlines' obligations and to send a clear signal to our international negotiating partners. they should understand that europe wants to reach an international agreement, is open to negotiating the best market-based measures, but does not intend to wait indefinitely for the aviation pollution issue to be addressed in the same way as other sectors.
in writing. − the inclusion of the aviation sector in the eu emissions trading scheme is a natural step towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the transport sector. this inclusion must be universal and cover the entire aviation sector. on the other hand, third parties are understandably concerned about the future negative impact on competition. while supporting today's decision to postpone the inclusion of third country airlines in the eu atl scheme, i call on both the eu and the rest of the world to adopt as soon as possible an international agreement to combat climate change in the aviation sector.
in writing. − greenhouse gas pollution from the aviation sector is a problem not only for the eu but also for the world. it is worth noting that the sector is experiencing rapid increases in greenhouse gas emissions, which require global cooperation. joint research projects and measures should be developed to mitigate the climate change impact of the aviation sector. i believe that more favourable market measures should be applied to emissions from international aviation. however, distortions of the market and competition must be avoided in all cases. it is also necessary to ensure that the regulation adopted does not have a negative impact on the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution and believe that today’s decision makes european banks more resilient, so that no more taxpayers’ money has to be used to prop them up. the new set of rules is the most comprehensive and far-reaching banking regulation in the history of the eu. an important part of the new rules is that for the first time, there will be a cap on bankers’ bonuses. bonuses may not be higher than salary. in exceptional cases only, bonuses may amount to a maximum of twice as much as the fixed salary. i believe that this rule will bring fairness and transparency into the banking sphere and contribute to a change in culture. parliament also supported new rules regarding tightened capital requirements for banks. from 1 january 2014 onwards, european banks have to put aside more and better capital to be prepared for possible crises. the new rule that banks have to publish, country by country, what their profit is, how much tax they pay, and how much they receive in subsidies is unprecedented. i strongly believe that this requirement will increase transparency and will help to avoid crises.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on prudential supervision of credit institutions. the proposal aims to impose stricter requirements on the 8 200 eu banks, which control 53% of global assets, in order to strengthen the resilience of the sector to crises. it is necessary to ensure that banks continue to finance economic activities in order to have more and better quality capital and to be able to cover losses incurred. i agree that bankers should not be allowed to receive a premium higher than their fixed annual salary, because they are the ones who, by following the huge bonuses, are risking big, but foreign money. the bank of greece has also provided a detailed description of the measures to be taken to address the specific problems of the banking sector in greece. such banks will have to increase their reserves by an additional 1 to 3%. i believe that these changes will allow the eu to be better prepared for possible crises and, if they occur, depositors and creditors will be able to withdraw their money immediately. i agree that from next year all eu banks should be accountable to the european commission be required to report on income, profit, loss, other operating results. it is essential that such data should already be made public from 2015.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the light of the economic and financial crisis, a rigorous assessment of the costs and benefits of internal liquidity in credit institutions is needed. it is also essential to encourage institutions to reduce the external costs arising from their financial difficulties or failure. it is appropriate to encourage credit institutions and relevant investment firms to hold, in addition to other own funds requirements, a capital protection buffer and a countercyclical capital buffer to ensure that credit institutions and investment firms accumulate sufficient capital base to cover losses in times of economic growth. it is also important to note that the smooth functioning of the internal banking market requires not only legal rules but also close and regular cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states and much closer convergence of regulatory and supervisory practices. in addition, recovery plans are an important tool to help resolve the problems of financial institutions effectively. in the event of a failure, they should help to reduce the negative impact on the real economy and avoid the need to use taxpayers' money. member states should encourage institutions and their groups to develop and implement resolution plans and to submit those plans for approval to resolution authorities with the full involvement and coordination of the european banking authority.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal because i believe that today there is a need for stricter capital requirements for banks and for limiting bankers' bonuses and for stronger supervision of banks. the adoption of rules aimed at tightening capital requirements for banks, facilitating lending to small businesses and limiting bankers' bonuses is necessary. we must seek to protect the interests of depositors and investors in institutions and ensure the stability of the financial system. i believe that prudential supervision of institutions and the protection of customers of credit institutions should be strengthened, and that auditors should be required to inform the competent authorities immediately whenever, in the course of their duties, they become aware of certain facts which may have a significant impact on the financial situation of an institution or on its administrative or accounting systems.
in writing. − i believe that the same rules should apply throughout the eu as regards the access to the activities of credit institutions and investment firms, as well as the same management methods and supervisory frameworks and risk mitigation rules. it should be noted that in order to halt the fragmentation of financial markets and ensure the effective functioning of the internal market, legal rules alone are not sufficient, and close and regular cooperation between the authorities of the member states is required in this respect. on the other hand, the regulation imposed should not create a disproportionate burden for credit institutions. the supervisory mechanism envisaged must ensure the stability of the financial system and protect the interests of depositors, investors and consumers. it is essential to encourage institutions to reduce external costs and to have a sound remuneration policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on risk mitigation requirements for credit institutions and investment firms. the proposal aims to impose stricter requirements on the 8 200 eu banks, which control 53% of global assets, in order to strengthen the sector's resilience to crises, ensure that banks continue to finance economic activities, have more and better quality capital and be able to cover losses. i agree that bankers should not be allowed to receive a premium higher than their fixed annual salary, because they are the ones who, by following the huge bonuses, are risking big, but foreign money. the bank of greece has also provided a detailed description of the measures to be taken to address the specific problems of the banking sector in greece. such banks will have to increase their reserves by an additional 1 to 3%. i believe that these changes will allow the eu to be better prepared for possible crises and, if they occur, depositors and creditors will be able to withdraw their money immediately. i agree that from next year all eu banks should be accountable to the european commission be required to report on income, profit, loss, other operating results. it is essential that such data should already be made public from 2015.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in order to eliminate the remaining barriers to trade and the significant distortions of competition caused by differences in national laws, and to prevent any possible obstacles to trade, it is necessary to adopt a regulation laying down uniform rules applicable in all member states. risk mitigation requirements applicable to credit institutions and investment firms should be set out, relating only to the functioning of banking and financial services markets and designed to ensure the financial stability of operators operating in those markets and a high level of investor and deposit protection. in addition, credit institutions and investment firms should be required to establish robust credit-granting criteria and procedures for credit-granting decisions. external credit ratings may be used as one of the criteria in this process, but should not be relied on exclusively or mechanically and should not be decisive. it is also important that a member state should be allowed to adopt more stringent national regulatory measures that it considers necessary to safeguard the financial stability of the country, provided that internal market principles and agreed minimum standards are respected.
in writing. − i supported this proposal because of the need to take consistent action to increase transparency, accountability and regulation by improving the quantitative and qualitative capital ratios of the banking system in order to ensure economic growth. it is necessary to introduce an additional non-risk-based measure to limit the growth of leverage in the banking system and to create a stronger system of liquidity buffers. the prudential requirements applicable to credit institutions and investment firms are, in my view, limited to the functioning of the banking and financial services markets and are designed to ensure the financial stability of operators operating in those markets and a high level of investor and deposit protection. all credit institutions and investment firms should follow the same rules in order to increase confidence in the stability of credit institutions and investment firms, in particular in the event of adverse circumstances.
in writing. −improving the transparency, accountability and regulation of the banking system and removing obstacles to the smooth functioning of the internal market. risk-management requirements will help to make banks stronger and more accountable in europe. we must not allow the mistakes of the past to be repeated. i believe that a common set of rules should be applied throughout the eu and a stronger system of liquidity reserves should be established. the banking sector should have more and better quality capital. this is a crucial step towards a new approach to risk. the risk mitigation requirements provided for must ensure not only the financial stability of the operators but also a high level of protection for investors and depositors.
in writing. − i am pleased that the european parliament has endorsed the proposed package of reforms for financial institutions. i voted for this report because i agree that banks have been playing risky games with people's deposits for too long. the financial sector has long operated in a kind of savage capitalism, with no poverty, taking all the profits but shifting the burden of losses to taxpayers in the event of a crisis. i agree that all credit institutions should maintain their capital reserves. banks cannot play billions of virtual euros when only a few hundredths of a percent of them are backed by real assets. i also strongly support the report's limitation of bankers' bonuses. from next year, the bonus cannot exceed the annual salary. and only in exceptional cases, after approval by the general meeting, can the premium be up to two salaries. i would suggest that the european union could follow the swiss example and limit bonuses not only to bankers but also to the managerial staff of other companies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the application of higher standards to groundhandling at airports. i fully agree with the rapporteur's proposal that the possibility of more than two companies providing ground services at the largest eu airports should be allowed. this is how competition is maintained. we also propose that ground handling companies operating at eu airports serving more than 5 million passengers per year set minimum service quality standards. this will improve the quality of the services provided. for example, there will be a maximum time for re-checking baggage, a maximum time between the first and last check-out, a minimum number of staff providing information at the boarding gate, and so on. the safety of airport workers also needs to be given greater attention.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because ground services are a highly competitive and capital-intensive business (with a turnover of around eur 50 billion in ground services worldwide) with high fixed costs for staff and equipment. there are eleven categories of ground services: 1) administrative and maintenance services at the airport; (2) the provision of passenger services; (3) the handling of baggage; (4) handling of freight and mail; (5) services provided at the aircraft parking area; (6) services to aircraft; 7) services related to fuels and lubricants; 8) maintenance of aircraft; 9) flight services and crew administration; 10) ground transport services; 11) food and drink. currently, market access is restricted for the services listed in categories 3, 4, 5 and 7. since the opening of the market for ground services, airlines have been able to achieve steady reductions in charges for these services, but this market must be opened in a sustainable manner. it is important to note that full liberalisation could lead to significant volatility as more and more service providers would be forced out of business. in the long term, full liberalisation would create an oligopoly of the few remaining companies providing groundhandling services. such an oligopoly would be contrary to the interests of airlines, employees and passengers and would have a negative impact on competitiveness, growth and job creation.
in writing. − i voted against because the eu's ground services market must be opened in a harmonised way, full liberalisation could lead to high volatility and more service providers would be forced out of business. the ground handling companies are the backbone of air transport and the resulting instability of the ground handling market would lead to a continuous disruption of european airports and a massive redundancy. however, in the long term, full liberalisation would create a pan-european oligopoly of the few remaining terrestrial operators. such an oligopoly would be contrary to the interests of airlines, employees and passengers and would have a negative impact on competitiveness, growth and job creation. if other service providers were allowed to be included, the increased burden of prices would be passed directly to the employees by reducing staff costs. the last relaxation of the provisions has shown the need to prevent such burden shifting. the wage decline in the ground handling sector cannot be allowed to continue and more permanent jobs must be replaced by temporary contracts. ground service personnel shall be responsible for flight safety, technical flight safety and counter-terrorism. the transfer of social burdens to workers and the forced labour in poor conditions are contrary to the right of the population to be protected. wage dumping will not improve quality. this threatens existing standards, smooth operation and employee motivation.
in writing. − it is natural that, with the rise in customer service standards in the private sector in the european union and in third countries, and in aviation that is partly being taken over by the public sector, provisions establishing minimum standards for passenger service have been necessary. i therefore support this document and hope that it will contribute to faster and more comfortable air travel.
in writing. − it is worth noting that efficient ground services increase airport capacity and improve airport use. moreover, the sector plays an important role in creating new jobs, especially at regional level. it is therefore necessary to protect the ground services sector from harmful liberalisation and to ensure that the operations carried out are safe and reliable. the measures envisaged must not only benefit eu consumers but also the eu economy as a whole. improve the quality and competitiveness of ground services and ensure their efficiency. i am in favour of collective agreements in this sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on technical and control measures in the skagerrak strait, norway. objective of the proposal a discard ban in the skagerrak. in order to win the support of european union citizens for the reform of the common fisheries policy, it is necessary to change the arrangements for the discarding of large quantities of food-producing fish. i agree with the proposals made for the establishment of technical and control measures, the list of species subject to the landing obligation and the timetable for their progressive implementation. i agree with the landing obligation and the other rules listed necessary for the control and verification of compliance with this obligation, which are necessary to enhance the protection of marine biological resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important at this time to improve the control and enforcement of fishing in the skagerrak strait and to identify ways of harmonising the eu and norwegian regulations on technical and control measures in the area four nautical miles from the baselines. since 1986, fishing in the skagerrak strait has been regulated by an international agreement, but norway has denounced the agreement. the termination took effect on 1 november 2012 and a new limited agreement was negotiated. the main objective of the proposal is to introduce a discard ban in the skagerrak. to achieve this objective, flag member states should develop and operate a remote electronic monitoring (rem) system for vessels fishing in the skagerrak and all vessels of 12 metres' length overall or more should be required to install a cte. such equipment should be used primarily on a voluntary basis. the obligation would only apply to vessels which have been found to have failed to comply with the new rules on several occasions. in such a case, national authorities should be able to require shipowners to install a cte system or to remain in port.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal because it aims to introduce a ban on discarding fish in the skagerrak. the current regime based on the common fisheries policy, which in some cases releases relatively large quantities of all caught fish back into the sea, is perhaps the most difficult for the general public to understand and support. throwing the best fish overboard in this age of global food security is considered unthinkable.
in writing. - i agree with this report. the new regulation will help to harmonise the eu and norwegian regulations on technical and control measures and will improve the control of fishing in the skagerrak strait, taking into account the special regime applicable to this strait. i think it is appropriate to introduce a ban on discarding fish in this strait as far as possible. the first consideration in setting such a prohibition is whether the catch may be discarded. it is essential to ensure that the burden of control measures is proportionate to the controls that are necessary. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to amend this regulation by supplementing it with new technical specifications. a more flexible approach should therefore be applied to vessels that fish only sporadically in the skagerrak.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive on the consequences of the implementation of directive 2004/113/ec in the member states and on the identification of the main shortcomings and possible solutions to overcome them. the purpose of the directive is to implement the principle of equal treatment between men and women in access to goods and services in the european union. i support the proposals put forward to increase transparency in the commission's infringement procedures and actions, to create a public database of legislation and case law on gender-based discrimination, and to improve monitoring of the work of national gender equality bodies. it is necessary to provide financial support for training for lawyers working in the field of gender discrimination and to coordinate such training at eu level and to develop information campaigns for eu citizens on their rights. it is important to encourage member states to transpose the directive into national law within the time limits set and to focus their legislative work on ensuring legal certainty and clarity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to address the current gender issues at european union level, not only in employment but also in other areas. in addition, the implementation by member states of the council directive on the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services should be assessed. it is also essential to assess progress in this area and to identify legal gaps. i would therefore urge the european commission to monitor closely any cases of discrimination and breaches of the principle of equal treatment between women and men, particularly in relation to pregnant and breastfeeding mothers, single mothers who have difficulties in obtaining medical goods and services or who have difficulties in obtaining loans for an apartment or business credit. this council directive, which implements equal treatment for women and men, was adopted almost a decade ago, but there are still a number of problems relating to discrimination on grounds of sex in the access to and supply of goods and services. member states should pay greater attention to discrimination on grounds of sex and transpose the provisions of this directive into their national law as soon as possible in order to avoid legal loopholes.
in writing. − i supported the proposal because it is necessary to ensure that both women and men can take full responsibility for the directive and use it as an effective tool to protect their rights to equal access to all goods and services. both direct and indirect discrimination on grounds of sex in access to goods and services available to the public and in the supply of goods and services in the public and private sectors must be prohibited. it also prohibits discrimination against women on the grounds of pregnancy and motherhood, harassment and sexual harassment, and discrimination in the offering or supply of goods or services.
in writing. − the principle of equal treatment between women and men in access to and supply of goods and services must be guaranteed. i support the call to take this principle into account in particular in those states which have not yet transposed the directive implementing the equal treatment of women and men in the access to goods and services into national law. i believe that joint efforts to ensure equal treatment between men and women in the member states and the work of the bodies set up by the commission to work in this field can help to reduce discriminatory practices.
in writing. −discrimination and unjustified price increases must be prevented. goods and services must be available to consumers on equal terms. the principle of equal pricing for both sexes must be applied in both the private and public sectors. it should be noted that gender equality is one of the fundamental rights of the european union. in particular, it is necessary to establish a common approach in the insurance market to the rights of women and men in the use of life insurance services. the gender of the insured person should not be one of the main factors in assessing the level of risk of individuals. it is also essential to make infringement procedures more transparent and effective.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the commission and the eu member states should do more to combat all forms of discrimination. i regret that the commission has not yet presented a report on the implementation of council directive 2004/113/ec. the report should describe how eu member states have transposed the provisions of the directive into national law, what measures they are taking to eliminate still occurring cases of gender discrimination. it may be noted that there is already a fair amount of public discussion about discrimination in employment or measures to combat gender pay gaps. however, discrimination also occurs in other areas of life in the taking of loans or in the acquisition of other goods or services. i congratulate you on the closure of the test-achats case, which outlawed sex discrimination in the insurance industry. i would encourage the commission to monitor more closely the situation in the eu countries where discrimination still exists in the areas mentioned above and to propose measures to change it.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on promoting development through trade. i agree with the rapporteurs that in order to have a significant impact on the development of poor countries, it is important to apply trade policy instruments properly. to achieve development objectives more effectively, eu trade policy must focus not only on national economies but also on the situation and level of development of local and regional authorities, and promote smarter and more profitable production accordingly. i believe that good governance and effective fight against corruption are crucial to the country's ability to develop trade and reap the benefits it provides. as we know, widespread corruption hinders the development of society at all levels. we, the members of the european parliament, therefore call on the european union to promote transparent governance in its trade policy. the eu cannot ignore corrupt systems and i believe that the eu should insist on transparency and the use of appropriate methods before it starts to cooperate. however, it should be noted that real change in a country, both in terms of social and economic development, must be carried out on the initiative and goodwill of the country itself.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on promoting development in developing countries through trade. the proposal aims to increase the trading capacity of developing countries. i agree that the european union's trade policy must be more geared to promoting the diversification of the economies of developing countries, encouraging them to pursue smarter and more profitable production. i agree that protectionist measures must be prevented, both by the eu and by the member states. the eu must promote good governance in the implementation of its trade policy and should require transparency before cooperation is undertaken. i support the proposals made to encourage the development of small and mediumsized enterprises in these countries by providing targeted aid. adequate wages, decent and healthy working conditions and the possibility of forming trade unions should be the unconditional requirements to which european businesses in developing countries should comply
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because trade is one of the most important policy areas in ensuring the coherence of european union policies for development. if properly implemented, trade policy measures can have a significant impact on the development of poor countries. to help achieve development goals more effectively, eu trade policy must be geared towards positive spill-over effects on local, regional and national economies, promoting the diversification of developing countries' economies, and encouraging smarter and more profitable production. in this context, trade support should be diversified and focused on those countries that need it most, in particular the least developed countries and low-income countries. new issues related to support for development through trade, such as differentiation of development levels, support for local production, and the promotion of social and environmental standards, need to be taken more into account. furthermore, european support for development through trade must cover all aspects of innovation - financial innovation, as well as technological and organisational innovation - based on best practice. developing countries should also be encouraged to make sustainable economic development a goal that forms part of the overall set of policies, strategies and actions taken at national level to diversify their economies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because this important trade instrument is designed to enable developing countries to participate more actively in international trade and to obtain additional export revenues and to support income growth and the implementation of their own sustainable development and poverty reduction policies. trade is one of the most important policy areas for ensuring eu policy coherence for development. if properly implemented, trade policy measures can have a significant impact on the development of poor countries. the main objective of eu trade policy towards developing countries must be to exploit and improve the results achieved by eu aid policy. promoting global development through non-aid measures. to help achieve development goals more effectively, eu trade policy must be geared towards positive spill-over effects on local, regional and national economies, promoting the diversification of developing countries' economies, and encouraging smarter and more profitable production.
in writing. − only by working together can we ensure policy coherence for the development of poor countries. in particular, there is a need to make effective use of the instruments for supporting development through trade and investment. particular attention should be paid to foreign direct investment, by creating a transparent, investment-friendly environment. this will promote competition, reduce red tape and implement sound macroeconomic policies, and enable developing countries to become full participants in the global economy and reap the benefits of globalisation. trade between the eu and developing countries should be based on the octs, high social and environmental standards. in addition, existing trade barriers and trade-distorting subsidies should be removed. provisions relating to corporate social responsibility should become a mandatory part of any agreement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on promoting development in developing countries through trade. the proposal aims to increase the trading capacity of developing countries. the european union's trade policy must be more geared to promoting the diversification of the economies of developing countries, encouraging them to pursue smarter and more profitable production. the eu must promote good governance in the implementation of its trade policy and should require transparency before cooperation is undertaken. i support the proposals made to encourage the development of small and mediumsized enterprises in these countries by providing targeted aid. adequate wages, decent and healthy working conditions and the possibility of forming trade unions should be the unconditional requirements to which european businesses in developing countries should comply. it is also important to increase the use of european union instruments to promote foreign direct investment and to combine eu subsidies with loans or venture capital. it is necessary to help developing countries to improve their domestic business environment and to meet international standards of quality, labour and environmental protection.
in writing. − i voted for this report because trade and investment between the eu, developing countries and least developed countries is a tool to promote sustainable and inclusive growth for all countries, facilitating the transfer of technologies and skills and helping to create jobs. it can also provide opportunities to increase competitiveness and productivity, to achieve greater social cohesion and to combat inequalities. the main challenges for investment policy in developing countries are twofold: at national level, investment policy must be integrated into a development strategy that includes the sdgs; and at international level, there is a need to strengthen the provisions of international investment treaties (iits) relating to development and to ensure a balance between the rights and obligations of states and investors. in this context, it is necessary to improve the cis in order to give greater emphasis to the development dimension, to achieve a balance between the rights and obligations of states and investors, to ensure sufficient political space for sustainable development policy and to make the provisions on investment promotion more specific and aligned with the objectives of sustainable development. it is important to emphasise that foreign direct investment does not in itself have a positive impact on development, and this requires appropriate regulation covering policy areas outside investment policy, such as trade, taxation, intellectual property, competition, labour market regulation, environmental policy and access to land, etc.

in writing. − the economic crisis has forced the european union and the eu member states to rethink their economic policy priorities. no country has been able to do so without significant cost cuts. in many cases, this has also affected aid to developing countries. if the eu still wants to maintain its role as a major global donor, it must adopt other, new, forms of financial partnership. it is equally important to review priorities and to improve the management of available funds on a priority basis. i voted in favour of this report because it sought to find a way out of the situation. the european parliament encourages beneficiaries to formulate national needs and to integrate strategic development plans into their policies. the document contains specific proposals. they should take technical assistance on a partnership basis. for example, the eu's strong influence in the wto (world trade organisation) may be aimed at integrating developing countries into the organisation. this would allow these countries to participate fully in world trade. it is also important to keep in mind the regional level, to promote institutional contacts and to reduce trade barriers.

thank you, chairman. i would also like to thank the rapporteur for the document he has produced, and i believe that a review of the current regulation is necessary and timely. non-euro area member states also need to have greater guarantees of receiving assistance when the economic situation so requires. but when it comes to the banking sector and its recapitalisation, we need to be consistent and open. the direct role of banks in the ongoing economic and financial crisis is already widely recognised and all financial assistance documents must therefore clearly provide for increased liability of commercial bank managers and shareholders and a greater and much more responsible role for the european central bank. in the current draft document, member states will also have to provide for an adjustment of macroeconomic indicators to address the issue of failing banks. this means that the member states or their taxpayers will again have to cover those losses. i therefore hope that the new commission proposal will take a broad assessment and provide for greater responsibility for the banking sector.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the light of the initial conclusions of the joint bureau and committee on budgets working party on the budgetary questions of the european parliament, structural and organisational reforms should be implemented with the aim of improving the efficiency of the parliament without compromising the quality of legislation and working conditions. the aim is to find ways of saving even more and using funds even more efficiently. reductions are proposed (compared to the 2013 budget) in the area of translation (-56%) and interpretation (-23%), as well as in the area of rental charges (-60%), the online tv channel web tv (-38%) and the provision of premises (-31%). it is important to note that the principle of multilingualism cannot be jeopardised by the savings in translation and interpretation services, as equal access to linguistic services must be guaranteed for members of the european parliament. in addition, appropriate working conditions should be maintained in the services providing these services. the provision of independent scientific advice and the capacity to improve the european parliament's performance as an institution vested with legislative and democratic control powers should also be improved. more efforts should be made to implement further changes, to save money and to implement structural reforms, and to align budget increases more closely with inflation.

in writing. − i think it is appropriate to increase the funds in 2014 as this increase is linked to specific legal obligations. however, we must continue to make efforts to use resources rationally and economically, and to carry out structural and organisational reforms. attention should be paid to ensuring that efforts to achieve greater efficiency do not create obstacles to quality working conditions and the implementation of the legislative process. the measures envisaged shall not be implemented in a hurry. in order to make more efficient use of the funds, the issue of the one-seat parliament should be resolved as soon as possible. in this time of economic crisis, we cannot afford to have money wasted unnecessarily. this is too costly a burden for all of europe. it is also essential to resolve the issue of the european house of history project. i think that this project should at least be stopped, we cannot allow millions of euros to be spent on unfounded ambitions
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for financial assistance to member states whose currency is not the euro. i believe that a review of the existing regulation is necessary and timely, but i have some doubts about its effectiveness. non-euro area member states also need to have greater guarantees to receive assistance when the economic situation so requires. but when it comes to the banking sector and its recapitalisation, we have to be very consistent and very careful. the direct role of banks in the ongoing economic and financial crisis is already widely recognised and therefore the liability of commercial bank managers and shareholders, and the increased and much more responsible role of the ecb in the oversight of eu banking policy, must be clearly identified in all financial assistance related documents. we would expect the commission to come up with proposals to ensure that the activities of failed and dysfunctional commercial banks are not compensated by eu-guaranteed loans, which would then have to be covered by the same eu taxpayers. if this is not done, the eu will have to borrow money to deal with the consequences, and i therefore very much hope that the new commission proposal will fundamentally assess and review the responsibility of the banking sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the global economic and financial crisis has had a profound impact on all member states, increasing national budget deficits, worsening the balance of payments and increasing the general debt. the balance of payments facility is welcomed as a means of harmonising conditions between euro-area and non-euro-area member states. this would aim to simplify financial support procedures in the euro area and outside the euro area. this agreement, inter alia, significantly increases the transparency and accountability of the procedures for requesting and awarding financial assistance by member states in difficulty. policy makers are currently laying the foundations for the future banking union. the latter consists of three main components: the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), the single resolution mechanism and the deposit guarantee scheme. the council, parliament and the commission have just concluded negotiations on the first pillar of the structure, which provides for a single supervisory authority for the euro area member states under the european central bank. the mechanism is also open to non-euro area member states that would like joint supervision.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because this balance of payments proposal aims to simplify financial support procedures in the euro area and outside the euro area. the balance of payments proposal does not provide for the possibility for member states whose currency is not the euro to have recourse to financial instruments that are fully equivalent to those under the european stability mechanism (esm). the update would help to ensure a level playing field between euro-area and non-euro-area member states and simplify the procedure for triggering the application of the balance of payments facility. in order to ensure a genuine level playing field between euro-area and non-euro-area member states, a trend towards the use of bank recapitalisation by non-euro-area member states should be maintained.
in writing. − i support this report, which focuses on the important issue of balance of payments, with the aim of simplifying financial support procedures in euro area and non-euro area countries. balance of payments financial assistance is important in helping member states to improve their administrative capacity. as the european financial stabilisation mechanism is abandoned and the balance of payments is switched to the euro, the aid balance between current and future regulation is important for non-euro area countries. in addition, in order to ensure a level playing field between euro-area and non-euro-area member states, it is necessary to ensure that non-euro-area member states have access to bank recapitalisation.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. this is the first major step forward in the process of harmonising conditions and simplifying the financial assistance procedure in the euro area and outside the euro area. in view of the consequences of the financial and economic crisis, i believe that it is appropriate to allow non-euro area countries to participate in the single supervisory mechanism. this will give these countries the same rights and obligations as euro area countries. it should be noted that the balance of payments facility will contribute to a more efficient use of union funds, as well as to reducing the deficit of national budgets, the general debt and the balance of payments.
in writing. − the crisis has prompted the european union to embark on economic reforms. they are mainly targeted at euro area countries. however, it is important to keep the unity of the eu in mind when implementing reforms, otherwise the integrity of the internal market will be compromised. i was in favour of this regulation because it aims to ensure a level playing field for all eu countries. the crisis has not just affected the euro area. comparing the euro area countries with a stability mechanism (eur 500 billion) with the amount of aid available to non-euro area countries (eur 50 billion) shows that the latter have very limited access to assistance. the new regulation will not only ensure the functioning of the stability mechanism. it will also provide for more favourable credit standards and better borrowing conditions for both euro and non-euro area countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the continuing severe economic downturn in a number of euro area member states is having a negative impact on the economies and budgets of a growing number of euro area members. the economic crisis has led to huge cash flows in certain countries, which have increased the difficulties in financing the economies of those countries and have made them unstable in the short and even longer term. this imbalance has a major distortive effect, with costly negative externalities, and poses challenges to the stability of the euro area and all its economies. the imbalances can only be reduced by fully implementing the broader euro area crisis solutions in order to develop a harmonised approach that helps to reconcile solidarity and responsibility. the european central bank should implement a single supervisory mechanism in the eu as soon as possible to enhance the soundness of the euro area banking system. the bank should make every effort to contribute to the stabilisation of markets, in particular through the securities markets programme, the longer-term refinancing operations and the open money operations, and to identify and develop structural solutions to the crisis as soon as possible. in the long term, these actions need to be underpinned by a more unified banking system and the integration of finance and policy to the point of eventually establishing a common deposit insurance and partial debt-sharing system.
in writing. − i supported the proposal because the european central bank (ecb) needs to do more to ensure that the low-cost loans it provides to banks reach the real economy. i also believe that the ecb should be made more transparent. over the past two years, the ecb has stepped up its activities in financial markets to help ease interest rate pressures on debt-ridden euro area countries. in addition, the ecb, together with the european commission and the international monetary fund (the so-called 'creditors' network'), monitors how countries implement the conditions for financial assistance. the ecb and the european commission should be more accountable to european and national parliaments.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the impact of the economic and social crisis should be a primary consideration in assessing the actions of the european central bank. however, the dialogue on the future of european monetary union should be a key factor. the ecb must do more to maintain price stability and prevent excessive inflation. moreover, the ecb must take bold and decisive action not only within the euro area but also beyond it. i think that using non-standard measures to restore the monetary policy transmission mechanism is quite risky. this may increase volatility and create favourable conditions for asset bubbles in financial markets.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the annual value of the cheques market in the european union is more than eur 52 billion. almost 70% of the cheques market is made up of prepaid telecommunications, with a smaller share of gift and discount cheques. differences in national vat rules for cheques have a negative impact on the market. instead of actually being able to benefit from the benefits of the single market, companies face double taxation problems and difficulties in expanding their business outside the country. the eu rules applicable to the vat arrangements for the taxation of cheques should therefore be harmonised, as such harmonisation could have a positive impact on businesses. in addition, it would be possible to avoid double taxation and avoid uncertainties regarding the tax compliance obligations. it would also remove the loopholes which could be exploited by certain companies to avoid paying taxes, due to the discrepancies between member states. a distinction should be made between prepaid telecommunications credits (i.e. cheques) and mobile payment services, which are charged differently. it is necessary to ensure that confusion does not arise as payment technologies change, in particular with the rise of mobile payments.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance. the purpose of this proposal is to ensure the effective recovery of such benefits at international level. the early entry into force of the convention in the european union is important in order to strengthen the protection of children. i support the rapporteur's proposal to make the necessary amendments to the convention decision as soon as possible, which would bring the convention into force.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance is an important instrument for citizens, as it provides a mechanism by which child support obligations can be imposed on a debtor residing in a third country and required to be enforced. the european parliament has already approved this convention, which was signed on behalf of the european union on 6 april 2011. however, the deposit of an instrument of approval is necessary for the application of this convention to the european union. as is customary in the case of such international conventions, the deposit of the instrument of approval must include information on the national central authorities and any doubts that might be raised by certain articles of the convention. after consultation with the member states, certain amendments are now necessary in order to allow the deposit of the instrument of approval. in particular, the amendments relate to the situation in cyprus, latvia, luxembourg and portugal. however, these amendments need to be approved as soon as possible in order to enable the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance to enter into force as soon as possible with regard to the european union.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal because the hague convention of 23 november 2007 on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance is an important instrument for citizens, as it provides a mechanism by which child support obligations can be imposed on a debtor residing in a third country and required to be enforced. the convention has already been approved by parliament and signed on behalf of the european union on 6 april 2011. however, the deposit of the instrument of approval is necessary for the application of the convention to the european union. as is customary in the case of such international conventions, the deposit of the instrument of approval must include information on the national central authorities and any doubts that might be raised by certain articles of the convention. after consultation with the member states, it is now necessary to make certain amendments to the decision on the approval of annexes ii and iii to the convention in order to allow the deposit of the instrument of approval. in particular, the amendments relate to the situation in cyprus, latvia, luxembourg and portugal. i agree with the view that it is necessary to adopt these amendments urgently in order to enable the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance to enter into force as soon as possible with regard to the european union.
in writing. - i support the commission's proposal to amend the council decision. given the importance of the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance, it is necessary to accelerate its entry into force in the eu. this will simplify the procedure for recovery of maintenance not only within the eu but also outside it. it will be possible to recover maintenance faster and more easily not only from persons living in the european union but also from persons living in other countries. this will prevent abuse and will ensure that parents are properly responsible for the material support of their minor children.
in writing. − the hague convention on the international recovery of child support and other forms of family maintenance of 23 november 2007 should be seen first and foremost as a measure to protect children by ensuring the conditions of living necessary for the child's development. even though it is their primary responsibility under the law, many people try to avoid paying family maintenance by moving to another country. the convention specifically concerns the situations when recovery of maintenance for the child from responsible persons has to be secured, where such persons live in a state different from that of the child. in 2010 the ep took an appropriate measure and approved the council decision on the conclusion of the hague convention on behalf of the eu. unfortunately, due to the procedural aspect the convention is still not in force for the european union. i voted in favour of this report, since i believe the changes to the text of the council decision have to be approved as soon as possible for the convention to be enforced in the member states, so that the eu citizens could benefit from the international mechanism of the child support and other family maintenance recovery.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on ship recycling. under the eu waste shipping regulation, exports of hazardous waste from the eu to countries outside the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) have been prohibited since 1998. any ship carrying various hazardous materials and which is towed out of the eu for dismantling is itself a dangerous vessel. the ships can therefore only be legally dismantled in oecd countries. however, experience shows that very often this legal provision is violated and ships are dismantled outside the oecd, for example in pakistan, india, etc. such non-compliance has negative effects both on the environment and on human health. we in the european parliament are in favour of stricter controls on the export of ships for dismantling. i agree with the rapporteur that a mechanism for the financing of safe ship recycling should be established and that scrapping plans should be drawn up for all ships over 20 years old. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because there is currently fierce and unfair competition between recyclers in the main recycling countries (bangladesh, india and pakistan) and their higher technical standards competitors (eu, turkey and china) and because the current legislation does not take into account the characteristics of ships and it is difficult to determine when ships become waste, which could avoid the legal obligation to deregister ships. during a flood, ships are lowered as close to shore as possible and are usually moored on a muddy shelf near the shore, which the sea floods. they are cut vertically into very large pieces using only a casting lamp and the heavy cut pieces of the ship just fall on the muddy slope. this poses a significant both immediate and chronic risk to workers, there is no proper storage of hazardous substances and some hazardous substances that are removed separately are not handled properly. most shipowners try to make the most profit by selling their vessels to places where there are no labour and environmental standards and therefore they can offer the highest price. in this context, measures must be taken to substantially reduce the negative impact of the recycling of eu-flagged vessels, in particular in south asia, by avoiding unnecessary economic burden.
in writing. − the proper recycling of waste, whatever its form and size, is essential to ensure a high level of environmental protection. i therefore support the measures set out in this document, which are intended to provide both incentives and penalties to ship owners to behave responsibly with ships that are no longer fit for navigation.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution. it is essential to ensure that no additional economic burden is created in order to reduce the negative impact of ship recycling. the dismantling of ships under conditions harmful to man and the environment must be prohibited. in order to contribute adequately to waste prevention, the use of hazardous materials on board ships should be limited and safer and greener ship recycling operations should be promoted. in addition, the use of recycled materials in ships and other products should be steadily increased in order to develop the market for recycled materials. it should be noted that the measures envisaged will only achieve their objective if an incentive-based system is in place across the eu to encourage safe and sound ship recycling.
