and the rapporteur ivo belet and the draftsman of the opinion of the legal affairs committee, eva lichtenberger, for the good cooperation. i believe that the agreement on the first reading agreed by mr belet is an acceptable compromise between the commission's initial proposal, the position of the eu member states and the ambitions of parliament. as rapporteur for envi, i wanted to pay even more attention to the environment. however, in the trilogue i saw that the rapporteur was determined to defend parliament's position and in most cases succeeded. this means that offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production will be safer and disaster risk will be reduced. i am sure that the european union will support such a move. the text of the position reflects most of the proposals of the committee on the environment and the socialist and democratic group. in the tripartite negotiations, parliament achieved the maximum degree of independence between the member states' authorities responsible for the safety of offshore oil and gas production and those responsible for the economic development of natural resources. member states will only be able to grant licences for offshore extraction activities after an early and transparent public consultation and an environmental impact assessment. the financial capacity of applicants to cover possible environmental and economic losses in the event of accidents will be taken into account, if provided for by national law. strengthen the mandate of the european maritime safety agency. it will have more powers to monitor oil spills from offshore platforms and help member states respond in the event of a disaster. complaints about safety and environmental breaches in extraction will be dealt with without prejudice to the anonymity of the reporting persons. this is all really important. for the arctic. the council did not agree with envi's recommendation that member states refrain from exploration and exploitation activities in the arctic. as rapporteur for the committee on the environment, i had to come down because the member states of the european union maintain sovereignty in the exploitation of natural resources on their territory. moreover, no eu country has a maritime border that reaches the arctic ocean. however, i would call on the countries of the european union to pursue the highest possible environmental standards, both through the arctic council and through the united nations structures.
the extent of tax evasion by european states today is sufficiently high to suggest that the underlying problem is not the efforts of businesses or individuals to conceal these taxes. it seems that the problem is deeper. perhaps the tax burden has reached an inadequate level? perhaps those taxes are too high, and their tariffs too high? and most importantly, the use of the money collected is inefficient. so i would suggest: 1. try to make paying taxes worthwhile. some should be reduced, others should be abolished, and others should be applied only under certain conditions. 2.taxation must be fair not only must it be fairly redistributed to the needs of states, but tax systems must be adjusted to better promote economic growth and reduce the overall tax burden on low-income persons and the most vulnerable groups. and three, taxes must be unavoidable. we will severely punish companies and corporations that deliberately avoid paying taxes, regardless of their country of origin or their size. let's change the law so that big corporations can't look politicians in the eye and laugh at them.
in writing. madam president, the employment and fair taxation policy should become a priority for the economies of the member states of the european union. this is particularly important in the context of the economic crisis in which the union is currently engaged, which requires additional impetus to stimulate economic growth. this is why we need to improve the tax system to focus more on growth. the restoration of the credibility of budgetary policy thus requires strict adherence to budgetary discipline and the simultaneous launching of structural reforms. raising taxes on wages is not a good idea, as low taxes promote economic growth and employment in the long run. member states should be encouraged to design their tax systems in such a way that taxation is more favourable to people starting an economic activity, especially those who are engaged in it for the first time. the reduction and elimination of tax barriers to cross-border activities should follow, as cross-border activities also have a significant potential for eventual economic growth. reducing the administrative burden, which requires considerable resources in cross-border trade, can also be beneficial. it should be borne in mind that, when advising on changes to existing tax laws, we must be particularly careful, since tax policy is the responsibility of the member states and therefore everything must be done with respect for the tax systems of those countries. more importantly, these changes must not in any way affect the situation of the lowest-earning citizens of the union, who are always the biggest victims of each difficult year.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on certain aspects of the eu-sri lanka air services agreement. under bilateral agreements between eu member states and third countries, a third country may refuse to issue and revoke an operating authorisation or a power of attorney to an air carrier designated by a member state but not owned by a member state and not its national. in 2002, the court of justice of the european union ruled that this situation discriminates against eu carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned by nationals of other member states. the commission notes that the sri lankan authorities have not provided any evidence that the air carriers certified in sri lanka are in compliance with the applicable safety standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, as a rule, international relations between member states and third countries in the field of air transport services are governed by bilateral agreements. those bilateral agreements include a designation clause allowing a third state to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or authority of an air carrier designated by a member state but not owned or effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. in 2002, the court of justice of the european union ruled that this normal condition for appointment was contrary to european union law. it was found that this condition discriminates against community carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. the normal designation condition replaces the eu designation condition, which allows all eu carriers to exercise the right of establishment and provides for non-discriminatory conditions for the operation of flights between the eu and third countries. in this case, sri lanka has concluded 15 bilateral agreements with individual member states, the relevant provisions of which are to be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a general agreement concluded on behalf of the union, expressly stating that, in the exercise of its rights, sri lanka will not discriminate against air carriers of member states on the basis of their nationality.
in writing. - i voted yes. in this case, sri lanka has concluded 15 bilateral agreements, the relevant provisions of which are to be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a general agreement concluded on behalf of the union. in particular, article 2 of the agreement provides for the appointment, issue and withdrawal of authorisations and expressly states that sri lanka will not discriminate in the exercise of its rights against air carriers of member states on the basis of their nationality. article 4 removes possible inconsistencies with the union competition rules. the agreement was signed on 27 september 2012. by decision of 26 november 2012, the council requested parliament to give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement in accordance with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. rule 81 of parliament's rules of procedure provides that where parliament's consent is required for an international agreement, parliament shall take a decision by a single vote.
in writing. - i am in favour of concluding this agreement. this will provide a strong legal basis to ensure the stable and reliable provision of air services. this agreement will create a level playing field for eu air carriers in the conduct of their activities. all carriers will be able to exercise their right of establishment in an appropriate manner. moreover, the strictly regulated equal assessment of national and foreign entities will prevent not only open discrimination on grounds of nationality or place of residence as regards companies, but also all hidden forms of discrimination. so, what do you think? non-discriminatory conditions for the operation of flights shall be established. fair and equal opportunities will also prevent distortions of competition. this will remove barriers to the provision of services and maintain the attractiveness of the provision of services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to strengthen cooperation between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation (eurocontrol), which plays a key role in european air traffic management. the objective of this proposal is an agreement between the eu and eurocontrol, whereby eurocontrol commits to support the european union in the latter's implementation of the common european sky and related eu policies. the agreement shall identify the areas of cooperation and define the modalities and mechanisms of cooperation. i agree with the importance of ensuring synergies with the work of the european aviation safety agency in areas such as safety and environmental issues and the establishment of a joint committee responsible for the administration and application of the agreement. i believe that the agreement will contribute even more to the implementation of the single european sky.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to strengthen and consolidate the cooperation between the eu and eurocontrol in order to enable eurocontrol to support the eu in the implementation of the single european sky (ses) and related policies. eurocontrol is an intergovernmental organisation made up of 39 contracting countries from across europe, including all eu member states except estonia. it plays a key role in european air traffic management. in line with the single european sky legislation, the commission appointed eurocontrol as the performance evaluation body of the cef in 2010 and as the network manager of the air traffic management network functions in 2011. the agreement confirms that eurocontrol is the technical and operational body of the eu for the development and implementation of the single european sky project, lists the areas of cooperation and defines the modalities and mechanisms of cooperation. the agreement also aims to ensure interoperability with the work of the european aviation safety agency in areas such as safety-related air traffic management issues and environmental protection issues.
in writing. - i voted for this document. eurocontrol is an intergovernmental organisation made up of 39 contracting countries from across europe, including all eu member states except estonia. it plays a key role in european air traffic management. the purpose of this agreement is to strengthen and consolidate the cooperation between the eu and eurocontrol in order to enable eurocontrol to support the eu in the implementation of the single european sky (ses) and related eu policies. the main aspects of this agreement are: the confirmation of eurocontrol as the technical and operational eu body for the development and implementation of the bed project; the listing of areas of cooperation and the definition of modalities and mechanisms for cooperation; the aim of ensuring interoperability with the work of the european aviation safety agency (easa) in areas such as safety-related air traffic management issues and environmental protection issues. it is proposed to establish a joint committee responsible for the administration and application of the agreement. the joint committee would be empowered to adopt and amend annexes falling within the scope of the agreement. the agreement was signed on 20 december 2012. it shall apply provisionally. the council's approval of the european parliament is required for the conclusion of the agreement. in accordance with rule 81 of its rules of procedure, parliament shall take a decision by a single vote.
in writing. - i am in favour of concluding this agreement. given the european dimension of eurocontrol's activities and the need for further institutional reforms, more effective and closer cooperation is needed. in addition, this agreement between the eu and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation is also of great importance to the eu, as it is the sole regulator of air traffic management. it should be noted that the technical expertise of eurocontrol will not only contribute to the implementation of the european sky initiative, but will also help improve air traffic management in europe. it will also be another step towards more effective cooperation in civil and military air traffic management.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to amend the provisions of regulation no 354/83 relating to the deposit of the historical archives of the institutions at the european university institute (eui) in florence. this proposal establishes a stronger legal and financial framework for cooperation between the eu and the eui, while strengthening the role of the eui, which will be responsible for the historical archives of the eu institutions. the archives of the institutions of the european union are of great importance for the preservation of historical information, for the public's awareness of the history of the eu and for research on european integration. i agree that it is necessary to make these archives accessible to the public, including by electronic means, including archives which have been digitised and which have been created only in digital format, and to lay down clearly the rules applicable to archives in order to ensure adequate data protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the historical archives of the eu institutions are an important source of information on the history and heritage of the european union. it is therefore essential to make archives accessible to the public in order to make their records available to the public, to preserve information on the eu institutions and to support research into the history of european integration. the proposal for this council regulation, which parliament supported, provides a stronger legal and financial framework for eu-eui cooperation. this regulation does not alter the main aspects of the regulation already in force, such as the definition of historical archives and when and what documents are to be made available to the public. however, the amendments clearly set out the obligation to finance the european university institute through contributions from the depositary institutions of the general budget of the union and specified that the financial contributions would cover the costs of the archives but not the costs of the buildings and storage facilities, which are to be covered by the italian government. the proposed method of sharing costs is based on the criterion that the amount of the financial contribution will be proportional to the size of the staff plans of the depositing institutions concerned.
in writing. - i support the draft regulation submitted by the council. the importance of historical archives is undeniable. it is part of europe's cultural heritage, a source of information on the history and legacy of the eu. the european university institute plays a key role in the storage of the historical archives of the institutions. the institute's sound legal and financial basis for cooperation with the eu is a guarantee of its effectiveness. the preservation and continuous enrichment of the archive requires appropriate financial support. however, a strict financial reporting mechanism must also be established. the appropriations must be used only for the costs of archiving and any waste or misuse of funds must be prevented.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the eighth direct elections to the european parliament by universal suffrage. it is proposed that next year the elections to the european parliament in the countries of the european union will take place from 22 to 25 may instead of june. eu citizens elect their representatives to the european parliament for a five-year term. these direct elections have been held since 1979, when meps were appointed by the national parliaments of the eu member states. the purpose of the early elections is to give newly elected members more time to prepare for the european commission president elections in july.

in writing. − the european parliament plays the role of an assembly of representative democracy in the union. it is therefore essential that elections to the european parliament are organised on reasonable terms. they must be free to vote in secret. conditions must be created to guarantee the freedom of expression of the people. i think it is appropriate to change the election period, as in many member states the long rite weekend coincides with the dates that elections should normally be. attention should be drawn to the fact that failure to change the date of the elections would create many obstacles to the proper implementation of the right to vote in direct universal suffrage. the new proposed election dates will ensure that all citizens have the opportunity to exercise their political rights properly. this will preserve their role and allow them to be more actively involved in eu life.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to assess the application of directive 2004/25/ec on takeovers. in the light of the financial developments and crisis of recent years, it is difficult to assess properly the application of the directive. the crisis has had a very significant impact on the financing of takeovers. merger and acquisition activities generally require financial support, but there is a lack of credit and low share prices make acquisitions less attractive. the application of this directive cannot be properly assessed on the basis of the limited data available. i therefore support the proposals set out to gather more necessary and relevant data to identify not only the need for amendments to the directive but also the specific further harmonisation actions to be taken.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the proposal for a directive on takeovers provides the minimum guidelines to ensure transparency and legal certainty in the execution of takeover bids and to give shareholders, employees and other stakeholders the right to access and disseminate information. given that the transposition of the directive coincided with the onset of the financial crisis, which eventually turned into the economic and debt crisis, it is difficult to determine the extent to which further harmonisation measures should apply to takeovers. however, in order to increase the transparency of the capital market and to strengthen the rights of the acquired companies and of the stakeholders, new measures are needed to regulate takeover bids by related companies. during the impact assessment, the representatives of the employees expressed their dissatisfaction with the situation of workers' rights, and therefore the necessary steps should be taken to address the relevant issues more effectively. it is necessary to ensure that employee representatives are fully involved in consultations before, during and after the takeover phase and enjoy broad rights of access to information. it is important to ensure that all types of workers are provided with transitional support, regardless of their status, type of company or the characteristics of the individual worker.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the takeover directive provides the minimum guidelines to ensure transparency and legal certainty in the execution of takeover bids and to give shareholders, employees and other stakeholders the right to access and disseminate information. the need for harmonised rules on the enforcement of takeover bids was and remains evident in europe. in view of the financial and economic developments of the last few years, it is difficult, if not impossible, to make a proper and definitive assessment of the scope of the directive. the application of the directive cannot be properly assessed on the basis of the limited data available. the committee therefore proposes to collect more relevant data in order to identify not only the need for amendments to the directive but also the specific further harmonisation actions to be taken. it therefore asks the commission to continue to monitor developments in the corporate control market closely and to reassess the application of the directive once takeovers have returned to normal.
in writing. − in the european union, where the free movement of capital is guaranteed, takeovers are a natural, albeit infrequent, part of the business cycle. this process affects many actors, in particular workers. this influence is not always positive. i therefore support this document, which more clearly defines the rights of employees working in the company being acquired, ensuring legal certainty for the employees. in particular, the right to receive information on planned and ongoing legal developments.
in writing. - i support this resolution. europe is still reeling from the capital markets, the economy and the debt crisis. this has undoubtedly had a painful effect on takeover activity. in this context, a detailed study is needed to identify not only the need for amendments to the directive but also the actions to be taken to ensure that the market functions properly and efficiently. it should be noted that the effective implementation of the directive ensures the integration of eu capital markets and greater transparency of liability. to this end, it is essential to ensure that the takeover process is transparent, that the conditions for the acquisition of the apartments are equal and that adequate financial support is provided. all interested parties must be given objective and correct information. moreover, greater attention should be paid to the protection and rights of workers.
in writing. − i voted for this report because european industry still accounts for around 16% of the european union's gdp, despite the fact that the eu's industrial sector has been in decline for the last 50 years. the decline of a large proportion of traditional industries such as coal, steel, textiles or machinery, which for several decades contributed to the prosperity of many regions, is causing problems in many regions of the european union today. many regions of the european union therefore depend on european union funding support for the conversion and restructuring of their old industrial sites. in this context, it is clear that, in the context of the financial and economic crisis, the broad ambitions of the eu's industrial policy and strategy 'europe 2020' cannot be achieved through sectoral policies alone. other aid measures aimed at helping old industrial regions, in particular those with a dominant monopoly, to successfully find new paths of development, with particular attention to the cultural and creative industries, and at encouraging the use of unoccupied land for industrial development activities, which can play a key role in the redevelopment of derelict areas, should also be used. effective policies need to be developed in areas such as cohesion, economic governance, competitiveness, research and innovation, energy, the digital agenda, sustainable development, cultural and creative industries, new skills and employment and others.
in writing. − i am pleased that there is a growing understanding in the european union that most problems can be solved by an integrated approach. the problems of industrial regions also need to be addressed in a way that takes account of social, economic, environmental and historical aspects. on the other hand, the development of strategies should not in itself become an additional bureaucratic and financial burden. the eu strategy for the baltic sea region has already proven that this is possible. i support this document and would like to invite you to follow the good practice of developing the strategy itself.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. cohesion policy must help old industrial regions to emerge from the crisis and become new, modern regions. given the role of industrial regions, only through cohesion and the structural funds can we help these regions to meet all the challenges of maintaining growth. first, the local population must be guaranteed a safe and prosperous future. the appropriate support will help to eliminate the traces of a neglected industry that was particularly pronounced during the economic downturn. more attention should be paid to public-private partnerships, which would not only help to create more added value, but also ensure the proper implementation of the regional strategy for industrial areas.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on safety in offshore oil and gas exploration, exploitation and production. in view of the number of accidents on oil rigs and the extent of the damage to the environment, i support the rapporteur's position that the standards for oil and gas extraction should be tightened. i fully support the new safety rules which require companies seeking authorisation to extract these resources to prove their ability to compensate for the damage they may suffer. the use of best practices in the control of major hazards by undertakings active in this field should thereby enhance cooperation and exchange of information between member states. it is also important to ensure that the authorities responsible for the assessment of the safety and environmental risks of operations are independent of the authorities responsible for issuing permits for drilling.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document, which aims to introduce stricter rules for offshore oil and gas production. in 2010, an explosion occurred on the deepwater horizon platform, killing 11 people and spilling 4.9 million barrels (780,000 m3) of crude oil. this tragedy has highlighted regulatory shortcomings in this area and the new rules will therefore eliminate the common differences and inconsistencies in member states' practices and legislation in the field of offshore oil and gas operations. it is important that this regulation will extend the mandate of the european maritime safety agency, in particular in the field of emergency preparedness and response. in addition, detailed information on member states' resources and emergency plans will have to be provided to the european maritime safety agency.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because major accidents related to offshore oil and gas operations can have devastating and irreversible consequences for the marine and coastal environment and can also have a significant negative impact on the coastal economy. the aim should be to minimise the number and impact of major accidents related to offshore oil and gas operations, thereby increasing protection of the marine environment and the coastal economy from pollution, establishing the conditions necessary for the safe exploration and production of oil and gas at sea and limiting the potential disruption of the local energy production resources of the european union, and improving the emergency response mechanisms. in line with best practice in the european union, the installation's licence holders and/or operators must establish an effective company safety and environmental policy to establish appropriate major accident prevention procedures and to identify in detail and systematically all major hazard scenarios associated with all hazardous activities that may be carried out with the installation, including the environmental impact of a major accident. control and emergency measures are also required, with a comprehensive safety and environmental management system and an emergency plan for the installation.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the current challenges and opportunities for renewable energy in the european energy market. i agree with the rapporteur that the potential for renewable energy supply is not yet fully exploited at european level, that the market for renewable energy is growing and that it is increasingly important in the overall energy context. it is therefore essential to take a structured and forward-looking approach to renewable energy sources. by 2030, targets must be set for the use of energy from renewable sources. each eu country must also aim to achieve a share of at least 30% of the total resource mix from green energy by 2030. i would stress that the use of renewable energy not only combats climate change and increases europe's energy independence, but also provides significant additional environmental benefits through reduced air pollution, waste generation and water use. moreover, the strong growth of the renewable energy sector will not only have a positive impact on european industry, prices and the further development of existing and new technologies, but could also lead to the creation of more than 3 million jobs by 2030.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important report. the lisbon treaty gives member states the right to define their own energy mix and therefore the mix varies considerably between member states. however, common eu objectives are being set, such as completing the internal market for gas and electricity, increasing the share of renewable energy in the overall eu energy mix, etc. this requires some coordination at eu level. renewable energy sources can be important in the long term in combating climate change and increasing europe's energy independence, but as far as eu energy policy is concerned, i agree that it must be pursued with a constant balance between security of supply, competitiveness, economic efficiency and environmental sustainability. the impact of renewables on the competitiveness of eu industry needs to be properly assessed and i therefore support the call for the commission to carry out a long-term cost-benefit analysis of renewables.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the eu is currently dependent on energy imports, which account for more than half of its final energy consumption. the commission's energy action plan to 2050 concludes that any scenario for the european energy system requires a substantially higher share of energy from renewable sources. in addition, the eu's renewable energy policy has benefited the eu economy and helped create more than 500 000 jobs. however, the supply of renewable energy sources to the transmission grid is decentralised, remote from load centres, weather dependent and variable, and requires an energy infrastructure different from the current one, which has been developed on the basis of conventional energy sources only. it is necessary to create cross-border electricity balancing services markets and to develop european transmission systems as soon as possible in order to improve the cross-border integration of hydropower from storage, in particular in the scandinavian, alpine and pyrenean regions. in addition, the possibility of cooperation mechanisms and trade with third countries should be explored in order to better exploit the potential of renewable energy sources. to this end, the infrastructure needs to ensure the safe and efficient operation of national electricity systems and the costs of the transit countries should be assessed.
in writing. − i supported this proposal to set binding targets for the use of energy from renewable sources by 2030 and to aim for a share of green energy in the total resource mix of at least 30% by then. a secure, reliable, affordable and sustainable supply of energy is essential for the competitiveness of european industry and the economy. almost half of the eu's power plants will need to be replaced over the next decade, and the energy supply system will need to be upgraded and made considerably more flexible to allow for an increase in the share of renewable energy. the share of renewable energy in electricity generation, heating and cooling and transport should be increased in a cost-effective manner, taking into account all the benefits and all the costs associated with renewable energy, including system costs, and without compromising security of energy supply. the increasing competitiveness of renewable energy technologies and the fact that renewable energy resources and clean technology-related industries are important factors for the growth of european competitiveness, with a high potential for creating new jobs and contributing significantly to the development of new industries and export markets, should be recognised.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. renewable energy is becoming more popular and plays a greater role in the energy supply chain. this is a great opportunity to reduce europe's dependence on conventional energy sources and to ensure a secure, reliable, sustainable and affordable energy supply. the implementation of the renewable energy targets would be another major step towards a single internal european energy market and reduce disparities between member states. it should be noted that consumers are currently facing a significant financial burden. this requires a common european strategy to develop both markets and regulatory measures, to ensure fair competition and, ultimately, to significantly reduce prices for end users. the commission should take more active steps to set an eu-wide binding 2030 target for renewable energy sources, following in-depth analyses and impact assessment measures.
in writing. − the renewables sector is growing at 6% per year in the eu. the impact of renewable energy is visible: the use of fossil fuels is reduced, global warming is reduced, new jobs are created. this brings many benefits to eu citizens. the technologies used to produce renewable energy are rapidly improving. the price of this energy has fallen considerably. the calculations show that the most advanced renewable energy plants are able to produce electricity cheaper than new nuclear power plants. the main challenge for the social democrats in this area is, in particular, the strong europeanisation of the development of renewable sources. we call on the eu and its member states to invest in this energy infrastructure - the development of distribution networks and their interconnections. this should grow into a european grid for the distribution of affordable energy. i voted in favour of this report because it also calls on eu countries to provide more security for the private sector investing in renewable energy.

in writing. − i have endorsed this important report, which considers the commission's plan to ensure adequate, secure and sustainable pensions. life expectancy in the eu continues to increase, from 76.7 years in 2010 to 78.6 years in 2020 for men and 82.5 years in 2010 to 84 years in 2020 for women, while the eu's fertility rate remains low. in 2008, there was one pensioner for four employees: in 2060, there will be one pensioner for two employees. in its plan, the commission has clearly identified the pension issue and has proposed concrete measures, such as the development of additional private pension funds to which the vn would apply tax and other incentives and the enhancement of the security of such funds. i share the european parliament's position that, in the light of the increasing mobility of eu citizens, it is necessary to ensure adequate safeguards for the maintenance and transfer of pension rights and to that end, to adopt minimum standards for the acquisition and maintenance of accrued pension rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a very important document concerning the legitimate expectations of all citizens of the european union to have a good old age and to receive a normal pension. these expectations can only be met by adapting pension strategies to changing economic and demographic conditions. the number of people aged 60 and over is increasing by about two million a year in the eu. meanwhile, the number of people of working age will decline every year for the next few decades due to low birth rates. rapid economic and productivity growth is also unlikely. we are not immune to economic crises. new policy solutions are therefore needed to ensure that pension systems are sustainable, secure and responsive to people's expectations. the economic and financial crisis has been a serious test for the financial sustainability of pension systems. not all countries have passed this test. we expressed regret that saving at the expense of pensioners has increased their poverty. it is necessary to find other ways to increase the financial sustainability of pension systems. the most important of these are high employment and a good balance between the labour market and retirement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because tax fraud and tax evasion cost the eu an outrageous sum of money - around €1 trillion - each year. this worrying tax gap amounts to about eur 2 000 per year for each eu citizen. the current loss of tax revenue in the eu is equal to the total amount that member states spend on healthcare and is more than four times the amount that the eu spends on education. the current tax gap in europe represents not only a worrying reduction in public revenues, but also a threat to the eu's social model based on quality public services accessible to all. this threatens the proper functioning of the single market and is detrimental to the efficiency and fairness of the eu tax systems. the unrealized revenue continues to push up the deficit and debt levels of member states, all at the crucial moment of the crisis. tax fraud and tax evasion reduce the funds that could be used to promote public investment, economic growth and employment.
in writing. − with the increasing mobility of workers in the european union, the issue of their salary and pension mobility is also becoming relevant. it is therefore essential to resolve the issue of double taxation of pensions as quickly as possible and to remove other obstacles to the movement of pensions after the worker.
in writing. − a decent standard of living and economic independence must be guaranteed to people of retirement age without any reservations. each of us must care not only for today but also for the future. in many member states, social welfare for older people is not guaranteed. furthermore, each country faces different pension system problems, making it difficult to identify a common eu typology. but the eu must remain united in its goal of protecting the right to a peaceful and healthy old age. the proposal to increase the retirement age is unacceptable. this is fundamentally wrong and will have even more negative social consequences. first, responsibility must be promoted. such socially sensitive decisions cannot be rushed without taking into account the level of social welfare in each country. in considering this social issue of vital importance to people, the views of citizens must also be taken into account. i believe that a sound governance framework for the public financial system is the key to achieving adequate, secure and sustainable pensions.
in writing. − the number of older people in the eu is increasing. one third of eu citizens are now over 65. many eu countries have huge budget gaps, making it increasingly difficult for them to bear the burden of pension systems. the retirement age is increasing in the eu. the european parliament calls on eu countries to reform their pension systems to make them even more secure and sustainable. we cannot apply the same standards to all countries, but we must offer more effective and better regulation of pensions for people. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for ensuring that people's lifelong pensions are not collapsed by economic hardship, that the retirement age is not raised constantly, that the level of pensions guarantees a dignified life, that the elderly are allowed to work according to their will and ability.
in writing. at the beginning of this parliamentary term, we set ourselves the great and important goal of creating by the end of the term a much more effective and closer common area of freedom, security and justice in the european union, where our citizens can feel safe and their rights protected, no matter where they live in the eu. the european protection order was the first important step towards making protection measures imposed by a competent authority in one country in criminal proceedings almost automatically binding in all countries of the european union. today, in the plenary, we will vote in favour of a similar document which will allow citizens in europe to have access to the protection measures they are entitled to, irrespective of whether the specific act which threatens them is considered a criminal offence in the host country to which the person using the protection measures arrives. this is a necessary measure to protect individuals from the threat of physical or psychological violence and to prevent them from being victimized by the different legal systems in the member states. the objective of this regulation is to establish a system whereby victims of crime or persons facing a real risk of becoming victims of crime can benefit from the protection measures available to them without unnecessary administrative burden.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens, as the european union loses around eur 1 trillion a year due to tax fraud, tax avoidance and evasion, which is seven times the eu's annual budget. i agree with the rapporteurs that this is a serious, multifaceted problem requiring coordinated policy at national, eu and international levels. in my view, given the current economic situation, it is very important to recover at least part of the money lost. the main objective should therefore be to halve the tax gap by 2020. in addition, in order to prevent tax evasion, the principle of banking secrecy and the legal loopholes in tax collection must be removed, taxpayers' identity must be improved and tax havens must be curbed. i stress that eu leaders must do more to tackle the problem of tax avoidance.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. the eu loses around €1 trillion every year to tax fraud and tax evasion, or €2,000 for every eu citizen. in recent years, eu countries have had to improve tax collection and abolish tax incentives, but experience has shown that large companies in member states simply move to another member state because of tax incentives. i support the commission's action plan and recommendations to member states to take urgent action against tax havens. i support calls for member states to harmonise the tax base, agree on a 'tax haven' deadline, draw up a common blacklist of such territories and prevent companies from shifting their profits to them. the commission should not allocate funding to undertakings that breach tax standards and should ensure that member states do not allow such undertakings to participate in cross-border procurement. i agree with the need to expand the tax base already in place, rather than raising tax rates or introducing new taxes. action is needed to suspend banking authorisations of financial institutions where they are found to be contributing to tax fraud by offering products or services that can be used by clients to evade taxes. member states should empower the commission to negotiate tax agreements with third countries on behalf of the eu and to encourage the eu to take a leading role in global forums on tax fraud and tax havens.
in writing. - i voted for this report because tax fraud and tax evasion cost the eu an outrageous sum of money - approximately eur 1 trillion - each year. the current loss of tax revenue in the eu is equal to the total amount that member states spend on healthcare and is more than four times the amount that the eu spends on education. a strategy based on concrete legislative actions to close the eu tax gap needs to be developed. member states should allocate sufficient resources to their national tax administrators and tax auditors, and should revoke banking authorisations for financial institutions that actively contribute to tax fraud by offering products and/or services that can be used by clients to avoid taxes, or refuse to cooperate with tax authorities. the scope of the savings income tax directive should also be extended to effectively remove the principle of bank secrecy. action is also needed to improve taxpayer identification, taxation of electronic commerce, the efficiency of tax collection mechanisms, the transparency of business registers and mutual fund registers, as well as to improve the effectiveness of the code of conduct on business taxation and to develop a new code of conduct for auditors and consultants. the establishment of a european union blacklist should suspend or terminate existing double taxation treaties.
in writing. − with many eu countries facing budget deficits due to uncollected taxes, effective control of so-called tax havens, even those within the eu itself, is becoming a real concern. in support of this document, i would like to point out that one of the necessary steps is to establish appropriate cooperation with third countries whose entities, by taking advantage of tax incentives in the eu countries themselves, often legalize the proceeds of crime in this way.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. tax fraud and tax evasion is a serious, multifaceted problem requiring coordinated policies at national, eu and international levels. cross-border tax fraud and tax evasion are now widespread. effective and progressive taxation is essential for public authorities to fulfil their obligations and to meet the needs and expectations of citizens. the reform of the tax system and its efficiency is a matter of particular importance for society as a whole. tax systems need to be adjusted to better stimulate economic growth and reduce the overall tax burden on low-income earners and the most vulnerable groups. i call for strict punishment of companies and corporations that deliberately avoid paying taxes, regardless of their country of origin and their size. let's change the law so that big corporations can't laugh in your face.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the eu economies - in many cases due to the current policy mix with little focus on investment, competitiveness, employment and fair and effective taxation - will have little or no growth prospects in terms of economic growth and employment in the near future. the crisis, which has exposed structural weaknesses in some eu member states and continues to damage the eu's growth potential, has put member states in a difficult position to balance budgets while promoting growth and job creation. a so-called advanced, coordinated and flexible tax snake system should be established, under which the tax systems of all member states are not coordinated but only coordinated in such a way as to take account of the reduced or increased taxes applied in the national systems. the restoration of fiscal credibility and the reduction of public debt require the maintenance of fiscal discipline and the implementation of structural reforms, with a focus on growth-oriented fiscal measures and taxes geared to consumption rather than to work. tax policy should stimulate the economy, inter alia, by creating tax structures that stimulate aggregate demand in the long term, facilitate export-oriented activities and create jobs and promote sustainable development.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it supports the european council's request not to convene a convention to deal with the question of the accession of the czech republic to protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom to the treaty on european union. eu conventions are normally convened to address key issues relating to the constitutional order of the union, including the adoption of the eu charter of fundamental rights. the european council proposes not to convene a convention on the accession of the czech republic to the said protocol, as the eu-wide impact of this issue would be limited or non-existent.
in writing. - i voted for this decision. i support the proposal not to convene the convention on the protocol supplementing the treaty on european union and the treaty on the functioning of the european union on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to the czech republic. it should be noted that the rights, freedoms and principles set out in the charter of human rights of the european union have the same legal value and binding force as the treaties. this charter does not restrict the scope of national law or limit the powers of national authorities. i believe that the solution presented is the right one and that it meets the requirements of the most democratic and efficient decision-making systems in the eu. furthermore, the integrity of the czech legal order is guaranteed. it is neither appropriate nor necessary to convene a convention in order to approve amendments to certain provisions and to add a protocol on the application of the charter to the czech republic.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the european parliament's position on the czech republic's request to apply to it protocol no 30 to the treaty on european union, which confers a derogation on a member state from the application of the european charter of fundamental rights. the treaty of lisbon, signed by all the member states of the european union in 2009, recognised that the rights, freedoms and principles set out in the charter have the same legal value and binding force as the eu treaties, but the provisions of the charter do not in any way extend the eu's competence, but only aim to give greater emphasis to fundamental rights and to ensure their visibility. for this reason, the european parliament has always been sceptical of the former czech president's request to grant his country a derogation from the charter of fundamental rights. however, at the time of the signature of the treaty of lisbon, the president of the czech republic was promised that this provision would apply to his state in the future, and the european parliament therefore decided not to prevent the further ratification of the said protocol in that member state, provided that the ratification process would be initiated by the approval of both chambers of the czech parliament for the accession of that member state to protocol no 30.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution. in view of the position expressed by the czech republic and in the light of the legal application of the treaty of lisbon, i support the proposal to extend the protocol to the czech republic. attention should be paid to the fact that the application of the protocol will not have adverse consequences for the maintenance of a high and uniform level of protection of rights throughout the eu. the high standards of protection of fundamental rights and freedoms will continue to apply to czech citizens, as the czech republic will not be exempted from the application of the binding provisions of the charter. another important aspect is that the charter has no effect on the validity of the beneš decrees on expropriation after the second world war.

in writing. − i voted in favour, as the new agreement aims to strengthen the improvement of customs-related aspects of the security of the international trade logistics chain (including container security), while facilitating legitimate trade. the agreement provides the legal basis for enhanced eu-canada customs cooperation in areas such as risk standards, security checks, minimum standards for risk management techniques, exchange of information and data, strategic partnership on cargo screening, as well as participation in multilateral fora such as the world customs organization. it also opens the door to mutual recognition of agreements on customs security measures, including the mutual recognition of relevant trade partnership programmes with equivalent trade facilitation measures, i.e. the european union authorised economic operator and canada's 'partners in protection' programmes. the european union delegated economic operators programme has been a cornerstone of the eu's supply chain security policy since 2008, allowing customs to focus limited resources on high-risk cargo. more than 10 000 european companies have already been certified as safe traders. the eu has already negotiated and agreed on the mutual recognition of authorised economic operators with japan and the usa. the eu-canada supply chain security agreement will allow for the negotiation of a similar agreement with canada.

convinced that they are our little friends. the rapporteur's professional experience was particularly useful in the trialogue negotiations. the position of the parliament was not only represented union in the debate. and that is important. the coordinated position of the three eu institutions will facilitate the travel of pets and their owners within the european union, and also when moving to has also assured, in a written statement, that a study will be carried out to assess whether it is appropriate to set up such a database. i join the call to do so as soon as possible and to report the findings to parliament.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the introduction of the customs code. the modernised customs code regulation aims to adapt customs legislation to the electronic customs and trade environment. the aim is to reform the customs rules in a fundamental way, with a view to simplifying them and improving their structure. the regulation is to apply from 24 june 2013, but it is proposed to replace it with a new one before the envisaged date of application in order to bring it into line with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon. i am in favour of postponing the date of application of the regulation in order to bring it into line with the treaty of lisbon and to give administrations and economic operators sufficient time to make the necessary investments and to ensure that the mandatory electronic processes are gradually put into practice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the renewal of the access of myanmar/burma to the common tariff preferences. the purpose of the proposal is to re-establish the benefit of the common preferential tariff for myanmar. since 1971, the eu has provided a 'general system of preferential customs tariffs' (gst) for developing countries. in 1997, myanmar was provisionally excluded from the gsp tariff because of the prevalence and widespread use of forced labour in the country. since 2011, myanmar has made significant efforts to reform, including in the area of forced labour, and the commission therefore proposes to reinstate preferential tariffs under the existing gsp regulation. i think that although some progress has been made, forced labour in myanmar has not been completely abolished. i support the calls on the commission to continue to monitor developments in relation to forced labour in myanmar. i believe that the eu should ensure that european trade and investment in this country is driven by the highest standards of corporate social responsibility.
in writing. − it is welcome that the myanmar government has managed to find a compromise on the abolition of all forms of forced labour. this is a major boost to the effective implementation of reforms to abolish forced labour. in the light of the report submitted by the commission, i consider it appropriate to renew the preferences for myanmar. however, there is a need for continuous monitoring and strict control measures, as forced labour has not yet been completely abolished. moreover, the scale of human rights violations is high, impunity has not been lifted and measures to prevent these violations have not been properly implemented. the government of myanmar must take action to prevent economic disadvantage and all forms of discrimination.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution. foreign direct investment is part of the union's common commercial policy. in this context, the eu needs to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the allocation of financial responsibility between investors and the state. i agree with the position in the draft regulation that the financial responsibility arising should be borne by the body which established the regulation at issue. however, it should be noted that such a mechanism for allocating responsibility cannot have any impact on the union budget and cannot infringe the principles of sincere cooperation and other principles governing foreign actions. in addition, the third-country investor should not be placed under an additional burden when financial liability issues are dealt with within the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal on the non-commercial movement of pet animals. the objective of the proposal is to facilitate animal owners' travel with their pets within the union or to third countries, while ensuring a high level of safety, taking into account possible risks to public or animal health. dogs and cats transported for commercial purposes are often transported clandestinely as if for non-commercial purposes in order to avoid the application of stricter rules on the trade and import of such animals. the proposal provides for the format of the relevant animal identification document, taking into account the animal species and the nature of the non-commercial movement (travel between eu member states or entry from third countries), as well as any relevant entries to be made by the veterinarian. it is important that the commission proposal is clearer, so that animal owners, veterinarians, the staff involved and the competent authorities are clear on how to apply it and so that no misunderstandings arise.
in writing. − the possibility for eu citizens to move between member states with their pets one of the elements of the free movement of persons. i therefore support the reduction of obstacles to such movements, while ensuring that animal safety requirements are also met.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution. the proper implementation of the provisions of this regulation will not only facilitate animal owners' travel with their pets, but will also allow the risk of disease spread to be adequately controlled and illegal trade to be prevented. first, a high level of security must be ensured. strict, clear and generally understandable rules must apply. animal owners shall not create unjustified obstacles to the movement of animals. however, it is essential to ensure that animals introduced from third countries do not pose a risk to human and animal health in the eu territory. in view of this, a strict control system must be applied in the eu. increased protection of identification documents is needed. pet health certification shall be carried out in a lawful and correct manner.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on animal health requirements for the trade in dogs, cats and ferrets. the purpose of the proposal is to facilitate animal owners' travel with their pets within the union or to third countries, while ensuring a high level of safety, taking into account possible risks to public or animal health. dogs and cats transported for commercial purposes are often transported clandestinely as if for non-commercial purposes in order to avoid the application of stricter rules on the trade and import of such animals. the proposal provides for the format of the relevant animal identification document, taking into account the animal species and the nature of the non-commercial movement (travel between eu member states or entry from third countries), as well as any relevant entries to be made by the veterinarian. it is important that the commission proposal is clearer, so that animal owners, veterinarians, the staff involved and the competent authorities are clear on how to apply it and so that no misunderstandings arise.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. continuous progress is needed in the area of animal welfare. we must ensure better protection and respect for animals. it is essential to provide for an adequate and scientifically justified period during which the animals are to be clinically examined by a veterinarian authorised by the competent authority before they are transported. in view of the risks posed by imports of dogs, cats and ferrets into the eu, an effective control and surveillance mechanism should be put in place. legislation must be consistent and simplified, without imposing additional administrative or financial burdens on animal owners. a common health certificate should be applied at eu level and misleading or unfair certification should be prevented.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a legislative act on economic and monetary union. the purpose of the proposal is to help member states to prepare, decide and implement reforms for growth, competitiveness and jobs. the commission's convergence and competitiveness instrument aims to oblige member states to undertake concrete reforms, with financial support. i believe that reforms should focus on employment, the functioning of goods and services markets, network industries, tax systems, financial stability and fiscal sustainability. agreements with member states must specify the main measures which the member state undertakes to implement within an agreed time-limit. i agree with the call on the commission to analyse how the agreement could be extended to non-euro area member states, and in particular those preparing to adopt the euro. i support calls for the publicity of reform plans and the promotion of social dialogue on these issues. the new spc measure must apply to all euro area member states and be open to all other eu member states. i believe that the reform plans must be drawn up by the member states with the appropriate involvement of the national parliaments, in accordance with their internal constitutional procedures, and in cooperation with the commission.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is important that all major economic policy reforms that states are planning to implement are discussed ex ante among themselves, with the involvement of the european union institutions, as required by european union law. the ex ante coordination mechanisms established should be applicable to all euro area member states and open to all member states of the union, while taking into account the increased interdependence of the euro area member states. europe's fiscal capacity should be further developed and structural reforms for sustainable growth should be implemented in a timely manner, supporting the principle that action to promote greater accountability and economic discipline should be combined with greater solidarity and greater integration of decision-making in policy areas such as taxation and labour markets. the introduction of a reform-supporting incentive mechanism would help to mitigate the short-term negative effects of structural reforms, in particular social and political difficulties, and to ensure that those effects are more acceptable to citizens. in this process, it is important to guarantee the effective independence of the european statistical system at both national and european union levels.
in writing. − the eu's governance must respect the prerogatives of the european parliament and national parliaments. the right of citizens to express their will is absolute and cannot be withheld or restricted. they alone have the sovereign right to decide on economic policy. economic policy coordination must be carried out through increased solidarity. only national parliaments and the european parliament can ensure democratic decisions on economic policy reforms. attention should be drawn to the fact that the reforms undertaken must be geared to the overall objective of achieving effective economic and social cohesion. in this context, the budget should be strengthened by a proportionate increase in contributions to those countries with higher gross national income. it is also essential that the redistributive function fosters convergence driven by social progress.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion on the situation of syrian refugees in neighbouring countries. as the armed conflict in syria continues and the humanitarian situation deteriorates, the number of refugees and people in need of assistance is increasing rapidly. in total, 1 523 626 syrian refugees have already been registered in neighbouring countries, but the total number of refugees could be much higher. i support calls on the commission to ensure that the eu takes a leading role in preventing the spread of the armed conflict in syria to neighbouring countries. i support calls for the commission to provide a comprehensive aid package to tackle the humanitarian crisis in syria and neighbouring countries. it is necessary to provide for increased humanitarian assistance, including support to refugee-hosting countries, to help strengthen local communities and infrastructure.
in writing. − the syrian regime's continued violence against civilians is having a negative impact on a much wider region. one is the flow of refugees to neighbouring countries and north africa. the un estimates that there are over one and a half million registered, but the number is likely to be much higher. the eight host countries have welcomed the opening of their borders and the acceptance of refugees, but they face enormous financial, economic and often political challenges as a result, and refugees are in need of humanitarian assistance and protection. parliament therefore stresses the need to ensure the protection of refugees as provided for in international law, calls on the european commission to draw up a model aid package, on the eu member states to honour their pledges to donate, and on the eu as a whole to prepare responsible measures to deal with the possible flow of refugees into its member states.
in writing. - i believe that the main way to resolve conflict is through political mechanisms. the fate of syria must depend solely on the will of the syrian people. they alone have the right to decide the future and welfare of their country. there must be constructive negotiations to end the civil war. it is essential that a political solution to the conflict be found as soon as possible, that the violence be brought to an end and that adequate protection of the civilian population be ensured. the humanitarian crisis and the military conflict have spread beyond syria's borders and have had a particularly devastating impact on neighbouring countries. the flow of refugees is becoming a very serious problem. the quantitative needs of refugees are increasing very rapidly. in view of this, a political decision on their fate must be taken as soon as possible, as delay only exacerbates the problem. all parties to the conflict must ensure that international humanitarian law is duly respected and contribute to facilitating the delivery of humanitarian assistance so that it reaches the recipients.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the return of assets of the transitional arab spring countries. following the arab spring revolutions in egypt and tunisia, the european union froze the assets of former dictators, their families and others associated with the regime. today, the recovery of assets seized during the arab spring has a significant economic and social impact, as funds are lacking to stabilise the economy and create jobs and economic growth in these countries. i support calls for the eu and its member states to facilitate the return of assets seized and looted by the previous regime as soon as possible to the people of the arab spring countries. i support the proposals set out for all national asset recovery services in the member states to work closely together and develop relations with the relevant authorities in the arab spring countries. i support calls for the european external action service to play an active leadership role in coordinating member states' efforts, strengthening their capacities and promoting cooperation between all the countries concerned.
in writing. − during the arab spring revolutions in egypt, tunisia and libya, the eu swiftly froze the assets of former dictators, their families and some others associated with their regimes. the eu supports countries in the arab world committed to building free, democratic and tolerant societies. these countries are currently undergoing major political, economic and social changes. it is worth noting that the recovery of assets seized from arab spring countries also has an economic and social significance, as funds are needed to stabilise the economy and to create jobs and economic growth in these countries, which are facing serious economic problems. the european parliament is proposing a series of measures to ensure the smooth running of the process of returning assets belonging to arab countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the european union remains firmly committed to supporting an independent and united bosnia and herzegovina, which can expect to become a member of the eu, and this prospect is one of the most unifying factors for the country's population. the situation in the country is of concern due to the size of the informal economy and the high level of unemployment, especially among women and young people. the creation of a common economic space in the country, the creation of favourable conditions for the growth of enterprises, the strengthening of the internal sources of growth by reducing the dominance of the government in the economy and the participation of monopolies, the promotion of growth spending and the strengthening of competitiveness are therefore necessary. it is also important to undertake constitutional reforms at both the state and autonomous unit levels in order to make state structures at all levels more efficient, functional and transparent. the establishment of an independent, impartial and effective judiciary, supported by an impartial and independent police force, and the effective implementation of the justice sector reform strategy and the national war crimes strategy should be ensured.
in writing. − the eu supports bosnia and herzegovina as an independent and indivisible state, its economic and political development, stability and democracy, and is committed to granting eu membership when the country is fully ready. it is worth noting that the european perspective is one of the most unifying factors in the country's population. however, it is crucial at this stage that the political elite agree on a common vision of the country's overall direction and concrete eu integration strategy and cooperate constructively both with each other and with the eu. it is also essential to ensure that a culture of reconciliation is fostered in society and among the political elite. a democratic, dynamic and united state of bosnia and herzegovina is important both for the entire western balkan region and for the eu.
in writing. − in the run-up to eu membership, bosnia and herzegovina should make greater progress in implementing constitutional and political reforms. the country must have effective government structures that ensure the well-being of its citizens. delaying reforms only makes the preparation process more difficult. concrete action is needed to help solve political, economic and social problems. each country must respect the decisions of the european court of human rights and implement them properly and in a timely manner. failure to comply with these obligations must be subject to strict measures of effect linked to its membership of the eu. integration into the eu must be based on an unconditional commitment to european values. the law of a country may not be in conflict with the law of the european union. the legal and political system must be in line with the eu legal and political framework. it is also essential that the economy of a country is based on market principles and is adequately prepared for competition.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the 2012 progress report of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. the european council decided not to open accession negotiations with the former yugoslav republic of macedonia for the fourth consecutive year, despite a favourable recommendation from the commission. the further postponement of the negotiations is increasing public frustration with the deadlock in the eu integration process and raises the risk of deepening the country's problems and international tensions. bilateral issues should not constitute an obstacle to the formal opening of accession negotiations, but should be resolved before the accession process is completed. enhanced political dialogue is essential to continue to make progress towards a peaceful society of diverse ethnic groups, cultures and religions and to eliminate the risks of societal polarization due to ethnic differences. strengthening political dialogue, exemplary leadership demonstrating recognition and tolerance of other ethnic groups, and an education system that teaches the values of a multiethnic society are the best ways to achieve a multiethnic society. in order to contribute to the democratic progress of the country, it is important to develop a political culture based on an independent, pluralistic, multicultural and impartial civil society. in addition, civil society findings may provide greater scope for evidence-based policy-making.
