in writing. − in view of the progress made by the former yugoslav republic of macedonia and the fact that the country continues to meet the political criteria, a date for the opening of accession negotiations should be set as soon as possible. this would be a huge boost to further reforms to restore the daily political process and improve the situation in the country. first, the problem of unemployment should be tackled as quickly as possible, it is noteworthy that youth unemployment is one of the highest in the world. this is a very big problem, holding back the integration process. in addition, fiscal decentralisation must be implemented and the transparency and impartiality of public administration must be ensured. it is very important to eliminate the internal and inter-ethnic segregation and to have a society of different ethnic groups in the country. i support the proposal for a compound name with a geographical indication. this is a good compromise presented by the greek government.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's trade and investment negotiations with the united states. given that the eu and the us are the two most important actors in global trade and investment, all possible avenues for closer cooperation and the benefits of international trade must be exploited for a sustainable global economic recovery. we, the members of the european parliament, support a comprehensive and comprehensive trade and investment agreement with the us, but at the same time we argue that cultural and audio-visual services, including those provided online, should not be included in the negotiations on a future us-eu free trade agreement. the eu's cultural and linguistic diversity must not be jeopardised, i.e. member states must maintain the possibility to preserve and develop cultural and audiovisual policies in accordance with the laws in force in the member states. we also call for the opening up of public procurement markets and for the protection of personal data. i hope that the agreement will remove the remaining barriers to transatlantic trade, particularly in the area of customs procedures and regulatory restrictions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a trade and investment agreement between the european union and the united states of america. the eu and us markets are closely interlinked, with an average of almost eur 2 billion of bilateral trade in goods and services per day. it is estimated that the transatlantic trade and investment partnership could generate €119.2 billion per year for the eu as a whole and €94.9 billion per year for the us. eu exports to the us could increase by 28% and 6% in total. the agreement will ensure improved mutual access to the market for goods, services, investment and public procurement, the reduction of non-tariff barriers and the enhancement of regulatory consistency, the development of common rules to address global trade challenges and to seize opportunities. i agree with the proposals made to exclude cultural and audiovisual services, including those provided online, from the negotiations. the agreement should include strong protection of precisely and clearly defined areas of intellectual property rights, including geographical indications. it is also necessary to harmonise standards for corporate social responsibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union and the united states of america are the two most important players in world trade and investment, accounting together for almost half of global gdp and a third of world trade. the development and strengthening of the multilateral system is a key objective, and the strategic importance of eu-us economic relations should be reaffirmed and enhanced, and that the eu and the us should provide for a common approach to global trade, investment and trade-related issues, such as standards, norms and rules, in order to develop a broader transatlantic vision and a common set of strategic objectives. it is essential to exploit the untapped potential of a genuine integrated transatlantic market in order to create as many jobs as possible and to increase the potential for smart, robust, sustainable and balanced growth. the ambitious objectives of mutual access to markets for goods, services, investment and public procurement, the reduction of non-tariff barriers and the improvement of regulatory consistency and the development of common rules to address global trade challenges and opportunities should be pursued. the bilateral relationship should be based on the creation of high-quality jobs for european workers, direct benefits for eu consumers, new opportunities for eu companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, to sell their goods and services in the us, full access for eu companies to the us public procurement market and better opportunities for eu investment in the us.
in writing. − the european parliament expresses its support for the opening of negotiations on a comprehensive trade and investment agreement between the eu and the us. an agreement between the two largest and most influential economies in the world on a common approach, common rules, the reduction of non-tariff barriers and market access would further strengthen the strategic transatlantic partnership. the european parliament intends to follow the negotiations closely and looks forward to an ambitious and wide-ranging agreement that will help to realise the full potential and opportunities.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the envisaged agreement will provide a framework for a common eu-us approach to global trade and will allow the full potential of an integrated transatlantic market to be exploited. eu fundamental rights standards must play a special role in the negotiations for the eu-us trade and investment agreement. the economic and social crisis cannot be a justification for lower social, environmental and labour standards than those applied before the crisis. investors from both countries must be granted equivalent rights and operating conditions. in addition, the precautionary principle should be given particular attention when dealing with environmental and other sensitive issues, particularly those related to the use of gmos. i believe that the eu must take a firm stand and retain unconditional competence to define its own cultural and audiovisual policies. this area should not be the subject of negotiations for the conclusion of an agreement. furthermore, public procurement in the field of defence and security must also be excluded from the negotiations on the liberalisation of public procurement. otherwise, competition will be distorted and the european defence industry will be placed on a different competitive footing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the opening of negotiations on a free trade agreement between the eu and the us. i understand that negotiations will not be easy. both the eu and the us will reluctantly abandon the established subsidies that support local producers' practices. there is no guarantee that negotiators will be able to agree on a final text or that all eu countries will agree. but i think it's worth a try. the eu and the us could become the main global trade-shaping bloc. the standards agreed would become the de facto world standards. other economies around the world would have to catch up. i think we must exploit the situation that has arisen, where there is a positive mood on both sides of the atlantic towards negotiations. and the results of the negotiations, when we have them, will be able to be approved or rejected in the next ep plenary sessions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the report of the un special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in myanmar states that human rights issues remain a serious concern, as well as the continued use of unsanctioned detentions, forced displacements and land confiscation, the use of child soldiers, attacks against ethnic minorities and the weakness of the judiciary, despite the actions taken by the government of president thein sein. myanmar (burma) is geographically situated in a region of strategic and geopolitical importance, in particular for the european union, the united states, china, india and australia. due to a long period of military rule that has permeated and shaped all layers of burmese society, despite important initiatives aimed at democratisation, change is slow and requires international support and assistance. responsible and sustainable trade and investment, including with or by the european union, can help myanmar (burma) to fight poverty and ensure that the benefits of measures reach a wider population. strengthen the state's trade institutions and trade policies, taking into account their positive impact on the country's economy, and take all necessary steps to maximise the benefits of eu trade-related support and access to 'everything but arms' incentives.
in writing. − the renewal of the gsp benefits for myanmar depends solely on the progress made by the country itself and the stability, irreversibility and sustainability of the reforms carried out. the country has made significant changes in various areas, which are to be welcomed. however, violence against ethnic groups continues in the country. in view of this, the government of myanmar must take immediate action and ratify the convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment as soon as possible. in addition, the country must change its laws that are contrary to international human rights standards. a centralised mechanism should be in place for european companies operating in myanmar to be subject to an obligation to exercise due diligence in the field of human rights and to provide public and regular information.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regional strategy for the alps. the aim of the strategy is to make better use of existing resources to address territorial development issues in the region. the macro-regional strategy for the alps should be similar to the strategies adopted by the eu for the baltic sea and danube regions and will give the alps a greater importance in the eu and better access to funding. the alpine region is multi-country, its economic capacity is diverse, and the region faces increasing environmental, demographic, transport infrastructure and other challenges. policy coordination between all stakeholders would yield better results and i therefore support calls for the commission to present an action plan for this area. it is necessary to create the right conditions for economic growth and effective social and territorial cohesion in the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the alpine region belongs to several eu member states and non-eu countries. these countries are linked by a macro-region with different economic capacities and increasing environmental, demographic, transport infrastructure, tourism and energy-related challenges, and coordination of internal and external policies of all stakeholders could yield better results and additional benefits. the development of broad-based strategies, such as macro-regional strategies, should help to strengthen the role of the local and regional level in the implementation of eu policies. such an alpine strategy would effectively address the common challenges facing the entire alpine region, exploit its significant potential in a consistent manner and meet the need to improve mobility, energy security, environmental protection, socio-economic situation, cultural exchanges and civil security in the alpine region. it is important to increase the innovation capacity of the alpine region through such a strategy, by leveraging the capabilities of its workforce, by building partnerships and cooperation between key stakeholders (labour market, education, training and research actors as well as employers), by keeping young people active in the region, by supporting creativity and by building the capacities of the different regions in the fields of education, science and research.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on improving working conditions and health and safety standards in bangladesh following the recent factory fires and building collapse. bangladesh still has a low level of labour rights enforcement and often a low level of safety. the european market is the largest importer of textiles produced in bangladesh. it is essential that the commission ensures that eu companies based abroad better comply with the principles of corporate social responsibility. bangladesh is committed to ensuring the implementation of the un and ilo conventions on human rights and labour rights. i support calls on the commission to investigate bangladesh's compliance with these conventions and to review the preferential tariffs if it appears that bangladesh is systematically violating the principles laid down in them. the commission should do more to promote responsible behaviour by eu companies operating abroad and to ensure compliance with international standards and rules in the fields of human rights, labour and environmental protection. i support the development of a voluntary social labelling standard to confirm that the product has been produced in accordance with the basic octs labour standards throughout the supply chain.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because bangladesh is the second largest exporter of ready-made garments in the world, behind only china. it has over 5 000 textile factories employing over 4 million people, garment exports account for 75% of total exports, and the european market is the largest importer of bangladeshi-made clothing and textiles. on 24 april 2013, the collapse of a garment factory in dhaka, bangladesh, located in the 'rana plaza' building, killed more than 1 100 people and injured approximately 2 500, and approximately 600 garment workers have died in factory fires in bangladesh alone since 2005, before the 'rana plaza' factory tragedy. conditions in such textile factories are often poor and workers' rights, working conditions and safety requirements are not adequately guaranteed or respected. such tragic accidents call attention to the lack of safety standards at production sites and demonstrate the urgent need to take action to improve the implementation of core labour standards to enhance the corporate social responsibility of multinational textile retailers. retailers, non-governmental organisations and all other relevant actors, including the commission where appropriate, should cooperate to develop a voluntary social labelling standard to certify that the product has been produced in accordance with basic labour standards throughout the supply chain.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. only through joint efforts can all forms of modern slavery, child labour and exploitation be prevented, fundamental workers' rights guaranteed and social dumping prevented. the tragic events in bangladesh have shown that social responsibility programmes are ineffective and that ilo labour standards are not being implemented. it is essential that countries such as bangladesh properly respect the agreed labour directives and core environmental commitments and ensure transparency of labour standards at production sites, especially where european companies are present. it should be noted that the gsp is the eu's main trade policy instrument for promoting fundamental human and labour rights and sustainable development. given the persistence and systematic nature of violations and their scale in the area of human and labour law, i believe that strict liability must be provided for and even the possibility of withdrawing or restricting a country's right to freedom of movement and free access to the eu market.
mr president, 14 june is the day of mourning and hope – mourning for hundreds of thousands of innocent people, entire families arrested without charge and deported in cattle wagons to gulags in the far east of the soviet union for unpaid work in inhuman and degrading conditions, suffering constant torture and famine. almost half the deportees were children and infants. these horrific crimes against humanity took place over 12 years, from 1941 to 1953. 14 june is also the day of hope – hope for freedom from totalitarianism. this dream has now been realised, but history should not be forgotten. last week we celebrated the 25th anniversary of the reform movement sąjūdis, which brought freedom to lithuania and enabled my country, along with the others, to come back into the european family. i am happy to invite my colleagues to commemorate, here in the european parliament on 26 june, the baltic way – the human chain which brought together more than 3 million people. solidarity is our strength. remembering the history of a united europe makes us stronger.
social housing is a matter of concern to all member states of the european union and the right to housing is a fundamental right of every person. we must therefore ensure it, because it is one of the conditions for a person to be able to live a normal social, personal and family life, to be able to take care of himself, to rest, to look for a job, to have a bank account and finally to be able to vote. firstly, it is necessary to draw the attention of member states to energy poverty, where people with housing are unable to pay their heating bills. member states should take additional measures to reduce energy poverty through the application of social energy tariffs, the provision of social support, guarantees to households against energy supply interruptions, and the improvement of energy efficiency of housing. i would also like to stress that investment in social housing is not only addressing the needs of people living in poverty, but also helping the construction sector, which has been hit hard by the crisis, by promoting renovation sectors and the development of green jobs.
in writing. consumer protection is at the heart of all our objectives in many areas. when it comes to children, babies or people with special needs and food for them, in this case, we must aim to achieve the highest standards of quality. today we are talking about the regulation on food for infants and young children and food for special purposes, which has been under discussion for a long time. the vote will fill one of the last legal gaps in the regulation of food information for consumers. it is essential that consumers are not misled as to the composition and properties of food. i therefore welcome the position that this document will regulate the list of substances (components) used in food. this will ensure transparency and clarity and will also allow the consumer to evaluate the product in terms of the substances used in its composition when choosing the product. another very important aspect is the advertising and publicity of products. the consumer must not be exposed to the slightest risk by unfair advertising or incomplete or inaccurate information. therefore, the highest standards for labelling and information on products for infants should be maintained: only such information and visual material should be provided on the labelling or presentation of such products as to facilitate an objective choice of the product and not to overestimate the benefits of the product. i agree with this document and the strict provisions it contains on the substances permitted in such products and i am confident that after three years from the entry into force of this regulation, proper labelling of these products will be ensured.
first of all, i would like to congratulate rapporteur emer costello on a really good job. poverty and social exclusion are not declining in the european union. the economic and financial crisis has only increased poverty in europe. member states are no longer able to cope with these problems on their own and the european solidarity fund for the most deprived is therefore needed now more than ever. i therefore congratulate the committee on employment and social affairs on its vote to increase the fund's budget to eur 3.5 billion, because this is certainly not the time to cut the fund's resources. i am in favour of making this fund available and binding on all the member states of the european union, because that is the only way to give real help to the people in those countries. sadly, children are the most vulnerable to poverty and social exclusion. thus, the material shortage does not endanger them only in the way they eat. and so i support that support for people in need could be provided not only with food but with other forms of assistance such as clothing, shoes, educational resources. i would therefore like to conclude by saying that, in appreciating the importance of the fund for european aid to the most deprived for all people, i hope that those member states which have so far blocked the creation of such a fund will really appreciate its importance and act sensibly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a multiannual plan for cod stocks and the fishing methods used for these stocks. council regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 of 2008 establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fishing opportunities available for those stocks, adopted before the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, incorporated a number of provisions which conferred decision-making powers on the council, although this is no longer possible under the treaty. the commission has therefore proposed to align this regulation with the new framework established by the treaty. as this regulation is one of the first pieces of legislation in the fisheries sector to be brought into line with the new treaty, it is important to safeguard the powers conferred on parliament by the treaty of lisbon. at the same time, we aim to clarify fishing mortality rates and the levels of non-target stocks on the basis of scientific data and to establish rules on the method for calculating fishing capacity. i support the proposals set out to further define the circumstances in which the commission may adopt delegated acts and to include a clear reference to the ordinary legislative procedure, indicating that this procedure is to be used to amend any part of the plan, except in specific cases.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document, as it is not always clear what type of act is to be used. delegated and implementing acts have the advantage over legislative acts of being able to react quickly to a new situation. the ordinary legislative procedure and the delegated acts ensure that parliament is involved in the decision-making process on the same terms as the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a new european consumer policy agenda. in may 2012, the european commission published a draft european consumer agenda, with the main priorities of ensuring food safety and security in the areas of healthcare, energy, financial and digital products. some 80 million eu citizens cannot afford basic necessities such as paying rent or accessing adequate health and education services. the consumer agenda provides ways to reduce consumer inequality in europe. it also aims to ensure legal certainty for consumers, efficient and reliable delivery of goods and services, and consumer protection online. i agree that there is a need to increase consumer awareness of their rights, provide clear information, ensure simple and accessible redress mechanisms and support consumer organisations. i agree that a european association register should be set up to enable associations to be set up at european level. i support the proposal to set up a financial inspectorate to detect irregularities and, after receiving consumer complaints, to punish institutions that have infringed the legislation in force. it is essential to include food safety and labelling aspects in the consumer agenda and to discuss the problem of food waste, considering the need to ensure the safety of the food supply chain from production to consumption. it is also necessary to provide the user with a secure digital environment and access to telecommunications networks, in compliance with the provisions on the protection of personal data.
in writing. − i voted for this report because ensuring food safety and security in the areas of healthcare, energy, finance and digital products should be one of the top priorities on the european consumer agenda. around the world, european consumers are facing new challenges such as the globalisation of markets, financial deregulation, the digitalisation of the economy and an ageing society. for all these reasons, compensation and support for consumer organisations have become even more important actions. in addition, the current financial crisis has made the decisions consumers have to take more complex. it is therefore necessary to ensure that consumers have access to effective, transparent and reliable information. recent studies by the european commission show that consumers need to continue to develop their capacity to make decisions about markets. there is therefore a need to promote consumer empowerment, awareness of consumer rights and clear and transparent information, consumer organisations and simple and accessible redress mechanisms.
in writing. − i supported this proposal as the top priority of the european consumer agenda should be to ensure food safety and security in the areas of healthcare, energy, financial and digital products. the agenda also announced the final stage of the digital single market, which is necessary to ensure consumer protection online, legal certainty, guarantees of consumer rights and efficient and reliable delivery of goods and services. a consumer agenda is needed to reduce consumer inequalities in europe and to help build a low-carbon economy. on a global scale, european consumers are facing new challenges such as the globalisation of markets, the deregulation of financial markets, the digitalisation of the economy and an ageing society. all these factors have given rise to the importance of the compensation mechanism and the support of consumer organisations. in addition, the current financial crisis has made the decisions consumers have to take more complex. it is therefore necessary to ensure that consumers have access to effective, transparent, reliable and comparable information. the european consumer agenda gives concrete meaning to the principle of the treaty on european union that the interests of consumers must be taken into account in the implementation of all relevant eu policies. groups of persons who are particularly vulnerable because of their physical and psychological condition or age, or who become vulnerable because of their social or financial situation, must be given special protection to enable them to access essential services and the necessary financial resources.
in writing. - i support the document adopted today. i believe that the eu agenda still does not pay enough attention to the effective protection of consumer rights. the recent case of possible differences in the quality of food products of the same brand in different eu member states shows that the issue is relevant and i hope that the commission will take note of this and review the existing legal framework.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial disputes. directive 2003/8/ec of 2003 providing for the right to bring an action in international disputes and establishing minimum common rules on legal aid for such disputes aims to ensure that the poorest members of society have access to justice in another member state. the directive applies only to civil and commercial matters and does not apply to disputes in the fields of criminal or public law. in 2012, the commission presented the first evaluation report on the directive, which noted that all member states were in principle successfully applying the directive. the main problem identified in the report is the low level of awareness of the directive: only 12% of citizens are aware of the existence of crossborder legal aid. i agree that it is important to ensure that there is greater awareness of cross-border legal aid, especially among practising lawyers. i support the proposals made to ensure that applicants have the possibility of seeking legal aid in their member state of residence or in the member state where it is needed. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the international right to trial lays down similar rules on the right to legal aid applicable at international level. i support the encouragement of member states to sign the convention so that citizens can also exercise their right to legal aid in third countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the right to a trial in international disputes and the establishment of common rules on legal aid for such disputes is one of the most important legal acts for eu citizens. they are designed to ensure that people without resources also have access to justice in other member states. it is worth noting that this directive applies only to civil and commercial matters. the definition of civil and commercial matters is understood as being defined separately in eu law, which means that certain disputes which in some member states would be considered as public disputes may be covered by the provisions of this directive. the main problem is that the directive is not well known. the commission found that only 12% of citizens were aware of the existence of crossborder legal aid. if citizens are not aware of the possibility of requesting cross-border legal aid, it is unlikely that they will use this right when they are in a situation where they need it. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to submit a revised proposal to address the deficiencies and inaccuracies in interpretation identified in its report (com ((2012) 0071) and to address situations not yet regulated. it is necessary to take action to further harmonise the rules of the member states in order to avoid further misunderstandings and legislative gaps.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because this directive is too little known. the commission found that only 12% of citizens were aware of the existence of crossborder legal aid. if citizens are not aware of the possibility of requesting cross-border legal aid, it is unlikely that they will use this right when they are in a situation where they need it. it is therefore important to take measures to ensure that lawyers, in particular practitioners, are better informed about cross-border legal aid. applicants for legal aid should be able to apply for legal aid either in their member state of residence or in the member state where it is required. each institution should apply its own limits and guidelines. if the application is accepted by the authority of the member state of residence, the national would be issued with a certificate attesting to that right, which would in turn be accepted by the authorities of the other member states without reassessment of the situation. this would greatly facilitate the situation of citizens (and the relevant authorities) and speed up procedures.
in writing. − ensuring access to legal aid outside the home country is essential for eu citizens to access justice in other member states. unfortunately, due to lack of information and other reasons, these rights have not yet been actively exercised. i therefore support this document, which calls on the commission to improve the conditions for providing legal aid to citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs. intellectual property rights (ipr) ensure access to the benefits of research, innovation and creative activity. trade in infringing goods has negative economic effects on industry and products may pose risks to the health and safety of consumers. the proposal therefore aims to enable customs to better ensure the protection of intellectual property rights. the proposal aims to maintain the possibility of customs controls to safeguard intellectual property rights in all cases where goods are placed under customs supervision. procedures are also provided for which give the right to order the customs authorities to destroy the goods, under certain conditions, without the need for formal and costly judicial proceedings. if the owner of the counterfeit goods does not object to the destruction of the goods, he is therefore in agreement with the destruction of the goods. the proposal also clarifies the periods of detention of suspect goods, the conditions under which information on the consignment is transmitted by customs to rightholders, the procedures for allowing the destruction of goods under customs supervision in the event of suspected infringements of intellectual property rights, the conditions for the application of the procedure and the rights of defence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to provide guarantees to protect consumers against misleading information on the labelling, presentation or advertising of foodstuffs. it is of the utmost importance to establish restrictions or prohibitions on certain pesticides, to ensure that maximum residue levels are as low as possible and to seek to review the requirements for the advertising, promotion and commercial practices of food products (such as infant formulae) in the light of good agricultural practice and other sources of exposure. it is worth noting that the european parliament has negotiated the inclusion of the list of substances that can be added to foodstuffs in the basic act as an annex and its future updating by means of delegated acts. the compromise text also takes into account the request of the european parliament that the list should specify which categories of substances may be added to which categories of food and that not all substances may be added to all categories of food.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document, which aims to amend directive 2004/40/ec of the european parliament and of the council1 of 29 april 2004 on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields). the directive sets thresholds which must not be exceeded. however, health professionals themselves have asked the commission to submit new proposals for a directive, as the reality is different from the overly strict requirements of the directive and it is therefore desirable that less stringent limits apply. however, the reduction of the thresholds cannot be at the expense of the workers and must be based on long-term health effects. i support the amendments tabled by the european parliament and the calls for the european commission and the member states to do more research and collect more data on the long-term effects of exposure to electric, magnetic and electromagnetic fields. the compilation of these data will enable the commission to submit a new proposal on long-term health effects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as more appropriate and proportionate measures should be introduced to protect workers from the risks posed by electromagnetic fields. these measures should address the problems associated with any known direct and indirect biophysical effects of electromagnetic fields, with a view not only to ensuring the health and safety of each individual worker, but also to providing the minimum protection for all workers in the european union. the level of exposure to electromagnetic fields can be reduced more effectively by providing for preventive measures in the design of workplaces and by selecting work equipment, procedures and methods with a view to reducing risks at the source of the field. it is worth noting that, where exposure exceeds the limit values, the employer should ensure that the workers concerned are provided with adequate medical care, in accordance with national law and practice. i would therefore urge the european commission to seek to prevent any adverse health effects of exposure to electromagnetic fields and to diagnose such effects at an early stage, to carry out appropriate health checks in accordance with article 14 of directive 89/391/eec and to monitor more actively the health of workers in these sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that improvements are necessary, especially in the working environment, to ensure better health and safety protection for workers. every worker has the right to safe working conditions which are conducive to his or her health and dignity. therefore, more appropriate and proportionate measures should be laid down to protect workers from the risks posed by electromagnetic fields.
in writing. − in the modern world, with the increasing number of sources of electromagnetic fields surrounding humans, it is essential to prevent the radiation from these sources from affecting human health. therefore, i support the minimum risk reduction, health and safety requirements set out in the latter document.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to restore cod stocks while ensuring that it is supported by the stakeholders. regulation (ec) no 1342/2008 establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks was published on 18 december 2012. the plan represents what is considered a crucial step in the recovery of cod stocks in the northern waters of the eu. three years after its implementation, the plan was reviewed by the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries, which noted that fishing mortality had not decreased and that in many areas the plan was not supported by the stakeholders. i agree that the plan needs to be improved and that it is important to take more account of scientific advice when deciding on cod stocks. although overall cod mortality is decreasing, it is necessary to reinforce this trend. i welcome the proposals for expanding and strengthening cooperation between scientists and industry in the fisheries sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it should be possible to restore fish stocks by ensuring a constant fishing mortality rate and taking scientific advice into account. it is important to note that the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries, while acknowledging that only three years have passed since the plan was implemented, nevertheless noted that the current plan has not reduced fishing mortality and that in many areas the plan is not supported by the stakeholders. a plan supported by stakeholders is more likely to be successful, as it is the stakeholders who need to act to encourage its successful implementation. in short, if they agreed to the plan, they would also assume responsibility for the fulfilment of their obligations. the proposed amendments aim to strengthen and extend the cooperation between scientists and industry in the fisheries sector. we have already seen successful projects in several fisheries areas where cod is a concern. the aim is to limit cod catches and reduce discards while maintaining a stable catch of target species.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european parliament's special committee on combating organised crime, corruption and money laundering (crim) was mandated to examine the extent of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and to propose appropriate measures to enable the eu to prevent and prevent and combat these threats at international, european and national levels. according to europol, there are currently at least 3 600 criminal groups operating in the eu, of which at least 70% have members of different nationalities, reflecting the cross-border nature of the phenomenon. the global financial crisis has also created the conditions for more intensive criminal activity and the emergence of new activities such as fraud and corruption in professional sports, infiltration of the legal economy through fraud and money laundering. poverty also provides a breeding ground for organised crime, in particular for activities related to trafficking in human beings and their organs, forced prostitution, human slavery and the setting up of labour camps. i agree with the call for the commission to take all possible action as a matter of urgency to strengthen the fight against organised crime, corruption and fraud, to devote more resources to combating the use of social networks and electronic crime for trafficking in human beings and to increase cross-border judicial and police cooperation between eu member states and eu agencies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because criminal organisations have gradually extended their activities internationally, taking advantage of the opening of the european union's internal borders and the opportunities offered by economic globalisation and new technologies. it is clear that the development and implementation of measures to disrupt the financial resources of criminal organisations and, where appropriate, to declassify banking information is essential for the effective fight against all forms of organised crime. it is worth noting that money laundering, corruption and organised crime by european actors cause serious damage to developing countries and impede their development by plundering their natural resources, constraining fiscal resources and increasing public sector debt, and that it is therefore necessary to combat organised crime and money laundering by all means. for these reasons, member states should cooperate as closely as possible with the european parliament and the commission. at eu level, member states should develop as uniform and consistent as possible indicators for europol, eurojust and the fundamental rights agency to assess at least the prevalence, costs and social damage of eu-based organised crime, corruption and money laundering.
in writing. − the eu currently faces a great threat due to the globalisation of organised crime and how this has allowed it to become an economic global player. traditional criminal organisations have extended their reach and, through new technology, have begun working with criminal groups in other countries and continents. corruption and money laundering are separate phenomena but related to organised crime as the business frequently operates through these mechanisms. these enable organised crime to benefit from a significant illicit competitive advantage which, in turn, allows it to negatively impact the lawful economy. as organised crime reaches new global levels, the response must match. this report was created from meetings with various organisations that all cited the major problem they face in organised crime. therefore, it is imperative that the eu commits to fighting this problem and sets it as a priority. i voted in favour of this report because we must begin addressing organised crime in its new forms by developing new social and law enforcement paradigms. by recognising the threat posed by organised crime, we can be effective in fighting against it.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to show how the social housing sector can help the european union overcome the economic, social and environmental crisis. today, some 25 million citizens of the european union live in social housing. nevertheless, a large number of eu citizens still lack the means to buy adequate housing. investment in social housing is a means of addressing the challenges of an ageing society, the needs of young people and the inclusion of marginalised communities and the homeless. investment in social housing supports the construction and renovation sectors, and the adequate supply of such housing reduces the size of the real estate bubble. the added value of structural funds and eib loans to promote social housing investments should be emphasised. social inclusion must be based on a sufficient supply of quality social housing at an affordable price to overcome the associated health problems. i support the proposals in the next multiannual financial programme to provide for a sufficient amount of these funds and to facilitate their use and redistribution of unused funds to social housing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because social housing is of great importance to all the countries of the european union. unfortunately, there are currently 4.1 million homeless people in the european union and about 25 million in social housing. from an economic point of view, investments in social housing should be seen as cost-effective and long-term. adequate supply of social housing also helps to reduce the scale of property cycles and so-called property bubbles that destabilise the economy. the structural funds and the european investment bank also provide loans to promote social housing investments. i would like to stress that member states must inevitably address energy poverty where people with housing are unable to pay their heating bills. they should take additional measures to reduce energy poverty through the application of social energy tariffs, social support, guarantees to ensure that households do not lose energy supply, and the energy efficiency of housing. member states should take seriously the european parliament's proposals for concrete measures to overcome poverty and social exclusion in the european union. the solution of these painful problems cannot be postponed to tomorrow or left to future generations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to show how the social housing sector can help the european union to overcome the economic, social and environmental crisis. social housing is one of the means available to public authorities to respond to the inadequacy of the housing market, to meet all housing needs and to ensure that everyone can afford adequate housing at an affordable price (affordable rent). the market's inability to meet all housing needs affects not only those who simply cannot afford housing, but also those who live in unsuitable, unfurnished or overcrowded housing. there is a clear social need to invest in the social housing sector. europe is experiencing a major housing crisis, which is continuing and possibly intensifying despite the shocking information regularly provided to the european public in the winter, when the situation of homeless people is intolerable.
in writing. − the right to housing is a fundamental human right, and social housing is therefore essential. this is an important step towards eradicating poverty and achieving greater social cohesion. this is particularly relevant in the current period of economic stagnation and high unemployment. i support this proposal because i believe it will contribute to the welfare of single mothers, young people, roma and other social groups. for low-income households, heating taxes represent a very high proportion of the costs. i would therefore like to stress the importance of building renovation in the fight against energy poverty. the renovation of housing will also have a positive impact on the fight against climate change, while also contributing to the regeneration of the construction sector and the creation of green jobs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which highlights the persisting problems in the field of gender equality, particularly in relation to the mobility of women. women still face many obstacles when moving from one country to another, including insufficient integration and foreign language skills, inadequate working conditions and social protection, and less favourable conditions for reconciling family and work life. in particular, as regards women's mobility for employment, it is essential to ensure the integration of women into the labour market, i.e. the acquisition and exchange of qualifications, the development of skills and competences, and the provision of lifelong learning opportunities. we must create the conditions and ensure that women can find good, qualified and not just any jobs so that they can earn and support themselves. it is also essential to address the problem of 'women's waste of mind', i.e. the under-use of skills by women who go abroad. this is particularly evident in the care and household sectors, which are predominantly female. secondly, in education, more and more women are getting an education that helps them get better jobs, but there is still a gendered and stereotyped division of the labour market in the eu, which makes it difficult for women to get higher positions in the workforce, to participate in decision-making, and this has negative consequences for women's careers, salaries and, of course, their pensions.
in writing. − i voted for this document because europe has big challenges ahead of it to make the labour market more open and accessible. in particular, it is appropriate to aim at better adapting systems for the mobility of professionals, education and vocational training to the new requirements of the labour market, improving continuing education and skills and improving systems for the recognition of professional qualifications. secondly, the persistently low level of labour mobility in the member states shows that the benefits of the internal market are not being fully exploited. there are still too many barriers to mobility, including insufficient knowledge of foreign languages, poor work-life balance and outdated national social security laws. access to information on cross-border mobility is still limited, in many cases of poor quality, and this is holding many people back. i believe that all citizens have the right to an adequate level of education, to have the opportunity to update their knowledge and to acquire new skills in their professional lives. governments, public authorities, employers, social partners and individual citizens have a shared responsibility to achieve these goals. higher and better education leads to higher employment levels, and higher education levels contribute to higher female employment over the long term and have a direct positive impact on gdp.
in writing. - women's mobility is a major factor in achieving economic and social progress. it helps to improve women's professional skills and increase their employment rate, thus addressing gender inequality. by ensuring mobility, we will create more opportunities for women to take up promising jobs, develop their skills and express themselves in a variety of activities. particular attention should be paid to women working without contracts, who are often not provided with adequate social guarantees. i would also like to point out that increased mobility is a path towards greater solidarity between european citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the electronic toll service and the system of reverse charge for light passenger vehicles. the commission considers that the european electronic toll service (eets) project has not been a success. not enough attention has been paid to the rapidly developing technologies of global positioning system (gps) /general packet radio service (gprs). the commission has not yet carried out a thorough assessment of the possibilities available. i agree that the reduced roaming charges under the regulation should be a model for the commission to take into account when deciding on the eerp. this is the case where, after many years of unsuccessful negotiations to persuade operators to reduce their tariffs, the commission started to apply a regulation thus forcing operators to reduce their tariffs. i support the proposals set out to ensure data and privacy protection, to use online payment systems to ensure price transparency and convenience, to strengthen the polluter pays principle and, at the same time, to reduce the administrative burden on carriers, smes and car users. i agree that it is important to encourage member states to use road toll systems rather than time-based charging systems, as the latter systems do not accurately reflect actual road use and therefore do not respect the polluter pays principle.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the current european electronic toll service (eerp) system developed by the european commission is not functional and needs to be thoroughly revised. it is worth noting that the implementation of new electronic toll systems has consistently encountered certain problems in cross-border areas, which have led to protests and complaints about financial losses and discrimination. for these reasons, the european commission should consider appropriate legislative measures in this area as soon as possible in order to commit all stakeholders to the progressive implementation of the eerp project. it is known that the market-based approach has not produced the expected results and it is therefore necessary to examine the shortcomings that have led to this situation. the commission should provide in its work programmes relating to the trans-european transport networks for the possibility of financing projects whose implementation could allow the acceleration of the implementation of the eerp system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the current system of the european electronic toll service (eets) developed by the commission is not functional and needs to be thoroughly revised. the eu has a responsibility to ensure that this new change does not negatively affect crossborder travel and the daily lives or trade of people living in border regions. the eu must also promote the charging of road use without discriminating against road users who do not live in the country where the toll is charged. in the future, more money will be needed not only to build new roads but also, and above all, to maintain and maintain existing transport infrastructure. member states should be allowed to apply distance or time-based taxation schemes, but steps should be taken to ensure that, where possible, distance-based schemes are preferred as they are fairer and less discriminatory than time-based schemes. the technologies needed to ensure the interoperability of road charging systems are already in place. the overall main problem with the eerp is not market or technical issues but the lack of political will to implement the system.
while the lower can still live in the old, the upper still wants to rule the old. i am paraphrasing the famous theoretician who explained the theory of the origins of revolutions in this way many decades ago, but today europe is faced not with a theory but with a practice that looks at concrete social and economic problems through the eyes of 25 million unemployed europeans. a fifth of them (5 million) are young people under 30. the european commission's initiatives have had little effect. i'm being very diplomatic here. the causes of unemployment cannot be identified and eliminated. the problem is expected to be solved by imposing new taxes or increasing old taxes, but not by creating jobs to pay those taxes. the overall coverage of the active work instruments and the funding provided by the individual instruments are insufficient and the instruments are poorly targeted. the unemployment rate is particularly high among young people and unskilled workers. we need to create a network of industry and business that creates new jobs and sustains old ones. we must seek closer cooperation between academic institutions and business so that every young person who graduates from an educational institution has already been introduced through a professional internship and knows which company he will work for. the european commission and the member states must do much more to restore social well-being than to focus on geographical mobility, thus encouraging mass migration from the south of europe to the north.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. the proposal aims to adapt certain provisions of the regulation to the decision-making procedures laid down in the treaty of lisbon. iuu fishing is one of the greatest threats to marine biodiversity and can cause food security problems in many coastal and developing countries. the amendment of the regulation could allow the commission to set standards for the inspection of landing and transhipment operations by third country fishing vessels, to adapt the system of certification of catches to certain fishery products caught by small fishing vessels, to amend the list of products not covered by this regulation, to adapt the deadline for the submission of a catch certificate to the type of fishery product, etc. i agree with the commission's amendments. i agree with the proposal that, where delegated acts are proposed, the time limits for the delegation of power should be limited in order to allow for a continuous assessment of the way in which they are used.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is essential to prevent illegal and unregulated fishing, to establish rules to create a common framework and to ensure that the relevant documents are transmitted to the european parliament and the council simultaneously, in a timely and appropriate manner. it is important to note that the eu has not achieved good results in applying regulation (ec) no 1005/2008. the commission therefore concludes that the measures in force are in line with the principles of the union interest as set out in article 3 (1) of the basic regulation. in short, most member states complained that it would impede trade or that it would be too expensive and difficult to implement. however, illegal fishing is one of the greatest threats to marine biodiversity and can cause food security problems in many coastal and developing countries. it is worth noting that the united states recently published its third biennial list of countries whose vessels have been found to be engaged in illegal fishing. the us list, in contrast to the modest eu list, includes a number of larger illegal fishing countries - the eu has not done so - such as korea, mexico. it is therefore important to ensure that all commission services work together to find ways of ensuring and facilitating the effective application of the regulation to implement union policies and legislation.
in writing. − from an economic point of view, illegal fish may appear attractive. as they are caught in defiance of environmental, social and other standards, fishermen are usually able to sell them at a lower price. therefore, wholesalers and retailers find it more cost-effective to buy such fish. this explains why many people are not enthusiastic about a regulation that prohibits illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. it is easy to disapprove of illegal fishing in principle, but it is hard to approve of it anyway. but if opposition to illegal fishing disrupts the supply of fish to the eu market, reduces profits or creates barriers to trade with important eu trading partners, it will be much more difficult to fight illegal fishing. parliament has adopted a number of reports and resolutions calling on the commission to combat iuu fishing with all its available resources and by all possible means, including, inter alia, discouraging the re-registration of vessels in another country, collecting information on private agreements, improving product traceability and enhancing international cooperation and information exchange. i agree that all commission services must work together to find ways of ensuring and facilitating the effective application of the regulation, the implementation of union policies and legislation. in short, it is one thing to talk about tackling iuu fishing, but quite another to act. i am in favour of stopping the destruction of all our resources and taking action to protect and conserve them.
in writing. − illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing is a global problem, causing economic hardship for fishing communities, consumers and the sector as a whole. the eu is the world's largest importer of fishery products and one of the world's largest fisheries operators. it plays a key role in mobilising the international community to combat iuu fishing. in order to prevent illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, it is appropriate to empower the commission to adopt delegated acts. however, the mandate should be limited in time and should be subject to regular reporting requirements. this will enhance cooperation between eu institutions, improve information gathering and ensure the rigorous and transparent application of union fisheries legislation. in addition, a strict control system will ensure the effective implementation of the strategy to combat iuu fishing, enhance resource management and reduce illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation on the reception of applicants for international protection. this proposal aims to ensure stricter and more consistent requirements for the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection, ensuring that the protection needs of third-country nationals or stateless persons are adequately addressed, in accordance with the international and eu obligations of the member states. the proposal lays down new european rules on asylum which will harmonise the asylum procedure, the time limits for processing applications, and the basic rights of asylum seekers, and will help to avoid crises. the proposal aims to increase the efficiency of decision-making and to encourage member states to provide reasoned first-instance decisions within a reasonable time. the separation of asylum seekers and other migrants when they arrive together would be accelerated, thus rationalising the use of administrative resources. asylum staff will be able to better identify cases of unjustified and abusive requests, and member states should also be able to reduce their reception costs and remove asylum seekers who have not been granted asylum from their territory. real refugees will be able to benefit from their rights more quickly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because it amends the 2003 reception conditions directive, which sets minimum standards for the reception of asylum seekers, and aims to ensure a more perfect and harmonised standard of behaviour. it deals in particular with the grounds for detention and provides a detailed list of rules and guarantees. the right to work, material assistance, health care, legal aid is strengthened, better representation for unaccompanied minors is provided, special needs are identified and the commission's role in monitoring implementation is simplified.
in writing. - i support the draft directive presented. it is a step forward towards an effectively functioning common european asylum system. it should be noted that the new regulation must be based on the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility, including the financial burden, between the member states. the same status and equal reception conditions for beneficiaries of international protection would apply throughout the eu. aid applicants must be subject to high standards of protection and fair and effective procedures. each member state should ensure the necessary level of material assistance, a high level of equal treatment and a standard of living that does not impair dignity. particular attention shall be paid to the implementation of the principles of the importance of the well-being of the child and the unity of the family.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the criteria and mechanisms for determining the member state responsible for examining an application for international protection lodged by a third-country national or a stateless person in one of the member states. this proposal aims to ensure stricter and more consistent requirements for the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection, ensuring that the protection needs of third-country nationals or stateless persons are adequately addressed, in accordance with the international and eu obligations of the member states. the proposal lays down new european rules on asylum which will harmonise the asylum procedure, the time limits for processing applications, and the basic rights of asylum seekers, and will help to avoid crises. the proposal aims to increase the efficiency of decision-making and to encourage member states to provide reasoned first-instance decisions within a reasonable time. the separation of asylum seekers and other migrants when they arrive together would be accelerated and administrative resources better used. asylum staff will be able to better identify cases of unjustified and abusive requests, and member states should also be able to reduce their reception costs and remove asylum seekers who have not been granted asylum from their territory. real refugees will be able to benefit from their rights more quickly.
in writing. − i have agreed to this proposal because the common position is in line with the main objective of the commission's proposal. in particular, it shall improve the current standards of treatment of applicants under the dublin procedure. it guarantees the right to information and to an effective legal remedy when a transfer decision is taken, and lays down clear rules on detention and access to free legal aid. these issues are not addressed in the present document. it provides for a more predictable environment in relations between member states and more favourable conditions for the reunification of vulnerable persons, in particular unaccompanied minors, with family members or relatives.
in writing. - i agree with the council's position. applicants for international protection must be afforded the same protection in all member states. a full assessment of the needs of applicants for international protection is necessary. in particular, they must be guaranteed the right to information and effective legal protection. clear and strict rules on detention and access to free legal aid must be in place. attention should be paid to the fact that the development and implementation of the measures provided for in the proposal must not be contrary to the interests of the member states, the objectives and targets set out in the strategic documents and must not create an unreasonable burden on public finances. in addition, possible administrative and technical difficulties must be avoided.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on granting and withdrawing international protection. this proposal aims to ensure stricter and more consistent requirements for the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection, ensuring that the protection needs of third-country nationals or stateless persons are adequately addressed, in accordance with the international and eu obligations of the member states. the proposal lays down new european rules on asylum which will harmonise the asylum procedure, the time limits for processing applications, and the basic rights of asylum seekers, and will help to avoid crises. the proposal aims to increase the efficiency of decision-making and to encourage member states to provide reasoned first-instance decisions within a reasonable time. the separation of asylum seekers and other migrants when they arrive together would be accelerated, thus rationalising the use of administrative resources. asylum staff will be able to better identify cases of unjustified and abusive requests, and member states should also be able to reduce their reception costs and remove asylum seekers who have not been granted asylum from their territory. real refugees will be able to benefit from their rights more quickly.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal as it seeks to ensure that stricter and more consistent requirements are imposed on the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection, ensuring that the protection needs of third-country nationals or stateless persons are adequately addressed, in accordance with the member states' international and community obligations. the proposal aims to increase the efficiency and quality of decision-making by focusing on services, advice and expertise and encouraging member states to provide reasoned first-instance decisions within a reasonable timeframe. the measures envisaged are expected to increase the compatibility of eu asylum documents, to simplify, streamline and consolidate the relevant procedure throughout the european union, and to achieve a more reasoned first-instance decision, thereby preventing abuse and increasing the efficiency of the asylum process.
in writing. − to make the european union safe for refugees, the eu needs to increase the compatibility of asylum measures and facilitate access to asylum procedures. fair, strict and consistent requirements for procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection must be applied. it should be noted that national authorities play a crucial role in the reception of asylum seekers and in determining the material conditions for the reception of asylum seekers. in this context, member states should streamline their labour and administrative resources and adequately prevent abuse in the provision of housing, welfare, health and education services. on the other hand, the legal norms and measures adopted and implemented by the eu must be properly aligned with the interests of the member states and must not compromise the balance of human rights protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the fund for european aid to the most deprived. in the europe 2020 strategy, the european union set a target of reducing the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion by at least 20 million by 2020. however, poverty and social exclusion are increasing across the union as a result of the economic and financial crisis (almost 120 million europeans were at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2011). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the eu's support to the poorest europeans to at least eur 3.5 billion. particular attention shall be paid to support groups such as orphans, children and households with children and support measures for social inclusion. in addition, the fund should support not only food but also other means such as clothing, school supplies, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because poverty and social exclusion are not declining in the european union. even in the 21st century, poverty remains one of the greatest wounds of the european union. almost 120 million europeans are at risk of poverty or social exclusion. more than 40 million also suffer from severe material deprivation, the most severe of which is food shortages. unfortunately, children are more at risk of poverty and social exclusion than the rest of the population. their lack of material things is not limited to nutritional hazards. the committee on employment and social affairs has therefore proposed that support for people in need could be provided not only in the form of food but also in other forms of aid, such as clothing, shoes and educational equipment for children. almost six million children in the european union do not have new (unworn) clothes and almost five million do not have two pairs of shoes of the right size. moreover, children who suffer from such material deprivation are likely to do worse in school than their better-off peers, to suffer from poor health, and to be unable to reach their full potential as adults. in recognition of the importance of the fund for european aid to the most deprived for all europeans, i am very much looking forward to a swift agreement between member states and the continued success of this fund in providing support to europeans in need.
in writing. − in the europe 2020 strategy, the european union has set itself the target of reducing the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion by at least 20 million by 2020. however, the economic and financial crisis has led to an increase in poverty and social exclusion across the union. in 2011, almost 120 million europeans - an increase of six million in two years - were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, and now account for almost a quarter of the total population. more than 40 million are experiencing severe material deprivation. one in ten people under 60 lives in a household with low work intensity. one of the main signs of material deprivation is the inability to obtain sufficient food of adequate quality. 43 million europeans cannot afford to eat meat, chicken or fish (or vegetarian substitutes) every other day. the world health organisation (who) defines this need as one of the main ones. children are particularly sensitive to malnutrition and poor nutrition patterns can negatively affect brain development and learning ability and their future health. i agree with the need to create a new instrument to combat food shortages, while allocating part of its resources to material assistance for homeless people and/or children other than food, and to supporting measures for the reintegration of the social groups receiving assistance.
in writing. − the programme for food distribution to the poorest people in the union is currently one of the most effective ways of addressing food insecurity and providing the poorest with a decent life prospect. this programme is a way of moving towards social cohesion. i believe that this is an important symbol of european solidarity. however, it is important to ensure that the project is properly planned and financed in order to achieve its full effectiveness. i support the proposed amendments to ensure a more sustainable and transparent implementation of the project and the use of member states' funds.
in writing. − the number of people living in poverty is a sign of urgency. poverty and social exclusion are only increasing across the eu. meeting the basic needs of the poorest is becoming increasingly difficult. the eu faces wide-ranging and multifaceted challenges, which require more effective eu policy and funding. we cannot limit ourselves to the current european food aid programme for the most deprived, because homelessness, malnutrition and the material deprivation of families with children are interrelated. the fund for european aid to the most deprived is a major step forward in tackling the problems of material deprivation. only long-term, comprehensive assistance to the poorest will help overcome poverty and social exclusion. i believe that access to the fund should be granted to all member states without any reservations, because poverty has no borders and is spreading at an alarming rate. we must work together to ensure that the fund has sufficient financial resources to reduce the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion across the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the establishment of the eurodac system for fingerprinting. the eurodac system was established by regulation (ec) no 2725/2000 and the purpose of this proposal is to amend that regulation. the purpose of the exchange is to provide law enforcement authorities in the member states and europol with access to the eurodac central database for the purposes of preventing terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences. third-country organised crime networks use the asylum system to transfer members of the criminal network to eu member states and thus have contact persons for their criminal activities. once inside the eu, these network members apply for asylum by presenting forged identity documents in order to obtain legal residence in the eu without any trial. it is necessary to allow the authorities of the member states and europol to request the comparison of fingerprint data against the data collected in the eurodac database in the fight against terrorism and other serious crime, on a match-or-miss basis. i believe that giving law enforcement access to eurodac is a very important step in the fight against organised crime.
in writing. −third-country organised crime networks seek to use the asylum system to transfer members of the criminal network to eu member states and to have contact persons for their criminal activities. these members of the organised crime network, once they have entered the territory of an eu member state, seek asylum by presenting forged identity documents in order to obtain a legal right to reside in the eu without any criminal conviction. in addition, information provided by europol indicates that traffickers also seek to exploit the asylum system by misrepresenting the country of origin in their asylum applications. i welcome the possibility for the designated authorities of the member states and the european police office (europol) to request the comparison of fingerprint data on a match-or-miss basis with data collected in the eurodac database in the fight against terrorism and other serious crime. the granting of access to eurodac to law enforcement authorities is a major step towards preventing the above-mentioned cases, provided that the necessary safeguards are put in place. i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − i support this document because i believe that the effective functioning of the single european fingerprint identification system must be an integral part of the schengen system. the free movement of persons in the european union is also used by criminals, and borders must be removed to facilitate their tracing and identification.
in writing. − eurodac is of particular importance for ensuring the effectiveness of the european asylum system. the data contained therein are of particular importance to authorities fighting crime and terrorism. in this context, it is essential to ensure that the eurodac database is used more efficiently and reliably. the provision of access to this system to the law enforcement authorities of the member states and to europol will help those authorities to perform their functions more effectively, to respond appropriately and in a timely manner to potential threats and to prevent terrorist and other serious crimes. however, a high level of security must be maintained when granting access to eurodac. common requirements should be established and applied throughout the eu. in particular, data protection issues should be addressed and possible violations of fundamental human rights in this area prevented. there must be strict data protection and surveillance controls and access procedures to stored data throughout the eu. the data contained in the system would be used only in specific cases, in specific circumstances and under strict conditions.
