in writing. − hundreds of thousands of individuals seek asylum within the eu every year and the european parliament is focused on improving the process by which these people can remain in the eu. eurodac is an important part of regulation within the system by collecting virtual fingerprints of those that seek asylum. by having an eu-wide fingerprint database, an asylum seeker’s fingerprints can be run in multiple member states to ensure that they have only applied once. i welcome this measure as this allows member states to separate those that would take advantage of the benefits available through asylum from that are truly looking to escape a terrible situation. a new provision is the access national law enforcement would have to the eurodac system in order to investigate a major crime or terrorism. while i support the idea of much higher levels of cross-border communication to prevent crime, i believe that there must be safeguards on personal privacy. i voted in favour of this report because eurodac can provide many benefits to those looking for lawful asylum in the eu and national law enforcement. however, the privacy safeguards outlined in the report must play an important role as well.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the proper functioning of the schengen system is based on trust and coordination between member states. as early as 2011, some ngos began to speak about the need to strengthen the schengen system and allow member states to temporarily reintroduce controls at their internal borders when there is a serious threat to public policy or internal security. in 2011, the european commission proposed to strengthen the schengen area in order to strengthen the eu-level assessment system for the application of the schengen rules by eu member states and to establish a procedure for taking decisions to temporarily reintroduce internal border controls in the event of a serious threat to public policy or internal security. i agree with the european parliament's position that the right to reintroduce internal border controls should be only exceptional and that decisions should be taken in accordance with clear guidelines and not for political reasons. the commission should, on the basis of the experience gained so far in the functioning of an area without internal border control, develop guidelines for the reintroduction of internal border control, both where this measure is necessary as a temporary response and where urgent action is necessary, in order to ensure the consistent implementation of the schengen rules. the guidelines should include clear indicators to facilitate the assessment of threats to public policy and internal security.
in writing. − the free movement of persons is one of the eu's core values and therefore internal border control should only be reintroduced in extreme cases where there is a serious threat to public policy or internal security. a mechanism must be in place at eu level to respond to the threats posed to the schengen area and to protect it adequately. the measures applied must be proportionate to the threat and must prevent any application of internal border controls for political reasons. moreover, the reintroduction of internal border controls must strike a balance between the powers of the member states and the commission, since such a decision restricts the free movement of persons. the maintenance of public policy and internal security is a responsibility of the member states. in the event of a threat to public policy or public security, the member state itself must have the power to take decisions to prevent that threat, including the reintroduction of internal border controls. the commission should be empowered to take part in the adoption of decisions on the reintroduction of border control at the internal borders of the eu and to deliver an opinion.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the evaluation mechanism for the application of the schengen acquis to verify the draft establishment plan. the agreement will allow special inspection teams to visit different eu internal border areas without prior notification to check for illegal border checks. these teams will be composed of experts from the european commission, eu agencies and eu countries. it will also strengthen the ability of eu countries to return controls to the eu's internal borders. it will only be possible as an extreme measure of strictly limited scope and duration and monitored at eu level. it is important to note that eurobarometer surveys show that 62% of respondents believe that free movement is the best thing the eu has achieved in 50 years. the new evaluation mechanism removes the current double standards and both member states and candidate countries must be evaluated in the same way and under the same rules. i agree with the rapporteur that this new mechanism more european, more transparent, more efficient and more stringent is a significant step forward compared to the current situation.
in writing. − free movement is a distinctive principle of the european union and the ability to move within the european union without internal border controls is one of its greatest achievements. the abolition of internal border controls across the european union started in 1985. the entry into force of the schengen agreement has given over 400 million europeans the right to travel without passport controls. free movement is also of great economic importance, as it is the key to the success of the eu's single market and an important factor in the growth of the european economy. belonging to an area without internal border control means that these countries no longer carry out internal border checks and have reinforced external border controls. in november 2010, the commission presented a proposal to establish a legal framework for assessing the proper application of the schengen acquis. this evaluation mechanism will help to maintain mutual confidence between member states in each other's ability to apply effectively the additional measures allowing the area without internal borders to be maintained. this proposal also aims at a more effective evaluation mechanism of the schengen acquis, ensuring a transparent, efficient and consistent implementation of the schengen acquis.
in writing. − the proposal for a schengen evaluation mechanism is undoubtedly an important instrument for strengthening the governance of the schengen area. the evaluation system will help to ensure that member states comply with the provisions of the schengen acquis. a rigorous and effective evaluation mechanism will eliminate double standards and help to address issues of external border protection more effectively. undocumented checks and a stronger role for frontex and the commission in the evaluation process will prevent illegal checks at internal borders. however, there are doubts whether the new legal framework will maintain the appropriate level of mutual trust between member states and their important role in the evaluation process. i think we should seek an active role for the member states themselves in the process of evaluating the schengen acquis. in addition, provision should be made for certain safeguards for the application of appropriate exceptional measures when reintroducing controls at the internal borders of a member state.
in writing. − the ability to travel within the schengen area is considered one of the top benefits brought by the eu by many people; this right is not being challenged. however, recent events have shown that the internal regulations of the system are not as strong as they should be and challenge the delicate balance between security and free movement. the temporary reintroduction of internal borders is not to prevent migrants from coming to the eu but rather to be sure that no one member state acts unilaterally. i support the eu working together as a whole to acknowledge each member state’s interests while making sure the schengen area is secure. these new standards of internal movement will apply to both schengen states and schengen candidates, making the system far more unified. a balance can be found between member state’s need to react to unpredictable circumstances and collective-decision making. i voted in favour of this report because it will transform the schengen area from one based on agreements between governments to an area where all follow the same european standards.
in writing. - i agreed to this. the update of this directive, also known as the accountability directive, aims to reduce the administrative burden on small businesses. this is expected to save small and medium-sized enterprises eur 1,7 billion per year. the new provisions will simplify the procedure for drawing up financial statements, which should be clearer, more understandable and more comparable. this will allow users of the financial statements (shareholders, banks, etc.) to better understand the company's results and financial position.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to provide greater transparency for payments to public authorities and to ensure that users of financial statements in the european union can compare the financial position of companies by creating a single standardised balance sheet. it is worth noting that these commission proposals are similar to the us dodd-frank act adopted in july 2010 which requires companies in the extractive industries (oil, gas and mining) registered with the securities and exchange commission to publicly disclose information on payments to public authorities on a country-by-country and project-by-project basis. the proposal also builds on the existing voluntary extractive industry transparency initiative. greater transparency could improve governance, curb corruption, improve corporate accountability, while helping investors to make better informed decisions. the european parliament therefore stresses that comprehensive country-by-country reporting should be provided in all sectors, including pre-tax and after-tax profit information.
in writing. − i supported the proposal as the requirements for small enterprises (smes) need to be harmonised to a large extent across the union and disproportionate administrative burdens on these enterprises avoided. i also support the principle of 'thinking of the little ones first'. on 25 october 2011, the commission published a proposal to repeal and amend the accounting directives (78/660/eec and 83/349/eec), in particular with a view to reducing the administrative burden for small enterprises. both accounting directives have been in force for the past 30 years and contain all the rules necessary for the preparation of the statutory financial statements. as listed companies have been governed by the international accounting standard (ias) since 2005, smes have become the de facto main users of the accounting directives. the commission proposes to replace these two directives by a single directive that is better adapted to the needs of current and future financial reporting agents and users. on the basis of an impact assessment carried out in 2009-2011, the commission aims to reduce the administrative burden by 25% by 2012 and foresees that all undertakings falling within the scope of this directive could save eur 1,5 billion per year.
in writing. − the principle of 'thinking of the little ones first' should be the basis for the new legal regulation. the smallest undertakings may not be subject to a disproportionate burden. in this context, it is essential that the new legal framework is better adapted to the needs of current and future drafters and users of financial statements. the financial statements should present true and fair information about the financial position of the undertaking. in particular, the administrative burden and regulatory requirements for small enterprises should be reduced, given the scale of the activities and the limited resources available. these companies should be subject to the same financial reporting rules across the eu and should be able to opt out of certain obligations. this will make it easier for small businesses to take advantage of the market and to operate properly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to further enhance investment protection and high level investor confidence by ensuring appropriate transparency for issuers and investors of securities throughout the european union. to that end, the transparency directive requires issuers of securities traded on a regulated market to publish periodic financial information on the issuer's performance during the financial year and on the current status of the controlling shares of voting rights. this directive also lays down minimum standards for access to and retention of regulated information. the provisions of this directive are closely linked to the requirements laid down in other eu legislation in the field of corporate governance (society law) or financial markets (securities). the amendments to the directive will aim to include as many smes as possible and to facilitate their access. improving the regulatory environment and access to capital for small and medium-sized issuers is an important priority that has been taken into account in the update of the provisions of the directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, as volatility in global financial markets increases, investors are increasingly demanding more information about companies' practices. it is clear that more and more companies are adopting corporate governance standards, including those related to transparency, alongside voluntary guidelines for multinational enterprises. it is important to note that companies are not currently required to disclose financial performance on a country-by-country basis. this uncertainty distorts markets, allows tax avoidance and prevents investors from being informed about the long-term sustainability of companies. for these reasons, it is proposed that both large and small companies active in the extractive and forestry sectors be listed on stock exchanges and report on a country-by-country basis. the proposal provides for greater transparency and a level playing field between companies operating exclusively in eu markets and those operating in third countries. it should be noted, however, that reporting requirements should not impose a disproportionate administrative burden on businesses, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). the proposal would make reporting requirements clearer and simpler.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this draft decision of the european council. a permanent system for the allocation of seats is necessary for the efficient and constructive work of the european parliament. first, the system must be clear, consistent and transparent. it must be based on the principle of diminishing proportionality. this principle must be the basis for the allocation of seats in parliament and must therefore be clearly and objectively defined so that the number of seats held by no member state is reduced disproportionately. we must ensure that the fundamental rights and interests of the citizens of each member state and the political trends are properly represented in the european parliament. a stable, effective system before each election will not only ensure the smooth functioning of parliament but also enhance the democratic legitimacy of the representation of the population.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the sovereign debt crisis that has hit europe and the euro area countries in particular has triggered a major economic downturn with negative social consequences in many member states, with increased unemployment, poverty and social exclusion. it could be argued that the crisis has, in particular, revealed the economic interdependence of the member states and their very different capacities to deal with labour market and social problems. it is therefore more important than ever to increase targeted and effective social investment to ensure economic stability, promote employment and raise the skills of the workforce, which in turn will improve the eu's competitiveness in the long term. for these reasons, i would encourage member states to consider signing a social investment pact, setting investment targets and creating a stronger control mechanism, in order to make more efforts to achieve the europe 2020 objectives. it is important to note that member states should not necessarily have more expenditure but should use the funds more efficiently and effectively in order to increase the sustainability of social investment policies. it is also welcome that the european commission is focusing on the european social fund as the main instrument to promote social investment, which requires that at least 25% of cohesion policy funds be allocated to the esf and that 20% of esf funds in each member state be allocated to promoting social inclusion and combating poverty.
in writing. − budgetary discipline in the euro area should be assessed not only in terms of fiscal and macroeconomic indicators, but also in terms of employment and social indicators, which should receive equal attention, and in terms of progress reports on structural reforms, in order to ensure an adequate level of social investment in the member states and thus ensure the long-term sustainability of the european union's social model. it is necessary to take into account the public investment needs of the member states, in particular those relating to the social and educational objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. i agree that it is necessary to define measures to speed up the implementation of the european youth guarantee, to develop a quality system for boarding schools and work placements, to provide efficient and accessible public services, to provide for a living wage, by establishing a national minimum income that would help to avoid working poverty. ensure social protection and the transferability of pension rights, access to affordable and adequate social housing. ensure minimum social protection to provide universal access to basic health services, irrespective of income; implement the social protocol to protect fundamental social and labour rights. to establish equal pay for men and women for work of equal value or value. implement the updated health and safety strategy.
in writing. − social investment is one of the means of tackling unemployment and other social problems in the eu. i would point out that one of the most important sources where this investment should be used is in youth unemployment and entrepreneurship programmes. youth unemployment (young people who have never worked) is a concern in the eu countries at the moment. i therefore call for the eu funds to be used as soon as possible to address this problem.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. differences within and between member states are increasing, and there is no adequate regulation to guarantee a minimum, adequate and sustainable level of social protection across the eu. in addition, the lack of social investment has exacerbated the difficulties caused by the crisis in many countries. cohesion policy is one of the key factors in achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion. it should be noted that the european social fund is the main instrument for promoting social investment, which is the basis for increasing the efficiency, effectiveness and efficiency of social protection systems. it is essential that more cohesion policy investment funding should be directed towards youth employment, social inclusion and the fight against poverty. member states must be able to make the best use of eu funds to mitigate the effects of the crisis and austerity policies. they should be encouraged to use innovative financing methods more frequently and to target the use of structural funds in areas that promote growth and job creation. in this context, it is essential that the revision of the multiannual financial framework leads to political agreement and increases in funding for the youth employment initiative. only by working together to strengthen independent and socially responsible business across the eu will we create much more value added, boost growth and ensure decent living conditions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because i believe that the instruments of cohesion policy should contribute to a more competitive european union and the europe 2020 strategy, helping the less developed regions to balance their development with that of the more developed regions. the aim is to help the less developed regions, to promote their development, to help areas with lower living standards or regions suffering from a lack of jobs.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution. many regions are still in the grip of the crisis and are experiencing severe economic difficulties, which requires maintaining the current aid intensity. it is also time to modernise the state aid system so that it can stimulate private investment in these regions and have a positive impact on employment. aid must be granted on the basis of clearer, simpler and more lenient principles. the internal market must remain strong, dynamic and competitive. it should be noted that state aid policy and regional policy are interdependent and contribute to the elimination of regional imbalances. regional policy is part of wider systems of state aid which help to reduce socioeconomic disparities between regions and development disparities within regions. only through the proper implementation of regional policy objectives and the provision of state aid can balanced, sustainable and long-term development of the regions be ensured.
in writing. - i voted for this report. competition policy is one of the key factors in an efficient and competitive market. competition policy should be more geared to facilitating the entry of new players and the emergence of new ideas and technologies on the market, rather than to strengthening already established firms or suppliers of services and goods. the adoption of a special state aid regime during the economic and financial crisis has been a matter of considerable concern and has helped to prevent further financial and economic instability. however, for the third year in a row, the european parliament has expressed its concern to the commission that this arrangement is no longer temporary and that these temporary measures should be terminated as a matter of urgency, as they already distort competition in the internal market. the report also highlights another problem of importance to all eu consumers - the rise in food prices, which started as far back as 2007, and i therefore support calls for the commission, together with the national competition authorities, to carry out a thorough investigation of competition in the agri-industrial sector, in particular the development of support, transparency and consumer prices along the entire value chain.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because competition policy is crucial to respond to the economic and financial crisis, to support the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, to support the single market and to make progress towards a banking union, a genuine economic and monetary union, greater integration and convergence. it is important to note that competition policy is one of the key aspects of the european social market economy. it is essential to align eu competition policy with all other eu policies, including sectoral regulation, to ensure that the internal market for products and services functions well from the point of view of citizens, the environment and businesses. emphasising that competition policy in a broader sense should not only strengthen established firms and suppliers of goods and services, but should also pursue the overarching objective of facilitating the entry of new players and the emergence of new ideas and technologies, thus maximising the benefits for the citizens of the european union. i believe that only by supporting and implementing competition policy effectively can we strengthen the single market, revive economic growth and make the european market more attractive on a global scale.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal, as a competition policy based on the principles of open markets and a level playing field in all sectors is part of the so-called genetic code of the eu and one of the fundamental aspects of the european social market economy, a tool for the benefit of european consumers in order to ensure a socially and economically sound internal market and to combat abuses by certain economic operators, and a key factor in ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market. the removal of barriers to the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital is a crucial precondition for eu growth. protectionism will only deepen and prolong the crisis and strict compliance with competition rules is essential to revive the european economy. the annual competition policy report should be used not only as a description of the practical implementation of competition policy by the commission but also as a tool to help increase the overall competitiveness of the european union, develop competition and open markets to new entrants, thus expanding and strengthening the internal market.

in writing. − competition policy plays a crucial role in responding effectively to challenges in difficult times, especially in the context of the banking crisis. in order to maintain a level playing field and an open and dynamic market, it is essential to further improve the effectiveness of competition policy. in particular, competition policy must be aligned with all other eu policies. new entrants must be provided with favourable, non-discriminatory conditions for entering the market. only fair competition between market participants promotes innovation, efficiency and freedom of choice. each of us needs to feel the real benefits. the level of consumer welfare and protection must be continuously improved. the principles and rules of competition must ensure the accessibility, simplicity and flexibility of services of general economic interest and of general social interest. in addition, strict competition policy measures must prevent speculation on food markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on democratic decision-making in the future economic and monetary union (emu). the aim is to strengthen coordination of economic policy reforms at eu level in accordance with the community method and in line with the instruments of the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. i believe that any further initiative for a strong ems based on stability, sustainable growth, solidarity and democracy would be implemented in accordance with the community method. when new competences are transferred to or created at union level, or new union institutions are established, it is necessary to ensure an appropriate level of democratic control and accountability of parliament. the delay in the establishment of a banking union is a cause for concern. i agree that a strong and ambitious banking union is a key component of a deeper ems and that it is therefore essential to establish it as soon as possible.

the rapporteur. − i will speak about another document on the european union guidelines on the promotion and protection of freedom of religion or belief. i am pleased that the vote in the committee on foreign affairs on our draft recommendations adopted all the compromise amendments and additions, i.e. that all the political groups were able to agree on the most important points. i regret that the vote on the individual provisions of the draft recommendation did not result in agreement and that some of my colleagues from the political groups voted against the whole document. i would like to highlight a few points in this discussion, hoping that this will serve to bring about a better mutual understanding and agreement on the matter under discussion. i would like to recall, first of all, that back in 2010 and 2011, when the european parliament adopted its annual report on the situation of human rights in the world, it called on the other institutions of the european union, and in particular the council of the eu, to adopt a wide-ranging set of measures aimed at promoting the right to freedom of religion or belief in the context of the eu's external policy. the european parliament welcomed the commitment of the european union to develop guidelines on freedom of religion or belief, based on the eu action plan on human rights and democracy, and stressed the need for the european parliament and civil society organisations to be involved in the development of these guidelines. what prompted the european union and the european parliament to act? first, the recognition that the promotion of the right to freedom of religion or belief and the prevention of violations of that right must be a priority of the european union's external policy. secondly, there is a continuing pattern of violence, persecution and discrimination against religious communities and against people with minority or non-religious beliefs in many parts of the world. the lack of religious tolerance, of readiness for inter-religious dialogue and of ecumenical coexistence often leads to political unrest, which leads to violence and open armed conflicts that endanger human lives and undermine regional stability. our guidelines and recommendations aim to promote and protect freedom of religion or belief in third countries, to integrate freedom of religion or belief into all eu external action and human rights policy, and to develop clear guidelines, criteria, standards and practical guidance to enhance the promotion of freedom of religion or belief in the work of officials from the institutions of the european union and the member states. in this way, we aim to ensure greater coherence, effectiveness and visibility of the european union's external policy. we emphasise in our recommendations a number of important aspects that need to be clearly and unambiguously enshrined in the guidelines in order to avoid their excessive free interpretation and to ensure effective implementation of the guidelines, including proportionality, freedom of expression, the collective aspect of freedom of religion or belief, registration requirements, family and social law and many others. i must say that some of them have received mixed reviews in the political groups of the european parliament. some colleagues feel that our recommendations generally talk too much about religion or faith. but, ladies and gentlemen, that is precisely what the whole document is about: the promotion and defence of freedom of religion or belief, the right to exercise this universal and fundamental human right. and that's why we're talking about this freedom, about its place in the context of other freedoms, about finding the right balance between principles like freedom of religion and freedom of expression.
mr president, here in parliament where we are expected to voice the stand of the entire union, we often appear in a shaky position because of the political vocabulary we use. the same words – democracy, law, judiciary etc. – contain and express a range of meanings. law in a democracy and law in a dictatorship, or authoritarianism, are totally different things. they should not, therefore, be referred to in the same terms. who will dare to speak, in brussels or in ekaterinberg, about the full spectrum of russia’s undemocratic and oppressive laws – including laws that close down media outlets – and to call them not simply ‘laws’ but, putting it politely, ‘authoritarian laws’? when we are calling for or issuing directives about the rule of law, in relation to some new or mutant dictatorship, the request should refer to the rule of ‘non-authoritarian law’. i do not need to remind you of the variety of bloody regimes calling themselves, or defining themselves as, democracies – ranging right through to the democracy of cannibals. courts, when they are the merely procedural chambers for shaping punishments, in line with phone calls from the highest levels of the executive, should be referred to on paper not as ‘courts’ but rather as ‘specialised chambers of execution’. despite our talk of democracy as an international principle, a more appropriate way to describe such illegal institutions would be as courts of skull-hunters, torturing their victims with endlessly renewed or additional charges.
the rapporteur. − thank you to all the colleagues who have spoken in this debate on the report on the european union guidelines on freedom of religion or belief. i am sorry that for serious reasons i have not been able to be in this chamber all the time, but i would like to make a few more general remarks. some colleagues spoke about the right to refuse to act on grounds of religious belief and how it was reflected in our draft recommendations. it includes the right of a person to a clearly defined refusal to act on the grounds of personal, religious convictions, when this is relevant to other morally sensitive matters. i would remind you that the european council, in its resolution of 24 april this year, called on the member states to guarantee the right to a strict refusal of action on grounds of internal convictions, moral convictions or ethical considerations, for example in matters of military service, as well as in matters of health care and education. the draft recommendations are therefore fully in line with the position of the council of europe. this is all the more so since it is emphasised that the right to refuse to act on the basis of such convictions must be strictly and clearly defined, thus preventing excessive freedom of interpretation, discrimination and abuse of this right. another important aspect is education and training. our aim is to draw attention to the fact that, as established by internationally recognised standards, a child's parents or legal guardians are free to ensure that their child receives religious education in accordance with their religious or moral convictions. this provision is also enshrined in the united nations declaration on the elimination of all forms of intolerance and of discrimination based on religion or belief.
in writing. under international law, all states are obliged to ensure that citizens are effectively protected against persecution on account of their religion or belief. this discrimination still exists in all regions of the world. of particular concern are the violence and legal restrictions that are imposed on christian congregations. the communication underlines the need for the european union to condemn all forms of violence and discrimination in the field of religion or belief. the communication also encourages the strengthening of the legal protection of believers in third countries. the focus is on the promotion of greater religious freedom and respect for personal beliefs in the work of the institutions of the european union and the member states. unfortunately, this record is not fully respected even in the european parliament, and its members are experiencing this. examples of this phenomenon are two written statements i made concerning the protection of life and family values in europe, which were not even registered. the reason given was my articulated calls for the protection of life from conception to natural death, which arose out of my worldview. thus, the ep secretariat not only violated the freedom of speech and the independence of the activities of meps, but also applied censorship to the right to freedom of belief and expression. the report recommends that respect for religious beliefs be required of certain mep bureaucrats. i sincerely hope that my aforementioned written statement will be registered for the third time.
in writing. first of all, i am pleased to see a positive assessment of the achievement of the millennium development goals: the global target of halving extreme poverty by 2015, significant improvements in access to drinking water, an increase in school-age children and progress in reducing child and maternal mortality. with a view to the future post-2015 development agenda, i support the emphasis on the importance of supporting public health and ensuring decent work opportunities. full and productive employment and decent work should be set as the main objective of the post-2015 agenda. we must also support the objective of well-designed national minimum social protection systems in developing countries, as this is a crucial backbone in the fight against poverty and in building social resilience to poverty. we need to integrate the sdgs into the programme, in other words, taking care of vulnerable groups - women, children, the elderly and the disabled - and tackling the structural causes of poverty. because social inequality hinders economic development, increases crime rates, and fuels conflict within society. i also agree that the preparation and implementation of the post-2015 world development agenda should aim at ensuring respect for the principles of democratic governance and respect for human rights, and that the future agenda should clearly reflect a commitment to democratic governance that is respected.
rapporteur. − mr president, just to clarify a formulation in this paragraph, i propose to add one word: ‘religious’. the text will now read as follows: ‘the right of parents to educate their children according to their religious or non-religious convictions includes their right to deny any undue interference by state or non-state actors in their religious education opposed to their religious or non-religious convictions’.

i voted for this document because we all recognise that freedom of the press is an important issue and must be guaranteed in all countries of the world. these freedoms and the expression of ideas can be restricted in various ways. unfortunately, it also often depends on external actions, such as, say, a digital attack. this is the kind of attack that was recently launched on the largest internet portals in lithuania, my country. those attacks were organised from third countries, in relation to which certain texts were published which may have caused offence in third countries. these attacks are specifically tied to the content of specific news stories. i therefore believe that the european commission should pay more attention to digital security as one of the factors that safeguards press freedom. we should also talk more about creating a common framework for responding to digital attacks so that the same freedom of expression is guaranteed across the european union and the world.

(be careful, journalists are human rights defenders, whose rights are often violated and who are often persecuted and killed.) therefore, i think that we need to have our own policies and programmes that promote freedom of speech and media freedom around the world. it should be noted that the law on media freedom ensures the protection of the rights of the public, in particular the rights of the government, but the government also has the right to defend the rights of the public in the cases described below, and to lodge complaints with the judicial authorities if appropriate legal information is required. of course, the free, independent and pluralistic internet and the mainstream media are the only democratic and pluralistic foundations, and it is therefore of the utmost importance to ensure freedom of movement worldwide. the european union should set an example by ensuring that the media continue to be independent, pluralistic and diverse, and by protecting journalists and journalists' rights, freedom and security. the european commission, in particular the directorate-general for development and cooperation (devco) and the european external action service (eeas) should therefore manage their cooperation and programme coordination, in particular by ensuring the coordination of police and diplomatic activities, the use of funds and the implementation of projects, including joint monitoring and evaluation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu needs a sound financial sector to revive the economy. in order to improve the efficiency and resilience of the financial markets in the european union as quickly as possible, it is necessary to urgently adopt the outstanding proposals of the european commission on financial services and to work towards the establishment of a common bank resolution mechanism. it is important to note that the european parliament, in its resolution on shadow banking, called for additional measures on money market funds, in particular to improve their resilience and cover liquidity risks. the council should therefore resume negotiations on deposit guarantee schemes, as this issue is of particular importance and concerns the direct interests of citizens of the european union, and is also important for confidence in the financial system and its stability. it is envisaged that, once an effective resolution system and an effective single supervisory mechanism are in place, the long-term objective could be to establish a single european deposit guarantee fund, backed by adequate funding, thus enhancing credibility and investor confidence. i believe that the council and the member states need more capacity and determination to implement the agreements which could lead to the creation of a banking union.
in writing. − on the morning of 31 may 2013, turkish police used disproportionate force to disperse a group of protesters protesting against construction in istanbul's gezi park, killing four people and injuring over a thousand. the right to freedom of expression, the right to freedom of legitimate assembly and the right to peaceful protest are integral to a democratic state. the position of the turkish leadership at this stage is particularly important in terms of its ability to adopt a moderate, compromise and reconciliatory stance, to take into account the demands of a part of the public, to properly investigate and prosecute the officials responsible for the use of excessive force and the injury and death of people. closer contact with the public, for example through consultations on community and urban projects, would help to avoid similar incidents in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to ensure better coordination and good governance of development issues at international level in order to enable the eu to be united and visible. the european external action service (eeas) established for this purpose is a new service based on community and intergovernmental resources, unparalleled in the eu, and cannot therefore be expected to operate at full capacity two years after its establishment. despite the significant progress made in establishing the eeas, the adoption and implementation of operational decisions on the common security and defence policy is seen as an excessively slow process, in many cases for structural and procedural reasons. the eeas's capabilities should therefore be developed, and previous operational experience analysed and learnt, in particular on conflict prevention, conflict mediation, crisis management, reconciliation and peace-building. in the light of these comments, it is appropriate to simplify the governance structure of the eeas and to strengthen the role of the executive secretary-general by establishing a clear chain of command to help to improve decision-making efficiency and timely political response.
in writing. − the eeas assists the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy in ensuring the coherence of the union's external action in the various fields, the unity, consistency and effectiveness of the eu's external action, and is involved in the protection of the rights of eu citizens in third countries. the eeas started its operations in 2011. building on two years of experience of the work of the eeas, the european parliament makes recommendations to strengthen the flexibility of the service, its rapid response to crises, to enable rapid reallocation of resources, efficient management of funds and other aspects that strengthen the functioning and organisation of the eeas.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft council decision and in favour of opening the possibility for the contracting parties to the vienna convention to accede to the 1997 protocol. international nuclear liability is governed by two instruments: the vienna convention and the 1960 paris convention on third party liability in the field of nuclear energy. the two conventions set out similar basic principles. the vienna convention was adopted to provide adequate and fair compensation for the victims of nuclear accidents and it establishes a specific civil liability regime in the field of nuclear energy. in order to address the remaining differences between member states regarding the rules on the recognition and enforcement of judgments in the field of nuclear damage, the commission undertook to consider how the future proposal could address the issue of the priority of union rules in the member states that ratified the 1997 protocol before its accession to the european union, namely latvia and romania, and in the member states that are parties to the paris convention. the council therefore proposes to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, lithuania, poland, slovakia and hungary, to ratify or accede to the 1997 protocol. a similar solution was proposed for the 2004 protocol amending the paris convention.

in writing. - i voted for this document. international nuclear liability is governed by two instruments: the vienna convention and the 1960 paris convention on third party liability in the field of nuclear energy. the two conventions share similar basic principles: the first was adopted to compensate victims of nuclear accidents, thus providing for specific civil liability. in order to eliminate the remaining differences between member states in the rules on the recognition and enforcement of judgments in the field of nuclear damage, the commission undertook to consider and make proposals for the formulation of the primacy of eu law in the individual member states. the council proposes to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, lithuania, poland, slovakia and hungary, to ratify or accede to the 1997 protocol. the proposal for a council decision provides that the united kingdom and ireland are to be bound by and subject to this decision if they participate in its adoption, in accordance with protocol 21 annexed to the treaty on the functioning of the european union, and that denmark is not bound by it if it does not participate. i therefore supported the rapporteur's recommendation to endorse the council decision.

in writing. − operators of nuclear power plants are responsible for any damage caused by them, regardless of fault. nuclear damage is not an event that affects only one country, which creates difficulties when attempting to figure out how to manage the process of handling the damage caused. therefore, regulations governing international nuclear liability are necessary and have been created. the two main forms of this regulation are the vienna convention and the paris convention on third party liability. these conventions provide adequate and fair compensation to victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents. however, although the eu is part of these conventions, some member states ratified the 1997 protocol prior to their accession. this has resulted in a lack of uniformity among member states and means that there are differences in how some member states would handle the procedure for recognition and enforcement of judgments in cases of nuclear damage. i voted in favour of this report because it is important for there to be uniform accountability in all member states so that victims can be compensated correctly.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to support and ensure the application of roadworthiness tests for motor vehicles to improve road safety and environmental protection. the proposal improves compliance with roadside inspection and roadworthiness tests, in particular where the technical condition of a vehicle poses an immediate risk to road safety, by means of measures such as temporary suspension of registration of a vehicle and final withdrawal of registration. it also simplifies bureaucratic procedures, for example by providing for the possibility of withdrawing the registration of a vehicle in the member state in which it is registered if the vehicle is re-registered in another member state or dismantled and scrapped. in order to reduce the administrative burden and to facilitate the exchange of information between member states, information relating to vehicles should be stored in national electronic registers, and in order to facilitate checks and, in particular, to prevent fraud and illegal trade in stolen vehicles, as well as to check the validity of the certificate of inspection, it is appropriate for member states to cooperate closely and to exchange information effectively by using national electronic databases.

in writing. − i have voted in favour of this document, which establishes a list of chemicals that pose a serious threat to or through the eu's aquatic environment. chemical pollution is one of the reasons for the continuously increasing impact on the aquatic environment and the availability and quality of safe and clean water. therefore, one of the most important aspects of sustainable water management is the implementation of appropriate water chemical pollution control measures. the commission proposal amends the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive in order to update the list of priority substances in the field of water policy, as required to be done at least every four years under the water framework directive. the commission proposal adds 15 new priority substances to the list of chemicals, 6 of which are identified as priority hazardous substances, introduces a requirement to measure the concentration of several substances, for example in fish or crustaceans, and introduces a new watch list mechanism for monitoring substances of potential concern in order to collect data for future priority determinations of substances.

first of all, i would like to thank mrs ingeborg gräßle for her truly enormous work and efforts to strengthen the european anti-fraud office. olaf is a very important institution, it is the backbone of the european union's budgetary protection and anti-fraud system. the number of fraud cases and irregularities reported is constantly increasing, which shows not only the growing importance of this service but also the need to strengthen it. the proposed reform aims to further improve the efficiency of its operations while ensuring the independence of the investigations carried out by the office. it is regrettable that the debate today is much more intense on the current disagreements and the division of powers between olaf and its supervisory committee than on the reform of olaf itself, which, as the commissioner said, is the result of seven years of hard work. olaf has about 500 staff and their work should not be hindered by similar interinstitutional disputes. the proposed reform would not only improve the efficiency of the work of these staff but also strengthen cooperation between olaf and the national competent authorities and enhance the rights of persons involved in investigations. this compromise text between the council and parliament may not be ideal for both sides, but the rules it lays down will make olaf's investigations much more effective than they are now. no reform is perfect, but a reform of olaf would be a first serious step towards improving the work of this institution and ensuring its independence. as a shadow rapporteur, i therefore propose, in the light of reality, that this compromise text, as agreed with the council, be adopted without amendments.

i would like to begin by thanking the rapporteurs, both derek vaughan and ms a. česková, for their efforts in preparing this very important report on the 2011 anti-fraud report. the same problem emerges every year: some member states do not provide data on fraud and irregularities in a timely manner or their data are not accurate and reliable. in order to obtain all the necessary and reliable data, it is necessary to adopt as soon as possible uniform reporting principles in all member states, as i noted in my report on this matter back in 2012. this would allow us to see the real, i repeat, real scale of fraud in the member states and identify the member states where it is highest and take appropriate measures, which is not the case in current practice. this would also allow the member states to monitor the implementation of olaf's investigative recommendations. i would therefore like to reiterate that i propose that the commission take responsibility for the introduction of a uniform system in all member states in this respect.

'united in diversity' is the motto of the union. the european union promotes cultural and linguistic diversity. unfortunately, even today, in the 21st century, there are countries in the union that do not follow these rules and do not respect the rights of indigenous minorities. denmark or finland can be good examples in dealing with these issues. i hope that the president will implement these standards. europe, in order to emerge from the crisis of values, must go back to its roots, must return to the founding ideas and ideas of which robert schumann spoke so much, must build its identity on the basis of universal christian values. like my colleagues in the cor, i believe that europe must remain the europe of the twelve. this will allow us to preserve our identity and cultural diversity. a europe of growth, a europe of equal opportunities, a europe of values, a europe of solidarity - these are the ideas that should define the direction of the lithuanian presidency.
for the efd group i am happy and proud that 3 million citizens of my country will be able to show their country, culture, traditions in six months. i believe that lithuanian politicians, ministers and diplomats will be able to find words and solutions that will bring together the heads of european states and the citizens of those states for joint work. the presidency of the council of the european union is not only an honour but also a great responsibility, especially today, when the european union is going through some very difficult times. in the economic and political spheres, new decisiveness and flexible diplomacy are needed to reach agreements. i do not know if we have been talking about the common european interest for too long. but i am sure that each member of the community has been too long looking only at its own interests in energy, trade or politics. the attempt to unify many things has been too long and too thorough, leaving aside the essential and most important things, the political and civil rights, culture and history of the states. these are the things that unite the countries of europe. i hope that the lithuanian presidency will be worthy of the achievement of king mindaugas, a process of european unity. i therefore welcome you, madam president, to the strasbourg chamber. i think that's what i'm saying, and you're going to hear a lot of different kinds of proposals here. i would just like to congratulate you, wish you success, fortitude, perseverance, rejoice in the right priorities and wish you well that after six months in the european union there will be more lithuanians. good luck to you. consolidated and sovereign party of global dialogue. it so happened that lithuania became a forerunner of the union’s policy of unbundling energy markets, turning them away from the temptations to in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the rules applicable to depositaries laid down in the ucits directive have not changed since 1985. the ucits master rule requires that all assets of the ucits fund be entrusted to the depositary. the depositary shall be liable under national law for losses resulting from the failure to fulfil its obligations. the ucits directive shall contain a reference to national law which further specifies those obligations. this reference leaves a wide margin of discretion to interpret the depositary's obligations and the liability for negligence in discharging them differently. different interpretations have led to different approaches across the european union and therefore to different levels of protection for ucits investors in different jurisdictions. recent high-profile cases such as madoff and lehman brothers have highlighted a fundamental change in the field of ucits: the ucits provisions for depositaries have remained unchanged, while the ucits investment environment has evolved, and ucits have been able to invest in a wider range of financial assets that can be more complex, as well as issued and held in a depository outside the eu (for example in emerging markets). the new rules will, inter alia, ensure that each ucits fund will be assigned a single depositary. this rule aims to ensure that a single fund does not use the services of several depositaries. it also aims to ensure sufficient harmonisation of the relevant regulatory requirements of the different member states and to further define the tasks and obligations of depositaries, the legal entities that may be designated as depositaries and the responsibilities of depositaries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it supports the european parliament's amendments to the directive on the laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities, which are designed to take account of market developments and the experience gained so far by market participants and supervisors. in particular, this directive aims at harmonising national provisions relating to the obligations and liability of depositaries, remuneration policies and sanctions. the amendments to this directive were initiated to address the potential adverse impact of poorly designed remuneration structures on sound risk management and control of the risks assumed by individuals. the revised directive will aim to impose a clear obligation on management companies of collective investment undertakings to develop and implement remuneration policies and practices for certain categories of employees that are consistent with sound and effective risk management.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. it should be noted that the wage policy in place has had a significant impact on the scale of the crisis, which makes it necessary to restore consumer confidence and ensure the functioning of an efficient and well-integrated financial system. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 concerning the conditions for the granting of authorisations for the placing on the market of securities issued by undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities. in this context, it is necessary to provide greater legal certainty and to ensure a uniform legal regulation. common provisions relating to depositary functions, remuneration policies and sanctions should apply throughout the eu. remuneration, costs and charges should be proportionate to the sound, effective management of risk. it is also essential that the variable remuneration component be linked to the size of the fund or the value of the assets under management. all entities responsible for remuneration policy shall be independent and competent in the management of risk and remuneration.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and the referral back to the environment committee. the eu emissions trading system is the most important tool to reduce industrial pollution in the eu in a cost-effective and efficient way. in 2008, emissions fell by 10% after the start of the second trading period. the initial objective was to create a market-based measure to stimulate the price of carbon dioxide, thereby encouraging investment in low-carbon technology and renewable energy. however, the decrease in emissions in the second trading period could be strongly influenced by the economic downturn, which reduced economic activity and production. by the end of 2011, there was a surplus of 955 million allowances and this is expected to increase. as the surplus of allowances far exceeds demand, the price of carbon dioxide has fallen from eur 30 per tonne to eur 7 per tonne. this decline in the price of carbon is in contradiction with the increase in sustainable scientific and technological innovation and therefore reduces the incentive to invest in low-carbon technologies and increases the risk of the european union becoming dependent on carbon-intensive infrastructure. however, this issue is of particular importance for the eu industry as sudden changes in this market can have a negative impact on the competitiveness of the eu industry as a whole. i believe that this issue needs to be considered in great detail and that an effective compromise needs to be found between the need to ensure the competitiveness of eu industry and eu climate change policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a contribution by parliament to the amendment of directive 2003/87/ec to clarify the provisions on the timing of the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances. the eu emissions trading system is the key tool to reduce industrial pollution in the eu in a cost-effective and efficient way. despite the fact that emissions have decreased since the introduction of the eu emissions trading system, there are currently significant inconsistencies in the system. in recent years, the market has experienced a large surplus of allowances, which has led to a sharp fall in their market price. this decrease in the price of allowances is in contrast to the significant increase in sustainable scientific and technological innovation and therefore becomes a disincentive to invest in low-carbon technology and increases the risk of the european union becoming dependent on carbon-intensive infrastructure. the report seeks to address the inconsistency in the current eu emissions trading system and proposes to adopt short-term and long-term measures.
in writing. − today we have just confirmed our position allowing the commission to intervene temporarily in the functioning of the ets. i can repeat my opinion that this is a necessary solution, but it does not solve the problem at its core. i therefore urge all stakeholders to present the guidelines for the ets reform as soon as possible.
in writing. − for legal clarity and market predictability and stability, it is essential that allowances are allocated optimally and fairly. in particular, the timing of the auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances should ensure fair competition. in addition, a properly balanced market must be in place, as too much short-term supply may lead to excessive price fluctuations. at eu level, we need to support the development of innovative low-carbon technologies. to address the challenges of the transition to a low-carbon economy as effectively as possible. in addition, common measures should be established to reduce costs and carbon emissions in energy-intensive industrial sectors in a cost-effective and cost-effective manner. only through joint efforts and effective measures will the eu have an effective emissions trading system.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in the light of recent crises such as the 2009 h1n1 pandemic, the 2010 volcanic ash cloud and the 2011 e. coli outbreak, the commission has put forward a proposal to establish measures and structures to effectively protect all eu citizens from a wide range of cross-border health threats. the commission proposal will extend and improve the system for the early warning and response of communicable diseases established in 1998 to strengthen the union's capacity to respond to major cross-border health threats by providing it with resources, networks and structures complementing the measures already in place to combat these threats. i share the european parliament's view that, given the global scale of such crises or pandemics, it is necessary to strengthen the cooperation of the actors in the system with the competent international organisations, in particular the world health organisation (who).
in writing. − the commission presented a proposal on 8 december 2011 to establish a set of tools and structures to effectively protect all eu citizens against a wide range of cross-border health threats. this proposal for a decision builds on existing structures by supplementing them with the following measures: extension of the risk assessment and coordination measures currently applied to communicable diseases to cover all threats of biological, chemical or ecological origin; strengthening of the role of the health security committee to better coordinate crisis response measures; better preparedness for crises in the member states in coordination with the ec; possibility of recognising a european 'public health emergency' to speed up the provision of medicines needed to deal with a crisis; adoption by the european commission of emergency international measures at eu level in the event of an exceptional situation. for the sake of clarity and legal certainty, this decision repeals decision no 2119/98/ec on the establishment of a community network for the epidemiological surveillance and control of communicable diseases. i appreciate the proposal and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. − transboundary health threats are associated with human pathogens. the general hygiene measures recommended by the world health organisation can be very useful in reducing the spread of these pathogens. national preparedness and response planning can help to reduce their spread. to achieve greater efficiency, it is useful to collect such information within the institutions of the european union, thus enabling member states to exchange knowledge and experience quickly and efficiently.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. it is essential that all eu citizens are effectively protected against cross-border health threats and have access to the necessary medicines in a timely manner. the eu must have an effective crisis management model that prevents serious economic consequences and ensures the independence and transparency of aid in this context, it is necessary to strengthen the capacity to respond to major cross-border threats to health. to ensure that the eu is adequately prepared to respond to potential threats, it is necessary to establish strict coordination, exchange of information and mutual consultation on preparedness and response planning, response procedures and rapid alert and response systems. in order to avoid negative consequences, cooperation with the competent international organisations and third countries should be strengthened. moreover, conflicts of interest should be avoided.
in writing. − recent health crises like the h1n1 ‘pandemic’ in 2009 or e. coli bacteria in 2011 have shown that the ability to respond to these types of incidents is vital. the measures in place at present do not allow for an appropriate reaction to these issues. misuse of medication and the sale of defective medical devices would prevent healthcare providers from responding effectively to a health crisis. i support the extension of the eu-wide early warning and response system to help improve our ability to fight serious health risks. i welcome the goal of increasing access to medication in the event of a european health emergency as well as access to vaccines. each member state must have approved procedures in place to spot and treat individual issues, but eu-wide measures are also necessary to coordinate treatment and prevent any further transmission or spread. i voted in favour of this report as i believe these measures must be taken as soon as possible to ensure readiness when the next health threat arises.
in writing. − in june 2011, the commission presented a package of proposals for reforming the union's own resources system. one of the main ideas was to harmonise the legislation on the taxation of financial transactions in the eu member states by introducing a financial transaction tax (ftt). the commission proposed that two thirds of the revenue from this levy be transferred to the eu budget as own resources. after several months of negotiations between the member states, it became clear that the rules of unanimity in the field of taxation made it impossible to adopt the fsm in the near future. in its report on the commission's initial proposal, the european parliament stated that it would support the proposal to introduce fsm in several member states under the enhanced cooperation procedure. in october 2012, eleven member states decided to pursue the establishment of fis, for the first time under the enhanced cooperation procedure in the field of taxation. although the fms will not be applied in all member states at this stage, the revenue from its collection in the participating countries (estimated at eur 31 billion per year) could be used in full or in part to finance the union budget, while the respective contributions based on gross national income (gni) of those countries would be reduced and contribute to the financing of the union budget from own resources.
in writing. − in 2010, the european parliament, in its report on the financial, economic and social crisis (mid-term report) by mr beres, called for the first time for a financial transaction tax (ftt). in september 2011, the european commission failed to adopt a legislative act on the application of fms at eu level. it was updated in 2012 following a request from 11 member states. in december 2012, the european parliament formally approved the request of eleven member states, and in january 2013 the economic and financial affairs council also endorsed this proposal. in february 2013, the european commission approved a revised proposal for the establishment of fms in 11 member states. i voted in favour of this proposal because the long-standing lack of regulation of financial services has come to the fore in the wake of the global financial crisis. the crisis quickly spread to the real economy and had serious consequences for growth, employment and public finances. to avoid a recurrence of economic crises, decisive and consistent steps are needed to contain them or at least to minimise their consequences for member states, the financial sector and our citizens.
in writing. − the ftt will provide an independent source of eu funding. it will also encourage the creation of a common financial market. enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax should prevent distortions of the tax system and avoidance and evasion of that tax. the measures taken must ensure fair competition and reduce the risk of financial activities being outsourced. it should be noted that the broad tax base and the two low tax rates reduce the harmful distortive effects of the tax. it should be noted that the scope of this tax excludes not only the primary but also other areas of daily financial activity of importance to citizens and businesses. the uniform rates and collection methods applied will ensure the prevention of fraud and tax evasion. it is also essential to ensure that the revenue from the levy is used to finance national and european investment programmes. this will help to ensure a rapid recovery of the economy and employment.
in writing. − i have endorsed the commission's proposal that latvia adopt the euro on 1 january 2014 and join the euro area. in its resolution, the european parliament calls on the latvian government to continue to apply prudent fiscal policy measures and to pursue a common policy of promoting stability by anticipating and reducing possible future macroeconomic imbalances and risks to price stability identified by the commission in the warning mechanism report, and calls on the latvian government to address these issues and to strengthen joint efforts to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 national strategy.
in writing. − this decision did not become a huge celebration in our neighbouring country, as the majority of latvian society is against the introduction of the euro. but is this what is best for a society whose majority is opposed to the euro? this reluctance is by no means based solely on human fears, stubbornness, or patriotic feelings. the first reason is that people do not know what is in store for them or why the euro is so urgently needed now. it is commendable that our neighbours have managed to manage the consequences of the crisis and meet the criteria for adopting the euro, but in view of the public opposition to this step, i abstained.
in writing. − latvia has successfully emerged from a severe economic recession and achieved sustainable and long-term results. the growing economy has made it possible to meet the criteria for the euro in a satisfactory manner. i hope that latvia has chosen the best timing and means for this important moment. the urgency of this matter is unjustified and can have extremely painful consequences. i believe that latvia will be able to continue to ensure fiscal consolidation, a stronger institutional environment and a reduction in the shadow economy. although employment has declined somewhat due to good growth rates, latvia still needs to make greater efforts to reduce long-term unemployment. it is a pity that the introduction of the euro did not receive sufficient support from the latvian citizens. on a matter of such national importance, only the people should have the final say. i would hope that the introduction of the euro will not cause public outrage. people don't know what's coming. solidarity between the authorities and the public is essential.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in 2011, more than 30 000 people were killed in road accidents in the european union and nearly 1,5 million people were reported injured (more than 250 000 people were seriously injured). more than half of all serious injuries occur in urban areas, particularly among pedestrians, motorcyclists, cyclists (including electric bicycles) and other vulnerable road users. pedestrians and cyclists account for 50% of all deaths and a significant proportion of serious injuries in urban areas. i support the european parliament's calls for better implementation of the various existing legislation and measures to reduce the impact of collisions, increase road safety and reduce serious injuries, support the development of safe and smart road infrastructure and combat drunk driving and drug-related driving, and exchange best practices in the assessment and rehabilitation of road traffic offenders.
in writing. − the main causes of road traffic fatalities and serious injuries are equipment failure, road construction, poor road maintenance and driver behaviour, including the ability to choose speed. speed is directly linked to the severity of injuries and some member states are even considering increasing speed limits on motorways. i support the commission's initiative to attach great importance to actions relating to serious injuries in the field of road safety. the commission has established a common eu definition of serious injuries based on the universally accepted classification of injuries according to the maximum abbreviated injury scale. member states shall apply without delay the common eu definition of serious road traffic injury and collect and report statistics by type of transport, including vulnerable road users, and by type of road infrastructure, in 2014 on the basis thereof. the commission should set a broad-based target of reducing road traffic injuries by 40% between 2014 and 2020 and, as a long-term objective, pursue the overall vision of a totally safe road, on the basis of the data collected. i welcome the priorities set by the commission in the development of an overall strategy to address the impact of collisions, the development of a traffic accident management strategy, first aid and emergency services and long-term rehabilitation processes, and therefore the commission should implement these priorities as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. road safety is a matter of great concern to society. the eu's road safety policy must ensure that road users are careful, respect each other and respect the rules of the road. it is essential that the vision of a totally safe traffic is implemented at eu level. it is worth noting that road safety also ensures long-term mobility. it is closely linked to the fields of energy, environment, employment, education, youth, public health, research, innovation and technology, justice, insurance, trade and foreign policy. it is essential that the rights of vulnerable road users are properly protected in the eu. i believe that a common definition of injury suffered in a road traffic accident should be applied throughout the eu. this will allow for better monitoring and evaluation of the effectiveness of road safety policy. only by working together can we reduce the number of people injured in road accidents. it is therefore appropriate to harmonise the road traffic rules, road signs and road marking of the member states. it should be noted that speed is a major factor in the increase in road fatalities and greenhouse gas emissions. therefore, the enforcement of road traffic rules and the deterrence of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs should be strengthened.
