in writing. − in every country, hungary and others alike, the principles of separation of powers, judicial independence, respect for private and family life and the right to effective legal protection must be strictly respected. any democratic institutional system must be based on the principle of the separation of powers and a system of checks and balances. no legal regulation may infringe fundamental rights or undermine mutual trust between member states. in this context, a monitoring system should be applied on a regular basis to ensure that member states properly respect the union's fundamental values, democratic requirements and the rule of law. it should be noted that the eu's general principles are not only political commitments but also legal indicators against which the eu legal system and the member states' legal systems are assessed. they must therefore be respected at both cross-border and domestic level. a proper balance must be struck between respect for national identity and presence in the eu.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in recent years, natural and man-made disasters have increased in severity, complexity and impact in europe. most of the natural disasters caused by floods have recently occurred in many central european countries, including austria, the czech republic, germany, hungary, poland, slovakia, france and spain. the floods have caused serious damage to cities and municipalities, infrastructure, businesses, agriculture and rural areas, and, by destroying parts of the natural and cultural heritage, have also caused deaths and injuries and forced thousands of people to flee their homes. the european union solidarity fund (esf) was set up to respond to major national disasters and provide financial assistance to disaster-stricken countries. the european union civil protection mechanism also helps member states to cooperate and minimise the impact of an emergency. however, there is a further need to strengthen the union's preventive capacity to respond to all types of natural disasters and to improve the effectiveness and coordination of the various union measures for the sustainable prevention of natural disasters.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the financial crisis was triggered by a weak european regulatory framework and excessive risk-taking, excessive levels of indebtedness, insufficient capital and liquidity requirements, an overly complex banking system as a whole, an overly large banking sector in small economies, inadequate control and supervision, excessive expansion of derivatives trading, mis-rating, excessive bonus schemes and inadequate risk management. i agree with the suggestions in the ep resolution that structural reform of the banking sector must reduce excessive risk, ensure competition, improve corporate governance and encourage banks to establish more transparent organisational structures, increase accountability and strengthen a reliable and sustainable remuneration system, and enable effective bank recovery and resolution.
in writing. − in february 2012, the commission set up a high-level expert group to examine whether further structural reforms of the eu banking sector would help reduce the likelihood and impact of bank failures and ensure the continuity of key economic functions in the event of a bank failure, in order to better protect retail banking customers. the experts' report indicates that the financial crisis was caused by excessive risk-taking, excessive leverage, insufficient capital and liquidity requirements and excessive complexity of the banking system as a whole. i voted in favour of this document because it is necessary to continue and implement structural reforms, in particular the legal separation of certain risky financial activities within the banking group from deposit-taking banks. separation of activities is the most effective way to ensure simpler and more transparent banking structures. it is essential that the reform of the eu banking structure establishes a safe, stable and efficient banking system, with a particular focus on lending to smes and start-ups. in order to change the banking culture, the document sets out the following key principles: reducing system complexity, increasing competition, reducing risky and commercial links, improving corporate governance, creating a sound remuneration system, creating the conditions for effective bank recovery and restructuring, increasing bank capital and lending to the real economy.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution. it should be noted that the eu banking sector has been facing radical structural changes, which require not only the strengthening of the european financial supervision and crisis management structure, but also the implementation of substantial structural reforms in banks. we need to ensure that the eu has a safe, stable, efficient and effective banking system. banking problems should not be solved at the expense of the taxpayer. first, fair competition must be ensured and the risk of redundancy reduced. banks should be encouraged to develop more transparent organisational structures and enhance accountability. it is essential that the eu single market is adequately protected against fragmentation. i think the commission should make a greater effort to establish a depositors' priority rule. in addition, in order to strengthen consumer protection, an agreement on the deposit guarantee schemes directive should be reached as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. last year, i was appointed as the draftsman of the 2010 annual report of the committee on budgetary control. it should be noted that only a small part of the shortcomings identified in my report last year have been addressed. however, the collection of data from member states on possible and detected and detected fraud remains a major problem, which has been ongoing for several decades. the failure of member states to provide data in a timely manner, or the inaccuracy and incomparability of the data they provide, means that there is no way to objectively assess the real extent of fraud in the eu member states, and that the ep, the commission and olaf cannot properly carry out their functions in relation to the assessment of the situation and the submission of further proposals. such a situation must not be tolerated and the commission must take full responsibility for the recovery of the funds wrongfully paid and collect all the necessary harmonised data that can be compared, establishing reporting principles in all member states. it is also incomprehensible that olaf does not receive from the member states information on the action taken when olaf has transmitted information on fraud to the responsible authority of the member state concerned. these issues are also reflected in the 2011 report, and i therefore urge the commission to take real action in the area of data collection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it expresses the european parliament's position on the 2011 annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests. fighting fraud. in its report, the european parliament welcomes the commission's annual report, but regrets that it contains only data from the member states. parliament notes that the data provided by member states alone should not be used as a basis for the annual report, as member states define similar offences differently and do not all collect detailed statistics of a similar nature using common criteria, making it difficult to obtain reliable and comparable statistics at eu level. for this reason, it is not possible to assess the actual overall extent of irregularities and fraud in individual member states or, as parliament has repeatedly requested, to identify and rank member states with the highest levels of irregularities and fraud.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because the protection of the financial interests of the european union (eu) is a priority for the european institutions and for all of us. the commission must closely monitor the effectiveness of the supervisory and control systems in place in the member states and ensure that information on the extent of irregularities in the member states reflects the real situation. member states do not provide data on fraud and irregularities in a timely manner or their data are not accurate. in order to obtain all the necessary and comparable data, uniform reporting principles in all member states should be adopted as soon as possible. this would allow the real extent of fraud in the member states to be seen and the member states where it is highest to be identified and appropriate measures taken. it would also allow the member states to monitor the implementation of the investigative recommendations of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the weaknesses prevent an objective assessment of the real extent of fraud in the eu member states and the proper performance by parliament, the commission and olaf of their functions relating to the assessment of the situation and the submission of follow-up proposals. this situation must therefore not be tolerated and the commission must take full responsibility for the recovery of the funds wrongfully paid and collect all the necessary harmonised data that can be compared to establish reporting principles in all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because fraud is a phenomenon that harms the eu's financial interests and must be eliminated without delay. the fight against tax fraud must be a priority for both the eu and each member state. in particular, fair, sustainable and more citizen-friendly tax systems are needed to combat tax evasion effectively. it should be noted that high taxation has particularly harmful effects and increases the potential for tax evasion and fraud. businesses are failing, businesses are moving to more favorable countries, and unemployment is rising. but tax evasion must not become the only way to survive. the fight against tax evasion and fraud must be legal. it shall not infringe the privacy and personal freedom and other fundamental rights of citizens. but prevention and detection alone are not enough. the need for effective law enforcement remains. it is necessary to ensure better cooperation and coordination in the application of strong sanctions and dissuasive measures against unfair practices.
in writing. − in november 2010, the european court of auditors stated for the tenth time that it did not have sufficient assurance on payments under all parts of the general budget. as early as 2005, the commission decided to take steps to obtain a positive statement of assurance (sfa). in june 2005, the commission adopted an action plan for an integrated internal control system, which was launched in 2006. this european parliament working document therefore aims to assess the progress and results achieved by the european commission in implementing the action plan and raises questions about the future of the integrated internal control system. i agree that there must be proper control and audit in the commission, but it must be acknowledged that this is much more difficult to do in the commission than in other eu institutions, since in that case the member states must be fully involved in this reform, as they now manage 80% of eu funds under shared management. the managing authorities of the member states are required to submit their accounts to the commission annually, together with a management declaration, their annual final audit report and a summary of the checks carried out, and the opinion of the independent audit body. member states may provide signed voluntary declarations, but in practice the main problem with the current system of annual summaries is related to the reliability of the data provided by the member states. i support the calls for a common form for voluntary declarations and a mandatory form for information to be provided in order to allow the information to be compared and used in the audit.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. effective integrated internal controls ensure the efficient execution of the eu budget. it is essential that both the commission and the individual member states make further progress in improving the quality of financial management. greater attention should be paid to simplification of legislation. in addition, urgent action is needed to reduce the persistent level of errors and to increase the accuracy and reliability of the data provided. it should be noted that the complex and unclear rules in place create an enabling environment for fraud. they are also the main obstacles to the effective implementation of programmes. i think that countries should pay more attention to strengthening their supervisory and control systems. the principles of sound financial management, which ensure the transparent use of taxpayers' funds, must be implemented in order to restore public confidence.

in writing. − following the inaugural meeting of the implementation committee, the ep delegation decided to give the ep negotiating team the mandate to open negotiations. four tripartite dialogues were held and a political agreement was reached. on the evening of 28 may 2013, a meeting of the conciliation committee on macro-financial assistance to georgia took place. the conciliation committee approved the final compromise text. the main objective of this package was to reach agreement on a procedure for providing macro-financial assistance to georgia (eur 46 million) to help it stabilise its economy and meet its balance of payments needs. the council and parliament have diverged on this issue. in the parliament's view, this should be done by the advisory procedure as proposed by the commission, but the council considers that the examination procedure would be more appropriate. instead of the tripartite dialogue, an informal meeting of parliament and the council took place, at which an informal agreement was reached on the 'actual text'. in this context, it was agreed that the advisory procedure would apply for macro-financial assistance up to eur 90 million and that the examination procedure would apply for amounts higher. other main aspects of the compromise can be summarised as follows: an agreement was also reached on a stricter wording relating to the payment of the aid. finally, it was agreed to include a recital in the decision on macro-financial assistance to georgia explaining that the application of the advisory committee procedure is approved as a general rule where the aid does not exceed eur 90 million. i voted for this proposal.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because it is essential to unlock the full potential of the digital single market in order to create a competitive and dynamic eu knowledge-based economy that benefits both citizens and businesses. the eu needs to act to maintain its global competitive edge, especially in fast-growing sectors of the economy such as online platforms and application software. universal connectivity, to which free access to high-speed broadband internet networks is essential, universal and uniform access to internet services for all citizens and a diversity of wireless broadband services are essential conditions for the development of the digital single market. restricting access to digital markets and internet users by eu companies, including through mass state censorship or market access restrictions imposed on eu internet service providers in third countries, constitutes a barrier to trade. therefore, it is necessary to include a safeguard in all future trade agreements, in particular those containing provisions relating to online services and online communities of users sharing content, to ensure that third parties do not require eu ict companies to restrict access to websites, remove user-generated content or provide personal data, such as personal ip addresses, in ways that infringe fundamental rights and freedoms. a strategy is needed to address the issue of measures taken by third countries that restrict access to global online markets for eu companies.
in writing. − the committee on employment and social affairs has for some time been concerned about the impact of so-called austerity measures on society and in particular on vulnerable groups. various reports have been made to draw attention to the situation. in the own-initiative communication, the rapporteur seeks to identify certain problems encountered by vulnerable groups or groups that are the result of specific situations. groups are under increasing pressure as costs are reduced and demand rises. this is reflected in the reduction in costs, both for services and social benefits, which affects both those who need care and those who provide it. short-term cost reductions may lead to long-term problems. this also contributes to increasing social inequalities, as the poor become poorer and are at odds with the europe 2020 goals. there is also an increase in 'hate speech', harassment and attacks against people with disabilities, people with mental health problems and other vulnerable groups. it is also a sector notorious for its low wages, poor working conditions and generally high turnover rates, so it is not surprising that it is often the sector that is most understaffed. i voted in favour of this proposal because at least a thorough assessment of the social impact of changes in social protection systems and the provision of care services is needed to avoid a worsening of an already bad situation.
in writing. − austerity measures have affected different parts of society disproportionately, hitting hardest those that are the most vulnerable. public sector budgets are being cut, challenging the healthcare system and making it far more difficult for older people, children and those with special needs to receive care. as evidence of this, older people are more likely to receive care from family members, rather than from professionals. healthcare barriers in a number of member states make access to healthcare difficult for these more vulnerable groups, creating greater social inequality and significant long-term problems. comparing rising healthcare costs to incomes explains why people do not seek care at an early stage, which results in a much costlier treatment later. some are even unable to complete treatment because they cannot afford to take time away from work. people are deterred from seeking healthcare due to other barriers like unavailable workplace health benefits or difficulty in accessing social security and welfare. i voted in favour of this report because people, especially those in already vulnerable situations, should have available access to healthcare.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because media pluralism, freedom of opinion, press and information are fundamental to the functioning of our democratic societies. the media perform educational, informational, entertainment and supervisory functions. connected television is an important technological step towards media convergence, which by its very nature raises questions about important media regulatory decisions. it was decided to apply a strict regulatory framework to linear services and to apply a less strict regulatory framework to non-linear services. the mixed reception unit allows the user not only to watch regular television programmes but also to connect to the internet. in the long run, we can expect a near-total media merger. the large amount of content offered makes its detectability and non-discriminatory access one of the biggest problems for connected television. the platform developer and/or the portal administrators pre-select which services are available and, in particular, whether they are given priority as provided, and only he decides on the technology that will be implemented. thus, access to opinion-forming content is controlled by the platform service provider, the portal administrator or the device manufacturer and is not subject to any media regulation. it is considered necessary to extend the audiovisual media services directive to its scope to include fully the operators of mixed portals and platforms. those who have a significant impact on the diversity of services and opinions reaching the end-user must also comply with the rules on ensuring the diversity of those services and opinions.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the number of registered partnerships, where partnerships are legalised without marriage, is increasing worldwide. such partnerships are inevitably associated with property consequences (when the partnership ends or one of the partners dies) and/or interracial couples. when decisions with a material impact are to be taken in connection with a division of property or a partnership, the persons concerned are faced with complex issues, in particular as regards the applicable law and jurisdiction. national provisions on these matters vary widely - even more so for registered partnerships than for marriages. this creates legal conflicts, legal uncertainty. moreover, in the event of a dispute, the better informed partner, as in the case of spouses, may be interested in applying as soon as possible to the court which, in his opinion, will apply the law which is more favourable to him. i agree with the rapporteur that the registration of a partnership would give individuals the opportunity to choose the law applicable to the legal regime of their property. i agree with the rules in the resolution which provide for the legal interpretation of the property rights of registered partners of an international nature.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because of the property consequences of registered partnerships. the aim of the proposal is to ensure legal certainty for persons entering into international registered partnerships. in 2007, some 211 000 registered partnerships were formed in the eu, of which 41 000 were international. the termination of such a partnership and the division of assets raise problems of applicable law and jurisdiction. the relevant national provisions vary widely. i support the proposals set out above to provide registered partners with the possibility of choosing the law applicable to the legal regime of their assets. it is important to provide for a legal consultation requirement for partners wishing to agree on the applicable law. i also support the establishment of a uniform statute for the institutions of marriage and registered partnerships in other matters of the legal regime of property.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because when decisions with a material impact have to be taken on the division of assets or on partnerships, the persons concerned are faced with complex issues, in particular as regards the applicable law and jurisdiction. the relevant national provisions vary widely, and even more so in the case of registered partnerships than in the case of marriage. this creates considerable legal uncertainty. moreover, in the event of a dispute, the better informed partner, as in the case of spouses, may be interested in applying as soon as possible to the court which, in his opinion, will apply the law which is more favourable to him. it is proposed to also provide for the possibility for registered partners to choose the law applicable to the legal regime of their assets. any choice of applicable law would have no effect, provided that the objective link remains with the law of the member state in which the partnership is registered. it also provides for a consultation requirement. although partners wishing to agree on the applicable law are usually given the relevant information and the parties concerned in particular are usually best informed of their rights, legal advice should be provided in the light of the specific need for protection. if consultation is provided for in one member state under the special requirements of an agreement on the applicable law, this condition would be fulfilled in one way or another (e.g. by the granting of an official endorsement).
in writing. − in order to create a clear legal framework, it is appropriate to allow registered partners to choose the law applicable to the legal regime of their assets. this will allow for more efficient and easier management of assets located in several countries. in particular, the substantial differences between the applicable substantive and international private law rules will be eliminated and common provisions will be established throughout the eu. moreover, the increased legal certainty of the partners will prevent the search for the most favourable court. it should be noted that in all cases the scope must be precisely defined and its boundary with other areas of law clearly defined. on the other hand, appropriate safeguards must also be established to prevent the choice of the applicable law from being made without the express consent of both parties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the property consequences of registered partnerships. the aim of the proposal is to ensure legal certainty for persons entering into international registered partnerships. in 2007, some 211 000 registered partnerships were formed in the eu, of which 41 000 were international. the termination of such a partnership and the division of assets raise problems of applicable law and jurisdiction. the relevant national provisions vary widely. i support the proposals set out above to provide registered partners with the possibility of choosing the law applicable to the legal regime of their assets. it is important to provide for a legal consultation requirement for partners wishing to agree on the applicable law. i also support ensuring equal status for marriage and registered partnership institutions in other matters of the legal regime of property.
in writing. - i supported this proposal because in all cases of divorce or death of one of the spouses in an international marriage, the spouses' property must be divided. the persons concerned face complex issues, in particular as regards the applicable law and jurisdiction. the legal regime of matrimonial property also raises issues of property management in marriage; third parties may also be involved, for example in the case of land or loan transactions. the legal regime of matrimonial property regimes and the rules of jurisdiction vary widely between member states. it may therefore be the case in practice that the court having jurisdiction in one member state will treat the matrimonial property regime in the same case differently from the court having jurisdiction in another member state. in particular, the acquisition of substantial property may make it necessary to apply to the court from which the party concerned expects the application of the matrimonial property regime considered more favourable to it. in this case, the better informed party has a clear advantage. in addition, there is a general degree of legal uncertainty and hence a high cost potential. the proposal on the matrimonial property regime can indeed significantly improve the legal situation of the spouses concerned. this is also in line with parliament's call for 'simpler, clearer and more accessible procedures in civil law'. with increasing mobility, this will be an issue for an even greater number of couples.
in writing. − with the increasing free movement of persons within the european union, and with it the increase in marriages between nationals of different member states, the question of the legal regime governing the property of spouses is also becoming relevant. this is especially true where one spouse dies and the property may be subject to several legal regimes. i support this document which simplifies the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of judgments on matrimonial property regimes and on the succession. i am sure that this decision will bring more legal clarity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of amending this regulation because the eu must ensure equal protection for international couples with regard to their property regime and property consequences. the new legal framework will help to remove the remaining obstacles to citizens' enjoyment of their rights in the european judicial area. it should be noted that, at present, couples of international origin face considerable practical and legal difficulties, ambiguities and discrimination in the management of their property. in this context, it is necessary to ensure that couples are able to exercise their rights in a conscious and purposeful manner. the legal framework for matrimonial property regimes would be uniform, simplified and accessible to all european citizens. the eu should establish a uniform legal framework and facilitate the movement of judicial decisions and other documents from one member state to another.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that all suspects and accused persons should be given the right to have a lawyer as soon as possible and in such a way that they can effectively exercise their rights of defence. moreover, those rights should be granted before the start of the questioning, before any procedural or evidence-gathering action and after the restriction of freedom. in some countries these rights vary considerably, i.e. the right of defence in criminal proceedings varies in scope depending on the particular legal system and its practical application. in addition, member states implement and comply with the provisions of the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights in different ways, resulting in different standards within the european union. i agree with the rapporteur that there should be specific rules governing legal aid. citizens should be guaranteed that their rights are fully respected and that they are guaranteed safety when they travel. they should also be assured of the same guarantees in all eu member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the right to have a lawyer during criminal proceedings and the right to be contacted after arrest. the purpose of the proposal is to strengthen the protection of the rights of victims of crime and the rights of suspects and accused persons by regulating procedural guarantees in criminal proceedings. over 8 million criminal trials take place in the eu every year, but the conditions for consulting a lawyer vary from one member state to another. i support the proposals set out to ensure that suspects have the right to be represented by a lawyer from the first police interview and the right to appropriate and confidential meetings between suspects and a lawyer. it is essential that suspects can contact their family members or employer, and suspects abroad their embassy. i also support the proposal to ensure that persons who have been issued an eu arrest warrant are able to obtain legal advice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european parliament has long called for strengthening: (1) the protection of the rights of victims of crime and (2) the protection of the rights of suspects and accused persons. following the failure of the commission's 2004 framework decision on certain procedural rights in criminal proceedings, parliament, in a report by mr pagano adopted on 7 may 2007, urged the drafting of a wide-ranging legislative act on procedural guarantees in criminal proceedings. the european parliament proposes to establish a basic principle according to which all suspects and accused persons should be granted the right to have access to a lawyer as soon as possible and in such a way that they can effectively exercise their rights of defence. furthermore, this notice states that in any event these rights should be granted before the start of the interrogation, before any procedural or evidence-gathering action and after the restriction of freedom. it is also essential to define the content of the law, i.e. that meetings between suspects or accused persons and their lawyer must be confidential, to list derogations from the general principles and to lay down the rules governing the waiver of the right to a lawyer.
in writing. −the right of defence in criminal proceedings varies in scope between member states, depending on the particular legal system and its practical application. this has an indirect but significant impact on the eu's policy of mutual trust and mutual recognition. the member states have implemented and applied the provisions of the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights in different ways, resulting in different standards within the european union. i therefore support the need to strengthen the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons, to strike the right balance between freedom, justice and security. citizens should be assured that their rights are fully respected and that their security is guaranteed. the right of suspects and accused persons to have access to a lawyer should be a key principle from the outset of criminal proceedings.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the new legal framework will allow citizens to exercise their procedural rights properly when they are confronted by law enforcement in other eu countries, and will also prevent the use of force by the investigating authorities. this will provide the basis for the implementation of the principle of mutual recognition of judgments in criminal matters and ensure the equality of the means of the prosecution and the defence. common minimum standards for the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings should apply throughout the eu. the timely provision of effective legal aid to suspects or accused persons is essential for the proper exercise of procedural rights. they should be granted the right to have a lawyer in order to exercise effectively their rights of defence. it should be noted that the lack of access to a lawyer may make it impossible to exercise effectively other rights of defence. they must be given the opportunity to contact a third party after their arrest. it is also necessary to ensure the confidentiality of meetings between suspects or accused persons and their lawyer.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on credit agreements for residential property. the purpose of the proposal is to establish new rules for the granting of housing loans. under the new rules, home buyers planning to take out a loan will have to be better informed about the costs and risks of a loan. at the same time, home buyers will be protected against market fluctuations that could lead to higher loan prices in the event of difficulties in refinancing the loan. the new rules will apply to loans related to residential property and to the land on which the property is located or is only planned to be built.
in writing. − i voted for this report because we have to protect people's interests when they take out loans for real estate. a mortgage is often the most important and longest-lasting financial commitment a family makes. unfortunately, during the economic and financial crisis, many people were unable to pay their loans, and this affected them and their families very badly. the european parliament therefore proposes in its report to address urgently important issues such as risk-based approach, financial literacy, good governance and transparency. in order to correct the excessive uniformity of the regulation, it is necessary to establish a definition of special risk arrangements. this is necessary to combat financial illiteracy, which is a cause of irresponsible behaviour. it is necessary to address the problems arising throughout the life of the credit agreement, ensuring the flexibility that can be achieved by strengthening the balance between competitiveness and stability. it is also necessary to develop transparent, well-functioning and reliable mortgage lending markets. moreover, the crisis has shown the importance of ensuring the traceability of residential property rights for creditors and investors in instruments where the right to residential property acts as collateral. new credit agreements should be assigned a european mortgage key identifier to ensure that the link between the loan and the property can be established in the primary and secondary markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because home buyers planning to take out a loan will need to be better informed about the costs and risks of a loan and will be better protected against market fluctuations that could lead to a higher cost of a loan. at the same time, borrowers will be better protected in the event of difficulties in refinancing their loans. the new rules will apply to loans related to residential property and to the land on which the property is located or is only planned to be built. the recipients of the state loan will have to receive information on the future loan in the same form, regardless of the state loan. before signing a credit agreement, the consumer should be provided with personalised information allowing him to compare the credits on the market, to assess their costs and their long-term financial implications, and to have a seven-day period before or after signing the contract to take a decision. the conditions for the granting of advances are made more flexible and the requirement for consumers to pay penalties is abolished. in the event of the borrowers' inability to repay the loan, the real estate should be sold at the best market price and measures to allow repayment of the debt on more favourable terms should be introduced. the amendments to the rules were accepted, but the final text was not voted on, as it was necessary to ensure that the eu countries were ready to implement these rules properly, on which a compromise had already been reached in principle.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion. irresponsible borrowing has created a huge debt problem. many home buyers became insolvent and were forced to sell their properties at very low prices. in order to avoid such negative consequences in the future, urgent action is necessary. in particular, the eu should operate an internal market in mortgage lending based on sustainable practices. sustainable lending needs to be promoted continuously in order to restore consumer confidence and financial stability. a reliable procedure for the evaluation of loan applications, harmonious relations between the parties involved and good consumer information are the basis for achieving the objectives set. it should be noted that only responsible lending will improve market conditions and prevent excessive indebtedness.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as both the commission's proposed regulation and the european parliament's report seek to enhance market integrity and investor protection while ensuring a harmonised set of rules and a level playing field, and extend the market abuse regime to all financial instruments covered by the markets in financial instruments directive. the aspect of the commission's proposed regulation on securities trading using inside information and market manipulation (abusive market) is that it provides for an exemption from the obligation to disclose inside information for market participants who are unlikely to be significantly affected by the pricing of allowances. the commission intends to set, by means of delegated acts, the minimum limit value (expressed in annual co2 emissions, heat output or a combination thereof) to be applied to this exemption. therefore, only information relating to the activities of the largest polluters participating in the eu greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme (typically those in the eu electricity sector) is likely to have a significant impact on carbon pricing.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this amendment to the regulation. in particular, environmental protection must be taken into account in the definition and implementation of the union's policies and activities, including in order to harmonise the regulation with the treaty of lisbon, on a case-by-case basis. technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources must be properly implemented to ensure the conservation and responsible exploitation of fishery resources. in view of this, it is necessary to lay down legal rules ensuring uniform conditions for the implementation of the regulation. on the other hand, it is essential that the amendments to this regulation are compatible with the provisions of the new regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the common fisheries policy. the commission should be empowered to do so for a limited period only.
i voted in favour of this document and i congratulate mr buzek on his important report. i would also like to thank my colleagues who supported my amendments to this document. the european union countries still have a long way to go to achieve the objectives they have set themselves. the fact that we are on the right track is also evident from the changing position of some external suppliers. solidarity between european countries is essential in relations with third-country suppliers. it is essential for negotiations, for reviewing outdated contracts, etc. a system of information exchange should be established and anti-competitive practices should be prevented. the commission has a crucial role to play in ensuring that the european union's neighbouring countries adhere to the highest standards of nuclear safety and provide all requested information on nuclear energy projects being developed along the european union's external borders. it is also time to strengthen the monitoring and evaluation of the transposition and implementation of the third energy package at eu level. competition, adequate infrastructure and connections are among the key elements to meet the needs and expectations of end-users.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the internal energy market. member states have committed themselves to completing the internal energy market by 2014 and to abolishing energy islands by 2015. as stated in the europe 2020 strategy, the internal energy market is necessary not only to consolidate the eu's overall energy security and sustainability, but also to increase the eu's global competitiveness, to accelerate economic growth and to create new jobs. in other words, the development of local energy resources will create new trading hubs and new gas and electricity markets in the eu, creating a real opportunity for the eu and its member states to set their own energy prices. i agree with the rapporteur that final energy consumers (individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, industry) are the most important in a favourable and transparent internal energy market and that their information needs to be given special attention. i would also like to stress that the internal energy market is not yet complete and that national energy markets are not meeting consumers' needs and expectations. for example, there are unreasonably high energy prices, a limited number of suppliers or producers, a limited choice of tariffs, a low quality of service, etc. it is therefore necessary to create a more user-friendly market in which consumers can play an active role.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the internal energy market is essential to consolidate the overall energy security and sustainability of the union and contributes significantly to increasing the union's global competitiveness, boosting economic growth and creating jobs, as recognised in single market act ii and the europe 2020 strategy. moreover, the european internal energy market and its respective national energy markets must be competitive and provide real choice and transparent information to all consumers, who play a key role in the energy market. the european parliament's report focuses on the consumer, because the energy market must be consumer-oriented. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. such measures will help consumers to better understand and manage their energy consumption, thereby enabling them to become more flexible and responsive (both in terms of demand and supply). in addition, such measures can improve access to renewable energy and attract the necessary financial investments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because an open, competitive, integrated and flexible european energy market will help to ensure security of supply and will allow for tariff reductions while providing transparency, will improve european competitiveness and will contribute to economic growth and consumer welfare, and it is therefore important to remove as soon as possible the physical, legal or regulatory barriers that hinder the opening up of the market and its effective functioning. member states committed themselves to a clear deadline to complete the internal energy market by 2014 and to eliminate the eu's energy islands by 2015. it is necessary to modernise existing infrastructure and to develop new, advanced and flexible energy generation, transmission (in particular cross-border gas and electricity links), distribution and storage infrastructure, and to ensure that no member state is left isolated from the european gas and electricity networks by 2015.
in writing. −the commitment to complete the internal energy market by 2014 and to eliminate the eu's energy islands by 2015 is already here. however, the creation of an eu internal energy market requires further strengthening of cross-border cooperation and coordination of action at eu level. it is important to ensure that member states lack the political will to fully implement the third energy package and related legislation, and to complete infrastructure and interconnection projects in a timely manner. at the same time, it is necessary to continue antitrust measures and reduce the eu's dependence on fossil fuels by increasing the share of energy from renewable sources. the eu must speak with one voice with third-country suppliers, both to help eu countries negotiate new supply contracts and to ensure the highest standards of nuclear safety in the eu's neighbourhood and the transparent functioning of the eu's internal energy market.
in writing. − as we are committed to completing the internal energy market by 2014 and to abolishing the eu's energy islands by 2015, it is essential to address the challenges of competitiveness, transparency and regulation in the energy sector in the eu energy markets as soon as possible. in particular, the most cost-effective provision of flexible services in the energy sector must be ensured in order to stabilise and improve the key conditions for the european energy sector, as well as to promote sustainable energy supply. it is necessary to reduce energy costs and prices to affordable and competitive levels and to ensure that consumers are protected from energy poverty. in view of this, i am opposed to the proposal to introduce a mandatory european tax, which would make the situation of consumers in many european countries more difficult. it is also essential that the eu has safe, sustainable, affordable and reliable energy production methods. more attention should be paid to the modernisation of infrastructure and the development of new, smart generation, transmission, distribution and storage infrastructure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the countries of the european union to make every effort to complete the internal energy market by 2014. only by fully connecting all eu countries' energy networks will eu countries be in a strong position to negotiate the terms of supply of energy resources with third countries. the commitment by eu member states to abolish eu energy islands by 2015 is of particular importance for lithuania. i hope that the baltic states and their neighbours will do their homework and that this goal will be achieved in time. investments in smart grids, renewable energy sources are still expensive, but the returns are also huge. the international energy agency has rightly pointed out that decisive action could reduce eu gas imports by a third by 2035.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the strategy for fisheries in the adriatic and ionian seas. given that fisheries are traditionally an important sector in most of the coastal regions of the adriatic and ionian seas, the development of a new strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in these seas would have a positive impact on local communities. the adriatic and ionian sea region, which comprises seven states italy, greece, slovenia, croatia, montenegro, albania and bosnia and herzegovina, is uneven in economic, environmental and cultural terms. i agree with the rapporteur that closer cooperation with neighbouring countries is needed in areas such as the common fisheries management regime, ensuring sustainable use of resources, etc. maritime activities are international in nature and involve common resources. the development of an integrated approach to maritime policy in the adriatic and ionian sea basin therefore requires dialogue. i also support the call for the commission to adopt an action plan and a regulation addressing the management of fishing activities in this macro-region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a strategy for fisheries in the adriatic and ionian seas. the aim of the proposal is to develop a new eu strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas to encourage the development of sustainable economic activities that would have a positive impact on coastal communities. the adriatic and ionian seas are an important maritime region, with coastlines spanning seven countries, four of which are members of the eu. i welcome the proposals made to contribute to the eu's response to the challenges in this region, such as the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, marine pollution, the economic disparities in coastal areas and the increasing urbanisation. closer cooperation with neighbouring countries is needed to establish a common fisheries management system and ensure sustainable use of resources. i agree that the specificities of the sea basin, including its specific geophysical characteristics, should be taken into account when setting measures relating to the fisheries and aquaculture sector. the european commission should adopt as soon as possible an action plan and a regulation addressing the management of fishing activities in this macro-region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the aim of this report is to call for a new european union strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas. the main objective of such an eu strategy is to encourage the development of sustainable economic activities that would have a beneficial impact on coastal communities and adjacent land areas. coastal countries share a wide range of resources, including fish stocks, and therefore all face different challenges, directly or indirectly linked to the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, such as marine pollution, coastal erosion, differences in the economic development of coastal areas and increasing urbanisation. the european commission has recently adopted a communication setting out a marine strategy for the adriatic and ionian seas, which should be the basis for the adaptation of the eu macro-regional strategy to the adriatic and ionian seas. in addition, the specificities of the sea basin, including its specific geophysical characteristics, i.e. its shallow sandy bottom and its lagoons, islands and coastal areas, should be taken into account when setting measures relating to the fisheries and aquaculture sector. accordingly, we call on the commission to adopt, at the earliest opportunity, the necessary action plan and regulation to address the management of fishing activities in this macro-region.

in writing. − i voted in favour of a resolution on more efficient and cost-effective interpretation in the european parliament. the european union is the only economic and political community in the world to have an official policy of multilingualism, based on 24 official languages. each member of the european parliament has the right to speak and be heard in the official language of his or her choice. this ensures the principles of openness and transparency, respect for linguistic and cultural diversity and equality of opportunity for persons of different origins and education. however, although multilingualism is a prerequisite for the work of the institution and its members, it is recognised that translation costs are increasing every year. we, the members of the european parliament, agree that multilingualism must be made more effective without compromising the quality of the translation and without jeopardising the right of members to use the official language of their choice. to this end, parliament must inform the committee on budgetary control more effectively of the evolution of expenditure in the field of interpretation and of its decisions which affect interpretation services, their efficiency and cost reduction. we ask the court of auditors to report to parliament by march 2014 on the translation costs of the european parliament, the commission and the council and to answer the following questions: whether the services provided are above requirements; whether all the services required are provided; whether the services are provided at the lowest possible cost and whether the services are of high quality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for more efficient and cost-effective interpreting in the european parliament. in 2011, there were 5 263 plenary sessions requiring 100 000 interpreting working days, of which 47,74% were for freelance interpreters and 52,26% for permanent interpreters. the commission notes that the 2012 sgei decision does not provide for any specific exemption for the provision of interpretation services. over the last three years, eur 15,93 million has been lost due to late applications and cancellations. the aim of this proposal is to ensure that the translation services provided by the ep do not exceed real needs, and that they are provided at the lowest possible cost while maintaining a high level of quality. i agree with the ep's demand that a system be developed and implemented as a matter of urgency to avoid providing interpretation services into languages that are not actually spoken at the relevant meeting. it is also important to carry out a detailed analysis of the interpretation of the languages provided in all meetings of the groups, committees and delegations and of the languages actually used in these meetings. i agree to the creation of possible translations as required by the script. i support the request to the court of auditors to submit a special report on the costs of interpretation and translation for the ep, the ec and the council by mid-2014 at the latest.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european parliament's linguistic services facilitate communication and thus ensure that parliament remains open to all european citizens, guaranteeing a unique multilingual interface of the union based on the 24 official languages. furthermore, multilingualism is one of the fundamental characteristics of the european parliament, as well as of the european union as a whole, and therefore respect for cultural and linguistic diversity and equal treatment for eu citizens of different origins and education must be ensured. it should also be emphasised that the use of official languages in the european parliament is governed by the parliament's multilingualism code and that interpretation into the other official languages must therefore be ensured. the democratic right to be elected to the european parliament must therefore be respected, regardless of language skills. in its report, the european parliament draws attention to the fact that, while maintaining high standards of work, it is also necessary to aim at a more efficient use of translation resources and to control their costs in the light of the overall workload of each language unit and by ensuring that costs are reduced due to late cancellations of applications for meetings and delegation visits providing interpretation.

in writing. − as the document notes, the european union is the only entity in the world to have an official multilingualism policy based on 24 official languages and using a total of 552 language pairs. as a directly elected political body whose members are chosen irrespective of their language proficiency, parliament grants all its members the right to speak in the official language of their choice, which is a fundamental principle of the european parliament's procedures and work. the quality of the interpretation must therefore be high, while at the same time the aim is to reduce as much as possible not only the accuracy and quality of the interpretation itself, but also the economic efficiency and costs associated with the service.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. i believe that multilingualism must be constantly improved and that cultural and linguistic diversity must be respected. it should be noted that multilingualism gives citizens the opportunity to exercise their right to democratic control. on the other hand, linguistic services help the eu institutions to remain open and transparent. it is therefore important for the european parliament to ensure equal access to translation services and to maintain language equality. the system of interpretation in the european parliament must be effective. however, translation resources should be used more efficiently and their costs controlled while maintaining excellent quality of work.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on online gambling in the internal market. today, online gambling services are widely offered and used in the eu and the economic importance of the sector is increasing. online gambling (e.g. poker, casino games, sports betting, etc.) is the fastest growing segment of the gambling market. statistics show that 2% of the european population is addicted to gambling, and the easy access to online gambling sites may not only worsen the situation but also create a favourable environment for criminal activities such as money laundering. the specific nature of the online gambling sector should make the protection of human health and consumers a key principle in the development of eu-level guidelines and national legislation. i agree with the rapporteur that special attention should be paid to minors and their parents. in other words, minors must be prevented from accessing online gambling, parents must be informed about the consequences of online gambling and gambling operators must provide clear and specific warnings to minors about the illegality of their participation in online gambling. it is also essential to emphasise the need to establish a clear demarcation between online gambling and other forms of online entertainment and to put in place effective measures to inform, in particular young people, about the dangers of gambling addiction.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on online gambling in the internal market. the aim of the proposal is to create a better regulated, safer online gambling sector, which would help to divert users away from unregulated sites. the annual growth rate of online gambling services is 15%, with annual operating revenues expected to reach eur 13 billion in 2015. however, thousands of gambling sites are unregulated, a large proportion of them outside the eu. this encourages fraud and money laundering. i agree that it is important to develop better age-checking tools and filters for online content, as well as more responsible advertising for gambling. it is important that member states implement fraud and money laundering prevention and deterrence measures in the field of online gambling. it is important to develop appropriate methods at eu level to combat this problem, agreed between the eu, the member states and the online gambling sector. it is important to carry out surveys and collect data on gambling-related disorders and to promote training of judges on fraud and money laundering.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because gambling is not a normal economic activity, given the potential negative health and social impact of gambling. sadly, however, gamblers often have an insatiable appetite for gambling, the consequences of which are difficult to measure. gambling also involves organized crime, money laundering, and match-fixing. as regards online gambling, it should be emphasised that it may lead to a higher risk of addiction than traditional offline gambling. this is thought to be due to easier access and lack of social control, but further research and data are needed on this issue. the european parliament therefore calls on all member states and the commission to carry out further research in a coordinated manner to understand the problem of gambling. parliament also asked the commission to examine the possibility of stopping the practice of some companies established in one member state offering online gambling services, for example via satellite television or advertising campaigns, in another member state where they do not have a licence to offer these services.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal, as the provision of gambling services is a specific economic activity, the restrictions on which can be justified by overriding reasons of public interest, such as consumer protection, the prevention of fraud, the fight against money laundering and the protection of public order and public health, but the restrictions on this activity must be proportionate to the objectives pursued and must be non-discriminatory. the main objective is to protect minors and vulnerable members of society and to combat addiction, crime and tax evasion and money laundering.
in writing. − we have already discussed the issue of better regulation of online gambling a few years ago. as i did then, i can only reiterate my position that the eu-wide regulation of online gambling is necessary. only in this way will it be possible to ensure that vulnerable groups of consumers are adequately protected against the undesirable effects of gambling.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in particular, the new regulation will make it possible to strictly regulate or even prohibit dangerous forms of gambling. it is essential that states properly implement the measures envisaged to reduce the negative impact of gambling. particular attention should be paid to the strict setting of betting limits and the limit of the player's own expected losses in online gambling, as well as to the protection of minors. in order to mitigate the potential negative consequences of gambling, a common voluntary online gambling cessation mechanism should be established at european union level. in addition, given the international nature of online gambling, it is necessary to develop a more coherent eu policy and, in some areas, a harmonised european approach.
i agree with all those who have spoken about the importance of reducing youth unemployment. we must do more to tackle this problem and in no way save the future of our young people. the report proposes a number of measures. i believe that all of them are important and necessary, since this problem can only be solved by a complex set of measures at national and european union level. i would say that the key measure is to improve the transition of young people from education to the labour market. it is necessary to find the most effective mechanisms for matching acquired competences, practical experience and labour market needs. the statistical concept of young people aged 15 to 24 should not be limited. it is important to note that young people are now studying longer and often enter the labour market after the age of 24. therefore, measures to reduce unemployment must target young people up to the age of at least 30. i would also like to point out that it is not necessary to understand that special measures are needed only when youth unemployment in a country is above 25%. i think that both 15 percent and 20 percent of people who are out of work are a painful enough problem. finally, the european union youth conference, which will focus on tackling youth unemployment, kicked off today in lithuania, which holds the presidency of the council of the european union. i think that the young people and the experts themselves will certainly come up with conclusions and recommendations on how to solve the problem of youth unemployment.
in writing. madam president, the situation of young people in the labour market is particularly difficult. according to the latest data, the unemployment rate for people under 25 in the european union is 23%, although in some countries, such as spain, it is as high as 55%. the economic crisis has caused a slowdown in job creation and employers are cutting back on existing employment to save money. the dismissals are most commonly those of temporary workers or those on civil and legal contracts, and thus mainly young people entering the labour market. the fight against youth unemployment therefore requires increased support from the european union institutions. the creation of a separate budget line, which could effectively help member states to support the employment of young people, the exchange of professional qualifications or the provision of further education, through the european social fund, is worth considering. in parallel, these actions need to promote self-employment. any action aimed at developing self-initiative, entrepreneurship by people under 30 years old, needs to be reflected in new legal decisions, especially in the context of the european union's programme for social change and innovation 2014-2020. interestingly, the fight against unemployment can also act as an incentive for greater occupational mobility. there are over a million registered job vacancies in the european union, but they are not being exploited. the plight of young people therefore requires decisive institutional intervention.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which aims to adopt new rules to limit the production of traditional biofuels and to speed up the transition to new methods of producing this type of fuel, i.e. using waste or seaweed. these new rules would help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the increasing use of land for biofuel-recyclable crops. i support the proposals set out above to ensure that by 2020 the share of first generation biofuels produced from food crops should not exceed 5,5% of the energy consumed in the transport sector and that the share of advanced biofuels should be at least 2% of that amount. it is also important to take into account the fact that food production is being replaced by the production of biofuels, as land is increasingly used for the cultivation of these fuels, with the consequent increase in greenhouse gas emissions. therefore, indirect land-use change may partially undermine the environmental benefits of biofuels. i also support the energy committee's proposal that the share of first generation biofuels should not exceed 6.5%.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. european eel stocks are facing a number of threats: overfishing, loss of key habitats, pollution, parasites, changes in ocean currents due to global climate change, and more. the problems to be solved include: unclear stock size, monitoring and control of the use of eel resources, inconsistent catch and export figures, international black market in eel, etc. according to the latest scientific advice on european eel published by the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) in 2012, the stock situation of european eel is critical and requires urgent action. sources are not within safe biological limits and the current fisheries are not sustainable. i agree with the rapporteur that the current council regulation is not sufficient to ensure the recovery of the european eel population and that a new regulation is therefore needed. i believe that until measures are taken to restore the eel stock to an abundant and biologically safe level, the european eel fishery should be completely stopped.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the establishment of stricter rules for the protection of european eel. over the last three decades, european eel stocks have been depleted to the extent that they have declined by 95 per cent. the european commission intends to propose new rules to protect these fish from extinction by march 2014. i agree with the proposals made to assess the measures for the recovery of the current stocks of eel by october 2013. this would contribute to the development of new safety rules. it is also important that eu countries inform the eu more frequently about the measures they apply to protect european eel. i support the proposals to impose sanctions on those eu countries which delay in providing information on these stocks.
in writing − if you have i voted in favour of this report because there are many threats to european eel stocks, such as overfishing, loss of key habitats, pollution, parasites, changes in ocean currents due to global climate change, etc. so solutions are not easy to come by, and there are many problems. the already complex problems are further complicated by the many uncertainties surrounding several important biological and management aspects of eels. these include the uncertain size of the stock, the lack of a clear understanding of the conditions under which the sex of the eels is formed, and the serious question of whether the eels that are introduced will actually be able to reproduce successfully. the european parliament therefore considers that introduction should be carried out in accordance with clearly defined scientifically based guidelines that limit its geographical scope, ensure that it does not spread diseases and are based on local overabundance of young eels (if such guidelines apply). in addition, a completely different approach could be adopted if member states select sites suitable for recovery, free of barriers, low in pollutants and with high levels of eel survival. member states could, in accordance with the abovementioned guidelines, restore the stock in these areas, and in particular prohibit fishing for eel in these river basins, and use this as the main measure for the conservation of these stocks. these recovery areas could act as marine reserves in the marine environment.

in writing. − i voted for this report because i agree that youth unemployment is a priority issue on the eu agenda. the figures speak for themselves in greece and spain, where the economic crisis has hit hard, some 55% of young people under 25 are unemployed. in other countries, the situation is less dramatic, but statistics show that more and more young people are only getting temporary contracts, and it is becoming increasingly difficult for them to gain a foothold in the labour market. both the eu and the member states, in cooperation with the private sector and academic institutions, need to look for possible solutions to prevent this generation from becoming a 'lost generation'. labour mobility between eu countries can reduce social tensions somewhat, but here we often face the problem of 'mind-flow' that is so relevant to lithuania. while only 2% of people in the eu as a whole live outside their country of origin, the numbers of people leaving the new eu countries are much higher. the economically weaker eu countries are losing young professionals to a heavy toll. i think we should find a mechanism at eu level to at least partially compensate for the costs of training the professionals who leave.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the internal market in services, on the assessment of the current situation and the next steps. services a new, dynamic, modern and promising market driver whose importance in the economy is growing every day. the services sector generates more than 65% of the eu's gross domestic product (gdp). it is safe to say that a better functioning internal market for services is the basis for a more competitive european economy. since 2006, the services directive has been and remains an important driver of structural reforms in the european services sector. however, three years after the deadline for transposition of this directive, it is not yet fully and properly applied in all member states. there are plenty of examples of cases where bureaucratic red tape and obstacles have slowed down economic growth, caused citizens to lose their jobs and caused discriminatory practices to undermine citizens' trust in the single market. as practice shows, there are many different requirements for enterprises which, taken individually, would appear to be unfair, but which, taken together, place a heavy burden on service providers, especially smes. the economic crisis and its perceived effects call for urgent action to unlock the full potential of the services sector to boost growth and create jobs. in this area, coherent and coordinated action throughout the european union is of particular importance.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it is time to act, given that, in the face of rising unemployment and a deteriorating budgetary situation, the services sector is more than ever a source of competitiveness, growth and job creation that cannot be ignored. thus, unnecessary and disproportionate administrative burdens, discriminatory practices and unjustified restrictions on the provision of services across the european union are blocking important sources of economic growth, hampering job creation and causing business opportunities to be lost. it is therefore essential to set better performance indicators for the single market, based on real experience and expectations of businesses and consumers, in order to improve functionality and to increase their knowledge of the various rights that can be exercised to ensure access to the single market for services. furthermore, in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market for services, it is necessary to link it to sector-specific rules which may require additional authorisations, which lead to increased costs, in particular for businesses. the commission should therefore assist member states in addressing the significant problems identified by them in the implementation and application of eu single market legislation, including problems relating to the improvement of transposition, compliance gaps and the provision of swift and effective judicial remedies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because it aims to remind member states of their responsibility to apply the content and substance of the services directive fully and correctly. the economic crisis has made it even more urgent to act to unlock the full potential of the services sector to boost growth and create jobs. the services sector generates more than 65% of eu gdp. this sector is a dynamic, modern and promising part of the european economy. innovation is constantly encouraging the emergence of different modes of service provision. digital and mobile services are changing the way the economy works. goods and services are increasingly sold together as a single package. in addition, we see an increasing convergence of services and a growing interconnection between the service and manufacturing sectors. for all these reasons, a better functioning internal market for services is therefore the basis for a more competitive european economy as a whole. however, there are still many examples of high bureaucracy and obstacles to growth, where citizens lose jobs and where discriminatory practices reduce citizens' trust in the single market, and this situation needs to be corrected and improved.
in writing. − by enabling the free movement of services between member states in the eu's founding documents, we must ensure that this movement is real and effective. i therefore support the position expressed in this document that it is necessary to continue to remove obstacles to the free movement of services, while ensuring the appropriate quality of services provided in several member states and the responsibility and accountability of service providers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution. i believe that more decisive action is needed to promote economic prosperity and the creation of quality jobs. the services directive must be properly implemented in all member states and existing obstacles to the free movement of services across borders must be removed. in this context, it is necessary to implement the governance of the internal market for advanced services. moreover, the single market performance indicators should be based on the experience and expectations of enterprises and consumers. particular attention shall be paid to the quality of the services provided to end-users. it is essential that consumers have more choice in the single market.
