rapporteur. − mr president, over the past 19 years parliament has adopted 37 resolutions exclusively on belarus. however, for what is probably the first time, we are discussing belarus and its relations with the eu not by reacting to the frequent negative news from this country, but rather by trying to analyse the situation and thus propose concrete policy actions. i would like to thank the 25 colleagues who tabled amendments to my recommendation and especially the shadow rapporteurs – jacek protasiewicz, werner schulz, johannes cornelis van baalen, paveł kowal. also of course commissioner stefan füle, officials from the eeas, the commission, as well as staff members of the committee on foreign affairs and my political group, and last, but not least, many citizens of belarus for constructive cooperation. some influential european politicians believe that belarus is lost to the eu. therefore, one might argue we should turn our backs on the country and focus on other eu neighbours. i strongly disagree with such an opinion. in this case we would turn our backs not only on the authorities, but more importantly on 10 million belarusian citizens, most of whom wish for closer relations with the eu. we recommend taking advantage of the lithuanian presidency and the eastern partnership summit in vilnius as an opportunity to improve relations with belarus, as soon as all political prisoners have been released of course, and to restart the political dialogue on, inter alia, democratic reforms, free and fair elections, and respect for human rights. it is important that the majority of opposition parties in belarus favour this position. the conditionality and ‘more for more’ principle in eu-belarus relations are particularly emphasised in the text. we emphasise that the general situation concerning respect for human rights remains deplorable. therefore, we urge belarus to lift any obstacles and restrictions to the exercise of freedoms of association, expression, movement, peaceful assembly, thoughts, for the democratic opposition and ngos. we recommend encouraging the wider civil society, including trade unions and business representatives as well as the political opposition, alongside officials, to increase their involvement in the dialogue on modernisation. it is a very important instrument and should be used for strengthening people’s understanding of the need for reforms and for the development also of an appropriate social net. the eu, however, distanced itself from belarus with a kind of financial visa wall. i mean the ungraspably high visa fees of eur 60. it is depressing to see all the queues for the consular departments in the eu states’ embassies in minsk. at the border checkpoints to eu states, lorry queues extend for 15 kilometres and more, and sometimes the infrastructure on the belarusian side is better than on the eu side. i believe that all these and other artificial barriers should be broken down as soon as possible. the eu should open all gates, doors and even windows for more people-to-people contacts. this recommendation, i believe, will send a strong signal that the european union is not turning its back on belarus despite these difficult 19 years of strained relations. this country in the centre of europe, i am sure is not and will not be lost to europe.
for the efd group belarus' participation in the european union's eastern partnership is a positive sign of the country's commitment to europe. it is very important that belarus continues to participate in european union initiatives and to make efforts to develop bilateral cooperation. in submitting my questions to the european commission, i noted that belarusian citizens face undue difficulties in moving across the border, and i therefore welcome parliament's proposal to consider unilaterally simplifying the issuing of visas and reducing their cost to the amount affordable to belarusian citizens, as well as the call to make full use of the flexibilities provided for in the visa code, including the possibility of abolishing or reducing the fee for short-stay visas. and especially young people, in order to facilitate and intensify people-to-people contacts and help prevent further isolation of belarusian citizens. today, more than 40 lithuanian municipalities cooperate very productively with partner cities in neighbouring belarus. i hope that this cooperation will only grow stronger in the future. lithuania has a saying: 'a good neighbour is twice as good as a bad relative', so the european union should be the good neighbour today, so that belarus can be the same tomorrow.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because when the financial crisis hit europe in 2008, there were 27 different banking regulatory frameworks based on national rules and national rescue mechanisms. some coordination was carried out at european level, but it involved exchanges of information and more informal cooperation procedures. this was not sufficient to address the financial sector crisis that has been felt in the union in recent years. the proposed banking union would change the approach to the supervision of euro area banks by establishing a single supervisory mechanism within the european central bank. i support the single supervisory mechanism in the euro area, and the need to further strengthen the european banking authority and ensure its proper functioning in order to improve the internal market in financial services and avoid a split between euro-zone and non-euro-zone members in terms of rules applicable to the financial sector.
in writing. - i support the motion for a resolution tabled. an effective and well-functioning single banking supervisory mechanism must be established in the european union. it is noted that this mechanism is a necessary measure to reduce the fragmentation of european financial markets that has emerged during the crisis, as well as to ensure financial stability and to restore confidence in the european banking system. this is the first pillar of the banking union and an important step towards restoring the normal functioning of the lending market and thus contributing to the economic recovery. in view of the objectives pursued, it is necessary to strengthen the european banking authority and ensure its proper functioning. it is also essential that common rules apply in the eu and that the supervisory mechanism is strengthened. the implementation of the envisaged provisions will provide a strong and stable banking union based on the principles of checks and balances and accountability.
in writing. − this communication gives the european central bank the task of establishing the eu banking supervisory framework. it's the right move. it will help to enhance the transparency and accountability of banks. from september next year, the european central bank will be responsible for supervising the 150 largest eu banks. it will have to develop common supervisory guidelines that other eu banks can follow. i agree with the rapporteur who emphasises the unrestricted access of this supervisory authority to bank documents, the possibility to conduct bank tests under the most unfavourable conditions for them. i support the provision in the report that other eu countries not yet in the euro area can join the banking supervision system. this would allow them to participate in decision-making on an equal footing.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in order to restore financial stability and accelerate economic recovery, particular attention should be paid to enhancing the integration of the banking sector. given the importance of the european central bank, it is appropriate to entrust it with specific tasks relating to the prudential policy for the supervision of credit institutions. this will ensure strict supervision of large banks, a high level of consumer protection and the prevention of money laundering. it should be noted that the ecb will not act alone in supervising large banks, but will have to cooperate closely with national supervisors. issues such as consumer protection, prevention of money laundering, supervision of financial services and markets, supervision of credit unions and of foreign branches of third-country banks will be addressed at national level.

lithuania has already established in its legislation the necessity of environmental impact assessment for the exploration and extraction of shale gas and i therefore welcome the intention to ensure fair and equal conditions of operation throughout the community and the strict implementation of the requirements of the european union safety and environmental legislation. i think those requirements should be even stricter. the environmental impact assessment and its optional nature should not be dependent on the planned gas production, but must be mandatory in all cases. the extraction of shale gas is only possible if the environment and the people living in it are absolutely safe and the impact of the production on ecological processes is minimal. and above all, we must ensure that environmental impact assessments are carried out by independent bodies, are objective, impartial and not bought-in.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because corruption and other human rights violations are usually linked to abuse of power, lack of accountability and various forms of discrimination within institutions. it is noted that corruption rates are higher where human rights are not adequately or fully guaranteed. according to the world bank, the scale of corruption is enormous, amounting to 5 percent of the world's gdp (about $2.6 trillion), with more than $1 trillion paid in bribes each year. the phenomenon of corruption is accompanied by a number of negative consequences, including a decrease in the state's ability to make the best use of available resources, an increase in the need for investment in the country's economy, and so on. it is also important to note that corruption is a threat to democracy and human rights and remains a major cause and catalyst of conflict in developing countries. the issue of corruption is particularly acute in developing countries, as it hinders foreign direct investment, job creation and modernisation, and investors avoid investing in those countries, thus preventing further constructive cooperation with external actors. i agree with the rapporteur that the eu can only become a credible and influential leader in the fight against corruption by tackling organised crime, corruption and money laundering properly on its territory. i would also note that in order to prevent the spread of corruption, it is necessary to invest in education, especially for young people.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. according to the world bank, corruption accounts for 5 percent of global gdp ($2.6 trillion), with more than $1 trillion paid in bribes each year. the alleged corruption of high-level officials is responsible for the theft and offshore concealment of us$20-40 billion from developing countries' public budgets each year, representing 20-40% of official development assistance. the number of investigations carried out annually by the european anti-fraud office (olaf) is also a major indicator of the problems in this area: 25% of all investigations initiated by olaf concerned european external assistance to third countries, and eur 17.5 million was recovered as a result of these investigations. the eu allocates large amounts of funds to developing countries and there is a need for an appropriate accountability framework for the use of these funds. i believe that olaf's role as the eu's main anti-fraud agency should be strengthened to allow much greater focus on the use of eu development funds. the commission should present an eu anti-corruption plan and development aid programmes to apply the principle of compliance with international standards in the field of corruption and to include anti-corruption provisions in public procurement contracts.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. on 12 december 2012, a new version of the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters was signed. this new version does not cover certain aspects of the rules of jurisdiction applicable to labour law, although when the draft regulation was being considered many experts felt that clarifications were needed in this area. although labour law is a very sensitive area of law, it would be appropriate in the future to include in the scope of that regulation, in the light of the free movement of workers within the eu, certain areas of labour law which would help to improve the protection of workers in the eu, in particular as regards collective and individual employment contracts.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is an attempt by the european parliament to draw attention to the aspects of labour law which have not been dealt with so far in the harmonisation of eu legislation on jurisdiction and the recognition of judgments in civil matters. some judgments of the court of justice of the european union in the fields of private international law and labour law have raised concerns that european union rules may affect the rules that protect workers' rights in the member states. labour law is an area in which the european union has relatively little influence. the various member states ensure a balance between workers' rights, trade union activity and the freedom to engage in a variety of commercial activities. however, the rights and obligations of trade unions and similar organisations and the role they play in the law vary from one member state to another. collective actions legally protected by the constitutions of some member states may be illegal in other member states, for example, if specific procedures are not followed. it is also necessary to avoid situations where the courts deciding on a collective action would have to apply foreign law, thus inevitably reducing the quality of justice by reducing their knowledge of foreign rules on collective actions. in its report, parliament proposes to introduce a provision in eu law to confer jurisdiction on the courts of the member state in which the collective action is to be taken or has been taken to decide on disputes relating to this action.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. this proposal for a directive is part of a broader package of eu legal measures adopted to ensure the implementation of several international labour organisation (ilo) conventions on maritime labour standards, adopted in geneva on 23 february 2006. the convention has now been ratified by 30 countries representing more than 59% of the world's fleet, and the necessary condition for its entry into force is therefore fulfilled: it must be ratified by 30 countries representing 33% of the world's fleet. the convention provides for the full rights and protection of more than 1.2 million seafarers worldwide. it covers such essential matters as minimum requirements for seafarers to work on board, conditions of employment, accommodation, rest, food and board, health protection, medical care, welfare and social protection and ensuring decent working and living conditions on board, as well as the procedures for implementing these provisions. the convention aims to create a level playing field in the global maritime sector by establishing common minimum standards for all ships flying the flag of any state and for seafarers. i agree that it is appropriate to incorporate the provisions of the convention in eu law in the fullest and most concrete way possible, in order to avoid divergent interpretations and different application of the rules by the member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it expresses the european parliament's position as eu legislator on the need to incorporate more fully and concretely into eu law the aspects of flag state control defined by the 2006 convention on maritime labour (hereinafter referred to as the convention). the advantage of incorporating the provisions of the convention into eu law is that it will provide for a more stringent enforcement regime in the european union, and the provisions of eu legislation on flag state control should reflect much better the specific and explicit requirements of the convention, which aims to avoid divergent interpretations by member states that could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. parliament therefore proposes that the provisions of the convention be transposed as precisely as possible into this directive, in so far as they relate to the area of eu competence.
in writing. - i agree with the proposal. in order to create a level playing field in the global maritime sector, it is necessary to transpose the provisions of the convention into eu law as accurately as possible. this would ensure that common minimum standards and the same guarantees apply to all seafarers and to all ships flying the flag of any state. it should be noted that the incorporation of the provisions of the convention into eu law will ensure a stronger enforcement regime in the european union and reflect the specific requirements of the convention. this will ensure that the rules are interpreted in the same way in the member states and will prevent unfair competition and social dumping.

in writing. − the eu fisheries agreement with mauritania covers the period 2013-2014 and is the most comprehensive agreement of its kind. under its protocol, approved by the ep, eu vessels are allowed to fish in mauritania's waters in return for eu support of €70 million per year. this is the case for vessels from seven eu countries, with the majority of licences issued to spanish and french fishermen. lithuanian vessels also fish in mauritian waters. i voted against the protocol because it provides for more expensive fishing licences and reduced fishing quotas in mauritian waters and prohibits the catching of octopuses. the current fishing protocol expires in 2014 and we must prepare to negotiate a new protocol and secure better fishing conditions and quotas for the future.
in writing. - i agree to the minutes. currently, 63 fishing vessels flying the flags of 7 eu countries, including lithuania, are operating in mauritanian waters. the commission estimates that the fisheries under the new protocol will generate €200 million in revenue in the first months. however, failure to conclude an agreement would undoubtedly have a negative impact on fishing opportunities and the opening of a niche would be immediately taken up by competing third parties. it is important that the draft agreement balances the fishing needs of the eu fleet and the buffers for fish stocks. importantly, the eu's financial contribution will not only help develop the developing country's fisheries sector, but also address broader challenges such as tackling radicalisation.
in writing. - i am not opposed to the conclusion of this agreement. i think we should start negotiating a new agreement. the agreement is not beneficial to either party and its provisions will not only harm the interests of the european fishing industry but also lead to higher prices for fish for eu consumers. in particular, it lays down incorrect technical conditions and provides for insufficient fishing opportunities. the new technical fishing conditions, which are very difficult to implement, will make fishing in mauritania impossible. it should be noted that all fleets are subject to a reduction in fishing areas and catches. this will prevent vessels from fishing efficiently and force them to withdraw from this vital fishing zone for eu countries. moreover, the entry into force of this protocol would significantly increase the costs for shipowners and would make fishing in mauritanian waters in the economic zone loss-making.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the eu-mauritania fisheries agreement because i believe that the text agreed by the european commission reflects the interests of the majority of eu fishermen. i understand that the prohibition on fishing for cephalopod in mauritanian waters will have a negative impact on some eu fishermen. but we cannot force a sovereign country to open up its natural resources if it does not want to. the ban will affect spanish industry, but after the recent concessions by mauritania, even the spanish government is supporting the deal. in the meantime, it is vital for lithuanian companies that the european parliament approves the fishing protocol. the mauritanian waters are the only area where lithuanian fishermen fish for pelagic fish. the agreed protocol will benefit not only eu fishermen but also the mauritanian economy. eu funding will help one of africa's poorest countries modernise its economy and generate additional budget revenue. the agreement also contains strict environmental rules, allowing only sustainable fishing. the provisions of this agreement will also apply to third-country vessels fishing in mauritanian waters.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. gender genocide, or the deliberate killing of people of the same biological sex for cultural, social or economic reasons, remains a global problem in many parts of the world. this distorts the gender balance of the population, which has a direct impact on the economic and social development of a country and is contrary to the principles of human rights. i agree that concrete and more tangible action is needed in this area, in particular through the creation of an educational and public environment, the provision of specialised training and, in particular, the mainstreaming of gender genocide in the political dialogue agenda with relevant third countries and its inclusion as a key issue in the post-2015 development agenda.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's position on gender genocide. gender genocide is a gender-neutral term that refers to the intentional killing of people of the same gender because of their biological sex. according to recent estimates, the number of missing women worldwide has risen to some 200 million. this figure has remained remarkably stable, having reached 100 million in 1990. girls continue to be ruthlessly discriminated against through sex-determination, abortion, female infanticide, and murder. gender genocide is a global problem, not only in asia and europe, but also in north america, africa and latin america. disproportionate gender ratio is an unacceptable expression of gender-based discrimination against girls and women and a violation of human rights, and gender-based genocide will always remain a crime and a gross violation of human rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because gender genocide is a biologically gender-neutral concept, meaning the systematic, intentional and mass killing of people of a particular gender on the basis of social sex, and in some countries it is a growing problem, with poor information and deadly consequences. this report specifically examines the causes, current trends, consequences and ways of combating gender biased practices based on biological sex selection. this practice may also include the killing of infants and the coercion to choose the biological sex of the infant. despite recent legislation to combat the practice of selection on the basis of biological sex, girls are disproportionately often the target of severe discrimination on the grounds of sex. this discrimination often involves unborn babies and fetuses of predetermined female sex: abortions, abandonment of babies, or killing for no other reason. gender genocide is a global problem, of concern not only in asia and europe but also in north america, africa and latin america. gender genocide remains a crime and a grave violation of human rights and therefore it is necessary to find effective ways of addressing and eliminating the issues related to all its root causes, which are rooted in the culture of patriarchy. all states and governments have a duty to promote and protect human rights and to prevent discrimination. this is the basis for combating all forms of violence against women.
in writing. − the practice of gender genocide is often deeply rooted in cultures that favour the son, gender inequality, and persistently discriminate against and stereotype daughters. the document we voted on estimates that in 1990, the world population was 100 million fewer because of the genocide of the sexes, and that's the number of women who, demographically speaking, were missing. this is a gross violation of human rights and a serious crime that is widespread in third countries. the commission therefore fully supports calls for third countries to organise information campaigns to ensure equal opportunities for girls and women, to review education and training programmes, and to call on third country governments to prevent any possible gender-based genocide through legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because gender genocide is a crime and a grave violation of human rights. only by working together can we prevent the spread of this phenomenon. a carefully planned and coordinated policy is therefore essential. the problem must be tackled with greater determination, as the scale of gender genocide is tragic. we can't just close our eyes and hope that it's going to go away. the cases of genocide against women must be investigated and the perpetrators punished severely. it is also essential that victims are provided with adequate healthcare and long-term support.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the global economic and financial crisis has undermined the social, economic and territorial cohesion of the eu, leading to increased unemployment, a decline in gdp, increased regional disparities and budget deficits at national, regional and local level. with the creditworthiness of national and regional governments deteriorating, banks and financial markets are increasingly refusing to lend. this has led to severe budgetary constraints in the member states in important areas and sectors, and is one of the main problems facing local and regional authorities in the current period. some member states, faced with the sovereign debt crisis, have decided to freeze or suspend financial support to local authorities for investment, which is having a negative impact on the economic and social recovery of the regions of those member states and of the country itself in general. i agree with the european parliament's position that priority must be given at eu level to the development of links between eu, member state and local and regional budgets, to further simplification of rules and increased flexibility and transparency in the programming and management of the structural funds, and to strengthening the capacity of regional and local authorities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it draws attention to the clear trend towards increasing inequality in the eu's regions, where many of the new member states and southern european regions are relatively poor and most of the central and northern european regions are rich. in the report, parliament underlines the importance of cohesion policy as a key investment instrument, with a key role to play in tackling the crisis, reducing imbalances and putting the eu and its regions on a path to sustainable growth. the last few years have shown that cohesion policy is resilient to the crisis by combining its programmes and funding instruments, thereby providing greater flexibility and contributing to areas where investment is needed to modernise the economy and improve competitiveness. parliament is therefore concerned that the continuation of austerity measures and tight economic management since 2011 and 2012, which have increased pressure on and tightened national budgets, risks reducing the scope of local policies to achieve the europe 2020 objectives. stresses also the need to further strengthen the administrative capacity of regional and local authorities and to continue to work towards reducing the bureaucratic procedures that also have a negative impact on these institutions when they are performing their role as beneficiaries and limit their capacity to implement eu-funded projects;
in writing. - i voted in favour because the current crisis is putting a severe strain on the public finances of the member states. moreover, as the financial and economic crisis continues, subnational (regional and local) authorities are increasingly faced with the complex challenge of their ability to ensure profitable investment. on the one hand, they see their incomes fall sharply as central government cuts transfers and asks regional and local authorities to contribute to austerity policies, and on the other hand, the crisis has left them with increasingly demanding social services, which only adds to the pressure on their public finances. in this particular context, it is important to make concrete proposals to ensure the maximum possible flexibility in the financing of overall national eu development spending through the rigorous implementation of the stability and growth pact. this will be done by analysing the extent to which the current crisis has affected the capacity of subnational authorities to meet the growth and job creation targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy and by proposing ways to improve the financing capacity of these entities for viable investments. it is necessary to identify promising opportunities for national, regional and local authorities to invest in smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it is necessary to exploit the full flexibility offered by macroeconomic governance frameworks to invest appropriately, and in particular to rethink the link between the stability and growth pact and profitable public investment.
in writing. − this report regarding the effects of budgetary constraints for regional and local authorities on the eu’s structural funds expenditure in the member states calls for the europe 2020 goals and the financial crisis to be separated. i voted in favour, because the financial crisis should not detract from investing in future goals such as employment, innovation, sustainable development and the low-carbon economy. the report stresses the need to strengthen the capability of regional and local governments, and to reduce red tape to create more efficiency. another proposal is to increase cooperation between budgets at national and european levels so that the roles and responsibilities of each are clear and do not overlap. community-led local development for local strategies to create smart and sustainable job growth is, i believe, a vital part of european goals. i support the suggestion made in the report that these goals should not be included as part of the stability and growth pact, because the spending is focused on europe 2020 goals and increasing competitiveness, growth and job creation. future generations should be able to benefit fully from the completion of these goals.

in writing. − i support the proposal not to approve the implementation of the budget of the european council and the council for the financial year 2011. in particular, as an eu institution, it draws on the general budget of the european union, which requires a close examination of its financial management and control of expenditure. it is noteworthy that the council still fails to ensure proper cooperation and to provide the european parliament with the necessary information in a timely manner and to respond to questions put to it. it is worth noting that by such behaviour the council does not ensure democratic accountability to its citizens. on the other hand, in order to increase transparency in financial management and accountability between the two institutions, i believe that the budgets of the governing council and the council should be separated. in this context, i support the proposal to set up an interinstitutional working group to negotiate possible decisions on the discharge of the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the renewal of the eia directive. the eia directive lays down criteria for the collection of information necessary for the authorisation of the development of the project concerned. the main aspect of the proposal is that new shale gas extraction projects would also be subject to a mandatory environmental impact assessment, i.e. the rules for shale gas extraction would be tightened. i agree that this impact assessment should be applied not only during the extraction process but also during the exploration process. the impact assessment during exploration should be carried out independently of the test method and during extraction independently of the amount extracted. the directive also proposes to include biodiversity, the use of natural resources, climate change, and the risk of natural and man-made disasters as factors to be taken into account in the environmental impact assessment of a project. it is also necessary to ensure that the environmental report is verified by environmental experts who are fully independent and have the appropriate technical competence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of allowing exploration and production of shale gas by hydraulic fracturing only after an environmental impact assessment has been carried out. it is necessary to strengthen public participation in environmental impact assessment and to establish clear rules to avoid conflicts of interest. we must conserve the soil, use natural resources, protect biodiversity. hydraulic fracturing is a concern. currently, environmental impact assessment is only required for projects producing at least 500 000 cubic metres of natural gas per day. such an assessment would henceforth be mandatory for all extraction of unconventional hydrocarbons, including shale gas, as well as for exploration by hydraulic fracturing. it is also proposed to provide for measures to provide the public with appropriate information and consultation before the projects are implemented. the new rules also provide for measures to avoid conflicts of interest. it is proposed that experts conducting impact studies should be competent, objective and independent.
in writing. − i am pleased that today we have finally adopted a position on the renewed eia directive. without going into the details of the new procedure, i would like to point out that the r & d process itself is now simpler and clearer for those involved. this is particularly true when citizens' rights to a safe and clean environment are properly respected.
in writing. − exploration and extraction of shale gas in europe is only possible with strong guarantees of safe extraction technology. we must be firmly convinced that this will not lead to a particularly large and painful ecological disaster. we have to have guarantees that the chemical will not contaminate the water and that there will be no seismic impact. i support the proposals put forward to better regulate the exploration and extraction of shale gas in europe. it is essential to ensure fair and equal conditions of operation throughout the eu and to ensure strict implementation of the requirements of eu legislation in this area. the obligation to carry out an environmental impact assessment should not depend on the amount of gas that is to be extracted. it must in any event be binding, objective, impartial and not bought. it should be noted that shale gas extraction is only possible if the absolute safety of the environment and the people living in it is ensured and the impact of the production on ecological processes is minimised.
in writing. − the current process for assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment is outdated. the original legislation needs to be modernised to include biodiversity and climate change and to bring the text into alignment with new directives adopted by the eu. around 200 types of projects fall within its scope, making the eia a big factor in the environmental assessment process. improving the directive by laying out clear criteria is important; experts must abide by it to avoid conflicts of interest between companies and investors. extraction and exploration of resources such as non-conventional hydrocarbons can be extremely harmful to natural sources of drinking water if done incorrectly. these processes too should be required to undergo eia. i voted in favour of this report because the new directive has the potential to provide the eu with a green economy and eu citizens with a better quality of life. the eia directive establishes the expectation of making informed decisions before granting development consent. the new eia directive will increase democratic participation in development, giving citizens the opportunity to express their own important opinions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal on pleasure and personal boats. the purpose of the proposal is to update the existing european union safety rules and environmental requirements for vessels designed for personal use, i.e. leisure, sport and training. the recreational and personal ships directive applies to recreational and personal ships designed for use at sea or on inland waterways, but does not apply to ships designed for the commercial carriage of passengers. i agree with the main aspects of the amendment of the directive: increased safety requirements, reduced noise and pollution.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it expresses parliament's position on the updating of eu safety rules and environmental requirements for vessels designed for personal use, i.e. leisure, sport and training, including chartered, crewed or uncrewed. it is important to note that this directive will not apply to ships designed and used for the commercial carriage of passengers. the main essential requirements for the ships concerned relate to stability and buoyancy, engine and electrical safety, emissions and noise emissions. the main aspects of the proposal are the alignment of the rules with more harmonised standards, the maintenance of noise emission limits by providing for the possibility of national measures to impose stricter requirements in sensitive geographical areas in order to better protect the marine environment, the introduction of an obligation to install collection tanks or on-board water treatment systems on vessels with toilets, and the updating of the rules on emissions and noise emission.
in writing. − the recreational and personal boat directive, which repeals directive 94/25/ec, has been under discussion in the council for several years. directive 94/25/ec is still in force and has been transposed into national law in lithuania. at present, lithuania sometimes faces certain difficulties in interpreting the requirements for the ce marking of recreational craft and their components. the new directive defines these issues in much more detail and its adoption and transposition should facilitate decision-making on issues relating to the marking requirements for recreational craft. a compromise was reached during the irish presidency in the first half of 2013 on the draft directive to be adopted by the council. the negotiations were difficult (some discussions involved representatives of the lithuanian maritime safety administration during the first half of 2013), but a major breakthrough was reached during the trialogue in may 2013, chaired by malcolm harbour. in view of the text of the directive, which i consider to have been drafted properly, and the difficult negotiations which have taken place, i consider that it was necessary to pursue the adoption of this directive. i therefore supported the proposals of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection (imco).
in writing. − despite the title of this document, which is at first sight controversial, it is primarily concerned with the safety of people. in some parts of the eu, water transport is the only way to achieve a high-quality transport system. i therefore support the establishment of higher safety standards at eu level, thus ensuring greater safety for those travelling in these vehicles.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion. it should be noted that at present many member states are facing certain difficulties in interpreting the requirements for the ce marking of recreational craft and their components. the new directive defines these issues in much more detail and its adoption and transposition should facilitate decision-making on issues relating to the marking requirements for recreational craft. i believe that the text of the new directive adequately reflects the legitimate expectations and interests of all stakeholders. it also creates the conditions for increasing the competitiveness of the sector to match the most advanced market sectors worldwide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because professional mobility is a crucial element of european competitiveness and employment. there are currently around 800 regulated professions in the eu, seven of which are covered by the automatic recognition system: doctors, dentists, pharmacists, nurses, midwives, veterinarians and architects. however, most professionals face the problem of not being recognised when they move to another eu country to live and work. in other words, there is a lack of simple and clear rules governing the recognition of professional qualifications. i believe that this is a major challenge to be overcome in order to make the most of the single market and put the idea of european citizenship into practice. i agree with the rapporteur that the creation of the european professional certificate and the electronic exchange of information between eu countries are a step towards greater mobility of professionals. doctors, pharmacists, architects and other regulated professions who have obtained a european professional certificate in their own country will find it easier to find employment in another eu country. it is also important to emphasise that the directive will also prevent the relocation of healthcare workers and childcare professionals whose activities have been suspended or restricted as a result of a disciplinary case or an indictment from their activities to another eu country.
in writing. − the eu has many challenges to face today. one of them is the increased demand for highly skilled workers in the eu. today's proposal on professional qualifications responds to the need for a smoothly functioning system of recognition of qualifications to ensure the mobility of professionals across europe. this would make it easier for highly qualified professionals to go where there are vacancies. and that will certainly be good for european economic growth. i am convinced that the idea of a european professional certificate-electronic certificate is the right solution, as it will help to simplify and speed up the procedures for the recognition of mobile professionals. the vocational qualifications directive is very important in enabling professionals to start a new business or find a job in another member state where a specific qualification is required for a specific occupation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because professional mobility is an extremely important element of competitiveness and employment in europe and an integral part of the europe 2020 strategy and the single market act. however, the mobility of professionals in the eu remains low, due to the lack of simple and clear rules governing the recognition of professional qualifications. the fundamental right of free movement is still not taken for granted and this legislative proposal should contribute to simplifying procedures for those wishing to work in another country, while maintaining a high level of quality and safety for consumers, patients, workers and all eu citizens and increasing trust between member states. simplification and trust can be ensured by continuously reviewing the common training requirements for the professions covered by the automatic recognition system and by increasing over time the number of professions covered by this system (currently only 7 out of 800 professions regulated in the eu).
in writing. − i voted in favour of making it easier for doctors, pharmacists, architects and other regulated professions who have obtained a european professional certificate in their own country to find employment in another eu country. meanwhile, those whose professional activities have been suspended or restricted as a result of a disciplinary case or an indictment will be prevented from being employed in other eu countries. the new system will be based on the european professional certificate and the electronic exchange of information between eu countries. previously, the host state administered the application to practise in another eu country, but the new rules transfer this responsibility to the specialist's home state, whose relevant authority will itself contact the host country if necessary. this will facilitate and accelerate the employment of specialists in another eu country. there are currently around 800 regulated professions in the eu, seven of which are covered by the automatic recognition system: doctors, dentists, pharmacists, nurses, midwives, veterinarians and architects. in order to increase the transparency of regulated professions, the new rules require the european commission to create a public database of representatives of regulated professions on the basis of information provided by the member states. before including new professions in this database, eu countries will have to justify that their decision to regulate individual professions is non-discriminatory and proportionate. the directive adopted by the european parliament will also prevent the relocation of healthcare workers and childcare professionals whose activities have been suspended or restricted as a result of a disciplinary case or an indictment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the vergnaud report, which focuses on the issue of mobility of professionals, which is of particular importance in the eu, as there is still a lot of controversy about the recognition of qualifications in different eu countries. in the absence of a uniform and clear system, the mobility of workers in some sectors is relatively low, which is detrimental to the provision of services to consumers. in this context, the aim is to simplify the procedures that professionals must comply with in order to provide services in other countries, and to ensure the quality of the services provided, it is proposed to introduce a provision on language fees. the purpose of the recast of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications is to facilitate procedures for workers while ensuring reliability, quality and safety in this area. to this end, it is proposed to extend the use of the internal market information system and the european professional certificate. the implementation of these changes would contribute to the creation of a transparent and competitive eu labour market and would help to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of these amendments because the new legal regulation is a very important step both in reducing the administrative burden on businesses and in promoting the mobility of professionals between member states. it should be noted that the recognition of professional qualifications is one of the rights of eu citizens, one of the guarantors and components of the principle of free movement of persons. it is therefore essential that the regulatory scope of regulated professions and the rationale for such regulation be sufficiently transparent and objective. the introduction of the european professional certificate on a voluntary basis is welcome. the proper implementation of the provisions of this directive will ensure a high level of reliability of the information transmitted and mutual trust between member states. in addition, business will be encouraged to recruit highly qualified professionals from other eu member states.

in writing. − on 19 december 2011, the council approved guidelines for negotiations with a view to concluding an agreement with armenia on visa facilitation. the negotiations were opened in yerevan on 27 february 2012 and the final text of the agreement was initialled on 18 october 2012. in accordance with the decision of the government of the republic of armenia of 4 october 2012, as of 10 january 2013 all citizens of the eu, as well as citizens of schengen associated countries, are exempted from the visa requirement. the eu has already concluded agreements on simplification of all regimes with nine non-eu countries. as regards the south caucasus countries, it should be noted that the agreement has so far been concluded with georgia, but that negotiations are already under way with azerbaijan. in the joint declaration on the eu-armenia mobility partnership of 27 october 2011, the parties to the agreement decided to establish a mobility partnership based on reciprocity with a view to better managing legal and labour migration, including exchange and temporary migration. i believe that after several rounds of negotiations, armenia is ready to conclude an agreement on the liberalization of the entire regime. i therefore voted in favour, as the visa facilitation regime can give a new impetus to cooperation, mainly the mobility of citizens, which will be facilitated by a more liberal visa regime. the new rules will make procedures faster, cheaper and less bureaucratic. the government of armenia has already abolished the visa requirement for eu citizens as of 10 january 2013.

in writing. - i have given my consent to the conclusion of the readmission agreement recently agreed. purpose to establish rapid and effective procedures for the identification and safe and effective return of persons, based on the principle of reciprocity. the decision to conclude the agreement shall include a set of standard elements to be included in readmission agreements concluded between the eu and third countries. readmission obligations shall be based on full reciprocity. they apply to nationals of the state concerned, to third-country nationals and to stateless persons, thus providing a basis for the establishment of a readmission obligation applicable to the latter two categories of nationals. the agreement lays down the procedures for the practical application of the agreement, including the establishment of a joint readmission committee, the definition of the conditions for the accelerated procedure and the articles on costs, data protection and the relationship with other international commitments. the agreement applies to the territories of armenia and the eu, with the exception of ireland, denmark and the united kingdom. the agreement applies in a manner that guarantees human rights and respects the obligations and responsibilities set out in the international instruments applicable to the parties concerned. armenia is a partner country in the eastern partnership, which is based on a commitment to the principles and fundamental values of international law, including respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, and on 15 july 2010 negotiations were launched on a new and more comprehensive eu-armenia association agreement. in addition, the eu-armenia human rights dialogue was launched in december 2009 and has already been held in four rounds.

in writing. − i believe that a regulation amending the regulation on the establishment of a list of certain authorised health claims made on foods other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk, to children's development and to health should not be adopted. first, it does not correspond to the purpose and content of the basic act. particular attention shall be paid to ensuring a high level of consumer protection and facilitating consumer choice. there must be an eu-wide imperative ban on the use of false, ambiguous or misleading claims about the nutritional and health characteristics of food.
in writing. − some health claims printed on foods tend to confuse consumers instead of educate them. this must be avoided because it makes claims irrelevant. health claims printed on food labels should be logical and serve a purpose. they need to be based on scientific research, providing the consumer with only beneficial, useful information. the information printed on labels should be used to positively influence diet choices. companies put false claims on their food labels in attempt to appeal to consumers and sell more of their product. this is unethical and contradicts the initial goal, which was to reduce the risk of disease by placing health claims on labels. the claims placed on labels should be carefully scrutinised to ensure that they serve a purpose and are factually supported by scientific research. the goal is not to place a ban on sugar products. products with high sugar content such as chocolate and soda already have nutrition labels on them, making the health claims unnecessary. i support the commission’s position to stop the use of health claims made on food labels. i voted against this motion for a resolution.

author. − madam president, the eastern partnership vilnius summit represents a historic opportunity not to be missed for the union. the eu may sign an association agreement, including a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta), with ukraine. such an agreement may entail large economic and commercial benefits for this country and tie its laws and standards to our single market. to capitalise on these gains, ukraine must do two things. firstly, it must run the last mile in fulfilling the political requirements set by the eu, enabling the eu to prepare the implementation of the dcfta together with our ukrainian friends. secondly, it must prepare the economic ground which would allow the dcfta to bring the expected results, in particular with regard to the following. ukraine still needs to improve its business climate, fight corruption and work together with the eu on fixing the bilateral trade irritants. while i am supportive of the ukrainian willingness to sign and implement the dcfta, i worry that not all efforts are being made to actually turn the country towards a more business-friendly environment and towards resolving serious commercial issues, such as the recently-introduced car recycling fee, the delays in vat reimbursements, etc. secondly, the demand by ukraine to renegotiate its tariffs at the wto over more than 300 tariff lines, just when it is about to sign and implement a dcfta which would slash bilateral tariffs, also raises concerns. thirdly, ukraine must broadly reform its economy, not only to prepare for implementing its commitments towards the eu, but also to improve its track record and convince the imf that it can be a serious and committed recipient of international loans and repay its debts. this raises concerns, and i know that commissioner de gucht went to ukraine a fortnight ago and that he has regular contacts with the ukrainian government. but can the commission quote at least some signs of progress made by ukraine towards meeting our expectations for the economic reforms? so i ask the commission: how can europe and ukraine effectively work on the future application of the dcfta when so many bilateral trade irritants remain? on moldova and georgia, i urge the commission to find ways to shield these countries from russian pressure: they must be allowed to prepare for the signature and the application of the dcftas in the coming years. there again, the case of ukraine should serve as a lesson that the eu should not stand still and should be proactive. i welcome the commission proposal to increase our autonomous trade preferences to moldova by removing eu quotas on their exports of wine. this gesture will go a long way towards countering russian pressure by showing the people of moldova that the eu can act swiftly and show solidarity. on georgia, i remain concerned that the implementation will be complicated by the georgian government’s lack of control over south ossetia and abkhazia. but we should note that, despite the world crisis and the conflicts, georgia has remained an open trading partner which can boast a very good economic record in recent years. encouraging it to continue on this path should be the key to sustaining the vilnius momentum into 2014, until the association agreement encompassing a dcfta is signed. finally, the upcoming summit is an opportunity to reassess our relations with armenia and azerbaijan, two countries which for different reasons are not on track towards signing a dcfta. i deeply regret armenia’s decision to join the customs union, mostly for geopolitical reasons which have nothing to do with the long-term economic needs and interests of this country, which is already largely integrated with the customs union partners through the commonwealth of independent states. this course of events determines the necessity not to reduce to zero but to redefine and if possible keep improving our trade relations with armenia. surely the armenian membership of a customs union does not facilitate such a task? but i look forward to hearing from the commissioner on this issue. as for azerbaijan, the eu cannot consider negotiating a dcfta because this country is not a wto member. but the commission should make good use of the opportunity to upgrade the trade-and-investment-related provisions of the partnership and cooperation agreement and should explore the value of sectoral agreements, for example in the field of trade in energy products. let us not be dogmatic about the notion of association agreements. after vilnius we should consider being innovative in proposing new forms of agreements with these two partners. finally, regarding belarus, i look forward to hearing from the commissioner on the status of belarus’s wto accession perspectives. to conclude, i want this vilnius summit to be a success, but it can only be successful if we see it not as an end in itself but as the beginning of the next phase of the eastern partnership towards implementing economic integration with the eu and finally seeing things change on the ground for the benefit of the citizens in our eastern partner countries.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the eu has established a system of exclusive trade arrangements for countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union's stabilisation and association process. in fact, this regulation provides for the duty-free admission to the eu market of almost all goods from albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia, on an exclusive and unlimited basis. the eu has concluded stabilisation and association agreements or interim agreements on trade and trade-related matters with the listed countries, with the exception of kosovo. kosovo has only a single gtc, but when other countries use this gtc, kosovo exporters lose access to the eu market on preferential terms. the proposed amendment corrects this situation and grants kosovo a tariff quota of 20 000 hl of wine.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on in vitro diagnostic medical devices. diagnostic medical devices (dmds) are among the most important medical devices and can be the basis for all therapies, including pharmaceuticals and surgery. proper diagnosis is essential to preventing diseases and ensuring effective treatment. the introduction of low-quality ivds on the market increases the risk that the results of the studies will be misleading and that the treatment chosen will not be beneficial or even life-threatening. since these devices can circulate freely in the eu single market and are not subject to national restrictions, we must ensure that they are as safe as possible. in other words, the hundreds of thousands of different types of medical devices currently on the european union market - from patches, syringes, catheters and blood sampling devices to sophisticated implants and life support technologies - must be safe not only for patients, but also for healthcare professionals who use or handle them and for non-specialists who come into contact with them. i agree with the rapporteur that the controls by member states on the use of these devices should be strengthened and that inspections can be carried out without prior warning.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to tighten controls on medical devices. the commission has proposed two more transparent and more scientifically and technologically advanced regulations in this area: the medical devices regulation and the in vitro diagnostic medical devices regulation. there are currently more than 500 000 different types of appliances on the market, worth around €95 billion. these include products such as patches, contact lenses, x-ray machines, pacemakers, hiv blood tests, and so forth. i support the proposed rules which will improve the availability of these products on the market and strengthen the control of in vitro diagnostic medical devices, especially after the scandal in europe over substandard breast implants and hip replacements. i support the proposals for stricter supervision of independent evaluation bodies, clearer rights and obligations for manufacturers, importers and distributors, and an expanded medical device database. it is essential to ensure better traceability of devices throughout the supply chain and to be able to respond quickly and effectively to safety concerns.
in writing. − i voted in favour as it will improve patient information on the use of diagnostic medical devices for hiv, pregnancy or dna testing. the proposed reinforcement will increase public safety and strengthen the oversight and control of the entire certification system.
in writing. − i agree with the position that patient safety must be ensured, especially in view of the incidents in recent years of substandard medicines being used in patients. however, as with medicinal products, i would point out that the proposed regulation has its shortcomings. in particular, the proposed verification procedure may, in my view, become a disproportionately complex and costly measure of a restrictive nature.
in writing. − the list of recent health scandals has become too long. it is important to stop these issues at the beginning, the diagnostic stage. without a sufficient diagnostic there is no proper treatment or disease prevention. low quality hiv tests placed on the common market are a good example of how a small diagnostic mistake can lead to major consequences. in the past these low quality tests have produced false negative results, leading the patient to believe he or she is virus free. consequently, the misinformed, infected patient will unknowingly spread hiv. it is up to the eu to ensure the highest possible safety for these ivd medical devices because there are no national borders for these products. further strengthening of the proposed system will only continue to enhance public safety. unannounced visits in production facilities will hold manufacturers accountable and a central approval authority is a good option for preventing future scandals. patient security and safety should always lie at the heart of our concerns, which is why i voted in favour of this report on in vitro diagnostic medical devices.

in writing. - i voted for the resolution on ship recycling. any ship carrying various hazardous materials and leaving the european union for dismantling is itself a dangerous vessel and can therefore only be legally dismantled by the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd). according to the european commission, the majority of dismantling operations are carried out outside the oecd (e.g. in india, pakistan, bangladesh) using a shore-to-shore mechanism, which has environmental and health implications. in such a situation, ship owners may decide not to invest in the costly refurbishment of their vessels, but to scrap them. i agree with the rapporteur that in order to ensure safe ship recycling, the following measures are necessary: the introduction of a financial mechanism to finance environmentally safe ship recycling; the establishment of a list of hazardous substances for all ships calling at eu ports; establish a ship recycling plan for all eu vessels intended for recycling or over 20 years old, subject to approval by the competent authorities; and apply specific sanctions for infringements.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. eu legislation has already introduced a ban on the export of hazardous waste from the eu to countries outside the organisation for economic cooperation and development (oecd) since 1998. however, according to the commission's impact assessment, this legal provision is very often circumvented due to the lack of ship recycling capacity, especially for the largest ships, in the oecd countries. there is very high and unfair competition between processors in the main processing countries (bangladesh, india and pakistan) and their competitors with higher technical standards (eu, turkey and china). the european parliament has already made its position clear on this issue on two occasions, calling for the full implementation of the ban on the export of hazardous waste, including ship-related waste, a clear ban on the landfill method, a list of hazardous materials for all ships entering eu ports, and the establishment of a mandatory shipping industry contribution fund to ensure environmentally sound ship recycling.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is important not to tolerate the dismantling of ships under conditions harmful to people and the environment. most shipowners try to make the most profit by selling their vessels to places where there are no labour and environmental standards and therefore they can offer the highest price. this is a clear market failure, with negative effects on workers' health and the environment. a financial mechanism should be provided to finance the environmentally sound recycling of the ship. all ships calling at eu ports could be charged a fee based on their tonnage. the fees would be transferred to a fund from which a premium would be paid for actual recycling to ship recycling facilities which comply with the provisions of this regulation, in order to ensure their competitiveness. the list of dangerous substances should also be used for all ships calling at eu ports. the appropriate list would be a key precondition for the proper recycling of ships. the ship recycling plan should apply to all ships over 20 years old in order to give owners time to reflect on their responsibilities. such a plan should be approved by the competent authorities. it is essential to ensure that recycling and waste management are environmentally sound.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because it would be unethical to continue to tolerate the dismantling of ships under conditions harmful to people and the environment. under the eu waste shipping regulation, exports of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries have been prohibited since 1998. this prohibition is intended to implement the eu's so-called partial amendment to the requirements of the basel convention on the control of transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and their disposal. any ship carrying various dangerous substances which leaves the eu for dismantling is itself a dangerous ship and can therefore only be legally dismantled in oecd countries. however, this legal provision is very often circumvented. according to the commission's impact assessment, in 2009, more than 90% of eu-flagged vessels were dismantled outside the oecd, mainly in south asia (india, pakistan and bangladesh), using the so-called 'shore-to-shore' method, which has significant environmental and health impacts. this poses a significant both immediate and chronic risk to workers, there is no proper storage of hazardous substances and some hazardous substances that are removed separately are not handled properly. this is the cruelest form of capitalism. most shipowners try to make the most profit by selling their vessels to places where there are no labour and environmental standards and therefore they can offer the highest price. this is a clear market failure, due to the extra cost of outsourcing, with a detrimental impact on workers' health and the environment.
in writing. − the proper recycling and recovery of waste is one of the key objectives of eu environmental policy. therefore, the establishment of detailed rules for the handling of ships and dangerous goods on board should be welcomed. however, this legislation only partially addresses the problem, as a large proportion of vessels belonging essentially to eu entities fly the flags of third countries. a more comprehensive discussion is therefore needed to ensure that such ships are also properly recycled and do not endanger people and the environment in third country ports or coasts.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on european demographic statistics, which aims to regulate the provision and compilation of population data. given the growing demographic challenges and their increasing importance for the development of the european union as a whole, statistical data are essential for making meaningful comparisons and drawing conclusions and identifying options for further action. we, the members of the european parliament, call for local, regional and national databases on demographic change to be made comparable, so that data can be evaluated at european level and to encourage the exchange of good practice between national, regional and local authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on european demographic statistics. this proposal aims to establish common principles for the production of systematic european demographic statistics, which would govern the collection, processing and transmission of data on population and natural change statistics. the eu and the world are facing increasing demographic challenges, which are increasingly relevant to the eu's development. clear, reliable and comparable data are therefore essential to draw conclusions and identify opportunities for action across all eu policies.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation amending the regulation laying down rules for the monitoring of trade between the community and third countries in drug precursors. the aim of the proposal is to prevent the use of medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine for the illicit manufacture of methamphetamine by introducing controls on these products when they are traded between the union and third countries, without preventing their free movement. unfortunately, drugs containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine that are used to treat flu symptoms or allergies are being used illegally to produce methamphetamine. they have not been subject to export, import or transit controls until now. the fact that they are not subject to the regulation prevents member states from seizing consignments of medicinal products that are clearly destined for illicit use. i therefore support the proposal to include this type of medicinal product in the list of controlled substances.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because its main objective is to fill the legal vacuum of the regulation. the proposal lays down rules for the monitoring of trade in precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances between the community and third countries. the regulation will cover medicines containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine used to treat colds, flu symptoms or allergies, which are still used illegally to produce methamphetamine. the exemption from the regulation on medicinal products prevents member states from easily seizing or detaining consignments of medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine that are clearly intended for illicit use. in this case, medicinal products would be included in the definition of scheduled substances and a new category of substances would be created in order to allow a slightly better adaptation of the controls to be carried out on scheduled substances.
in writing. − trade in precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances between the community and third countries is subject to strict monitoring rules, and controlled precursors are included in the official list. unfortunately, the current legal framework does not cover medicines. i agree with the rapporteur that there is a need to tighten controls in this area because some medicines, such as those used to treat influenza or the flu, contain ephedrine or pseudoephedrine which can be used to produce narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. a clearer regulation of this area and a systematic approach to the monitoring of trade in precursors would lead to better results in the fight against illicit drug trafficking.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. as is well known, precursors of drugs and psychotropic substances are chemicals that are often used in various industrial processes (for example, in the production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes or detergents). however, they may also be misused for the illicit manufacture of drugs. these substances are often stolen or bought for illicit activities. despite the existence of a licensing and registration system under the existing legal framework to monitor trade in precursors in the european union, the control measures applied are not sufficiently rigorous. i agree with the rapporteur that, in order to prevent the illicit acquisition of precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, it is necessary to strengthen the registration rules, to establish a european database on precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances and to focus more on monitoring the trade in acetic anhydride, which is the main ingredient in the production of heroin.

in writing. − if you have acetic anhydride is legally used in the production of plastics, textiles, paints, photochemicals, perfumes, explosives and aspirin, but may be used illegally in the production of heroin, amphetamines and cocaine. it is the main precursor of heroin, which accounts for the highest number of drugrelated deaths in the eu. i agreed that the problem of the illicit acquisition of precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances should be tackled. better monitoring of trade in acetic anhydride is necessary: the requirements to be applied are more stringent, the end-users of acetic anhydride will have to register with the competent authorities, whereas only producers and operators handling acetic anhydride have been registered so far. it is necessary to strengthen the rules for registration, i.e. to strengthen the definitions used and to establish more harmonised conditions and/or requirements for registration, while ensuring a certain flexibility to adapt the categories to changing circumstances. it is necessary to establish a european database on precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, containing information on precursors seized in the eu, and to establish a list of all operators and users of precursors licensed or registered in the eu. the proposal allows the legal marketing and use of acetic anhydride without creating any unnecessary administrative burden for the companies. this also allows the competent authorities to monitor trade flows more closely in order to identify and stop illegal acquisitions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the adoption of an e-justice action plan 2014-2018. the first european e-justice action plan was implemented in 2009-2013 and aimed to improve access to legal and judicial information and judicial and administrative processes for both citizens and lawyers. e. justice has an important role to play in improving mutual trust and understanding and thus in consolidating the mutual recognition of judicial and administrative decisions, which is one of the fundamental principles of the eu legal system. e-justice systems reduce the costs of judicial and administrative processes, in particular by automating the exchange of information, the service of documents and the translation of procedural documents. i support calls for member states and the commission to reduce cross-border red tape by increasing the exchange of documents electronically, using videoconferencing and better linking judicial and administrative registers. appropriate attention should be paid to the development of e-learning tools for judicial authorities and the possibility should be provided for to fund successful european and national e-justice projects that would bring real european added value to citizens.
