in writing. − i supported this proposal because the eu's civil law instruments and international procedures are relatively little known and because 73% of citizens believe that additional measures are needed to make civil law more accessible to them in other member states. e-justice is a means of improving access to legal and judicial information and judicial and administrative processes for both citizens and lawyers. e. justice has an important role to play in improving mutual trust and understanding and thus in consolidating the mutual recognition of judicial and administrative decisions, which is one of the fundamental principles of the eu legal system. the eu justice programme 2014-2020 should provide for the possibility to fund successful european and national e-justice projects that would bring real european added value to citizens. the time has therefore come to decide on an e-justice action plan 2014-2018 and this e-justice action plan should be drawn up on the basis of the principle of open access and all member states should be encouraged to participate.
in writing. − i support the ep resolution on the e-justice action plan 2014-2018. e. justice is a tool that improves access to legal and judicial information, facilitates access to judicial and administrative processes and contributes to reducing red tape. projects such as e-justice or the codex have helped to reduce the cost of judicial and administrative procedures and to make eu civil law easier and simpler for eu citizens. by supporting such projects, we contribute to the development of a european judicial culture and to the legal literacy of eu citizens.
the security of the member states of the european union, and the security of europe, depends in particular on neighbourhood. neighbourhood, understood as agreement and cooperation for the common good, is different from what is understood by one's neighbourhood, being next to each other, and is in fact competition, who will influence whom and who will control what. we have an old neighbour in central and eastern europe who has always been and still is dominating. the independence of central europe, and even more so the friendly relations with the eastern european countries which want to be closer to the european union, irritate and anger this neighbour who still thinks he must rule and dominate. the european union's policy on the eastern neighbourhood and all other energy links and relations should therefore be calm and firm, because this is the basis of our security. in the hope that this great geographical neighbour, who really feels like a rival and treats the european union as an unpleasant and dangerous rival, that this geographical neighbour will begin to understand the benefits of a different neighbourhood and the benefits of cooperation. this requires patience, a calm and firm policy, no conciliation and no attempt to appease a geographical neighbour who is unwisely angry.
in writing. mr president, the european union's common foreign and security policy is a major challenge in the face of rapid political change around the world. africa or the middle east are examples. for these reasons, the european union must adopt a new and more credible foreign policy to safeguard the interests and positions of the member states at international level. therefore, the common international policy should not replace the policies of the member states but should coordinate and provide diplomatic support. only by applying this rule consistently and collectively will we be able to achieve our strategic objectives and increase the european union's importance in international politics. for these reasons, we are concerned by the continuing lack of a clear strategy for relations with the rest of the world. as a result, the objectives of the lisbon treaty have not yet been achieved in this area. in the context of the council report, it is worth noting the development of 'strategic partnerships' as a form of cooperation between the european union and existing and emerging global leaders. however, it should be borne in mind that this idea requires clear criteria for the european union's position in international politics. there is another important aspect of the european union's international policy that deserves attention. this is the european union's neighbourhood policy, which is currently in a difficult situation. it should be given a higher priority and its importance should be enhanced, as it will help to ensure political stability in the european union's immediate neighbourhood.
madam president, the document that we are discussing today will guide our environmental policy for the next six years. whereas previous action programmes focused more on the protection of the environment, the current document – through its title, ‘living well, within the limits of our planet’ – reflects the principle of the integration of environmental issues into other policy areas. one of the principles of our future economic models is a resource-efficient europe. this means that we must perceive our environment and its protection not as restricting the economy but as offering further opportunities: stricter rules on waste management; the protection of natural resources, including drinking water; energy saving and efficiency; renewable energy. we can look to some non-eu members for good examples as regards technologies. we should look at environmental policy from the right angle: not in terms of increased costs, but rather as presenting new opportunities for business, including the creation of new jobs and new eco-industries, based on sustainable practices. this document does not set goals in a strict sense; rather it allows the european union to stay among the frontrunners in global environmental politics. therefore, i urge the commission to present proposals for swifter implementation of the programme and for achieving its goals. at the same time, i hope that representatives of my country, lithuania, will successfully complete the negotiations on the final text of this seventh environmental action programme. i would like to thank the rapporteur, gaston franco, and his colleagues who worked on this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2014. it should be emphasised that the priorities of the 2014 budget are sustainable growth, competitiveness, job creation and the fight against youth unemployment, as well as the eu's role in the world. we, the members of the european parliament, oppose the council of the european union's proposal to reduce the 2014 eu budget for research, employment and the digital agenda, as these areas are crucial for economic growth, and we propose to allocate an additional €34 million to these areas. we also reject the eu council's proposal to reduce aid to the middle east and refugees by eur 250 million, as ensuring peace and political stability in the middle east is an important part of the eu's foreign policy. we also propose to increase the budget for the eu external border management agency frontex, as it is necessary to provide the necessary resources for the implementation of eurosur as a pan-european border surveillance system. the scheme can help reduce the number of irregular migrants entering the eu and the number of irregular migrants dying at sea. it will also help to prevent transnational crime. compared to the 2013 eu budget, we propose €8.1 billion less for commitments and €4.3 billion less for payments. i also believe that the european parliament and the council should draw up a plan for the transition to single seat seat transport in order to ensure long-term budgetary savings.

in writing. − i voted against the council's proposal to reduce the eu's 2014 budget for research and employment. the parliament proposed that the eu budget for 2014 should be €142.6 billion for commitments (€141.8 billion proposed by the council) and €136.1 billion for payments (€134.8 billion proposed by the council). compared to this year's eu budget, the proposed reduction is €8.1 billion for commitments and €4.3 billion for payments. in areas such as the digital agenda, research, entrepreneurship and youth employment, which contribute to economic growth, i voted against the eu council's proposal to reduce funding by €629 million. i think that additional funding is needed in these areas. i am also convinced that this year's eu budget deficit should not be carried over to the next year. following this vote in plenary, the european parliament and the council of the eu must agree on the future budget within three weeks.

in writing. − i supported the proposal because it is necessary to pay sufficient attention to the importance of the collection, mapping and dissemination of fisheries data and to the usefulness and practical application of these data. it is necessary to promote the availability and accessibility of data, to ensure the efficient collection and compilation of data and to ensure that the processing and interpretation of data is clearly beneficial. a single digital map of the european seabed at variable resolution should be produced by 2020. the digital map will cover a wide range of areas, including information on seabed topography, geology, habitats and ecosystems, and human activities. marine mapping is essential for the safe extraction of any resource. although the lithuanian watershed is not large, its cartographic exploration is poor the mapping carried out at a scale of 1:200 000 and only the part of the watershed between klaipėda and šventa was mapped at a scale of 1:50 000. the state geological maps of the water area drawn up here are intended to be used to solve problems of the coastal and inland industry, to meet the needs of the protection of the territorial economic zone, fisheries, shipping and other environmental protection and natural production. unfortunately, the mapping has been interrupted by a lack of funds. the present report is therefore likely to encourage the development of such work. in addition, the possible developments in the hydrocarbon works sector will require a thorough environmental impact assessment, which in turn can only be done with cartographic data.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the european union's rights to apply and enforce international trade rules. the eu does not have a common legal framework for the enforcement of union rights under international trade agreements. the purpose of the draft regulation is to establish rules and procedures to ensure that, in the event of a third country's breach of international trade rules, the union can effectively exercise its rights to suspend concessions to parties in order to find a satisfactory solution, adjust them and adjust other commitments in trade relations with third countries. i agree with the rapporteur's suggestions to take retaliatory action only in the event of an emergency. it is also important to ensure a systematic exchange of information between the commission and parliament, without distorting the decision-making process.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the european maritime and fisheries fund, which sets out an ambitious objective to end overfishing and to put the european fisheries sector on a sustainable and profitable business path. i think it is particularly important to stress the need to provide more support for data collection and the development of controls and to stop encouraging the growth of fishing capacity. in particular, given that the european union's annual subsidies to the fisheries sector currently amount to some eur 836 million for structural measures and eur 156 million for fisheries partnership agreements, only eur 50 million is allocated to research, data collection and the provision of management and control measures. effective data collection and control are essential elements for the management of fisheries and therefore the amount allocated to data collection and control should be doubled. secondly, there is a high prevalence of overfishing in eu waters. in some regions, the level of eu fishing capacity is exceeded by two or three times. currently, 39% of the assessed stocks in the atlantic and 88% in the mediterranean are over-exploited. it should be borne in mind that this state of fish stocks can cost more than eur 3 billion per year in lost catches. we in the european parliament therefore oppose support for fleet renewal and measures to maintain or even increase excess fishing capacity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a european maritime and fisheries fund. the purpose of the proposal is to create a new fund for the eu's maritime and fisheries policies. the commission proposes to set up a new european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) for the period 2014-2020. the fund would finance projects that create new jobs and improve the quality of life in europe's coastal areas. this fund would replace the current european fisheries fund (eff) and various other instruments. the financial package proposed for the period 2014-2020 is eur 6,5 billion. i support the proposals to use the new fund to support innovative projects such as the replacement of fishing nets with more selective fishing gear, to reduce the number of fish being returned to the sea, and the development of new technologies to reduce the environmental impact of fishing and fisheries. at the same time, the emff should allocate sufficient resources for data collection, monitoring and control. i support the s&d group's position that the eu's fisheries policy should be renewed to ensure sustainable fisheries and the recovery of fish stocks.

in writing. - i support this resolution on the warsaw climate change conference. the aim of the conference is to ensure progress on the durban platform and to prepare for the conclusion of a global legally binding agreement by 2015. at the un climate change conference in durban, south africa, an agreement was reached that provided for international climate change strategies by nearly 200 countries. the eu is working to put the plan into practice. 90% of the world's emissions are still emitted by developing countries, which have not made any commitments to reduce emissions under the current kyoto protocol. a new green climate fund was created in durban, which will act as one of the main channels for distributing the $100 billion that the developed world has committed to raise annually by 2020 to help developing countries implement their climate change mitigation plans. i agree with the suggestions that the new agreement should include ambitious and sufficient greenhouse gas reduction targets for all polluters and the endorsement of appropriate policy measures to achieve these targets.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering. organised crime, corruption and money laundering have already become a global problem and require an adequate response. there are about 3600 transnational criminal organisations operating in the european union. the typical tools of organised crime already include not only violence and intimidation but also corruption. money laundering, in turn, is often seen as both a typical activity of organised crime and a phenomenon closely linked to corruption, tax fraud and tax evasion. thus, organised crime, corruption and money laundering, although different phenomena, often have interconnections and therefore require targeted action. we in the european parliament are in favour of creating a uniform and coherent legal framework to tackle the economic basis of organised crime and believe that police and judicial cooperation must be strengthened both at eu and international level. a more efficient and less complex system of public administration would allow for more responsible policymaking, a faster and more reliable criminal justice process, a more transparent banking system and more.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which provides for measures to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. ep the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering was set up in 2012 to investigate the impact of the mafia on the eu economy and to propose measures to enable the eu to combat this crime at international, eu and national level. the committee's figures show that vat evasion costs the eu €100 million a year, 880 000 workers are in forced labour, there are at least 20 million cases of petty corruption in the eu public sector and corruption costs 1% of eu gdp. i support the action plan foreseen by the committee for 2014-2019 to encourage the eu to focus on the sources of income and financial assets of organised crime. the seizure of assets acquired through criminal means could be used for social purposes, and the fight against match-fixing, corruption in sport and vote-buying is necessary. the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office is a very important step.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which sets out a package of measures and initiatives that need to be taken to combat organised crime, money laundering and corruption effectively. these phenomena have been increasing in the european union over the past few decades due to the openness of borders and the opportunities offered by new technologies, and they require effective measures to combat them at both national and eu level, as well as at international level. the usual means of action of organised crime already include not only violence and the expropriation of property, but also corruption. money laundering is closely linked to corruption, tax fraud and tax evasion. the european parliament therefore calls for enhanced cooperation between the law enforcement authorities of the member states, europol, eurojust, the european anti-fraud office (olaf) and the european network and information security agency. the ep calls on the commission to adopt as soon as possible a directive on the confiscation of proceeds of crime. bank secrecy and tax havens should be abolished in the fight against corruption and money laundering. it is important that member states themselves implement the proposed measures internally, pursuing a strong policy to combat these crimes. it is also necessary that they cooperate with third countries, as this is the only way to disrupt organised crime networks and prevent them from further developing and establishing themselves in the european union. only by working together and sharing information about criminals and their networks can we protect our citizens and their property.
in writing. - i supported the need to tackle the root causes of organised crime, corruption and money laundering. there are currently almost 4000 transnational criminal organisations operating in the eu. according to the european commission, corruption in the european union amounts to about €120 billion a year. according to the international labour organisation, 880,000 workers in the eu are in forced labour, of whom 270,000 are victims of sexual exploitation, the majority of whom are women. i believe that it is necessary to establish a european public prosecutor's office, to abolish banking secrecy and tax havens, to prevent economic operators convicted of organised and financial crime from participating in public procurement, and to provide for criminal liability for fraud in sport. it is necessary to eliminate the root causes of trafficking in human beings and forced labour, to establish, where appropriate, the legal liability of legal persons in cases of financial crime, to improve the methods of tracing and recovering the proceeds of organised crime, to put an end to cases of tax evasion and avoidance, to increase the transparency of public administration by providing greater access to documents for the public and, where necessary, to lay down specific rules to prevent and resolve conflicts of interest, and to establish a transparency register. the most effective means of combating organised crime are strict legal consequences, effective detection and confiscation of the means and proceeds of crime.
in writing. − despite deepening eu integration and a systematic response to many problems, the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering remains a major challenge for eu and national institutions. criminal activity also affects ordinary eu citizens. it is clear that the fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering requires better cooperation at international, eu and national levels. the fight against these crimes requires a uniform and coherent legal framework, the promotion of honest business practices by business entities and the establishment of a reliable and transparent banking system. successfully tackling organised crime, corruption and money laundering is essential to improving the opportunities for eu citizens to enjoy the freedoms offered by the internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a stronger european neighbourhood policy. the aim of the neighbourhood policy is to strengthen the partnership between the eu and neighbouring countries and societies in order to consolidate democracy, ensure sustainable economic growth and manage international relations. the next eastern partnership summit will take place in vilnius on 28 and 29 november 2013. the eu will seek to initial the association agreements, including the close cooperation and comprehensive free trade agreements with georgia and moldova, at this meeting. it is also important to seek cooperation with armenia, azerbaijan and belarus during the meeting. belarus should use the lithuanian presidency of the council of the eu and the meeting in vilnius as an opportunity to improve relations with the eu. the main objective of the meeting was the signing of the eu-ukraine association agreement on close cooperation and a comprehensive free trade area. i am in favour of concluding the agreement if all the eu's demands are met. i regret the recent trade sanctions imposed by russia on ukrainian exports, and russia should immediately end the economic and political pressure it is exerting on the eastern partnership countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the implementation of the european neighbourhood policy should strengthen the partnership between the eu and neighbouring countries in order to build and consolidate a thriving democracy, ensure sustainable economic growth and manage international relations. a functioning democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law are the key pillars of the eu's partnership with its neighbours. a sound democracy requires a strong and lasting commitment by governments to free and fair elections, freedom of association, expression and assembly, freedom of the press and media, the rule of law, and independent courts. it is also necessary to combat corruption, reform the security and law enforcement sectors and establish democratic control of the armed forces and security forces. the european union's foreign policy must be consistent, i.e. not contradict its internal policies, and avoid double standards. the economic and financial crisis cannot justify a reduction in the union's commitments to its neighbours. the eu should play a more active role in seeking a peaceful resolution of conflicts, including entrenched ones, which currently represent insurmountable obstacles to the development of full-fledged good neighbourly relations and regional cooperation in the eastern and southern partners. it is therefore important for the eu to strengthen cooperation with civil society in neighbouring countries and to provide its support through a range of funding instruments.
in writing. − parliament recommends that the eu council in vilnius sign an association agreement with ukraine if the necessary conditions are met. i believe that the eu must maintain its commitments to its eastern and southern neighbours and reward those countries that are successful in reforming. the eu's neighbourhood policy must be based on the principles of 'support for progress' and 'less support for less progress'. the main problems in the eastern partnership countries are related to the rule of law, the state of democracy, including electoral and judicial systems, and selective justice. until we have solved these problems, we cannot expect these countries to come closer to our systems and political values. i do not support the russian pressure to prevent these countries from working more closely with the eu. the ep regretted the fact that in the run-up to the vilnius summit, pressure of various kinds was being put on the eastern partnership countries, such as the application of trade measures, visa policies, restrictions on the mobility of workers, interference in frozen conflicts, etc. i believe that we need to show strong support for all the eastern partnership countries that have their aspirations and choices linked to europe. the sovereign right of each state to choose political and trade unions and the gradual integration of partner countries into the eu are consistent with the objective of good neighbourly relations with russia. meanwhile, in assessing the progress of the eu's southern neighbours, it is proposed to ensure a successful transition to democracy in these countries and to work more effectively towards social justice and a better quality of life.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy, with its 16 partners, contributes to the creation of a wider area of democracy, economic prosperity and stability. this policy is based on mutual willingness to cooperate and the principle of 'more for more', i.e. the more progress a partner makes and the commitment to strengthening democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and freedoms, the more the eu supports reforms and vice versa. the lithuanian presidency's eastern partnership summit in vilnius could be a very important one. after five years of the partnership, very important and progress-making decisions should be taken. even belarus has a window of opportunity if it is willing to take advantage of it. the countries of europe's southern neighbourhood face major challenges related to democratisation, economic conditions, conflicts and social problems. the eu is contributing to the solution of these problems to the extent possible. at the same time, the responsibility for peace, democratisation, progress in the region and national reforms lies primarily with the partners themselves.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a european semester for the coordination of economic policies. the european semester provides for the coordination of budgetary and economic policies of the eu member states. it is regrettable that in 2012 only 15% of the approximately 400 country-specific recommendations were addressed. it is important to better coordinate the implementation of this measure, taking more account of economic growth, employment, investment and social aspects. i support the proposals outlined to create a competitiveness and convergence instrument to help eu member states mitigate the short-term negative effects of economic reforms. unemployment has a significant bearing on priority investment in education, better financing for small businesses. it is also important to examine the possibility of a minimum unemployment benefit in the euro area. i support greater accountability and transparency for the european stability mechanism and the eurogroup.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is very important to assess the implementation of the priorities and objectives set at eu level, especially in the field of employment and social policy. the fight against unemployment, especially among young people, must be a top policy priority for the european union and the member states, and therefore more eu funds must be used for their intended purpose in implementing all the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular in the areas of growth and employment policies, including policies to combat youth unemployment and long-term unemployment. it is essential to allocate additional funds and develop new measures to tackle youth unemployment by reducing the number of young people out of work, education and training and youth poverty. the european parliament also calls on member states with low labour market participation, in cooperation with the social partners, to actively pursue comprehensive and inclusive labour market measures, such as the provision of training and employment services, and other reforms, the implementation of which would increase opportunities for quality employment, help reconcile work and private life, prevent early exit from the labour market, improve competitiveness and help combat labour market segmentation, and help adapt workers' skills to labour market requirements.
in writing. − i voted on the annual resolution on the european semester. the european semester provides for the coordination of budgetary and economic policies of the eu member states. member states need not only fiscal consolidation but also structural reforms to deliver real, sustainable and socially sustainable growth and increased competitiveness, while taking concrete and urgent action to tackle unacceptably high levels of unemployment, especially among young people. the commission should monitor the consistency of all member states' reports with the europe 2020 objectives, in particular those related to poverty reduction and employment, and closely monitor the interconnections and interdependencies between policy areas. the eu budget, although very modest in absolute and relative terms in relation to the union's economic well-being, provides a high added value as a means of promoting the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, given its role in stimulating investment. the eu youth guarantee and the proposed youth employment initiative should be supported as useful tools to combat the unacceptably high level of youth unemployment. the very low level of funding (from a budgetary point of view) for the youth employment initiative over the entire period of the next mff is a concern and it is necessary to use all available means to reinforce this activity. i believe that the european semester should take greater account of economic growth, employment, investment and social aspects.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the signing of the public procurement agreement (ppo). the gpa is an international agreement on market access to public procurement, which entered into force in 1996 and to which 15 countries, including the eu, are signatories. it defines the rules for the tendering procedure and the contracting parties specify the part of their public procurement market they open to international competition. i agree that the 1996 contract needs to be improved in order to improve the rules on public procurement and to include new goods and services in the list of public procurement. the approval of the renewed contract will provide the european union with additional market access opportunities with a potential value of up to eur 30 billion. it is important that the contract includes the possibility of using electronic auctions and provides for the establishment of a free centralised electronic database providing information on the contracting entities. i support the proposal that companies found guilty of serious crimes may be excluded from the procurement process.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because ensuring that services of general interest are provided to the population, in particular basic services such as water supply, housing, waste management, health care, education and cultural services, remains one of the most important tasks of any government. different countries use different approaches to combine this task with the need to use limited public resources efficiently and with the desire to purchase services and goods of the best value and quality. in many countries, the government and its agencies are collectively the largest purchasers of goods ranging from basic commodities to high-tech equipment. the eu has therefore put in place a set of rules that increase transparency and encourage the latest tendering practices, such as electronic public procurement. increasing transparency under eu public procurement rules increases legal certainty and helps to fight corruption and bribery in third countries. in many countries, public procurement is also used as a key tool to promote employment and economic activity in the region and to promote high standards of environmental protection and decent working conditions. given the differences in administrative levels of contracting entities, the task of a public procurement contract is difficult to establish a fair level playing field while allowing sufficient scope for political decisions and diversity. it is also essential that public procurement contracts provide legal certainty for eu companies to access foreign markets.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this regulation, which provides for eu financial support for the financing of the decommissioning of the ignalina nuclear power plant for the period 2014-2020. i am pleased that we have been able to secure much more funding than was originally proposed by the commission. lithuania will receive €450 million from the eu over the next seven years, rather than the €228 million proposed by the commission. after lengthy discussions in the itre committee, the members of the committee were convinced that, unlike slovakia and bulgaria, protocol 4 to the accession treaty would apply to lithuania as the legal basis for financial assistance, rather than the euratom treaty. we have voted in favour of this provision, which will ensure funding for the closure of ignalina beyond 2020.
in writing. − i voted in favour of a separate eu programme to support the closure of nuclear power plants (npps) in lithuania, bulgaria and slovakia between 2014 and 2020. during this period, eur 450 million in current prices will be allocated to the closure of ignalina ae. the new rules on the financing of the closure of nuclear power plants will allow the eu to extend its support to lithuania, bulgaria and slovakia, which have committed to decommissioning these plants. they need not only to shut down the reactor but also to remove spent fuel elements and radioactive materials, to deactivate and dismantle nuclear installations and to restore the environment of contaminated sites. the decommissioning of the ignalina nuclear power plant is a long-term process and represents an exceptional financial burden for lithuania, which is out of proportion to the size of the country and its economic capacity. the legal basis for the financing of the closure of this ae should be considered not the euratom treaty but protocol 4 to the eu treaty on the accession of lithuania, which would allow the eu support to be extended beyond 2020 if necessary. the financing is proposed subject to the condition that lithuania, bulgaria and slovakia transpose the eu council directives on nuclear safety and on spent fuel and radioactive waste management, and prepare plans for financing the decommissioning of nuclear reactors, clearly indicating the sources of financing. the european commission shall assess the progress of the closure of those nes by the end of 2017. if the commission decides to review the level of eu support, this should not be at the expense of the safety of the ae.

i thank the rapporteurs and commissioner reding for the good work they have done together. in fact, this directive, which aims to ensure gender representation in companies, is a model for ensuring gender equality in the european union and elsewhere. and for those who are still sceptical about the proposed directive on the inclusion of women in companies, i would like to emphasise that this directive does not oblige companies to appoint only women to board positions, the purpose of this legislation is to ensure that the candidate whose gender is less represented in companies is selected from a number of candidates with the same education and similar qualifications and to achieve the goal of at least 40% of company non-executive directors being representatives of the under-represented gender. lithuania, as the country holding the presidency of the council, is working very hard to reach an agreement on this directive. but the negotiations in the council are certainly not easy, there is still a blocking minority of member states. however, i hope that the council will take stock of the efforts made to achieve progress on gender equality and will be able to reach a common consensus so that we can adopt this directive during the current term of office of the european parliament. good luck voting for this directive tomorrow.
in writing. the question of the location of the seat of the institutions of the european union is a constant concern of our citizens and of our own members of the european parliament. it is becoming increasingly difficult for european citizens to explain why parliament meets in strasbourg for one week a month. moreover, such travel is uneconomical, harmful to the environment and makes it difficult to organise the work of the european parliament itself. this is a question that must be addressed particularly now that budgets are being cut in many member states and parliament is responding accordingly and is seeking to save money on the budget for strasbourg. in considering the arguments for and against the two european parliament seats, we do not wish to diminish the historical and symbolic value of the strasbourg seat, but perhaps there is another way to enshrine this historical value. because today strasbourg, once the symbol of european unity and integration, is the symbol of wasteful spending and bureaucracy. the european parliament should therefore pay particular attention to this issue and take into account the historical significance of its choice of seat, the historical agreement of the member states on the location of all the eu institutions, the opinion of the inhabitants of all the cities concerned and, in general, the opinion of the citizens of the european union. i hope that we will be able to take the views of our citizens into account and, having assessed the situation ourselves, agree that we must aim to do away with the caravan and work in one place.
in writing. mr president, the regulation on the common agricultural policy that we are now considering should primarily promote rural development and support the european agricultural fund, which helps to reduce the agricultural disparity between the so-called old and the new union. the cap must become a component of the wider cohesion policy to stimulate the sector. we must oppose any decisions that threaten local producers, who are the backbone of agriculture in central and eastern europe, especially in countries like lithuania. the separation of direct payments from production would also be necessary, as this would create a level playing field for agricultural trade between farmers from the new eu member states and farmers from the old 'fifteen' who have been subsidised for much longer. the regulation lacks a clear reference to multiannual funding programmes, which should include a specific declaration on the end of the unequal direct payments to farmers from the new member states. in eastern european countries, benefits are several times lower than in western europe. there is no rational justification for sanctioning existing disparities in agricultural financing, which would artificially divide europe into two parts with different rates of development in the agricultural sector. this is not only unfair but also reduces the competitiveness of our agriculture. our goal is to equalise the level of development among the members of the community. the unequal treatment of farmers must be brought to an end in the near future.
for the efd group the main challenges for the european union as a whole next year are to revive growth in an effective and sustainable way and to tackle unemployment. i agree with the commission that economic growth and job creation have been chosen as the top priority, with particular attention to tackling youth unemployment and facilitating access to finance. but i would suggest that we be much more specific. if the institutions of the european union today are trying to regulate the size of cucumbers, eggs or bananas throughout the community, it seems that they should also decide on the mandatory minimum income that the european union should guarantee to every member of the community, to every citizen. we can shout about strengthening the single market to the death, but if almost a fifth of the people in the european union live below the poverty line, we will never achieve that strength. i think that the commission should look for new ways and opportunities to promote youth employment in the community countries. this could be done by increasing subsidies to employers and by reducing or recommending a uniform, say halving, taxation of labour for those under 30 for the member states.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution setting out the objectives, measures and financing of the cap for the period 2014-2020. the milk quotas will expire as of 2015 and the sugar quota system is to be abolished on 30 september 2017, as indicated in the 2005 sugar reform, in order to allow the sector additional time to adapt. this will ensure greater competitiveness of eu producers both on the domestic and global markets (as eu exports are restricted by the world trade organisation's rules on quotas). private storage aid for white sugar will continue to be available after the end of the quota period. new safeguards will also be introduced for all sectors to allow the commission to take urgent action in the event of a single market disruption, such as the measures taken during the e. coli crisis of may-july 2011. these measures will be financed from the crisis reserve, which is financed by reducing direct payments annually. the funds not used for crisis measures will be returned to farmers next year. the school fruit and milk scheme will be continued in 2014-2020 with an increase in funding from eur 90 million to eur 150 million per year.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the reformed eu budget and provisions for the common agricultural policy (cap) for 2014-2020. during this period, the eu will focus more on environmental protection, make aid more equitable and help farmers to face market challenges. the new cap will ensure a better balance between food safety and the environment, help farmers meet the challenges of the future and be fairer. the ep's win additional support for young farmers who can expect an additional 25% of direct payments for land area of at least 25 and at most 90 hectares. more support is also provided for small farmers, while large farmers receiving more than €150 000 will have to accept at least a 5% reduction in support above that amount. parliament has ensured a fairer distribution of aid among eu countries. by 2020, farmers in all eu countries should receive at least 72% of the eu average of direct payments. in addition, almost a third of direct payments to the eu member state will have to be linked to environmental measures: crop diversification, maintenance of existing perennial grasses and the creation of ecological zones on agricultural land. the new rules will prevent the duplication of funding for these measures from different sources of eu support, and farmers who fail to adapt to these measures will not only lose their support but may also be penalised.
in writing. − this regulation is one of the documents governing the new eu agricultural policy based on sustainable growth. i agree with the view that measures to ensure sustainable agriculture (so-called 'greening measures') are necessary to ensure a high level of environmental protection, but that action must also be taken to avoid an additional administrative burden for farmers. it is also important to ensure that the same level of payments is achieved as soon as possible for farmers in all eu member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation. rural development policy will continue to follow the current basic concept of rural development for the next seven years: member states or regions will continue to draw up their multiannual programmes on the basis of existing measures at eu level to meet the needs of their areas. the new regulation sets out six priorities: promoting knowledge transfer and innovation; increasing the competitiveness of all types of agricultural activities and sustainable forest management; supporting the organisation of the food chain, including processing and marketing, and risk management; restoring, preserving and enhancing ecosystems; promoting resource efficiency and the transition to a low-carbon economy; and promoting social inclusion, poverty reduction and economic development in rural areas.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as it appears that the reformed cap will not be fully implemented by 1 january 2014. therefore, transitional rules are needed to define the technical measures to ensure a smooth adaptation to the new conditions while ensuring the continuity of the different forms of cap support. in the case of direct payments, it is necessary to allow sufficient time for the member states, their paying agencies and farmers to be well prepared and fully informed of the new rules well in advance of their application. the transitional rules provide for a procedure for external convergence and flexibility between the two pillars of the cap. in the field of agricultural development, transitional rules are a common practice to establish rules in the interim between two programming periods and to determine how existing measures will be continued in the new programming period, including their financing from new funds. a link between two successive programming periods is necessary. moreover, transitional rules are necessary to ensure that member states continue to make new commitments in 2014 even after the current transitional resources have been exhausted. these transitional rules also include a flexibility mechanism allowing member states to transfer funds between the two pillars of the cap.
in writing. − i supported the rapporteur's recommendation to reject this protocol and to negotiate a new protocol with the commission, which would take full account of the provisions of the western and central pacific fisheries commission (wcpfc) and the nsw, to which kiribati belongs. the protocol is not based on the lpd, is a serious violation of the wcpfc relevant rpa rules. it also distorts the market in terms of fishing rights and deprives kiribati and the region of much-needed revenue. the protocol may undermine the efforts of small island developing states to manage the exploitation of tuna resources and to increase their revenue. it therefore does not contribute to the sustainable management of tuna in the western and central pacific.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the location of the seats of the institutions of the european union. the eu treaty provides for the ep's headquarters to be in strasbourg, where as many as 12 plenary sessions are held each year. however, the lisbon treaty provides for the right of parliament to initiate amendments to the eu treaty. we in the european parliament agree that the principles of a policy of savings, efficiency and ecology must be respected. many member states, with their strict austerity policies, are rational in wasting money on travel between brussels and strasbourg. the estimated additional cost of the geographical location of the ep's premises is as high as €156 to €204 million (10% of the annual eu budget). i agree with the conclusions of the rapporteurs that parliament's ability to organise its activities in a modern and appropriate manner is essential for it to fulfil the functions conferred on it by the treaties and to meet the expectations of its constituents, and that it should therefore initiate the normal procedure for the revision of the treaties, which would give parliament the right to decide on its own matters relating to its internal organisation and timetable, including the question of the location of its seat.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the location of the seats of the institutions of the european union. the aim of the proposal is to amend the eu treaties in such a way that the european parliament (ep) is allowed to decide on its own seat. the cost of ep travel between brussels and strasbourg is about €200 million, or 10% of the parliament's annual budget. each plenary session brings about 5 000 workers, who lose a full day's work travelling. in addition, the parliament buildings in strasbourg are not used 89% of the time, but they need to be heated constantly and staffed throughout the year. the amendment of the current eu treaty is necessary to enable the ep to decide where and when to hold its meetings, and i therefore support it. the treaty would save considerable resources and enable parliament to fulfil its democratic functions fully and properly. having one seat would not only make parliament more efficient, but also save money.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the european parliament calls for it to be given the right to decide where and when ep meetings are to be held. currently, an article in the eu treaty, which can only be amended by the unanimity of all eu countries, stipulates that the ep's headquarters are in strasbourg, where twelve plenary sessions are held per year. although the seat is decided by common accord between the eu member states, the treaty of lisbon gave parliament the power to initiate amendments to the eu treaty. in the resolution adopted, the ep committed itself to initiating a treaty amendment which would allow it to decide on its own jobs. i believe that the european parliament would work more efficiently, more economically and more environmentally by having one seat.
in writing. − we constantly talk about the need to reduce costs, optimise conditions, and strive for sustainable growth. unfortunately, the european parliament (ep) does not always follow these guidelines. it is clear that the different ep seats, with committees working in brussels and plenary sessions in strasbourg, makes the work of the ep more difficult, unnecessarily increases expenditure, and is also criticised by eu citizens who are unhappy with this use of eu budget funds. i am glad that we are returning to this debate in this term of office and, in supporting this report, i hope that the right decision will soon be taken on the ep's place of work.
in writing. − the two seats of the european parliament that were considered a symbol of reconciliation in 1950 are now seen as a symbol of waste. maintaining two seats of the european parliament costs more than eur 150 million annually. it excessive to maintain a second building when only 11% of the year, or 48 days, is spent in plenary. the eu, which is supposed to be a leader in sustainability, wastes about 19 000 tons of co2 commuting back and forth between brussels and strasbourg each month. currently the european parliament is the only directly elected institution that does not have the power to decide on its own seat. parliament must have the right to decide where and when it would like to meet by a simple majority approach. a single seat is the most economical decision for the european parliament, and this report allows the decision of the parliament’s fate to be put into its own hands through an amendment of the current treaties. europe must move forward, and a shuffling parliament between two seats is not a successful plan for the future. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for this report because, for the first time, the 'horizon 2020' (h2020) programme brings together in a single programme the different elements of the eu's overall strategic funding for research and innovation, which have hitherto lacked a common perspective. horizon 2020 is a €80 billion programme for investment in research and innovation in the european union, running from 2014 to 2020. for the first time, horizon 2020 brings together all eu research and innovation funding in one place. more than ever, the focus is on turning scientific breakthroughs into innovative products and services that provide business opportunities and improve people's lives. at the same time, simplification of rules and procedures significantly reduces the administrative burden in order to attract more top-class researchers and more diverse innovative companies.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it expresses parliament's position on the strategic agenda of the european institute of innovation and technology. the european institute of innovation and technology was established in 2008 to contribute to sustainable economic growth and competitiveness by strengthening the innovation capacity of the eu and its member states. the institute is not only a direct innovation vehicle but also an educational one, thus providing an educational platform for eu research and innovation policy. this strategic agenda for the institute, endorsed by parliament, provides that the eit contributes to the scientific basis for innovation by promoting international mobility at disciplinary, sectoral and country level.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as it supports the commission's proposal to integrate the european institute of innovation and technology into the 'horizon 2020' programme, defining its budget and scope of activities. the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) was established in 2008 to implement the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs and to strengthen europe's innovation capacity. it was then decided that europe must find ways to develop its innovation capacity in order to recover from the crises it faces. the eit is the first attempt in the eu to integrate the three dimensions of the knowledge triangle higher education, research and innovation. the eit's main function is to promote closer cooperation between universities, research centres and businesses, with the aim of bridging the gap between research, education and business activities and strengthening the eu's innovation capacity.
in writing. − the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) was established in 2008 to implement the lisbon strategy for growth and jobs and to strengthen europe's innovation capacity. i supported this proposal because the eit aims to integrate the three parts of the knowledge triangle in order to promote competence, which accelerates innovation. the eit is the eit as the implementing instrument of the horizon 2020 programme. by providing for the activities of the knowledge and innovation communities (kics), the eit promotes closer cooperation between universities, research centres and businesses, with the aim of bridging the gap between research, education and business activities and strengthening the eu's innovation capacity. it is proposed to allocate a budget of approximately eur 3 billion to the eit and to integrate the eit's field of activity into the horizon 2020 programme. the budget would be divided into two parts: the first would be for the merger of existing kics and the establishment of three new kics in 2014, the second, taking into account the review carried out at the end of 2017, would be for the continuation of the activities of the existing kics and the establishment of three more kics.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it supports the creation of the cosme programme. this programme will be used to finance measures supporting entrepreneurship and innovation and promoting the development and growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the new multiannual financial perspective. the global competitiveness of european small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) is undermined by market, policy and institutional weaknesses, such as limited access to finance, market access and regulatory burdens. european smes are less productive and grow less quickly than companies elsewhere in the world, and they have more difficulty adapting to change than larger european companies. these difficulties were further exacerbated by the economic crisis of 2008, which disproportionately affected smes. for all these reasons, i welcome the proposal to establish the cosme programme, as it is the only eu spending programme specifically designed to promote smes.
in writing. − i agreed, as environment and business development are important sources of growth and job creation across the eu. the conditions for enterprises, in particular smes, and for citizens wishing to set up businesses must therefore be improved. several key areas need to be focused on that could help to achieve this objective: encouraging the uptake of new competitive business models and the cooperation of smes in new value chains and new markets; improving access to finance for smes in the development and start-up phases; reduce and simplify barriers that are time-consuming for smes; to increase the promotion of the cosme programme and the dissemination of information on the funds available to smes, so that smes are aware of the financial opportunities available to them; to finance the european enterprise network, in particular to identify eu programmes that could increase the competitiveness and growth of enterprises in the single market; support smes by providing advice and information on issues such as market entry barriers, business opportunities, standards and intellectual property rights in priority third countries; to promote the provision of information on digital services; in order to ensure that banks use funds and guarantees to increase lending to smes, a monitoring system should be in place.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it amends regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics. these amendments are necessary because of the recent detection of serious weaknesses, in particular in the statistical quality management system, which have led to inaccurate and in some cases incorrect statistics being published. reliable and accurate european statistics serve two essential purposes: they provide a basis for political decision-making and a means of assessing the state of the economy and society. we need to restore public confidence in statistics, and i therefore agree that the independence of statistical authorities from possible political pressure at national and union level must be guaranteed. one way of doing this is to remove the political aspects from the statistical data production process.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because reliable and accurate european statistics serve two essential purposes as a public good: they are the basis for political decision-making and a means of assessing the state of the economy and society, providing confidence to other governments and markets. unfortunately, events in recent years have shaken public and market confidence. misleading and false statistics can increase political and economic disorder. we need to restore public confidence in statistics. they say that when statistics are politicized, they quickly devalue them. it is therefore essential to remove political aspects from the statistical data production process. for example, this report proposes to prohibit member states from postponing the publication of periodic data. the transition to a european statistical system ensuring professional independence, adequate resources and strict supervision, including sanctions for breaches of quality requirements, is encouraged.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it expresses parliament's position on the regulation defining the european union's customs action programme 2014-2020 (customs 2020). the customs union shall protect the financial interests of the union and of the member states which levy customs duties, levies and taxes. it requires that goods originating in third countries are allowed to move freely within the union only if they comply with union law. this means that large trade flows (7 customs declarations processed every second) have to be managed on a daily basis and customs have to strike a balance between improving the trading conditions of businesses and protecting citizens from threats to their safety and security. this is only possible if the customs administrations of the member states cooperate intensively and efficiently with each other, with other public authorities and with trade and other third parties. the programme will support union customs cooperation, in particular with a view to building human resource networks and capacity building, as well as enhancing it capacity. the proposed 'customs 2020' programme will mainly support customs cooperation between each other and with other relevant parties.

in writing. mr president in recent years, there has been a marked increase in the number and magnitude of natural disasters. in the future, such events are likely to be even more sudden and complex, with longer-lasting effects. this has created an urgent need for coordination and a transition to an effective european disaster management mechanism based on an integrated approach. the eu should support, coordinate and complement the actions of the member states in the field of civil protection in order to improve the effectiveness of the systems for preventing natural disasters. closer involvement of regions, cities and municipalities is necessary, as their local authorities play an important role in preventing and responding to emergencies. that's why we can't ignore them. it should be recalled that the basic principle of civil protection should be to solve problems at the lowest possible level. particular attention should be paid to the regions bordering the eu's external borders and the outermost regions, which are at high risk of natural disasters, including nuclear power plant failures, and where interventions are much more complex and often require assistance from third parties. account should also be taken of the need to provide assistance in a rapid and flexible manner in cases where the scale of disasters exceeds the response capacity of the affected member state or its regional or local administration authorities. therefore, with regard to eu funds, there is a need to link the civil protection mechanism more effectively to the solidarity fund.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at liberalising the import of moldovan wine into the european union. the liberalisation of imports of wine will apply from 1 january 2014 and the liberalisation of imports of other goods, as set out in the eu-moldova free trade agreement initialled in vilnius on 29 november, will apply from the beginning of 2015. this year, russia banned the import of moldovan wine, citing quality violations. however, it is no secret that the ban on wine imports is politically motivated to prevent moldova from moving closer to the european union politically and economically. this document provides duty-free access to the eu market for moldovan wines and should help the country to cope with restrictions imposed by russia. this decision not only creates a free trade area between the eu and moldova, but also demonstrates the eu's strong political support for moldova's choice to move closer to the eu. it is important that the eu shows greater political will in responding to russia's unwarranted pressure on its eastern partners.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because regulation (ec) no 55/2008 provides for autonomous trade preferences (atp) for the republic of moldova, which eliminate all customs tariffs for industrial products and provide better access to the eu market for agricultural products. the period of application of the mrls in accordance with regulation (ec) no 55/2008 shall be until 31 december 2015. the application of the gsp regulation after 1 january 2013 is subject to the successful completion of certain procedures within the world trade organisation (wto). the european union has initiated these procedures and at present the time of their completion is unknown. it is therefore important to ensure unimpeded trade flows from the republic of moldova until 31 december 2015 before the wto procedures are concluded. it is also necessary to ensure legal certainty for economic operators to continue to import in compliance with the apa regulation. it is therefore necessary to provide for the continuous application of the autonomous trade preferences until their expiry date as laid down in council regulation (ec) no 55/2008.
in writing. − i support this regulation, which provides for autonomous trade preferences (atp) for the republic of moldova, eliminating all customs tariffs on industrial products and providing better access to the eu market for agricultural products. it aims to implement the agreement reached to fully liberalise trade in wine. agriculture accounts for about 40% of the moldovan economy. the wine sector is one of moldova's most important export products, employing some 300 000 people. in september, russia punished moldova by banning imports of wine in response to moldova's determination to continue its rapprochement with the eu. this regulation opens up a huge eu market for moldovan products that have lost access to traditional markets. it is important that this measure enter into force immediately. i commend the commission for its prompt and constructive response to the realities and challenges facing the eastern partnership countries with a european perspective.
in writing. - i support the proposal to liberalize bilateral trade. it should be noted that moldova has made significant progress in aligning its legislative provisions with union legislation and standards. in this context, it is necessary to support moldova's reforms and efforts in implementing the european neighbourhood policy and the eastern partnership project even more actively. in order to develop stable and long-lasting trade relations and to provide legal certainty for economic operators, all customs duties on industrial products should be abolished and access to the eu market for agricultural products should be improved. the autonomous trade preferences will facilitate access to a reliable and attractive market for moldova and ensure uninterrupted trade flows.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the protocol on cooperation in the fisheries sector of the kingdom of morocco, which will allow fishing vessels from 11 eu member states to fish in the waters of the kingdom of morocco. the previous protocol was terminated in december 2011 and since then eu vessels have not been fishing in those waters. for the lithuanian long-distance fishing fleet, moroccan waters are one of the most important fishing areas and, together with the fishing opportunities available under the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and mauritania, allow for the seasonal continuity of pelagic fisheries. in 2005-2011, lithuanian vessels caught between 16 and 45 thousand tonnes of pelagic fish per year in moroccan waters, but had to stop fishing activities in 2011 after not voting in favour of the extension of the protocol. the new protocol provides for a lower annual fee for the european union (€30 million instead of €36.1 million, i.e. 17%) and an increase in the overall quotas for each participating member state (33% compared to the previous protocols) than the previous protocol on cooperation between the eu and the kingdom of morocco in the fisheries sector. the new protocol will be in force for four years from its entry into force on january 2014. under the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement, lithuania received an annual pelagic quota of 15 520 tonnes and was the second largest eu member state in terms of its quota. under the new protocol, lithuanian vessels will receive an increased fishing quota of up to 20 693 tonnes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the signing of the fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco. some eu countries, including lithuania, do not question the benefits of such an agreement for fishermen, but opponents argue that such an agreement cannot be signed because morocco has occupied western sahara. i believe that it is necessary to sign it because an agreement allowing fishing in moroccan waters would benefit the fishermen of the member states, including lithuania, and without it the situation in the occupied western sahara would not change. the question of the occupation of western sahara is a political one and must be dealt with separately and not in the framework of a fisheries agreement. within the european union itself, there are major unresolved issues, such as the demarcation of borders with its eastern neighbours. but that does not mean that the whole of the european union has to break off relations with russia. asia, for example, has no active human rights policy, but the european union still has trade and relations with it. why should morocco be an exception? the agreement would provide morocco with €40 million per year: €30 million from the eu budget and €10 million from the shipowners. of this eur 30 million, eur 16 million would be paid by morocco for the resources, and eur 14 million would be allocated to support the moroccan fisheries sector. morocco must ensure that these millions bring direct economic benefits, creating jobs for the local population.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the signing of the protocol to the eu-morocco fisheries agreement. on 24 july 2013, the commission and the government of morocco agreed on a protocol to the eu-morocco fisheries agreement. a number of eu member states are seeking to ratify the protocol, in particular spain, portugal, france, germany, lithuania, latvia, the netherlands, ireland, poland and the united kingdom. this protocol would cover 6 categories of fisheries, including industrial and small-scale fisheries. the new protocol covers the ep's main requirements, as set out in the ep's resolution of 14 december 2011. morocco will have to ensure that this protocol brings direct benefits and benefits to the local population. the obligation to report on the economic and social impact of the protocol on employment, investment and other measurable benefits is provided for.
in writing. − i support the conclusion of this agreement, which is important from an economic, political and environmental point of view and is of particular importance for the eu's fishing fleet. the signature of this agreement will result in an increase in the overall quota for each participating member state. the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement will also ensure the sustainability of the stocks. we must give all eu fishermen the opportunity to engage in the activities that have been developed for many years in the waters of the kingdom of morocco. it should be noted that this fishing area is of particular importance for lithuania, as for many years lithuanian fishing vessels have been actively fishing for pelagic fish in moroccan waters. it is therefore essential that fishing vessels continue to operate successfully in this area and that fishermen are adequately protected.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ratify the protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms. the international convention on transnational organised crime, adopted by the un in 2000, is the first global instrument to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. the convention is further elaborated by three protocols which provide for specific measures to combat specific crimes. the european community has signed the convention and protocols on the illicit entry of migrants, on combating trafficking in human beings and on the illicit manufacturing and trafficking of firearms. this proposal seeks to ratify the protocol against the illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms. i support the recommendations to impose penalties for the illicit manufacture of firearms, their parts and ammunition, forging firearms markings and to provide for measures to confiscate illegally manufactured weapons. it is important that the marking of firearms at the time of their manufacture and importation be ensured by states parties to the protocol in order to identify the manufacturer, the country and the year of importation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of ratifying the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms. the international convention on transnational organised crime, adopted by the un in 2000, is the first global instrument to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. the convention is further elaborated by three protocols which provide for specific measures to combat specific crimes. the european community has signed the convention and protocols on the illicit entry of migrants, on combating trafficking in human beings and on the illicit manufacturing and trafficking of firearms. the protocol aims to prevent and combat the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts and ammunition. it recommends penalties for the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts and ammunition, and for the falsification of firearms markings. measures are in place to confiscate illicitly manufactured weapons.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the agreement with the people's republic of china. the people's republic of china is entitled to regain its previous trading rights in view of the slight deterioration of the situation due to the eu customs union enlargement with the accession of romania and bulgaria. the accession of bulgaria and romania to the eu has led to the enlargement of its customs union. the eu was therefore obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members with a negotiating power on any acceding country's list of commitments in order to avoid an increase in mandatory duties. two issues are addressed: the compensation of higher customs tariffs, which is usually carried out by setting a country tariff quota or by increasing an existing quota; the pre-accession erga omnes tariff quota for bulgaria and romania (not country specific but applicable worldwide) must also be added to the existing eu erga omnes tariff quotas. the products covered by the eu-china countervailing agreement are mainly garlic, mushrooms, chocolate, confectionery and biscuits. the eu has so far concluded similar compensation agreements with cuba, brazil and, with parliament's approval, australia, new zealand, argentina and the usa.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the eu-us memorandum of understanding to resolve the dispute over hormones in beef. this decision provided for the possibility of phasing out the us counter-sanctions on certain eu agricultural products in exchange for the introduction of an autonomous tariff quota of high-quality beef from bovine animals not raised by hormones. the parties failed to reach a lasting solution to the wto dispute and the mou expired in august 2013. the proposed updated mou provides for the use of the tariff quota for the next two years, allowing for the possibility to negotiate a clear dispute settlement by the end of 2015. if no action is taken, the eu will be able to stop applying the autonomous tariff quota of high-quality beef at zero duty and the us will have the right to re-impose sanctions on eu products with an annual value of usd 116.8 million. i support the extension and renewal of the memorandum of understanding as it provides legal clarity for economic operators and additional time to reach a final agreed solution.
in writing. − i supported the proposed extension and renewal of the memorandum of understanding, as it provides legal clarity for economic operators and additional time to reach a final agreed solution. purpose: to extend the eu-us memorandum of understanding to settle the dispute over hormones in beef. on 13 may 2009, the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding, which provided a final solution to the beef hormone dispute. this decision provided for the possibility of phasing out the us counter-sanctions on certain eu agricultural products in exchange for the introduction of an autonomous tariff quota of high-quality beef from bovine animals not raised by hormones. the parties failed to reach a lasting solution to the wto dispute and the mou expired in august 2013. the proposed renewed memorandum of understanding provides for a further extension of the second stage and the unchanged use of the tariff quota for a further two years, allowing for the negotiation of a clear dispute settlement by august 2015. if no action is taken, the eu will be able to stop applying the autonomous tariff quota of high-quality beef at zero duty and the us will have the right to re-impose sanctions on eu products with an annual value of usd 116.8 million.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the new agreement between the eu and côte d'ivoire setting out the eu's fishing opportunities and financial contribution. the eu's fisheries relations with côte d'ivoire formally began in 1990 with the conclusion of the first partnership agreement. the new protocol, which will apply from 2013 to 2018, provides for fishing opportunities for eu tuna vessels and applies provisionally from 1 july 2013 pending the ep's position. this new agreement is based on the results of the final evaluation of the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and côte d'ivoire (2007-2013), carried out by independent experts. the agreement is economically sound, rational, balanced and effective. the aim is to support the development of ivorian fisheries policy, i.e. to develop aquaculture, to combat illegal fishing, which is very successful in the area, and to modernise the system for reporting catches.
