in writing. - i voted for the cloud computing resolution. the economic and commercial prospects of cloud computing based on an internet connection, which allows the user to access all digital information, documents and software from any computer with an internet connection, are growing. companies are increasingly realising that by using the best-performing business tools and/or by significantly increasing infrastructure resources at affordable prices, they can significantly improve operational efficiency. i agree with the rapporteur that europe must promote research and technological development in the field of cloud computing. however, the development of a strategic action plan for cloud computing requires emphasising aspects such as: the integrity of cloud standards (customer switching, high interoperability and open specifications), secure and fair contract terms (enterprise-user contracts are fundamentally different from business-to-business contracts), public sector initiative (citizens could benefit from more efficient and innovative public services) and others. i believe that the full deployment of cloud computing is strategically important for the creation of a digital single market. the development of the european cloud therefore has a unique potential to become a powerful tool to accelerate the creation of the digital single market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at a european union-wide strategy for cloud computing. i welcome the commission's communication on the use of cloud computing in europe and the intention to develop a coherent approach to cloud computing services in the eu. cloud computing is the storage, processing and use of data on remote computers accessible via the internet. users have access to unlimited computing capacity, do not need to invest a lot of capital to meet their needs, and can access their data wherever they are with an internet connection. cloud computing has the potential to significantly reduce users' it costs and to create a wide range of new services. using remote computing, even the smallest businesses can reach ever-larger markets, and governments can make their services more attractive and efficient by reducing costs. in 2014, cloud revenues could reach eur 148,8 billion and 60% of server workloads will be virtual. i agree that the future strategy must address a variety of issues: technological issues related to the development, management and scalability of cloud systems, and non-technical issues such as legal aspects related to data privacy and security, which are major barriers to widespread use of cloud infrastructures.

in writing. - i voted yes. the purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the initial opinion of the rapporteur on the evaluation of eerri and the eerri office (swd(2013) 152) with a view to stimulating reflection and discussion on this issue with a view to producing a harmonised report. the notifier considers that erri is performing its activities properly. it appears that eerri (and the predecessors) have gradually built up the trust between national regulatory authorities, helping to achieve eerri's objectives effectively. however, this should not prevent discussion of the possibility of developing a set of broader ambitions and internal market-oriented objectives for eric and its structure. on the other hand, there appear to be some problems with the erri office itself and with the relationship between the erri office and the office. on the one hand, the evaluation report certifies and recognises the value of eerri and the eerri office since their establishment in 2009, as well as in the areas of network neutrality and international roaming. on the other hand, the evaluation notes that there is still room for improvement in erri's activities. this proposal may be made in view of the short time since the establishment of the erc (it was established following the most recent review of the regulatory framework for electronic communications), but it seems that a number of other structural aspects can still be considered, in particular in view of the fact that another comprehensive review of the electronic communications system will be carried out.
in writing. − i voted in favour of reforming the european union's common fisheries policy (cfp) to limit overfishing and to prohibit fishermen from discarding unwanted catches. the eu council will have to take sustainability into account when negotiating fishing quotas. i am in favour of fishermen following the principle of maximum sustainable yield, i.e. catching only as much of a given species as can be replaced in a year. it is important to apply this principle to eu vessels fishing in third country waters. a quarter of the eu's catches are discarded because of its unsuitability. i agree that from 2015 onwards, 95% of catches will be required to be landed in ports. catches of an inappropriate size or species shall not be authorised for food use but only for other uses. i agree that if it turns out that the fleet of one or another member state is too large, the nca concerned should submit a plan to reduce overcapacity and that if it does not comply with these provisions, the commission should impose financial penalties. it is important to change the rules on the labelling of fishery products from 2014 in order to better inform consumers about where and how the fish was caught.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because a successful fisheries policy can only be achieved if the rules are respected. the new framework regulation thus provides for a decision in principle that eu funds for fisheries can only be disbursed if the rules of the common fisheries policy are respected. this applies both to member states and to individual fisheries undertakings. those detailed rules will be laid down in the regulation on the european maritime and fisheries fund. a major achievement of the negotiating group is the establishment of the so-called fishing opportunities criteria, i.e. member states will in future be able to allocate fishing opportunities (quotas) to their fishermen on the basis of objective and transparent criteria. these criteria must include ecological, social and economic criteria. this could be beneficial for those fleet segments that can demonstrate that they create more than average jobs and have a lower than average environmental impact. the european parliament has ensured greater transparency beyond the allocation of quotas. scientific data on the situation of fish stocks collected by the member states should also be made available to all interested parties, subject to data protection rules.
in writing. − i am pleased that today we have finally adopted the document setting out the principles of the new fisheries policy. importantly, the negotiations between the eu institutions have succeeded in preserving provisions on the use of fishing quotas, which are based on scientific data and ensure adequate recovery of fish stocks.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the special conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east atlantic and the fishing regime for international waters in the north-east atlantic, which aims to strengthen deep-sea fisheries and protect seabed ecosystems. deep-sea fish are caught up to 4,000 metres in the atlantic, and their habitats include coral reefs dating back as much as 8,500 years and ancient species that have so far been little studied. it's a fragile environment and it won't give up if it's damaged. i agree that the licensing system should be improved and that the fishing gear used for deep-sea fishing should be phased out, as is the case with bottom trawls and bottom trawls. i also support the proposal to review the rules after four years to assess the consequences of bottom trawling and the need to ban it altogether. it is also important to provide fishing vessels whose crews use bottom trawls with access to the european maritime and fisheries fund to replace fishing gear, to carry out related ship improvements and to provide the necessary training.
in writing. - i supported the need to seek new regulatory measures for deep-sea fisheries in the north-east atlantic. the regulation aims to ensure sustainable deep-sea fisheries, reduce unwanted catches, limit the impact on vulnerable deep-sea habitats and collect more data on the biology of these species. it is proposed to improve the licensing system and to phase out the less sustainable deep-sea fishing gear, namely bottom trawls and bottom set gillnets.
in writing. - i approve this document. the protection of deep-sea fish stocks is an important element of eu fisheries policy. although we are committed to strengthening the protection of these resources, detailed technical measures to implement these commitments have not yet been established. i am referring to the regulation of the duties and responsibilities of the masters and owners of vessels flying the flags of the eu countries, both in terms of the fishing gear used and the fishing process. i therefore regard this legislation as a major step forward in the conservation and restoration of deep-sea fish stocks.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. the eu emissions trading system is the most important tool to reduce industrial pollution in the eu in a cost-effective and efficient way. in 2008, emissions fell by 10% after the start of the second trading period. the initial objective was to create a market-based measure to stimulate the price of carbon dioxide, thereby encouraging investment in low-carbon technology and renewable energy. however, the decrease in emissions in the second trading period could be strongly influenced by the economic downturn, which reduced economic activity and production. by the end of 2011, there was a surplus of 955 million allowances and this is expected to increase. as the surplus of allowances far exceeds demand, the price of carbon dioxide has fallen from eur 30 per tonne to eur 7 per tonne. this decline in the price of carbon is in contradiction with the increase in sustainable scientific and technological innovation and therefore reduces the incentive to invest in low-carbon technologies and increases the risk of the european union becoming dependent on carbon-intensive infrastructure. i agree that in order to strengthen and make the emissions trading system more efficient in stage 3, the commission needs to take concrete action by ensuring legal clarity and adapting the auction timetable accordingly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it aims to clarify the provisions on legal time limits for the auctioning of allowances laid down in directive 87/2003/ec. the european union emissions trading system is the key instrument to reduce pollution from eu industry in a cost-effective and efficient way. the current economic crisis, combined with the large volume of external carbon credits linked to the clean development mechanism and the many regulatory provisions related to the transition to the third trading period (2013-2020), has resulted in a clear surplus of allowances. by the end of 2011, there was a surplus of 955 million allowances and this is expected to increase. the european parliament therefore proposes to adopt short-term and long-term measures to address the inconsistency in the current eu emissions trading system. in addition, the rapporteur of this ep report proposes that the decision to adapt the auction timetables during the third trading period of the eu ets be made only once, in order to ensure that the stability and predictability of the eu ets is not undermined. therefore, this proposed short-term measure should not be seen as a solution to the current imbalances but as a possibility to ensure the stability of the eu emissions trading system pending the adoption of the necessary long-term structural measures.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on international trade. − madam president, as regards the regulation establishing a partnership instrument: the strategic interest of the eu is to boost growth and jobs by promoting fair and open trade and investment at the multilateral and bilateral level and by supporting the negotiation and implementation of eu trade and investment agreements. in the spirit of the above, in the committee on internal trade we have endeavoured to include provisions in order to better target and coordinate the global union instrument to foster partnership and union visibility globally. the current regulation should contribute to creating a secure climate for the increase of trading and investment opportunities for europe’s goods and services worldwide, especially in areas where europe has a competitive advantage. special attention should be given to improving market access, eliminating trade and investment barriers and fighting against unjustified protectionist measures, and opening up new business opportunities for european companies worldwide, with special focus on smes. the compromise reached last month in the trialogues ensures that the objectives above are duly included in the regulation. therefore we support the adoption of the current partnership instrument.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on women's rights and gender equality. - i thank the rapporteurs for a job well done. it is very important that we can confirm the operation of the globalisation adjustment fund for the next seven years, because overall unemployment rates in europe are still quite high, youth unemployment is not declining, and job creation has not yet returned to pre-crisis levels, while competition in global markets is indeed very intense. so we either have to enable our companies to compete in global markets, or we have to have the tools to help the workers of those companies that have not withstood the pressures of globalization and have had massive layoffs. and it is for these reasons alone that the globalisation fund must survive and continue to operate. it will also continue to help workers who have been affected by the mass redundancies caused by the economic crisis, as well as young people who are neither in education nor in employment, to enter the labour market. i am very pleased that the fund will also be able to be used to help temporary workers, those working on fixed-term contracts - and these are often women - return to the labour market, so it is very important that the fund can be used for this purpose as well.
in writing. i would like to emphasise that in many other countries of the european union, domestic workers are often working with low guarantees, are employed without a contract, are paid late, are required to work overtime without being properly compensated, have their rights to rest and holiday pay ignored, and are not paid their social security contributions. this category of workers is predominantly female. according to eurostat, there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the european union, of whom 89% are women and half are migrants. this international labour organisation convention no 189 requires the protection of domestic workers, who are often in a highly vulnerable situation, mostly women and migrants, and who are victims of discrimination and of various abuses linked to violations of their human rights. it is therefore essential that member states ratify this convention and take measures to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the home.
it is not the first time that the council has put on the agenda key issues of economic growth and employment. economic and monetary union, job creation will be on the agenda again. the talk is as much as it is, but it does not produce the desired results. we must admit in all fairness that the community has failed to achieve a major breakthrough in the economic sphere this year. growth is too low and efforts to boost it have not been backed up by any tax reforms or concessions to small and medium-sized enterprises. the job creation programme in the member states only works to the extent that there were vacancies in the warm period of the year, but this problem - not even a programme, but a temporary solution to it, which was solved by life, but not by the government - is gaining new momentum in the cold period of the year. its negative impact will be felt in the summer of next year, when youth unemployment will jump by a few more percent. in the meantime, i'm going to suggest a few things that i think will work. first, the european union's financial support and substantial tax incentives for businesses in the european union to hire new people under the age of 30. secondly, member states support loans and grants for young people to buy their first home. third, the €6 billion in funding foreseen in the youth employment initiative programme must be made available immediately, rather than waiting until 2015. and the tax burden on labour needs to be reduced much faster, and the earnings of families with young children should be taxed at a minimum.
the european council of 19 and 20 december will decide on the future guidelines of the common security and defence policy, examine proposals for a more effective economic and monetary union and enhance economic policy coordination in order to ensure the long-term economic and financial stability of the european union. the european union leaders will also assess progress in implementing measures to boost growth and employment. these are clearly issues of importance to the well-being of the people of europe. it is clear that the heads of state of the european union will discuss the creation of a banking union. this is one of the most important tasks of lithuania's presidency of the council of the european union. as you know, the first pillar of the banking union - the single supervisory mechanism for banks, which will ensure the prevention of financial crises - has already been agreed, and i hope that the leaders will also agree on the general provisions for the second - the bank resolution mechanism, which will help to deal with the insolvency of banks. this means that if banks are in difficulty, they will bear the costs of their own resolution, thus protecting european taxpayers' money. the banking union thus created will help to avoid possible future financial crises, improve the quality of supervision and restore confidence in the european union in international financial markets. all of this will make it easier for businesses and individuals to borrow. mr president, the european council will also discuss progress in the field of energy. we know that the new eu budget, which we approved last session, includes a line for funding strategic energy interconnection projects, and the european commission has approved a list of energy projects of common interest. given the current high cost of energy for the people of europe, it is essential to pay close attention to the proper implementation of these projects in order to complete the internal energy market of the european union and to eliminate existing energy islands. this will increase the competitiveness of the european economy and lower prices for consumers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to establish a multiannual action programme, pericles 2020, for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2020, to promote actions to protect the euro against counterfeiting and related fraud. in december 2011, the commission adopted two proposals for the programmes 'hercule iii' and 'pericles 2020'. the programmes, with a budget of eur 110 million and eur 7,7 million respectively, will be implemented over seven years. hercule iii is designed to combat fraud, corruption and any other illegal activities detrimental to the eu's financial interests. pericles 2020 is an exchange, assistance and training programme to ensure the safety of euro banknotes and coins in europe and worldwide. i agree that the proposed co-financing rates put a significant financial strain on the fund and should therefore be reduced accordingly. 70% is the more appropriate co-financing rate and 80% could be applied in exceptional circumstances. i agree that the monitoring, evaluation and management measures put in place should ensure that the funds are used in the most efficient way possible. the consultations organised by the commission during the various stages of the implementation of the programme should focus on the mutual exchange of ideas with a view to drawing on experience gained in the future implementation of the programme.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to establish a financial package for the four years 2013-2017 of the european statistical programme, financed by the 2014-2020 programming period (dfp). the implementation of eu policies in different areas requires comparable and reliable statistical information on the economic, social and environmental situation in the eu and its various national and regional components. statistics are essential for a better public understanding of europe, for citizens to participate in democratic processes and for debates on the present and future of the eu. on 15 january 2013, a regulation was adopted on the european statistical programme 2013-2017 establishing a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics for the period 2013-2017. the commission's proposal for this regulation provides for a financial envelope of eur 299,2 million for the five years of the programme.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the household. there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, of whom 89% are women and half are migrants. domestic work, given its isolated and individual nature, is one of the most unprotected and invisible forms of work. the international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers was adopted in 2011. it requires ngos to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the household. in 2013, the commission submitted a proposal authorising the un to ratify the convention. i support calls for member states to provide domestic workers with the means to ensure that fundamental rights at work are respected (freedom of association; abolition of all forms of forced or compulsory labour; effective abolition of child labour and discrimination at work). it is necessary to ensure adequate living conditions, the right to be informed of working conditions by means of a written contract, uninterrupted weekly rest of at least 24 hours, protection of the minimum wage and the right of domestic workers to a safe and healthy working environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is very important to draw attention to the fact that domestic work, given its isolated and individual nature, is one of the most unprotected and invisible forms of work. for these reasons, it is very often difficult for domestic workers to obtain information about their rights and to join associations or unions that represent them, which can give them the opportunity to defend their labour and social rights more effectively. in addition, domestic workers are often working with low guarantees, are employed without a contract, are late in receiving wages, are required to work overtime without being properly compensated, have their rights to rest and holidays ignored, and their social security contributions are not paid. member states should therefore be encouraged to ratify this international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189), as it is necessary for those member states that have ratified it to take measures to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the home.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because of the need to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the household. the supplementary convention of the international labour organisation on decent work for domestic workers was adopted in 2011. it requires member states to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the home. in 2013, the commission submitted a proposal authorising member states to ratify the convention. there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, of whom 89% are women and half are migrants. domestic work, given its isolated and individual nature, is one of the most unprotected and invisible forms of work. i believe that domestic workers should be given the means to ensure that fundamental rights at work are respected (freedom of association; abolition of all forms of forced or compulsory labour; effective abolition of child labour and discrimination at work). to set a minimum age for domestic workers which shall not be less than the age for workers in general laid down in national legislation; ensure: adequate living conditions; the right to be informed of working conditions by means of a written contract; at least 24 hours of uninterrupted weekly rest; protection of the minimum wage for domestic workers and the right of domestic workers to a safe and healthy working environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for accession to the international labour organisation's convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189), which requires ratifying member states to take measures to ensure decent working conditions and social rights and to prevent abuse, violence and child labour in the home. i believe that improving working conditions for workers is inseparable from the freedoms granted by the eu in the field of mobility of persons and workers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to conclude a protocol to enable armenia to gradually accede to or increase its participation in certain union programmes. the partnership and cooperation agreement between the republic of armenia and the european communities entered into force in 1999. armenia has been actively participating in the european neighbourhood policy since 2004 and in the eastern partnership since its implementation in 2009. this proposal provides for a general agreement on the general principles for the participation of armenia in union programmes. this agreement will allow armenia to progressively join or enhance its participation in certain union programmes, as well as to further promote links in the cultural, educational, environmental, technical and scientific fields, to strengthen people-to-people and sectoral cooperation and to strengthen policies and relations through the eastern partnership.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the right granted to spain to exempt or reduce taxes on certain products produced in the canary islands. council decision 2002/546/ec authorised spain to exempt or reduce the levies on certain products produced in the canary islands until 31 december 2011 in order to strengthen the local industry and make it more competitive. the 2009 global economic crisis, which affected travel, has caused a lot of damage to the canary islands' economy, with the unemployment rate reaching 26.2% in 2009 after hovering around 10.4% in 2001-2007. the spanish authorities have requested that the application of these special rules be renewed for the period 2014-2020. the extension of the period of application of the decision is requested for a further period of six months. as the measure aims to further stimulate economic activity and stabilise employment in this outermost region and as the extension of the application of the decision is proposed for a limited period, i support this proposal.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the coordination of european union donors should help to achieve the objective of ending all formal and informal geographically linked aid and changing the efficiency agenda for the delivery of aid. the development of efficiency in the agenda. such european union initiatives to improve donor coordination are voluntary and optional, but crucial for effective eu development policy. this requires better coordination with the international community and, more importantly, with local actors, in particular local authorities, national parliaments, civil society and non-governmental organisations. only by pooling the resources of donor countries can multilateral development organisations increase the effectiveness of aid and achieve maximum efficiency. it should also be noted that the resources provided by international organisations also help donors to exchange information on development activities, thereby increasing transparency and accountability. it is also important to support capacity building in these countries to enable them to develop skills, gain practical experience and establish the institutions needed to manage their development effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to strengthen europe's position in the world and to set a budget for external measures to support the eu's commitments and promote common values for the period 2014-2020. the proposal will enable the union to fulfil its commitments on the global stage: to fight poverty and to promote democracy, peace and prosperity. the eu will support developing countries, the european neighbourhood and countries preparing for eu accession through a range of instruments. the eu budget will be able to support 0.7% of eu gdp by 2015 to meet eu commitments at a similar level as before. the new commission approach change agenda, which aims to focus eu assistance on fewer sectors that help to consolidate democracy, human rights, good governance and promote inclusive and sustainable growth, will be supported. under the new differentiation principle, the eu will allocate a higher share of funds where the impact of aid is likely to be greatest, i.e. to countries and regions most in need of aid, including fragile states. the proposal includes nine instruments: the instrument for pre-accession assistance, the european neighbourhood instrument, the development cooperation instrument, the partnership instrument, the stability instrument, the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr), the instrument for cooperation in the field of nuclear safety, the greenland instrument and the european development fund.
in writing. − the european union's external action is based on six instruments, the implementation of which is governed by common rules and procedures. the aim is to ensure that the eu uses the resources allocated to these measures in the most efficient way possible to achieve the objectives set, ensuring their consistency, their interaction and their proper complementarity. in summary, all measures shall contribute to the universality and indivisibility of democracy, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principle of equality, solidarity and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law. at the same time, it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and accountability of the implementation of these measures, involving the european parliament, and to further enhance their visibility.
in writing. − the european union is well known in the world's hotspots not for military interventions but for civil, humanitarian and development aid. the eu's external action will be worth €32 billion between 2013 and 2020. this will continue to support, for example, civil societies outside the eu in their fight for human rights, democracy and the rule of law, as well as the economies of countries, especially their 'small' and 'medium' enterprises. the eu should give more support to those countries that are ready to implement reforms without delay. i voted in favour of this report because it stresses the need for the european parliament to have a weighty voice in decisions on external action policy. the ep has the right to be able to check how the european commission implements this policy not only at the time of the report but at any time.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the european globalisation adjustment fund (2014-2020). the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide an instrument of eu solidarity and support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation and the direct effects of the global economic and financial crisis. the european commission data show that as many as 48% of those who benefited from egf support returned to the labour market. the fund will also provide temporary support for young people who are out of work and/or education in regions where the rate of unemployment is disproportionate. the egf will continue to provide eu support for the re-skilling, job search and recruitment of redundant workers. the egf will provide eur 1 billion over seven years.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to extend the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for the period 2014-2020. this would allow the eu to continue to provide support for the re-skilling, job search and recruitment of displaced workers. the egf shall support job search, retraining of workers, related specialist advice and entrepreneurship measures. i regret that the fund's funding for this period has been reduced from eur 3.5 billion to eur 1.05 billion. i think his funding should be increased. i agree that support should also be provided to workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the financial or economic crisis. it is also important that the egf should be able to provide temporary support to young people who are not in employment or education and who live in regions where disproportionate numbers of people have lost their jobs. it is important that temporary or self-employed workers also benefit from the egf from the following year.
in writing. − i voted on this report on the european globalisation adjustment fund, which provides support to more than 20 000 eu citizens every year. in lithuania, two large companies in alytuje - snaigė and tekstilė - and two sectors that were most affected at the beginning of the crisis - construction and furniture - have already benefited from egf support. the foundation's support for the people of lithuania is therefore important. unemployment in the european union remains high and competition in global markets is intensifying. we are not immune to economic crises. it is clear that it is necessary to continue to have a financial instrument to help employees of bankrupt companies. therefore, we have not only extended the egf but also improved it to make it easier, faster and simpler for member states to access it. support will also be available for young people who are not in employment or education and who live in regions with high unemployment. aid may be granted to undertakings which lay off at least 500 workers over a four-month period, including workers made redundant by suppliers or downstream companies. before the crisis, firms which had made at least 1000 redundancies could count on the fund's support. the egf will be able to finance up to 60% of the costs, i.e. more than the european commission proposed, which planned to finance only 50% of these costs. the budget of the egf was approved during the negotiations, amounting to eur 1 billion.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal as it is necessary to continue to provide eu support for redundant workers as well as temporary or self-employed workers from 2014. the fund would support not only those who have lost their jobs as a result of globalisation, but also workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the economic crisis. the fund will be available if the company or its suppliers have had to lay off 500 workers for the reasons mentioned above. support will be provided for active labour market measures aimed at accelerating the reintegration of dismissed workers into the labour market (training, retraining, counselling, etc.). i believe that the european globalisation adjustment fund should be made more attractive and easier for member states to use.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to replace the national notification and authorisation procedures for carriers of radioactive materials by a single registration system. the implementation of this regulation should allow simplification of procedures and reduction of administrative burden while maintaining a high level of radiation protection. the replacement of national notification and authorisation procedures with a single transport registration system will help to simplify procedures, reduce administrative burdens and remove barriers to market entry, while maintaining the high level of radiation safety achieved. i support the proposals set out below to ensure that the criteria for issuing a registration certificate and the data models are uniform and that the registration process is harmonised, to introduce an electronic signature and to establish a mechanism for the exchange of information between the national authorities of the member states and the registration system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which welcomes the adoption of the european union's annual report on human rights and democracy in the world 2012. human rights are a key aspect of the eu's relations with all third countries, including its strategic partners. it should also be emphasised that eu human rights policy must consistently respect the obligations of the treaty, ensure coherence between internal and external policy instruments and avoid double standards in external policy. we should therefore call for the adoption of the eu foreign affairs council conclusions on human rights and strategic partners, which would set out common minimum standards for the human rights situation for member states and eu officials to be required to set at least for strategic partners at their level. in this report, the european parliament reiterates its condemnation of violence and all forms of violence against women, including domestic violence, and calls on all council of europe member states to sign and ratify the convention on preventing and combating violence against women, and on the eu to launch the accession process to the convention, in order to ensure coherence in the eu's internal and external action on violence against women.
in writing. − the world still faces many problems related to violations of human rights and the suppression of fundamental freedoms. human rights belong to everyone and everyone. recognition of this principle is an integral aspect of the eu's internal and external relations. the eu's internal and external policies differ from those of, unfortunately, many other countries. some important eu partners often express their discontent when the eu draws attention to problems or breaches. nevertheless, this should not diminish our resolve to speak out about wrongdoing. in today's world, it is important that the eu, together with like-minded people, makes even greater efforts and measures to improve the human rights situation in the world.
in writing. − the promotion of human rights and democracy is the backbone of the eu's foreign policy. the eu appointed its first high representative for human rights a few years ago. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for special attention to be paid to human rights in countries which have just been liberated from the yoke of authoritarianism and where democracy is still very fragile. i also agree with the rapporteur that special attention should be paid to countries which are still struggling to establish democracy and human rights. the eu must continue to promote and defend the universality of human rights directly and through other global organisations such as the united nations, the international criminal court. democracy and people's freedom must be created within countries, not imposed from outside. the eu can help, but only the states and their societies can do it. free elections are not enough, we need to build civil societies that guarantee human rights and freedoms step by step.
in writing. − twenty years after the creation of the single market, anti-competitive practices still have a significant impact on many consumers in different sectors of the economy. the public sector is often reluctant to open up important sectors of the economy to competition, such as railways, airports, electronic communications or electricity. furthermore, there are no fully independent regulatory authorities in the public sector to ensure that the market operates properly, fairly and without discrimination. another problem is the provision of state aid. state aid to banks is often viewed negatively, as at the same time social services are being restricted in many european countries in order to restore fiscal sustainability, and banks receive billions in public funds. i therefore support the proposals put forward to ensure that banks are fully accountable for the use of these public funds. it is also important to ensure that the burden on taxpayers is minimised.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the annual competition policy report should be used not only as a description of the practical implementation of the commission's competition policy, but also as a tool to help increase the overall competitiveness of the union, develop competition and open up markets to new entrants, thus expanding and deepening the internal market. the european parliament welcomes the commission's report and its focus on the contribution of competition policy to merger control, the removal of barriers, the abuse of a dominant position, the fight against collusion and state aid measures that distort competition, in order to benefit the common market and to take account of the evolution of the world economy. however, it should be noted that product prices still vary between member states, for example, because of the different agreements between member states and the pharmaceutical industry. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to examine the problem and to put forward proposals in the interests of consumers, to avoid unnecessary price differences and to make the internal market as transparent as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to ensure a fair standard of living for farmers in mountainous areas, less favoured areas and the outermost regions. i agree that it is important to focus on these most vulnerable areas in order to ensure a decent standard of living for farmers and a future for rural areas. the european milk sector is facing major changes as quotas expire in 2015. for the first time in 31 years, the sector will not be subject to milk quotas. this substantial change is liable to affect the functioning of the market in the milk sector, in particular in less favoured areas and the outermost regions. the so-called milk package aims to increase the bargaining power of producers and it is also important to further investigate the impact of the abolition of quotas, in particular in less favoured areas and the outermost regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to reduce the risk of disasters in developing countries. between 1992 and 2012, 64% of the world's population was affected by natural disasters. 1.3 million people died (230,675 of them in haiti alone) and the damage was estimated at $2 trillion. since 2000, there have been 50 to 65 food crises per year, compared with about 25 to 45 in the 1990s. despite the increase in disaster losses, more than 95% of humanitarian aid funds are still allocated to disaster response and recovery measures and less than 5% to disaster risk reduction. a commission working document on a resilience action plan for countries with a high risk of crisis for the period 2013-2020 has recently been presented. risk reduction (rr) is an essential condition for ensuring resilience. nrm includes risk analysis and management aimed at reducing vulnerability to the threat and thus strengthening resilience. i support the suggestions made to include resilience measures in development and humanitarian aid programming. the eu institutions and the un should better coordinate their development and humanitarian activities. it is also important to increase efforts to address the inefficient use of funds for nrm and resilience actions and the duplication of activities and efforts in this area.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. various examples show that women with disabilities are often in a much worse position than healthy women. this disparity must be eliminated. women with disabilities should be guaranteed the right to live a life of personal choice and ideas, as should other women. to facilitate this, social barriers need to be reduced and a positive awareness of the needs of diversity needs to be created. we, the members of the european parliament, believe that special attention should be paid to the childhood and adolescence of women with disabilities, as these periods can provide the basis for many positive changes in adult life. blended learning clearly helps to reduce social barriers and build confidence. it is essential to start talking about the problem of violence and discrimination in the language and media, in schools to help children and young adults have fair and equitable speech. i think it is very important that all women with disabilities who are able to work have the opportunity to pursue a career and be independent.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to create an accessible physical, mental and social environment for the 80 million disabled people in the european union, free from prejudices and stereotypes and free from barriers and obstacles to their full enjoyment of fundamental human rights and european citizenship. 15% of the european population are disabled; one in four europeans has a disabled family member. of the 80 million disabled people in the eu, 46 million are women and girls with disabilities, representing 16% of the total female population in the eu. the participation of women with disabilities in the labour market is still lacking. i agree that the involvement of disabled people and ngos in the development of new norms should become the norm, as this is the only way to act with disabled people and not in relation to them. i agree with the suggestions that a clear and non-discriminatory definition of disability, possibly using the un convention definition, is needed, as is the urgent implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities to ensure that the rights of persons with disabilities become a reality. it is also important to highlight the work of ngos on women with disabilities and its importance for the state and society.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because women with disabilities face a wide range of difficulties, including severe difficulties in obtaining adequate housing, access to health care, public transport, education and vocational training, employment, inequalities in access to credit and other production resources, and a low level of participation in decision-making processes. it is very important to note that as the number of disabled people increases, so will the burden on carers, especially those who care for close family members, and most carers of disabled people are women, who are forced to reduce their working hours and even leave the labour market to care for dependent family members. the european parliament therefore stresses the need to provide women and girls with disabilities with appropriate care in the medical sector, and to provide continuous and career-long specific training in the field of mental illness and/or disability in order to identify these illnesses as effectively as possible and to refer patients to specialist medical institutions. parliament also called on the eu and the member states to take all necessary legal, administrative, social and educational measures to protect women and girls with disabilities at home and abroad from all forms of exploitation, violence and abuse.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. there may be up to one billion people with disabilities worldwide, with up to 80% of them in developing countries. the situation of women in developing countries is often difficult, and even more attention needs to be paid to women and girls with disabilities. in order to implement the europe 2020 strategy, we must ensure the full participation of women with disabilities in social and economic life and in decision-making. at the same time, women with disabilities are more likely to be victims of physical violence and exploitation, and their integration requires support for a variety of educational and training programmes, increasing access to a range of public services and a balanced life. to reduce as far as possible the problems in the member states related to the lack of infrastructure or the negative attitude towards such women, even violence against them. i therefore fully support the call in the document for the immediate implementation of a comprehensive strategy to combat violence against women. cooperation between states and national governments is also essential, because we have 80 million of them in the european union, more than half of whom are women.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims at a european retail action plan. the retail and wholesale sector generates 11% of eu gdp, accounts for 29% of european smes and employs almost 33 million people. however, a number of barriers to cross-border supply of goods, access to cross-border retail services for consumers and market access for retailers remain. in 2013, the commission adopted the european retail action plan and is preparing to set up a permanent retail competitiveness group to help formulate further specific objectives of the action plan, monitor progress, make recommendations to ensure that the actions set out in the action plan are fully implemented, etc. i support the proposals to promote consumer awareness, to increase access to retail services, and to encourage the exchange of good practice in commercial spatial planning between ngos. it is necessary to create fairer trading relationships between the food and non-food supply chains and to create a better working environment.
for the efd group i also want to thank mrs meissner for this important document. the european union's maritime economy is crucial to achieving the europe 2020 objectives and has enormous potential to help ensure europe's competitiveness in a global world, and the european union should therefore take a leading position in strengthening marine and maritime research, innovation and growth in the maritime sectors. marine energy can also help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the european union's dependence on energy imports. the promotion and protection of marine aquaculture is also important. european ports, shipping lanes and the shipping industry play an important role in the supply chain and in connecting european companies and the european market to the rest of the world.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in the context of the economic crisis, high unemployment in many member states and high energy prices, the creation of sustainable jobs and the promotion of economic growth are important steps towards social cohesion. innovation is one of the ways to achieve this and must be given a high level of eu attention. environmental innovation is essential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to use resources more efficiently, to increase the use of recycled materials and to produce quality products with a lower environmental impact, and to develop greener production processes and services. green innovation can be very diverse: new water filters for wastewater treatment, thinner and stronger steel to reduce waste materials, or a business model that provides repair services instead of selling products. we, the members of the european parliament, call on all the main actors in each sector to work together for green growth, innovation and job creation and to use existing instruments (e.g. technology platforms, joint working groups, etc.) and call on the commission and the member states to develop new legislation in the areas of the development and use of renewable energy sources and energy efficiency and to strengthen existing legislation in these areas, ensuring legal certainty and a level playing field and encouraging public and private sector investment.
in writing. - i approve this document. i am convinced that we will achieve better results in implementing environmental policy not by banning but by encouraging businesses to engage in this type of activity. this is particularly relevant now that the need for economic stimulus is still present. i therefore join the calls on the commission to come forward with a more detailed proposal on the integration of the concept of eco-innovation into eu policy and the means to finance and accelerate its implementation.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the payment accounts. modern payment services are an integral part of physical and legal activities. i believe that all persons legally resident in the european union should be able to open a basic bank account, compare fees and transfer their account to another bank if necessary. in other words, core accounts should allow consumers to deposit or withdraw money and make transfers within the european union within the limits of the amount of money in the account. the information on invoice charges should be clear and consistent so that the consumer can understand and compare it, and the process of switching the invoice should be as simple as possible for the consumer. i do not think that nationality or residence should be a reason to prevent a person from opening a basic bank account. there should also be at least one independent website in each eu country that allows banks to compare their fees and interest rates.
in writing. − i supported the proposal because of the importance of the eu's marine and coastal areas and the marine economy. the eu's maritime economy is crucial to achieving the europe 2020 goals and has huge potential to help ensure europe's competitiveness in a global world. the eu should therefore take a leading role in strengthening marine and maritime research and innovation and in fostering growth in the maritime sectors. marine energy can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the eu's dependence on energy imports. the promotion and protection of marine aquaculture is also important. european ports, shipping lanes and the shipping industry play an important role in the supply chain and in the links between european companies and the european market and the rest of the world. but these activities are much more, such as the extraction of oil, gas and other raw materials and resources or maritime and coastal tourism. to ensure sustainable economic growth and avoid conflicts between different sectors, it is necessary to coordinate the current and future needs of the maritime domain. i agree with the proposal that a procedural framework for the development and implementation of maritime spatial plans and integrated coastal zone management strategies should be established. we must work to secure the union's energy supply, to promote the development of maritime transport, to promote sustainable fisheries, and to preserve and protect the environment.
in writing. − i have agreed to the proposal as it is important to ensure that the delegated regulation on electronic procurement enters into force as soon as possible, bearing in mind that the essential provisions of the basic legislative act, including the provisions on the submission of declarations of performance, apply from 1 july 2013. the possibility of publishing these declarations online, in line with the legislative authority's wishes, would allow the construction product manufacturers to reduce costs and would also increase flexibility in the construction sector. the commission should have drawn up the delegated regulation in advance in order to avoid undue delay in derogating from the obligation for manufacturers to provide a copy of the declaration of performance in writing or electronically for each product placed on the market. it is essential that parliament and the council be able to exercise their legislative powers as defined in the treaties, as well as to decide which powers should be conferred on the commission in future basic legislative acts, and that parliament, together with experts from the member states and other stakeholders, be able to participate in transparent consultations prior to the adoption of a delegated act.
mr president, the report on ukraine went along with the situation. it was not as positive as expected and in some points it does not describe the situation absolutely correctly. i voted in favour, but something needs to be commented on. mr yanukovych should never be called ʻukraineʼ and his decision, or obedience to the decision of the kremlin, could be seen not as a harsh withdrawal from the neighbourhood agenda but rather as a disappointing postponement. of course it was an authoritarian step by two persons, rather than failure by the eu. we may appeal to moscow to ask permission for mr yanukovych to keep to his electoral promises, but we must also recognise that, long before this, our own policies have been too hesitant, without a clear line. step by step, the principle of openness of the eu became reality. the barriers put up to cope with homework as well – to ukraine some of them looked rather artificially hardened. the treatment of yulia tymoshenko lacks humanitarian and political neutrality. the request to change it was just and human. nevertheless the very formula about selective justice may be seen as hypocritical. while underlining that this sort of justice in the ukraine is to be condemned, we endorse scandalous selective justice on a gross scale towards millions of victims of both totalitarian tyrannies in europe, those who caused the second world war. victims of one of them are honoured; victims of the other are not.
in writing. - i fully support the position set out in this document. indeed, despite the fact that the amendments to the eu's basic law made by the lisbon treaty, which give the european parliament greater powers in the legislative field, have been in force for more than four years, the eu council often continues to ignore the european parliament and its position. the european parliament is the only institution directly elected by eu citizens, and the council of the eu must take account of the ep's position in the legislative process and align its negotiating positions with it.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to establish when sorted waste is not waste. the draft of this regulation defines that paper is not waste when the sorted waste is used as paper fibre for the production of paper, i.e. before it is processed in a paper mill, which is contrary to the current definition of recycling, according to which waste must be recycled. i therefore support the rapporteur's position to oppose the adoption of this council regulation.
mr president, systematic and state-sanctioned organ harvesting from prisoners of conscience in china, including from falun gong practitioners – according to the information i have received – in prison for their religious beliefs, is absolutely unacceptable and should be ended immediately. voluntary and informed consent is a precondition for ethical organ donation and this is not the case in china as far as i know, and my knowledge is based on the information i have. it is a shame that the great country china, which, a month ago, was elected to serve on the united nations human rights council for a period of three years, is on the list of countries with a lamentable human rights record. finally, all prisoners of conscience in china, including falun gong practitioners, should be released immediately.
in writing. – united nations human rights commissioner navi pillay visited sri lanka in august and welcomed the governmentʼs impressive achievements on resettlement, reconstruction and rehabilitation. we all welcomed the elections to the northern provincial council which were held successfully in september, and we hope for a constructive dialogue between the government and the new northern provincial council. certainly, there are issues to be resolved, but we call on the leadership of sri lanka and encourage them to take further steps in the same direction, i.e. towards reconstruction and reconciliation. speaking about reconciliation, we all understand what is needed to achieve it: political will, action and finally – time. the legacy of the war, which lasted for 26 years, is visible everywhere. let us remember how long it took for us europeans to achieve reconciliation. let us remember northern ireland or spain, at least. the european union should continue its support for the reconciliation process in sri lanka in order to achieve tangible results.
